## Reading the evidence

The primary reading copy covers the entire original session. Complete JSON exports preserve message IDs, timestamps, text and tool events for ten related sessions. Original conversation language is retained. Known runtime credential values and common credential patterns were checked in memory before saving. The scan required zero credential replacements. Export hashes and message counts are in [Export-Manifest.json](redacted-exports/FR01/Export-Manifest.json).

Annotations below paraphrase actual user directives and their stated constraints. The rationale describes the engineering purpose apparent in the instruction. Messages reporting terminal results remain supplied execution evidence. A reported peer approval with placeholder names or dates is an incomplete historical record.

The complete exports are evidence of what was said and generated. Personal contribution and final approval should be described using the actual division of work. The [D6 report](../Report.md) provides the contribution account and personal reflection.

Load existing market and sentiment inputs; attach verified metrics and coverage; run debate and candidate generation; gate candidate before official sinks. Treat any display of intermediate model text as unverified and keep candidate text out of official output on refusal. Historical settlement is outside the metered analysis scope.\n14: \n15: Use fixed fixtures and fake transports for deterministic tests, then separately smoke-test configured live integration. Emit run ID, publication status/reason, verified metric counts, sentiment coverage, request count and message byte size without credentials or raw prompts. Deduplicate only optional history, preserve paired tool calls/results, prioritize newer optional messages, serialize deterministically as UTF-8 and drop optional blocks oldest first until within the configured cap. Trigger compaction above 64 KiB at the proposed gate settings. This is a byte cap, not a token guarantee; do not infer one token budget for all providers. Reassemble and assert all standing constraints and required blocks are present after reduction; reject before transport if they cannot fit.\n18: \n19: **Consequences.** Minimal upstream changes and explicit rejection states; shared dispatch and publication integration must be reviewed together. Keep course fixtures isolated from users' local caches and memory. Reports may contain nonsecret source metadata; users control local retention. No credentials, raw model sessions or student identifiers belong in public logs. Repeatability claims require a new run or an explicitly versioned snapshot, not a retained LLM answer.\n\n(End of file - total 11 lines)\n</content>"

Do not assume this filename is auto-discovered. Before using it, inspect the effective configuration with `OPENCODE_CONFIG=\"$PWD/.opencode/permissions.jsonc\" opencode debug config --pure` locally and check that no merged user/project config grants extra tools or MCP access. Use a clean profile if it does. Verify Plan/Verify deny edits, Build asks for a designated module and denies frozen paths. Do not paste full resolved config into public evidence. This is tool-level enforcement, not an OS sandbox; any failed guard check blocks agent use.\n\n(End of file - total 15 lines)\n</content>"

tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config, run_config_context, set_config\nfrom tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import get_current_date, is_historical\nfrom tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\nfrom tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\nfrom tradingagents.llm_clients import create_tier_client, tier_provider\nfrom tradingagents.memory import TradingMemoryLog, settlement\nfrom tradingagents.memory.reflection import Reflector\nfrom tradingagents.reporting import write_report_tree\n\nfrom .checkpointer import checkpoint_step, clear_checkpoint, get_checkpointer, thread_id\nfrom .conditional_logic import ConditionalLogic\nfrom .propagation import Propagator\nfrom .setup import GraphSetup\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef _validate_trade_date(trade_date) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The run date as a canonical ``YYYY-MM-DD`` string no later than today.\"\"\"\n    value = str(trade_date)\n    try:\n        canonical = datetime.strptime(value, \"%Y-%m-%d\").strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\") == value\n    except ValueError:\n        canonical = False\n    if not canonical:\n        raise ValueError(f\"trade_date must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format, got {trade_date!r}\")\n    if value > get_current_date():\n        raise ValueError(f\"trade_date cannot be in the future: {value}\")\n    return value\n\n\n# Config keys that do not change what a run writes: where it keeps its files,\n# whether it checkpoints, and how often it retries a provider.\n_NOT_IN_SIGNATURE = frozenset({\n    \"results_dir\", \"data_cache_dir\", \"memory_log_path\", \"checkpoint_enabled\", \"llm_max_retries\",\n})\n\n\nclass TradingAgentsGraph:\n    \"\"\"Main class that orchestrates the trading agents framework.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"),\n        debug=False,\n        config: dict[str, Any] = None,\n        callbacks: list | None = None,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Initialize the trading agents graph and components.\n\n        Args:\n            selected_analysts: List of analyst types to include\n            debug: Whether to run in debug mode\n            config: Configuration dictionary. If None, uses default config\n            callbacks: Optional list of callback handlers (e.g., for tracking LLM/tool stats)\n        \"\"\"\n        self.debug = debug\n        self.config = config or DEFAULT_CONFIG\n        self.callbacks = callbacks or []\n\n        set_config(self.config)\n\n        os.makedirs(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n        os.makedirs(self.config[\"results_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n\n        extra = {\"callbacks\": self.callbacks} if self.callbacks else {}\n        self.deep_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"deep\", **extra).get_llm()\n        self.quick_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"quick\", **extra).get_llm()\n\n        self.memory_log = TradingMemoryLog(self.config)\n\n        self.conditional_logic = ConditionalLogic(\n            max_debate_rounds=self.config[\"max_debate_rounds\"],\n            max_risk_discuss_rounds=self.config[\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"],\n        )\n        # An analyst takes two graph steps per tool round, plus its first turn\n        # and its wrap-up; a limit past the recursion limit would end the run\n        # there instead.\n        max_tool_rounds, max_recur_limit = self.config[\"max_tool_rounds\"], self.config[\"max_recur_limit\"]\n        if 2 * max_tool_rounds + 2 >= max_recur_limit:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"max_tool_rounds={max_tool_rounds} needs max_recur_limit above {2 * max_tool_rounds + 2}\"\n            )\n        self.graph_setup = GraphSetup(\n            self.quick_thinking_llm,\n            self.deep_thinking_llm,\n            self.conditional_logic,\n            max_tool_rounds,\n        )\n\n        self.propagator = Propagator(\n            max_recur_limit=max_recur_limit,\n        )\n        self.reflector = Reflector(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n\n        # Graph-shape-affecting run choices, kept for the checkpoint signature.\n        self.selected_analysts = tuple(selected_analysts)\n\n        # Set up the graph: keep the workflow for recompilation with a checkpointer.\n        self.workflow = self.graph_setup.setup_graph(selected_analysts, memory_node=self._memory_step)\n        self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n        self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n        self._resuming = False\n\n    def resolve_instrument_context(self, ticker: str, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n                                   trade_date: str | None = None) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Resolve ticker identity once and return the full instrument context.\n\n        Deterministic yfinance lookup (cached, fail-open) injected into a\n        context string so every agent anchors to the real company instead of\n        hallucinating one from the price chart (#814). Both the propagate()\n        path and the CLI call this so the resolved identity reaches the whole\n        graph regardless of entry point.\n        \"\"\"\n        identity = resolve_instrument_identity(ticker)\n        return build_instrument_context(ticker, asset_type, identity, trade_date)\n\n    def _memory_as_of(self, trade_date) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Point-in-time cutoff for past-context lessons (#1251).\n\n        A historical/backtest run (trade date before today) filters lessons to\n        those already resolved by the trade date. A current-date run returns\n        None, disabling the filter so live behavior and pre-migration entries\n        (which have no stored resolution date) are unaffected.\n        \"\"\"\n        return str(trade_date) if is_historical(trade_date) else None\n\n    def _run_signature(self, asset_type: str, portfolio=None) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Run inputs that must invalidate a checkpoint if changed.\n\n        Keyed into the checkpoint thread ID so a resume under a different analyst\n        selection, debate/risk depth, or asset mode starts fresh instead of\n        silently continuing the previous graph (#1089). The rest of the config\n        counts too (provider, models, endpoint, language, vendors, limits): a\n        resume must not carry reports that other settings produced. Only where\n        the run keeps its files and how it retries are left out.\n        \"\"\"\n        settings = {k: v for k, v in self.config.items() if k not in _NOT_IN_SIGNATURE}\n        digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(settings, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]\n        return \"|\".join([\n            \"analysts=\" + \",\".join(self.selected_analysts),\n            f\"debate={self.config['max_debate_rounds']}\",\n            f\"risk={self.config['max_risk_discuss_rounds']}\",\n            f\"asset={asset_type}\",\n            # None, an empty book and a changed book are three different runs.\n            f\"portfolio={portfolio.fingerprint() if portfolio is not None else 'none'}\",\n            # The layout itself: a checkpoint saved when analysts ran one after\n            # another has pending nodes this graph no longer has, and one saved\n            # before the Memory Log step would resume without the lessons.\n            \"analysts=parallel\",\n            \"memory=parallel\",\n            f\"settings={digest}\",\n        ])\n\n    def propagate(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n        \"\"\"Run the trading agents graph for a company on a specific date.\n\n        ``asset_type`` selects between the stock pipeline (default) and the\n        crypto pipeline (``\"crypto\"``) shipped in #567 — the CLI auto-detects\n        from the ticker; programmatic callers pass it explicitly. When\n        ``checkpoint_enabled`` is set in config, the graph is recompiled with\n        a per-ticker SqliteSaver so a crashed run can resume from the last\n        successful node on a subsequent invocation with the same ticker+date.\n\n        Returns ``(final_state, signal)`` where ``signal`` is one of the 5-tier\n        ratings (Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) or ``\"REVIEW\"``\n        when the decision had no parseable rating (#1170); guard with\n        ``tradingagents.agents.rating.is_review`` before mapping it to the\n        PortfolioRating enum.\n        \"\"\"\n        trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n\n        with run_config(self.config), \\\n                self.checkpoint_scope(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio) as thread_id_value:\n            return self._run_graph(\n                company_name, trade_date, asset_type=asset_type,\n                checkpoint_thread_id=thread_id_value, portfolio=portfolio,\n            )\n\n    def begin_checkpoint(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None) -> str | None:\n        \"\"\"Recompile the graph with a per-ticker checkpointer and return the\n        ``thread_id`` to inject into the stream/invoke ``config`` (or ``None``\n        when checkpointing is disabled).\n\n        Pair every call with :meth:`end_checkpoint` in a ``finally``. Both\n        ``propagate`` (via :meth:`checkpoint_scope`) and the CLI stream path use\n        this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup\n        lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less\n        graph, making the flag a no-op.\n        \"\"\"\n        self._resuming = False\n        if not self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n            return None\n        signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)\n        self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name)\n        saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()\n        self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)\n\n        step = checkpoint_step(\n            self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature\n        )\n        self._resuming = step is not None\n        if step is not None:\n            logger.info(\"Resuming from step %d for %s on %s\", step, company_name, trade_date)\n        else:\n            logger.info(\"Starting fresh for %s on %s\", company_name, trade_date)\n        return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)\n\n    def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):\n        \"\"\"The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,\n        else the initial state for a fresh run.\n\n        LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;\n        re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message\n        reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).\n        \"\"\"\n        return None if self._resuming else init_state\n\n    def end_checkpoint(self):\n        \"\"\"Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run.\"\"\"\n        if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:\n            self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)\n            self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n            self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n        self._resuming = False\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n        \"\"\"Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path.\"\"\"\n        try:\n            yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n        finally:\n            self.end_checkpoint()\n\n    def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n        \"\"\"Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249).\"\"\"\n        if self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n            clear_checkpoint(\n                self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date),\n                self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),\n            )\n\n    def run_settings(self) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.\n\n        An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and\n        local paths are never recorded.\n        \"\"\"\n        cfg = self.config\n        return {\n            \"version\": tradingagents.__version__,\n            \"llm_provider\": cfg.get(\"llm_provider\"),\n            \"deep_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"deep\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n            \"deep_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"deep_think_llm\"),\n            \"quick_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"quick\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n            \"quick_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"quick_think_llm\"),\n            \"analysts\": list(self.selected_analysts),\n            \"max_debate_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_debate_rounds\"),\n            \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"),\n            \"output_language\": cfg.get(\"output_language\"),\n            \"data_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"data_vendors\") or {}),\n            \"tool_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"tool_vendors\") or {}),\n        }\n\n    def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.\n\n        Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass\n        an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the\n        report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.\n        \"\"\"\n        if save_path is None:\n            save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)\n        return write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html)\n\n    def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now.\"\"\"\n        stamp = datetime.now().strftime(\"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S\")\n        return Path(self.config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"reports\" / f\"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}\"\n\n    def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n        \"\"\"Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.\n\n        Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The\n        memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles\n        and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).\n        \"\"\"\n        trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n        return self.propagator.create_initial_state(\n            company_name,\n            trade_date,\n            asset_type=asset_type,\n            instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),\n            portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else \"\",\n        )\n\n    def _memory_step(self, state):\n        \"\"\"The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every\n        ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the\n        trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).\n\n        Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,\n        so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here\n        does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in\n        the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.\n        \"\"\"\n        note = \"\"\n        try:\n            # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.\n            done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)\n            if done.failed:\n                note = (f\"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run \"\n                        \"and stay pending.\")\n        except Exception as exc:\n            logger.warning(\"Settling past decisions failed: %s\", exc)\n            note = f\"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending.\"\n        try:\n            past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(\n                state[\"company_of_interest\"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state[\"trade_date\"]))\n        except Exception as exc:\n            logger.warning(\"Reading the memory log failed: %s\", exc)\n            past_context = \"\"\n            note = note or f\"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__}).\"\n        return {\"past_context\": past_context, \"memory_note\": note}\n\n    def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:\n        \"\"\"Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.\n\n        A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own\n        decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done\n        analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to\n        settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.\n        \"\"\"\n        with run_config(self.config):\n            return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)\n\n    def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:\n        \"\"\"Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).\n\n        For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would\n        otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.\n        With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.\n        \"\"\"\n        with run_config(self.config):\n            return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)\n\n    def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):\n        \"\"\"Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log\n        for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here.\"\"\"\n        self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)\n        decision = final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\")\n        if not decision:\n            logger.warning(\"No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log\",\n                           company_name, trade_date)\n            return\n        self.memory_log.store_decision(\n            ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,\n            rating=run_rating(final_state),\n        )\n\n    def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n                   checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):\n        \"\"\"Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log.\"\"\"\n        init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n        args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()\n\n        # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same\n        # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).\n        if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:\n            args.setdefault(\"config\", {}).setdefault(\"configurable\", {})[\"thread_id\"] = checkpoint_thread_id\n\n        # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).\n        graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)\n        if self.debug:\n            # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).\n            final_state, printed = {}, set()\n            for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):\n                for msg in messages:\n                    key = getattr(msg, \"id\", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, \"content\", None))\n                    if key not in printed:\n                        printed.add(key)\n                        msg.pretty_print()\n                if state is not None:\n                    final_state.update(state)\n        else:\n            final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)\n\n        self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)\n\n        # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state.\n        self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n\n        return final_state, run_rating(final_state)\n\n    def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):\n        \"\"\"Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.\n\n        ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``\n        is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's\n        graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.\n\n        Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the\n        analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages\n        and reports come from their own finished steps (\"tasks\") as they happen.\n        \"\"\"\n        args = {**args, \"stream_mode\": [\"values\", \"tasks\"]}\n        # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even\n        # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the\n        # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.\n        context = run_config_context(self.config)\n        stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)\n        try:\n            while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:\n                namespace, mode, chunk = step\n                if namespace:\n                    result = chunk.get(\"result\") if mode == \"tasks\" else None\n                    if isinstance(result, dict):\n                        report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != \"messages\" and v}\n                        if result.get(\"messages\") or report:\n                            yield result.get(\"messages\", []), report or None\n                elif mode == \"values\":\n                    yield chunk.get(\"messages\", []), chunk\n        finally:\n            context.run(stream.close)\n\n    def _log_state(self, trade_date, final_state):\n        \"\"\"Write a run's final state to JSON under the run's own ticker.\"\"\"\n        entry = {\n            \"company_of_interest\": final_state[\"company_of_interest\"],\n            \"trade_date\": final_state[\"trade_date\"],\n            \"market_report\": final_state[\"market_report\"],\n            \"sentiment_report\": final_state[\"sentiment_report\"],\n            \"news_report\": final_state[\"news_report\"],\n            \"fundamentals_report\": final_state[\"fundamentals_report\"],\n            \"investment_debate_state\": {\n                \"bull_history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"bull_history\"],\n                \"bear_history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"bear_history\"],\n                \"history\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"history\"],\n                \"current_response\": final_state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\n                    \"current_response\"\n                ],\n            },\n            \"trader_investment_plan\": final_state[\"trader_investment_plan\"],\n            \"risk_debate_state\": {\n                \"aggressive_history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"aggressive_history\"],\n                \"conservative_history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"conservative_history\"],\n                \"neutral_history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"neutral_history\"],\n                \"history\": final_state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"history\"],\n            },\n            \"investment_plan\": final_state[\"investment_plan\"],\n            \"final_trade_decision\": final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"],\n            \"final_rating\": run_rating(final_state),\n            \"run_settings\": self.run_settings(),\n        }\n\n        # A ticker that would escape the results directory is rejected.\n        safe_ticker = safe_ticker_component(final_state[\"company_of_interest\"])\n        directory = Path(self.config[\"results_dir\"]) / safe_ticker / \"TradingAgentsStrategy_logs\"\n        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n        log_path = directory / f\"full_states_log_{trade_date}.json\"\n        with open(log_path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n            #                 "text": "<path>[REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: \"\"\"Portfolio Manager: synthesises the risk-analyst debate into the final decision.\n2: \n3: Uses LangChain's ``with_structured_output`` so the LLM produces a typed\n4: ``PortfolioDecision`` directly, in a single call. Its rating is the run's\n5: ``final_rating``, and the decision is rendered to markdown as\n6: ``final_trade_decision`` for the memory log, CLI display and saved reports.\n7: When a provider does not expose structured output, the agent falls back to\n8: free-text generation and the rating is read from that text.\n9: \"\"\"\n10: \n11: from __future__ import annotations\n12: \n13: from tradingagents.agents.context import (\n14:     get_instrument_context_from_state,\n15:     get_language_instruction,\n16:     get_portfolio_context_from_state,\n17: )\n18: from tradingagents.agents.rating import parse_rating\n19: from tradingagents.agents.schemas import PortfolioDecision, render_pm_decision\n20: from tradingagents.agents.structured import NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS, bind_structured, invoke_structured\n21: \n22: \n23: def create_portfolio_manager(llm):\n24:     structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, PortfolioDecision, \"Portfolio Manager\")\n25: \n26:     def portfolio_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n27:         instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n28:         portfolio_context = get_portfolio_context_from_state(state)\n29: \n30:         history = state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"history\"]\n31:         risk_debate_state = state[\"risk_debate_state\"]\n32:         research_plan = state[\"investment_plan\"]\n33:         trader_plan = state[\"trader_investment_plan\"]\n34: \n35:         past_context = state.get(\"past_context\", \"\")\n36:         lessons_line = (\n37:             f\"- Lessons from prior decisions and outcomes:\\n{past_context}\\n\"\n38:             if past_context\n39:             else \"\"\n40:         )\n41: \n42:         prompt = f\"\"\"As the Portfolio Manager, synthesize the risk analysts' debate and deliver the final trading decision.\n43: \n44: {instrument_context}\n45: \n46: {portfolio_context}\n47: \n48: ---\n49: \n50: **Rating Scale** (use exactly one):\n51: -                 "text": "<path>[REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/agents/schemas.py</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: \"\"\"Pydantic schemas used by agents that produce structured output.\n2: \n3: The framework's primary artifact is still prose: each agent's natural-language\n4: reasoning is what users read in the saved markdown reports and what the\n5: downstream agents read as context.  Structured output is layered onto the\n6: three decision-making agents (Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager)\n7: so that:\n8: \n9: - Their outputs follow consistent section headers across runs and providers\n10: - Each provider's native structured-output mode is used (json_schema for\n11:   OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic)\n12: - Schema field descriptions become the model's output instructions, freeing\n13:   the prompt body to focus on context and the rating-scale guidance\n14: - A render helper turns the parsed Pydantic instance back into the same\n15:   markdown shape the rest of the system already consumes, so display,\n16:   memory log, and saved reports keep working unchanged\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: from enum import StrEnum\n22: from typing import Literal\n23: \n24: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator\n25: \n26: # LLMs sometimes write a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\", ...) into an optional\n27: # numeric field instead of omitting it. Coerce those to None so the structured\n28: # call validates instead of erroring (#1058). Pydantic still parses real numeric\n29: # strings (\"189.5\") to float.\n30: _NULLISH_FLOAT = {\"\", \"none\", \"n/a\", \"na\", \"null\", \"nil\", \"-\", \"tbd\", \"unknown\"}\n31: \n32: \n33: def _coerce_optional_float(value):\n34:     \"\"\"Normalise an LLM-written optional numeric field before validation.\n35: \n36:     Three shapes show up in practice: a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\") in\n37:     place of an omitted value (#1058); a percentage where a price was asked for\n38:     (\"15%\", #1288); and a human-formatted price (\"$1,234.50\"). A percentage\n39:     cannot be salvaged into an absolute level -- reading \"15%\" as 15 would put a\n40:     stop at $15 on a $600 stock -- so it is dropped like a placeholder, leaving\n41:     one bad field to null out instead of failing the whole proposal. A formatted\n42:     price is reduced to its number.\n43: \n44:     Anything that is not a single number is dropped the same way. A range\n45:     (\"150-160\") or a hedge (\"around 150\") would otherwise reach pydantic, fail\n46:     validation, and discard the whole decision, losing every field the model got\n47:     right along with the price.\n48:     \"\"\"\n49:     if not isinstance(value, str):\n50:         return value\n51:     text = value.strip()\n52:     if text.lower() in _NULLISH_FLOAT or text.endswith(\"%\"):\n53:         return None\n54:     cleaned = text.replace(\",\", \"\").lstrip(\"$€£¥\").strip()\n55:     try:\n56:         return float(cleaned)\n57:     except ValueError:\n58:         return None\n59: \n60: \n61: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n62: # Shared rating types\n63: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n64: \n65: \n66: class PortfolioRating(StrEnum):\n67:     \"\"\"5-tier rating used by the Research Manager and Portfolio Manager.\"\"\"\n68: \n69:     BUY = \"Buy\"\n70:     OVERWEIGHT = \"Overweight\"\n71:     HOLD = \"Hold\"\n72:     UNDERWEIGHT = \"Underweight\"\n73:     SELL = \"Sell\"\n74: \n75: \n76: class TraderAction(StrEnum):\n77:     \"\"\"3-tier transaction direction used by the Trader.\n78: \n79:     The Trader's job is to translate the Research Manager's investment plan\n80:     into a concrete transaction proposal: should the desk execute a Buy, a\n81:     Sell, or sit on Hold this round.  Position sizing and the nuanced\n82:     Overweight / Underweight calls happen later at the Portfolio Manager.\n83:     \"\"\"\n84: \n85:     BUY = \"Buy\"\n86:     HOLD = \"Hold\"\n87:     SELL = \"Sell\"\n88: \n89: \n90: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n91: # Research Manager\n92: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n93: \n94: \n95: class ResearchPlan(BaseModel):\n96:     \"\"\"Structured investment plan produced by the Research Manager.\n97: \n98:     Hand-off to the Trader: the recommendation pins the directional view,\n99:     the rationale captures which side of the bull/bear debate carried the\n100:     argument, and the strategic actions translate that into concrete\n101:     instructions the trader can execute against.\n102:     \"\"\"\n103: \n104:     recommendation: PortfolioRating = Field(\n105:         description=(\n106:             \"The investment recommendation. Exactly one of Buy / Overweight / \"\n107:             \"Hold / Underweight / Sell. Conflicting arguments alone are not a \"\n108:             \"reason to Hold: commit to the stronger side, sized by how \"\n109:             \"decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still \"\n110:             \"balanced after weighing, or too thin to support a call.\"\n111:         ),\n112:     )\n113:     rationale: str = Field(\n114:         description=(\n115:             \"Conversational summary of the key points from both sides of the \"\n116:             \"debate, ending with which arguments led to the recommendation. \"\n117:             \"Speak naturally, as if to a teammate.\"\n118:         ),\n119:     )\n120:     strategic_actions: str = Field(\n121:         description=(\n122:             \"Concrete steps for the trader to implement the recommendation, \"\n123:             \"including sizing guidance relative to a standard allocation. The \"\n124:             \"research team does not see the caller's holdings; the trader and \"\n125:             \"portfolio manager apply the actual position.\"\n126:         ),\n127:     )\n128: \n129: \n130: def render_research_plan(plan: ResearchPlan) -> str:\n131:     \"\"\"Render a ResearchPlan to markdown for storage and the trader's prompt context.\"\"\"\n132:     return \"\\n\".join([\n133:         f\"**Recommendation**: {plan.recommendation.value}\",\n134:         \"\",\n135:         f\"**Rationale**: {plan.rationale}\",\n136:         \"\",\n137:         f\"**Strategic Actions**: {plan.strategic_actions}\",\n138:     ])\n139: \n140: \n141: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n142: # Trader\n143: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n144: \n145: \n146: class TraderProposal(BaseModel):\n147:     \"\"\"Structured transaction proposal produced by the Trader.\n148: \n149:     The trader reads the Research Manager's investment plan and the analyst\n150:     reports, then turns them into a concrete transaction: what action to\n151:     take, the reasoning that justifies it, and the practical levels for\n152:     entry, stop-loss, and sizing.\n153:     \"\"\"\n154: \n155:     action: TraderAction = Field(\n156:         description=\"The transaction direction. Exactly one of Buy / Hold / Sell.\",\n157:     )\n158:     reasoning: str = Field(\n159:         description=(\n160:             \"The case for this action, anchored in the analysts' reports and \"\n161:             \"the research plan.                 "text": "\"\"\"Pydantic schemas used by agents that produce structured output.\n\nThe framework's primary artifact is still prose: each agent's natural-language\nreasoning is what users read in the saved markdown reports and what the\ndownstream agents read as context.  Structured output is layered onto the\nthree decision-making agents (Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager)\nso that:\n\n- Their outputs follow consistent section headers across runs and providers\n- Each provider's native structured-output mode is used (json_schema for\n  OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic)\n- Schema field descriptions become the model's output instructions, freeing\n  the prompt body to focus on context and the rating-scale guidance\n- A render helper turns the parsed Pydantic instance back into the same\n  markdown shape the rest of the system already consumes, so display,\n  memory log, and saved reports keep working unchanged\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom enum import StrEnum\nfrom typing import Literal\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator\n\n# LLMs sometimes write a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\", ...) into an optional\n# numeric field instead of omitting it. Coerce those to None so the structured\n# call validates instead of erroring (#1058). Pydantic still parses real numeric\n# strings (\"189.5\") to float.\n_NULLISH_FLOAT = {\"\", \"none\", \"n/a\", \"na\", \"null\", \"nil\", \"-\", \"tbd\", \"unknown\"}\n\n\ndef _coerce_optional_float(value):\n    \"\"\"Normalise an LLM-written optional numeric field before validation.\n\n    Three shapes show up in practice: a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\") in\n    place of an omitted value (#1058); a percentage where a price was asked for\n    (\"15%\", #1288); and a human-formatted price (\"$1,234.50\"). A percentage\n    cannot be salvaged into an absolute level -- reading \"15%\" as 15 would put a\n    stop at $15 on a $600 stock -- so it is dropped like a placeholder, leaving\n    one bad field to null out instead of failing the whole proposal. A formatted\n    price is reduced to its number.\n\n    Anything that is not a single number is dropped the same way. A range\n    (\"150-160\") or a hedge (\"around 150\") would otherwise reach pydantic, fail\n    validation, and discard the whole decision, losing every field the model got\n    right along with the price.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(value, str):\n        return value\n    text = value.strip()\n    if text.lower() in _NULLISH_FLOAT or text.endswith(\"%\"):\n        return None\n    cleaned = text.replace(\",\", \"\").lstrip(\"$€£¥\").strip()\n    try:\n        return float(cleaned)\n    except ValueError:\n        return None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Shared rating types\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\nclass PortfolioRating(StrEnum):\n    \"\"\"5-tier rating used by the Research Manager and Portfolio Manager.\"\"\"\n\n    BUY = \"Buy\"\n    OVERWEIGHT = \"Overweight\"\n    HOLD = \"Hold\"\n    UNDERWEIGHT = \"Underweight\"\n    SELL = \"Sell\"\n\n\nclass TraderAction(StrEnum):\n    \"\"\"3-tier transaction direction used by the Trader.\n\n    The Trader's job is to translate the Research Manager's investment plan\n    into a concrete transaction proposal: should the desk execute a Buy, a\n    Sell, or sit on Hold this round.  Position sizing and the nuanced\n    Overweight / Underweight calls happen later at the Portfolio Manager.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    BUY = \"Buy\"\n    HOLD = \"Hold\"\n    SELL = \"Sell\"\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Research Manager\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\nclass ResearchPlan(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Structured investment plan produced by the Research Manager.\n\n    Hand-off to the Trader: the recommendation pins the directional view,\n    the rationale captures which side of the bull/bear debate carried the\n    argument, and the strategic actions translate that into concrete\n    instructions the trader can execute against.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    recommendation: PortfolioRating = Field(\n        description=(\n            \"The investment recommendation. Exactly one of Buy / Overweight / \"\n            \"Hold / Underweight / Sell. Conflicting arguments alone are not a \"\n            \"reason to Hold: commit to the stronger side, sized by how \"\n            \"decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still \"\n            \"balanced after weighing, or too thin to support a call.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    rationale: str = Field(\n        description=(\n            \"Conversational summary of the key points from both sides of the \"\n            \"debate, ending with which arguments led to the recommendation. \"\n            \"Speak naturally, as if to a teammate.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    strategic_actions: str = Field(\n        description=(\n            \"Concrete steps for the trader to implement the recommendation, \"\n            \"including sizing guidance relative to a standard allocation. The \"\n            \"research team does not see the caller's holdings; the trader and \"\n            \"portfolio manager apply the actual position.\"\n        ),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_research_plan(plan: ResearchPlan) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a ResearchPlan to markdown for storage and the trader's prompt context.\"\"\"\n    return \"\\n\".join([\n        f\"**Recommendation**: {plan.recommendation.value}\",\n        \"\",\n        f\"**Rationale**: {plan.rationale}\",\n        \"\",\n        f\"**Strategic Actions**: {plan.strategic_actions}\",\n    ])\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Trader\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\nclass TraderProposal(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Structured transaction proposal produced by the Trader.\n\n    The trader reads the Research Manager's investment plan and the analyst\n    reports, then turns them into a concrete transaction: what action to\n    take, the reasoning that justifies it, and the practical levels for\n    entry, stop-loss, and sizing.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    action: TraderAction = Field(\n        description=\"The transaction direction. Field descriptions double as the model's\n    output instructions, so the prompt body only needs to convey context and\n    the rating-scale guidance.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    rating: PortfolioRating = Field(\n        description=(\n            \"The final position rating. Exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / \"\n            \"Underweight / Sell, picked based on the analysts' debate. \"\n            \"Conflicting arguments alone are not a reason to Hold: commit to the \"\n            \"stronger side, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only \"\n            \"when the evidence is still balanced after weighing, or too thin to \"\n            \"support a call.\"\n        ),\n    )\n    executive_summary: str = Field(\n        description=(\n            \"A concise action plan covering entry strategy, position sizing, \"\n            \"key risk levels, and time horizon. Named even when absent: a missing line reads as a field nobody asked for,\n    # so a reader cannot tell \"no target\" from \"target not reported\".\n    target = decision.price_target if decision.price_target is not None else \"not provided\"\n    parts.extend([\"\", f\"**Price Target**: {target}\"])\n    parts.extend([\"\", f\"**Time Horizon**: {decision.time_horizon or 'not provided'}\"])\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Sentiment Analyst\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\nclass SentimentBand(StrEnum):\n    \"\"\"Discrete sentiment direction produced by the Sentiment Analyst.\n\n    Six tiers keep the signal granular enough to be actionable while remaining\n    small enough for every provider to map reliably from its JSON output.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    BULLISH = \"Bullish\"\n    MILDLY_BULLISH = \"Mildly Bullish\"\n    NEUTRAL = \"Neutral\"\n    MIXED = \"Mixed\"\n    MILDLY_BEARISH = \"Mildly Bearish\"\n    BEARISH = \"Bearish\"\n\n\nclass SentimentReport(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Structured sentiment report produced by the Sentiment Analyst.\n\n    Replaces the previous free-form prose output so downstream consumers\n    (dashboards, audit logs, PDF renderers, other agents) can read\n    ``overall_band`` and ``overall_score`` without maintaining fragile regex\n    fallbacks that drift with every model release. ``narrative`` preserves the\n    rich source-by-source analysis; ``render_sentiment_report`` prepends a\n    deterministic header so the saved report stays human-readable.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    overall_band: SentimentBand = Field(\n        description=(\n            \"Overall sentiment direction. After\n58:     ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and\n59:     that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools\n60:     cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).\n61:     \"\"\"\n62:     output = TypedDict(f\"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report\", {spec.report_key: str})\n63:     graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n64:     graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n65:     graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n66:     if not spec.tools:\n67:         graph.add_edge(\"agent\", END)\n68:         return graph.compile()\n69: \n70:     def calls(messages):\n71:         return [call[\"name\"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None) or [])]\n72: \n73:     def rounds(messages) -> int:\n74:         return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n75: \n76:     def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n77:         return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n78: \n79:     def wrap_up(state):\n80:         repeated = \", \".join(f\"{name} x{n}\" for name, n in Counter(calls(state[\"messages\"])).most_common())\n81:         logger.warning(\"%s used its %d tool rounds (%s); asking for its report\",\n82:                        spec.agent_node, max_tool_rounds, repeated)\n83:         return agent({**state, \"messages\": [*state[\"messages\"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})\n84: \n85:     graph.add_node(\"tools\", ToolNode(list(spec.tools)))\n86:     graph.add_node(\"wrap_up\", wrap_up)\n87:     graph.add_conditional_edges(\"agent\", _tools_or_done, [\"tools\", END])\n88:     graph.add_conditional_edges(\"tools\", more_or_wrap_up, [\"agent\", \"wrap_up\"])\n89:     graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", END)\n90:     return graph.compile()\n91: \n92: \n93: class GraphSetup:\n94:     \"\"\"Handles the setup and configuration of the agent graph.\"\"\"\n95: \n96:     def __init__(\n97:         self,\n98:         quick_thinking_llm: Any,\n99:         deep_thinking_llm: Any,\n100:         conditional_logic: ConditionalLogic,\n101:         max_tool_rounds: int,\n102:     ):\n103:         \"\"\"Initialize with required components.\"\"\"\n104:         self.quick_thinking_llm = quick_thinking_llm\n105:         self.deep_thinking_llm = deep_thinking_llm\n106:         self.conditional_logic = conditional_logic\n107:         self.max_tool_rounds = max_tool_rounds\n108: \n109:     def setup_graph(\n110:         self, selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"), memory_node=None\n111:     ):\n112:         \"\"\"Set up and compile the agent workflow graph.\n113: \n114:         Args:\n115:             selected_analysts (list): List of analyst types to include. Options are:\n116:                 - \"market\": Market analyst\n117:                 - \"social\": Sentiment analyst\n118:                 - \"news\": News analyst\n119:                 - \"fundamentals\": Fundamentals analyst\n120:             memory_node: Node that settles past decisions and returns the run's\n121:                 ``past_context``. It runs alongside the analysts.\n122:         \"\"\"\n123:         plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analysts)\n124: \n125:         analyst_factories = {\n126:             \"market\":                 "text": "import logging\nfrom collections import Counter\nfrom typing import Any, TypedDict\n\nfrom langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage\nfrom langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph\nfrom langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents import (\n    create_aggressive_debator,\n    create_bear_researcher,\n    create_bull_researcher,\n    create_conservative_debator,\n    create_fundamentals_analyst,\n    create_market_analyst,\n    create_neutral_debator,\n    create_news_analyst,\n    create_portfolio_manager,\n    create_research_manager,\n    create_sentiment_analyst,\n    create_trader,\n)\nfrom tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\nfrom tradingagents.agents.state import AgentState\n\nfrom .analyst_execution import build_analyst_execution_plan\nfrom .conditional_logic import ConditionalLogic\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n# Every target a shared conditional router can return. Each edge driven by the\n# router maps all of them, so a fall-through return (e.g. under prompt/i18n/\n# refactor drift in the speaker labels) can never hit a missing path_map entry\n# and crash LangGraph mid-run (#1088).\nDEBATE_PATH_MAP = {\n    \"Bull Researcher\": \"Bull Researcher\",\n    \"Bear Researcher\": \"Bear Researcher\",\n    \"Research Manager\": \"Research Manager\",\n}\nRISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP = {\n    \"Aggressive Analyst\": \"Aggressive Analyst\",\n    \"Conservative Analyst\": \"Conservative Analyst\",\n    \"Neutral Analyst\": \"Neutral Analyst\",\n    \"Portfolio Manager\": \"Portfolio Manager\",\n}\n\n\ndef _tools_or_done(state) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Route an analyst's turn: run its tool calls, or finish with its report.\"\"\"\n    return \"tools\" if state[\"messages\"][-1].tool_calls else END\n\n\ndef _analyst_graph(spec, agent, max_tool_rounds: int):\n    \"\"\"One analyst as a graph of its own: the model and its tools, on a private message history.\n\n    It returns only its report, so analysts running side by side never write the\n    same key, and its tool calls never reach the other analysts' messages. After\n    ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and\n    that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools\n    cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).\n    \"\"\"\n    output = TypedDict(f\"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report\", {spec.report_key: str})\n    graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n    graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n    graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n    if not spec.tools:\n        graph.add_edge(\"agent\", END)\n        return graph.compile()\n\n    def calls(messages):\n        return [call[\"name\"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None) or [])]\n\n    def rounds(messages) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n\n    def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n        return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n\n    def wrap_up(state):\n        repeated = \", \".join(f\"{name} x{n}\" for name, n in Counter(calls(state[\"messages\"])).most_common())\n        logger.warning(\"%s used its %d tool rounds (%s); asking for its report\",\n                       spec.agent_node, max_tool_rounds, repeated)\n        return agent({**state, \"messages\": [*state[\"messages\"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})\n\n    graph.add_node(\"tools\", ToolNode(list(spec.tools)))\n    graph.add_node(\"wrap_up\", wrap_up)\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"agent\", _tools_or_done, [\"tools\", END])\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"tools\", more_or_wrap_up, [\"agent\", \"wrap_up\"])\n    graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", END)\n    return graph.compile()\n\n\nclass GraphSetup:\n    \"\"\"Handles the setup and configuration of the agent graph.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        quick_thinking_llm: Any,\n        deep_thinking_llm: Any,\n        conditional_logic: ConditionalLogic,\n        max_tool_rounds: int,\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Initialize with required components.\"\"\"\n        self.quick_thinking_llm = quick_thinking_llm\n        self.deep_thinking_llm = deep_thinking_llm\n        self.conditional_logic = conditional_logic\n        self.max_tool_rounds = max_tool_rounds\n\n    def setup_graph(\n        self, selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"), memory_node=None\n    ):\n        \"\"\"Set up and compile the agent workflow graph.\n\n        Args:\n            selected_analysts (list): List of analyst types to include. Options are:\n                - \"market\": Market analyst\n                - \"social\": Sentiment analyst\n                - \"news\": News analyst\n                - \"fundamentals\": Fundamentals analyst\n            memory_node: Node that settles past decisions and returns the run's\n                ``past_context``. It runs alongside the analysts.\n        \"\"\"\n        plan = build_analyst_execution_plan(selected_analysts)\n\n        analyst_factories = {\n            \"market\": lambda: create_market_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"social\": lambda: create_sentiment_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"news\": lambda: create_news_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n            \"fundamentals\": lambda: create_fundamentals_analyst(self.quick_thinking_llm),\n        }\n\n        bull_researcher_node = create_bull_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        bear_researcher_node = create_bear_researcher(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        research_manager_node = create_research_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n        trader_node = create_trader(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n\n        aggressive_analyst = create_aggressive_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        neutral_analyst = create_neutral_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        conservative_analyst = create_conservative_debator(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n        portfolio_manager_node = create_portfolio_manager(self.deep_thinking_llm)\n\n        workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)\n\n        for spec in plan.specs:\n            workflow.add_node(spec.agent_node,\n                              _analyst_graph(spec, analyst_factories[spec.key](), self.max_tool_rounds))\n\n        workflow.add_node(\"Bull Researcher\", bull_researcher_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Bear Researcher\", bear_researcher_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Research Manager\", research_manager_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Trader\", trader_node)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Aggressive Analyst\", aggressive_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Neutral Analyst\", neutral_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Conservative Analyst\", conservative_analyst)\n        workflow.add_node(\"Portfolio Manager\", portfolio_manager_node)\n\n        # The analysts work at the same time; the research debate starts once\n        # every one of them has filed its report. The memory log settles past\n        # decisions alongside them: only the Portfolio Manager reads its lessons.\n        first_steps = [spec.agent_node for spec in plan.specs]\n        if memory_node is not None:\n            workflow.add_node(\"Memory Log\", memory_node)\n            first_steps.append(\"Memory Log\")\n        for node in first_steps:\n            workflow.add_edge(START, node)\n        workflow.add_edge(first_steps, \"Bull Researcher\")\n\n        # Both research-debate edges share the complete DEBATE_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n        for debate_node in (\"Bull Researcher\", \"Bear Researcher\"):\n            workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n                debate_node,\n                self.conditional_logic.should_continue_debate,\n                DEBATE_PATH_MAP,\n            )\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Research Manager\", \"Trader\")\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Trader\", \"Aggressive Analyst\")\n        # All three risk edges share the complete RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP (#1088).\n        for risk_node in (\"Aggressive Analyst\", \"Conservative Analyst\", \"Neutral Analyst\"):\n            workflow.add_conditional_edges(\n                risk_node,\n                self.conditional_logic.should_continue_risk_analysis,\n                RISK_ANALYSIS_PATH_MAP,\n            )\n\n        workflow.add_edge(\"Portfolio Manager\", END)\n\n        return workflow",

                "text": "<path>[REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/agents/structured.py</path>\n<type>file</type>\n<content>\n1: \"\"\"Shared helpers for invoking an agent with structured output and a graceful fallback.\n2: \n3: The Portfolio Manager, Trader, and Research Manager all follow the same\n4: canonical pattern:\n5: \n6: 1. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``\n7:    so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the provider does\n8:    not support structured output (rare; mostly older Ollama models), the\n9:    wrap is skipped and the agent uses free-text generation instead.\n10: 2. At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to\n11:    markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason\n12:    (malformed JSON from a weak model, transient provider issue), fall\n13:    back to a plain ``llm.invoke`` so the pipeline never blocks.\n14: \n15: Centralising the pattern here keeps the agent factories small and ensures\n16: all three agents log the same warnings when fallback fires.\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: import logging\n22: from collections.abc import Callable\n23: from typing import Any, TypeVar\n24: \n25: from pydantic import BaseModel\n26: \n27: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n28: \n29: T = TypeVar(\"T\", bound=BaseModel)\n30: \n31: # Schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool (the schema itself), so a\n32: # model that reaches for a search tool emits an unknown tool call and the whole\n33: # structured attempt is discarded for a free-text retry. Agents on this path\n34: # state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone\n35: # (#1130).\n36: NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (\n37:     \"Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools \"\n38:     \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n39: )\n40: \n41: \n42: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n43:     \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n44: \n45:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n46:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n47:     \"\"\"\n48:     try:\n49:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n50:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n51:         logger.warning(\n52:             \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n53:             \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n54:             agent_name, exc,\n55:         )\n56:         return None\n57: \n58: \n59: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n60:     \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n61: \n62:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n63:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n64:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n65:     \"\"\"\n66:     if structured_llm is None:\n67:         return None\n68:     try:\n69:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n70:         if result is None:\n71:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n72:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n73:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n74:             raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n75:         return result\n76:     except Exception as exc:\n77:         logger.warning(\n78:             \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n79:             agent_name, exc,\n80:         )\n81:         return None\n82: \n83: \n84: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n85:     structured_llm: Any | None,\n86:     plain_llm: Any,\n87:     prompt: Any,\n88:     render: Callable[[T], str],\n89:     agent_name: str,\n90: ) -> str:\n91:     \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n92:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n93:     if result is not None:\n94:         return render(result)\n95:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content\n\n(End of file - total 95 lines)\n</content>"

                "text": "\"\"\"Shared helpers for invoking an agent with structured output and a graceful fallback.\n\nThe Portfolio Manager, Trader, and Research Manager all follow the same\ncanonical pattern:\n\n1. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``\n   so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the provider does\n   not support structured output (rare; mostly older Ollama models), the\n   wrap is skipped and the agent uses free-text generation instead.\n2. At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to\n   markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason\n   (malformed JSON from a weak model, transient provider issue), fall\n   back to a plain ``llm.invoke`` so the pipeline never blocks.\n\nCentralising the pattern here keeps the agent factories small and ensures\nall three agents log the same warnings when fallback fires.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom typing import Any, TypeVar\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nT = TypeVar(\"T\", bound=BaseModel)\n\n# Schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool (the schema itself), so a\n# model that reaches for a search tool emits an unknown tool call and the whole\n# structured attempt is discarded for a free-text retry. Agents on this path\n# state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone\n# (#1130).\nNO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (\n    \"Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools \"\n    \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n)\n\n\ndef bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n    \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n\n    Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n    will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n    except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n        logger.warning(\n            \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n            \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n            agent_name, exc,\n        )\n        return None\n\n\ndef invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n    \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n\n    ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n    invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n    shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n    \"\"\"\n    if structured_llm is None:\n        return None\n    try:\n        result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n        if result is None:\n            # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n            # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n            # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n            raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n        return result\n    except Exception as exc:\n        logger.warning(\n            \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n            agent_name, exc,\n        )\n        return None\n\n\ndef invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n    structured_llm: Any | None,\n    plain_llm: Any,\n    prompt: Any,\n    render: Callable[[T], str],\n    agent_name: str,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n    result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n    if result is not None:\n        return render(result)\n    return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content",

Interface contracts\n\n### 2.1 New owner module (proposed): `tradingagents/graph/publication_gate.py`\n\n**Run-local evidence/argument model (proposed, needs approval):**\n\n```\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass EvidenceRecord:\n    evidence_id: str           # minted this run only, e.g. \"ev:<run_id>:<n>\"\n    source: str                # e.g. \"market_report\", \"fundamentals\", \"news\", tool result id\n    excerpt: str               # resolvable pointer/material\n    run_id: str                # owned by this run; used to reject cross-run refs\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ArgumentRecord:\n    argument_id: str           # e.g. \"arg:bull:1\"\n    speaker: str               # \"Bull Analyst\" / \"Bear Analyst\"\n    text: str\n    evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass GateOutcome:\n    status: Literal[\"APPROVED\", \"BLOCKED\"]\n    reason: Literal[\"INVALID_RATING\", \"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\", \"MISSING_REFERENCE\",\n                    \"UNKNOWN_ID\", \"CROSS_RUN_REFERENCE\"] | None\n    rating: str | None          # only when APPROVED\n    resolved_references: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]  # (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n```\n\n**Functions / contract:**\n- `build_evidence_index(run_id, state) -> EvidenceIndex` — collects resolvable evidence from the run's analyst reports / tool results; mints run-scoped IDs. *Pure, deterministic, no model text trusted as IDs.*\n- `PublicationGate(index).evaluate(candidate) -> GateOutcome` — validates: (a) rating ∈ allowed 5-tier set; (b) `final_trade_decision` references ≥1 accepted argument; (c) every referenced evidence ID resolves in **this** index; (d) no ID from another `run_id`.       "text": "请继续使用中文，基于固定提交 0da00bc0c57af9bd45e146245e3849e9cb757e4b，为 FR-01 / INV-01 更新只读实施计划。本轮只做规划，不生成或修改业务代码、\n测试或配置，也不进入 Build。\n\n\n先补读关键入口：\n- tradingagents/agents/rating.py\n- tradingagents/agents/context.py\n- tradingagents/memory/log.py（store_decision 的实际实现）\n- cli/display.py（CLI 展示路径）\n- tradingagents/backtest.py（现有调用方的兼容性）\n\n\n若关键文件仍被拒读，列出需要人工开放 read 的确切路径，并停止规划。\n不要修改权限或猜测接口。\n\n\n按以下已确定的设计更新计划：\n\n\n1. 发布状态与评级分离\n   拒绝时返回发布状态 BLOCKED 和原因码，不把 BLOCKED 写入 final_rating，\n   不保留正式评级或最终建议正文。Python API 的结果状态必须明确包含\n   BLOCKED 和原因；若需兼容原二元组，第二项可返回非交易哨兵 REVIEW。\n   CLI 和正式报告应明确显示 BLOCKED，不能只显示 REVIEW。\n\n\n2. 证据链由程序建立\n   辩论前，由程序为本次运行中实际存在的材料建立证据索引；首版只用非空\n   分析师报告即可。Bull/Bear 只能引用索引中已有的 evidence_id。程序校验\n   引用后，才采纳论点并分配 argument_id；Portfolio Manager 引用已采纳的\n   论点。发布闸门必须验证「建议 → 已采纳论点 → 本次运行材料」的完整链路。\n   ID 必须绑定运行；模型自造的 ID 或自由文本里的 ID 不算有效引用。\n   本轮只验证引用完整性，不判定材料是否在语义上支持投资结论。\n\n\n3. 拒绝原因\n   对外只使用 INVALID_RATING 和 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE。缺失、无法解析、\n   未知或跨运行引用统一为 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE；评级和证据同时不合格时，\n   优先返回 INVALID_RATING。不得用自由文本评级回退绕过闸门。\n\n\n4. 单一闸门与发布时机\n   由同一个确定性闸门决定是否发布。候选只在内部流转，CLI（含实时流式展示）、\n   Python API、正式报告（Markdown 和 HTML）及决策记忆都只消费闸门结果。\n   请明确检查 CLI 在闸门执行前是否会把候选展示为正式建议，并给出阻断方案。\n   被拒候选不得作为正式决策写入记忆。\n\n\n请输出一份可交给队友审批的计划，包含：\n- 候选从生成到四个出口的实际路径，以及闸门接入点和执行时机。\n- 输入输出契约、确切的新增/修改文件及各自用途、回滚方式。\n- 逐项对应 FR-01 / INV-01 的离线测试：写明确切测试路径、输入、预期断言，\n  以及预计哪条断言会在实现前失败。使用固定样本和假模型，不联网。\n- 至少覆盖合法评级与有效证据（能回溯到材料）、非法评级、缺失或无法解析\n  的引用、未知 ID、跨运行引用。用被拦截的 Buy 验证四个出口均无漏放，\n  特别要验证它没有在 CLI 流式阶段提前作为正式建议出现。\n- 仍未核实的接口、所需只读权限和剩余风险。\n\n\n输出后停下，等待队友批准同一版计划和测试。最后一行必须是：\nWAITING FOR PLAN AND TEST APPROVAL",
      "type": "user"
    },

X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n# bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. \"rating\"\n# must start a word, so \"Operating margin: Sell-side\" is not a label.\n_RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<![a-z])rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n                              re.IGNORECASE)\n\n# The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to\n# open with (\"- **Rating**: X\", \"**Final Rating**: X\", \"## Our rating - X\"): an\n# optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the\n# decision itself before \"rating\". \"Consensus rating: Buy\" or \"Trader's rating:\n# Buy\" is someone else's rating.\n_OWN_QUALIFIER = r\"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\\s+)*\"\n_RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"\\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\\u2022]|\\d+[.)])\\s+)?[\\s*_#]*\" + _OWN_QUALIFIER\n    + r\"rating[^\\w:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(?P<value>\\w+)\",\n    re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# A line presenting the scale rather than a decision (\"Rating Scale: Buy, ...\").\n_RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\s*(scale|options|legend)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\ndef extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.\n\n    Reads an explicit \"Rating: X\" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the\n    NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``\n    matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own\n    rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not text:\n        return None\n    norm = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", text)\n\n    # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any\n    # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote\n    # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's\n    # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label\n    # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing\n    # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the\n    # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.\n    lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]\n    first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"#\")\n                  or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), \"\")\n    m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)\n    opening = m if m and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET else None\n    if opening and not opening.group(\"item\"):\n        return opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()\n\n    own = [opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()] if opening else []\n    labels = []\n    for line in lines:\n        m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)\n        if m and not m.group(\"item\") and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET:\n            own.append(m.group(\"value\").capitalize())\n        labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]\n    # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be\n    # one the text argues against (\"not a Sell\"), and reading it reports a\n    # direction nobody decided.\n    found = own or labels\n    return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None\n\n\ndef parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.\n\n    For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's\n    entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.\n    \"\"\"\n    rating = extract_rating(text)\n    return rating if rating is not None else default\n\n\ndef run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.\n\n    The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older\n    version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.\n    \"\"\"\n    return final_state.get(\"final_rating\") or parse_rating(final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\", \"\"))\n\n\ndef is_review(signal: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170).\"\"\"\n    return signal == RATING_REVIEW",
