                "text": "\"\"\"Prompt context shared by the agents: instrument identity, output language and portfolio.\"\"\"\n\nimport functools\nimport logging\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import is_historical\nfrom tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.fundamentals import get_company_profile\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef get_language_instruction() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a prompt instruction for the configured output language.\n\n    Returns empty string when English (default), so no extra tokens are used.\n    Applied to every agent whose output reaches the saved report —\n    analysts, researchers, debaters, research manager, trader, and\n    portfolio manager — so a non-English run produces a fully localized\n    report rather than a mix of languages.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n    lang = get_config().get(\"output_language\", \"English\")\n    if lang.strip().lower() == \"english\":\n        return \"\"\n    # The labelled lines are read by the program, so they keep their English\n    # label and value: a translated rating line leaves the reader prose to\n    # search, where a negated rating (\"not a Sell\") reads as the call (#1435).\n    return (\n        f\" Write your entire response in {lang}, except the labelled lines the format\"\n        f\" asks for (the \\\"**Rating**:\\\" line, \\\"FINAL TRANSACTION PROPOSAL:\\\"):\"\n        f\" keep their label and value in English, exactly as specified.\"\n    )\n\n\ndef opponent_argument_or_opening(text: str, opponent: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Opponent's latest argument, or an explicit opening marker when empty.\n\n    The first speaker in each debate round receives an empty opponent response;\n    interpolating it into a \"refute the opponent\" prompt makes the model\n    fabricate the other side's position. Returning a clear \"has not spoken yet\"\n    marker instead lets it open with its own case (#1176).\n    \"\"\"\n    text = (text or \"\").strip()\n    if text:\n        return text\n    return f\"(The {opponent} has not spoken yet — open the debate with your own case.)\"\n\n\ndef _clean_identity_value(value: Any) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return a trimmed string, or None for empty / placeholder-ish values.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(value, str):\n        return None\n    cleaned = value.strip()\n    if not cleaned or cleaned.lower() in {\"none\", \"n/a\", \"nan\", \"null\"}:\n        return None\n    return cleaned\n\n\ndef resolve_instrument_identity(ticker: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Resolve deterministic identity metadata (company name, sector, …) for a ticker.\n\n    This exists to stop the pipeline from hallucinating a *different* company\n    when a chart pattern suggests a different industry than the real one\n    (#814): without a ground-truth name, the market analyst would pattern-match\n    the price action to a narrative and invent an identity that then cascaded\n    through every downstream agent.\n\n    Best-effort by design: if yfinance is unavailable, rate-limited, or doesn't\n    recognise the ticker, we return ``{}`` and the caller falls back to\n    ticker-only context rather than failing before analysis starts. An answer\n    is cached for the process; a failed lookup is asked again next time.\n\n    Identity resolves for the same instrument the price path fetches\n    (``XAUUSD`` -> ``GC=F``, #983).\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        return _identity(ticker)\n    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail open, never block the run\n        logger.debug(\"Could not resolve instrument identity for %s: %s\", ticker, exc)\n        return {}\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]_cache(maxsize=256)\ndef _identity(ticker: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The vendor's identity fields for ``ticker``; raises if the lookup fails.\"\"\"\n    info = get_company_profile(ticker)\n    identity: dict[str, str] = {}\n    company_name = _clean_identity_value(info.get(\"longName\")) or _clean_identity_value(\n        info.get(\"shortName\")\n    )\n    if company_name:\n        identity[\"company_name\"] = company_name\n    for source_key, target_key in (\n        (\"sector\", \"sector\"),\n        (\"industry\", \"industry\"),\n        (\"exchange\", \"exchange\"),\n        (\"quoteType\", \"quote_type\"),\n    ):\n        value = _clean_identity_value(info.get(source_key))\n        if value:\n            identity[target_key] = value\n    return identity\n\n\ndef build_instrument_context(\n    ticker: str,\n    asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n    identity: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,\n    trade_date: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Describe the exact instrument so agents preserve identity and ticker.\n\n    When ``identity`` is provided (resolved deterministically via\n    :func:`resolve_instrument_identity`), the company name and business\n    classification are injected so agents anchor to the real company rather\n    than pattern-matching the price chart to a wrong one (#814).\n\n    That profile carries no historical vintage: it describes the company today.\n    A run dated earlier gets the current name alone, as a way to tell the\n    company apart from others rather than as what it was called then; a sector,\n    industry or exchange it holds today is not given, since it may not have held\n    on the analysis date.\n    \"\"\"\n    is_crypto = asset_type == \"crypto\"\n    instrument_label = \"asset\" if is_crypto else \"instrument\"\n    context = (\n        f\"The {instrument_label} to analyze is `{ticker}`. \"\n        \"The tools serve this instrument; refer to it by this exact ticker in every report and recommendation, \"\n        \"preserving any exchange suffix (e.g. `.TO`, `.L`, `.HK`, `.T`, `-USD`).\"\n    )\n\n    identity = identity or {}\n    name = identity.get(\"company_name\") or identity.get(\"name\")\n    label = \"Name\" if is_crypto else \"Company\"\n    details = []\n    if is_historical(trade_date):\n        if name:\n            details.append(\n                f\"{label}: {name} (its current name, given only to identify it; \"\n                f\"on {trade_date} it may have been named differently)\"\n            )\n    else:\n        if name:\n            details.append(f\"{label}: {name}\")\n        sector, industry = identity.get(\"sector\"), identity.get(\"industry\")\n        if sector and industry:\n            details.append(f\"Business classification: {sector} / {industry}\")\n        elif sector:\n            details.append(f\"Sector: {sector}\")\n        elif industry:\n            details.append(f\"Industry: {industry}\")\n        if identity.get(\"exchange\"):\n            details.append(f\"Exchange: {identity['exchange']}\")\n\n    if details:\n        context += (\n            f\" Resolved identity: {'; '.join(details)}. \"\n            \"Do not substitute a different company or ticker unless a tool \"\n            \"result explicitly disproves this resolved identity.\"\n        )\n\n    if is_crypto:\n        context += (\n            \" Treat it as a crypto asset rather than a company, and do not \"\n            \"assume company fundamentals are available.\"\n        )\n    return context\n\n\ndef get_instrument_context_from_state(state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the instrument context for the current run.\n\n    Prefers the identity-resolved context computed once at run start and\n    stored on the state (see ``TradingAgentsGraph.resolve_instrument_context``).\n    Falls back to a ticker-only context — with no network lookup — when the\n    state was constructed without it (bare programmatic states, tests), so a\n    consumer is never forced to make a yfinance call mid-graph.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = state.get(\"instrument_context\")\n    if isinstance(context, str) and context.strip():\n        return context\n    return build_instrument_context(\n        str(state[\"company_of_interest\"]),\n        state.get(\"asset_type\", \"stock\"),\n    )\n\n\ndef report_or_absent(text: str, source: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An analyst's report, or a marker saying it was never produced.\n\n    A report is empty when its analyst was not selected, refused, or returned\n    nothing. Interpolating that into a labelled section presents an absence as a\n    blank finding, and the reading agent fills it in from nothing, the same way\n    an empty opponent argument used to invite an invented rebuttal (#1176).\n    \"\"\"\n    text = (text or \"\").strip()\n    if text:\n        return text\n    return f\"(No {source} report in this run: it is not available, not an empty finding.)\"\n\n\ndef get_portfolio_context_from_state(state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the caller's portfolio block, or a notice that none was given.\n\n    A run without portfolio context must not read as a flat book: the agents\n    would otherwise size as if the caller held nothing, which is a claim about\n    an account we were never told about.\n    \"\"\"\n    context = state.get(\"portfolio_context\")\n    if isinstance(context, str) and context.strip():\n        return context\n    return (\n        \"Portfolio context: not provided. You do not know the caller's current \"\n        \"holdings or cash, so do not assume a flat book; give direction and \"\n        \"sizing guidance in terms the caller can apply to their own position.\"\n    )",

| None                         # 仅 APPROVED\n    resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str,str,str],...]  # (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n```\n\n- `build_evidence_index(run_id, state) -> EvidenceIndex`：仅用非空分析师报告（`market/sentiment/news/fundamentals_report`）；mint `evidence_id` 并绑 `run_id`。不信任模型文本中的 ID。\n- `accept_arguments(index, debate_texts) -> tuple[ArgumentRecord,...]`：程序解析 Bull/Bear 引用的 `evidence_id`，仅当 ID 属于本索引才接受并分配 `argument_id`；模型自造/自由文本 ID 丢弃。\n- `PublicationGate(index, accepted_args).evaluate(candidate) -> GateOutcome`：\n  1. 评级 ∈ `RATINGS_5_TIER` 且非 REVIEW → 否则 `INVALID_RATING`；\n  2. 决策引用 ≥1 个**已接受** `argument_id`，其 `evidence_ids` 全部 ∈ 索引且 `run_id` 相同 → 否则 `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`；\n  3. 二者皆不合格时先返回 `INVALID_RATING`。\n- **发布后处理**：`apply(outcome, final_state)` 写 `publication_status/publication_reason`；BLOCKED 时令 `final_rating=RATING_REVIEW` 并从正式副本移除候选正文（保留于内部 `candidate_decision` 供审计，**不进**任何 official sink）。\n\n**四出口消费：**\n| 出口 | 位置 | 消费方式 | BLOCKED 行为           "text": "`llm_clients/__init__.py` 不能读。但 `trading_graph.py:79-80` 调用 `create_tier_client(self.config, \"deep\").get_llm()`，且测试可在 `TradingAgentsGraph` 构造**之前**用 `monkeypatch.setattr` 替换 `tradingagents.graph.trading_graph.create_tier_client`（该名字已绑定在 `trading_graph` 模块命名空间），返回一个假 client，其 `.get_llm()` 给假模型。这不需要读 `__init__.py`。\n\n我需确认假模型要实现的接口。图里会调用：\n- 分析师：`(prompt | llm.bind_tools(tools)).invoke(...)` 与 `(prompt | llm).invoke(...)`\n- 研究者/debater：`llm.invoke(prompt)`\n- PM/RM/Trader：`bind_structured(llm, ...)` → `llm.with_structured_output(schema)`，然后 `invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, ...)`。\n\n为让流程走到 PM 并产出「合法 Buy 但无证据」，最简做法：假模型让**结构化输出失败**（`with_structured_output` 抛 `NotImplementedError` → `bind_structured` 返回 None → `invoke_structured` 返回 None → PM 走 `llm.invoke(prompt).content` 自由文本回退），自由文本返回一段**合法评级的决策正文**（含 `**Rating**: Buy`），但无任何证据引用。这正对应「合法 Buy 但无有效证据」，且走的是原版真实路径。\n\n不过 `invoke` 需要返回带 `.content` 的对象；`take_turn` 里 `result.tool_calls` 需要属性。用一个小的 `_FakeResponse`。\n\n分析师走 `take_turn`：`prompt | llm.bind_tools(tools)` 是 LangChain 链，会调用 `llm.bind_tools(...)` 返回可调用对象，再 `.invoke(messages)`。为完全绕开 LangChain 链的复杂度，在测试里把假 LLM 实现为满足最小协议的普通对象，但 `prompt | llm` 需要 `Runnable`。这较复杂。\n\n更稳妥：假模型直接实现为一个**真实的 langchain `RunnableLambda` 兼容**对象不现实。改为让假 LLM 具备 LangChain 协议所需方法（`bind_tools`、`with_structured_output`、`invoke`），并让 `prompt | llm` 成立——`prompt` 是 `ChatPromptTemplate`，`|` 需要右侧为 Runnable。普通对象不行。\n\n因此最可靠：继承 `langchain_core.language_models.chat_models.BaseChatModel`（已随 langchain-core 安装），实现 `_generate`，并覆写 `bind_tools` 与 `with_structured_output`。`BaseChatModel` 是 Runnable，`prompt | llm` 成立。假模型 `_generate` 恒返回 AIMessage，无 tool_calls，内容为分析师报告或最终决策正文。\n\n这是标准做法。我先写测试，再请人类运行确认。现在创建唯一允许新增的文件。"

              "content": "\"\"\"INV-01 key counterexample — a valid Buy with no valid evidence must not publish.\n\nRequirement: FR-01 / INV-01 (requirements.yaml).\nPlan: revision 1, key counterexample test. Approved: <approver>, <time>, <plan version/link>.\n\nThis test drives the *real* ``TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()`` entry point with a\nfake chat model, so it exercises the baseline's actual publication path — not a\nstub. No new project modules imported. No new state fields depended on.\nThe fake model and all fixed samples are inlined in this file.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun\nfrom langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult\n\n\n# --- fixed samples (inlined, not a fixtures directory) -----------------------\n\n# A decision that carries a legal Buy rating but no argument/evidence citation.\n# This is exactly the \"valid rating, no valid evidence\" counterexample.\nBUY_NO_EVIDENCE_DECISION = (\n    \"**Rating**: Buy\\n\\n\"\n    \"**Executive Summary**: Enter a full position now.\\n\\n\"\n    \"**Investment Thesis**: The setup looks strong. All\n    on-disk state (cache, results, memory) goes to ``tmp_path``.\n    \"\"\"\n    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"create_tier_client\", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_BuyNoEvidenceModel()))\n\n    config = {\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n        \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n        \"memory_log_path\": str(tmp_path / \"memory.md\"),\n        \"checkpoint_enabled\": False,\n    }\n\n    graph = tg.TradingAgentsGraph(\n        selected_analysts=(\"market\",),\n        debug=False,\n        config=config,\n    )\n    _, signal = graph.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-01-05\")\n    return signal, graph.memory_log\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_buy_without_evidence_is_not_returned_as_official_rating(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Exit 1 — Python API: a legal Buy with no valid evidence must not be returned.\n\n    On the baseline, ``run_rating`` echoes the model's ``**Rating**: Buy`` label,\n    so ``propagate()`` returns ``\"Buy\"`` even though nothing is cited. FR-01 says\n    that must be blocked, so this assertion is expected to FAIL on 0da00bc because\n    the Buy leaks through the API — the precise behavior INV-01 forbids.\n    \"\"\"\n    signal, _ = _run_through_propagate(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n\n    assert signal != \"Buy\", (\n        \"API returned Buy for a candidate with no valid evidence; \"\n        \"the publication gate must block it (FR-01/INV-01).\"\n    )\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_buy_without_evidence_is_not_written_to_decision_memory(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Exit 2 — decision memory: the blocked candidate must not be persisted.\n\n    Asserted separately from the API check so one failure never masks the other.\n    On the baseline, ``record_decision`` calls ``store_decision(... run_rating)``\n    unconditionally, so a Buy entry lands in the memory log for this run. INV-01\n    says a rejected candidate never enters decision memory, so this is expected to\n    FAIL on 0da00bc because the Buy is written.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, memory_log = _run_through_propagate(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n\n    entries = memory_log.load_entries()\n    buy_entries = [e for e in entries if e.get(\"rating\") == \"Buy\"]\n\n    assert not buy_entries, (\n        \"A Buy with no valid evidence was written to decision memory; \"\n        \"a rejected candidate must never be persisted (INV-01).\"\n    )",

                "text": "from tradingagents.agents.state import AgentState\n\n\nclass ConditionalLogic:\n    \"\"\"Handles conditional logic for determining graph flow.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, max_debate_rounds=1, max_risk_discuss_rounds=1):\n        \"\"\"Initialize with configuration parameters.\"\"\"\n        self.max_debate_rounds = max_debate_rounds\n        self.max_risk_discuss_rounds = max_risk_discuss_rounds\n\n    def should_continue_debate(self, state: AgentState) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Determine if debate should continue.\"\"\"\n\n        if (\n            state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"count\"] >= 2 * self.max_debate_rounds\n        ):  # max_debate_rounds turns each for bull and bear\n            return \"Research Manager\"\n        if state[\"investment_debate_state\"][\"current_response\"].startswith(\"Bull\"):\n            return \"Bear Researcher\"\n        return \"Bull Researcher\"\n\n    def should_continue_risk_analysis(self, state: AgentState) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Determine if risk analysis should continue.\"\"\"\n        if (\n            state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"count\"] >= 3 * self.max_risk_discuss_rounds\n        ):  # max_risk_discuss_rounds turns each for the three risk analysts\n            return \"Portfolio Manager\"\n        if state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"latest_speaker\"].startswith(\"Aggressive\"):\n            return \"Conservative Analyst\"\n        if state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"latest_speaker\"].startswith(\"Conservative\"):\n            return \"Neutral Analyst\"\n        return \"Aggressive Analyst\"",

          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Deterministic publication gate for FR-01 / INV-01.\n\nOwner module for the release decision described in\n``architecture-blueprint.md`` (FR-01 row) and ``docs/architecture/invariants.md``\n(INV-01). The gate is the single authority for whether a candidate recommendation\nbecomes an official decision. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the\nprogram itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating\nfallback is honoured around the gate.\n\nDesign (plan revision 1):\n- Evidence is indexed from the run's own non-empty analyst reports *before* the\n  first debate turn, so every accepted argument cites material that exists in\n  this run.\n- Bull/Bear submit structured ``evidence_ids``; the program validates each against\n  the run index and only then mints an ``argument_id`` for the accepted argument.\n- The Portfolio Manager selects from those accepted ``argument_ids``.\n- ``evaluate`` checks the whole chain (recommendation -> accepted argument ->\n  this run's material) and returns one ``GateOutcome``. ``apply`` projects that\n  outcome onto the run state used by the sinks (CLI, API, reports, memory).\n\nOnly two outward rejection reasons exist: ``INVALID_RATING`` and\n``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references\nall map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,\n``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.rating import RATINGS_5_TIER, RATING_REVIEW\n\n# The analyst state keys whose non-empty text is admissible as run material.\n_ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS = (\n    \"market_report\",\n    \"sentiment_report\",\n    \"news_report\",\n    \"fundamentals_report\",\n)\n\n# Outward rejection reasons (D1 / runtime-policy-catalog.md).\nINVALID_RATING = \"INVALID_RATING\"\nINSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE = \"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\"\n\n# The five-tier scale as a set of canonical strings, for O(1) membership tests.\n_RATING_SET = frozenset(RATINGS_5_TIER)\n\n# Publication status values carried on the run state.\nAPPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\nBLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass EvidenceRecord:\n    \"\"\"One admissible piece of run material, addressed by a run-bound id.\"\"\"\n\n    evidence_id: str\n    source: str      # analyst state key the material came from, e.g. \"market_report\"\n    excerpt: str     # short, human-resolvable pointer into the material\n    run_id: str\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ArgumentRecord:\n    \"\"\"An argument accepted only because each cited evidence id resolved in this run.\"\"\"\n\n    argument_id: str\n    speaker: str                  # \"Bull Analyst\" / \"Bear Analyst\"\n    text: str\n    evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass GateOutcome:\n    \"\"\"The single release decision for a run.\"\"\"\n\n    status: str                              # APPROVED | BLOCKED\n    reason: str | None                       # INVALID_RATING | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n    rating: str | None                       # a 5-tier rating only when APPROVED\n    resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)\n    # resolved_chain items: (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n\n    @property\n    def approved(self) -> bool:\n        return self.status == APPROVED\n\n\nclass EvidenceIndex:\n    \"\"\"Run-scoped evidence and accepted arguments built by the program.\n\n    Constructed at the start of a run from its own analyst reports, so ids from a\n    different run can never resolve here. Immutable after build; ``accept`` adds\n    accepted arguments but never rewrites evidence.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, run_id: str, evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord]):\n        self.run_id = run_id\n        self._evidence = dict(evidence)\n        self._arguments: dict[str, ArgumentRecord] = {}\n\n    # --- evidence ---\n\n    def has_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool:\n        return evidence_id in self._evidence\n\n    def evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> EvidenceRecord:\n        return self._evidence[evidence_id]\n\n    @property\n    def evidence_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._evidence)\n\n    # --- accepted arguments ---\n\n    def accept(self, argument: ArgumentRecord) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Accept an argument iff every cited evidence id resolves in this run.\n\n        Returns whether it was accepted. Rejection leaves the index unchanged;\n        the caller must not mint an argument id for a rejected submission.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not argument.evidence_ids:\n            return False\n        if any(eid not in self._evidence for eid in argument.evidence_ids):\n            return False\n        self._arguments[argument.argument_id] = argument\n        return True\n\n    def has_argument(self, argument_id: str) -> bool:\n        return argument_id in self._arguments\n\n    def argument(self, argument_id: str) -> ArgumentRecord:\n        return self._arguments[argument_id]\n\n    @property\n    def argument_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._arguments)\n\n\ndef build_evidence_index(run_id: str, state) -> EvidenceIndex:\n    \"\"\"Index this run's non-empty analyst reports, one ``evidence_id`` per report.\n\n    Only material actually present in the run is indexed. Deterministic: ids and\n    iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.\n    \"\"\"\n    evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}\n    for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:\n        text = state.get(key)\n        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():\n            continue\n        evidence_id = f\"ev:{run_id}:{key}\"\n        excerpt = _excerpt(text)\n        evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n            evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=excerpt, run_id=run_id,\n        )\n    return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n\n\ndef _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n    flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n    return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n\n\ndef _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n\n    Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n    ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n    \"\"\"\n    if value is None:\n        return None\n    rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n    if not isinstance(rating, str):\n        return None\n    return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n\n\ndef evaluate(\n    index: EvidenceIndex,\n    candidate_rating,\n    candidate_argument_ids,\n) -> GateOutcome:\n    \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n\n    Order matters: an invalid rating is reported before a missing chain, so a\n    candidate that fails both returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is\n    consulted here.\n    \"\"\"\n    rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n    if rating is None:\n        return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n\n    cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    for argument_id in cited:\n        if not index.has_argument(argument_id):\n            continue\n        argument = index.argument(argument_id)\n        for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n            if index.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n                resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, index.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n    if not resolved:\n        return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n\n    return GateOutcome(\n        status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n    )\n\n\ndef apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n\n    On APPROVED the official rating and the resolved chain are published. On\n    BLOCKED the run carries no official rating (``final_rating`` becomes the\n    non-tradeable sentinel) and no candidate body reaches an official field; the\n    candidate decision is kept only in the internal ``candidate_decision`` key for\n    audit and is never read by a sink.\n    \"\"\"\n    status = outcome.status\n    final_state[\"publication_status\"] = status\n    final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = outcome.reason\n    final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = outcome.resolved_chain\n\n    # The candidate body is moved out of the official decision field, so a sink\n    # cannot publish it as the run's recommendation.\n    candidate_body = final_state.pop(\"final_trade_decision\", None) or final_state.get(\n        \"candidate_decision\"\n    )\n    if candidate_body:\n        final_state[\"candidate_decision\"] = candidate_body\n    final_state.pop(\"final_trade_decision\", None)\n\n    if outcome.approved:\n        final_state[\"final_rating\"] = outcome.rating\n        final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = candidate_body or \"\"\n    else:\n        # No tradeable rating leaks: the sentinel keeps legacy readers safe when\n        # they guard with ``is_review``.\n        final_state[\"final_rating\"] = RATING_REVIEW\n        final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n    return final_state\n",

              "newString": "    def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):\n        \"\"\"Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log\n        for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here.\n\n        FR-01 / INV-01: a run the publication gate blocked writes nothing to\n        decision memory — not a rating, not even a REVIEW entry — and its state log\n        omits the candidate body.\n        \"\"\"\n        self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)\n        if final_state.get(\"publication_status\") == \"BLOCKED\":\n            logger.warning(\n                \"Publication blocked for %s on %s (%s); nothing added to the memory log\",\n                company_name, trade_date, final_state.get(\"publication_reason\"),\n            )\n            return\n        decision = final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\")\n        if not decision:\n            logger.warning(\"No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log\",\n                           company_name, trade_date)\n            return\n        self.memory_log.store_decision(\n            ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,\n            rating=run_rating(final_state),\n        )",

          "text": "Now the counterexample: fake model `with_structured_output` raises → `bind_structured` catches `NotImplementedError` → returns `None`. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references\n23: all map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,\n24: ``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.\n25: \"\"\"\n26: \n27: from __future__ import annotations\n28: \n29: from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n30: \n31: from tradingagents.agents.rating import RATINGS_5_TIER, RATING_REVIEW\n32: \n33: # The analyst state keys whose non-empty text is admissible as run material.\n34: _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS = (\n35:     \"market_report\",\n36:     \"sentiment_report\",\n37:     \"news_report\",\n38:     \"fundamentals_report\",\n39: )\n40: \n41: # Outward rejection reasons (D1 / runtime-policy-catalog.md).\n42: INVALID_RATING = \"INVALID_RATING\"\n43: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE = \"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\"\n44: \n45: # The five-tier scale as a set of canonical strings, for O(1) membership tests.\n46: _RATING_SET = frozenset(RATINGS_5_TIER)\n47: \n48: # Publication status values carried on the run state.\n49: APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n50: BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n51: \n52: \n53: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n54: class EvidenceRecord:\n55:     \"\"\"One admissible piece of run material, addressed by a run-bound id.\"\"\"\n56: \n57:     evidence_id: str\n58:     source: str      # analyst state key the material came from, e.g. \"market_report\"\n59:     excerpt: str     # short, human-resolvable pointer into the material\n60:     run_id: str\n61: \n62: \n63: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n64: class ArgumentRecord:\n65:     \"\"\"An argument accepted only because each cited evidence id resolved in this run.\"\"\"\n66: \n67:     argument_id: str\n68:     speaker: str                  # \"Bull Analyst\" / \"Bear Analyst\"\n69:     text: str\n70:     evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n71: \n72: \n73: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n74: class GateOutcome:\n75:     \"\"\"The single release decision for a run.\"\"\"\n76: \n77:     status: str                              # APPROVED | BLOCKED\n78:     reason: str | None                       # INVALID_RATING | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n79:     rating: str | None                       # a 5-tier rating only when APPROVED\n80:     resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)\n81:     # Deterministic: ids and\n143:     iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.\n144:     \"\"\"\n145:     evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}\n146:     for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:\n147:         text = state.get(key)\n148:         if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():\n149:             continue\n150:         evidence_id = f\"ev:{run_id}:{key}\"\n151:         excerpt = _excerpt(text)\n152:         evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n153:             evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=excerpt, run_id=run_id,\n154:         )\n155:     return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n156: \n157: \n158: def _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n159:     \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n160:     flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n161:     return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n162: \n163: \n164: def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n165:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n166: \n167:     Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n168:     ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n169:     \"\"\"\n170:     if value is None:\n171:         return None\n172:     rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n173:     if not isinstance(rating, str):\n174:         return None\n175:     return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n176: \n177: \n178: def evaluate(\n179:     index: EvidenceIndex,\n180:     candidate_rating,\n181:     candidate_argument_ids,\n182: ) -> GateOutcome:\n183:     \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n184: \n185:     Order matters: an invalid rating is reported before a missing chain, so a\n186:     candidate that fails both returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is\n187:     consulted here.\n188:     \"\"\"\n189:     rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n190:     if rating is None:\n191:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n192: \n193:     cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n194:     resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n195:     for argument_id in cited:\n196:         if not index.has_argument(argument_id):\n197:             continue\n198:         argument = index.argument(argument_id)\n199:         for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n200:             if index.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n201:                 resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, index.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n202:     if not resolved:\n203:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n204: \n205:     return GateOutcome(\n206:         status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n207:     )\n208: \n209: \n210: def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n211:     \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n212: \n213:     On APPROVED the official rating and the resolved chain are published.           "type": "text",
          "text": "Now I'll rewrite `publication_gate.py` to make state fully serializable (dict-based, no `EvidenceIndex` object in graph state). The `EvidenceIndex` class stays for in-memory logic/tests, but the graph stores plain dicts and rebuilds a view via a `from_state` helper."

          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"Deterministic publication gate for FR-01 / INV-01.\n\nOwner module for the release decision described in\n``architecture-blueprint.md`` (FR-01 row) and ``docs/architecture/invariants.md``\n(INV-01). The gate is the single authority for whether a candidate recommendation\nbecomes an official decision. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the\nprogram itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating\nfallback is honoured around the gate.\n\nDesign (plan revision 1):\n- Evidence is indexed from the run's own non-empty analyst reports *before* the\n  first debate turn, so every accepted argument cites material that exists in\n  this run. The index is carried on the graph state as **plain, msgpack-safe\n  data** (``evidence_index`` = a dict of primitive values), never as an object,\n  so checkpointed runs can be saved and resumed.\n- Bull/Bear submit structured ``evidence_ids``; the program validates each against\n  the run index and only then mints a run-bound ``argument_id``.\n- The Portfolio Manager selects from those accepted ``argument_ids``.\n- ``evaluate`` checks the whole chain (recommendation -> accepted argument ->\n  this run's material) and returns one ``GateOutcome``. ``apply`` projects that\n  outcome onto the run state used by the sinks (CLI, API, reports, memory).\n\nOnly two outward rejection reasons exist: ``INVALID_RATING`` and\n``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references\nall map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,\n``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.rating import RATINGS_5_TIER, RATING_REVIEW\n\n# The analyst state keys whose non-empty text is admissible as run material.\n_ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS = (\n    \"market_report\",\n    \"sentiment_report\",\n    \"news_report\",\n    \"fundamentals_report\",\n)\n\n# Outward rejection reasons (D1 / runtime-policy-catalog.md).\nINVALID_RATING = \"INVALID_RATING\"\nINSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE = \"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\"\n\n# The five-tier scale as a set of canonical strings, for O(1) membership tests.\n_RATING_SET = frozenset(RATINGS_5_TIER)\n\n# Publication status values carried on the run state.\nAPPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\nBLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass EvidenceRecord:\n    \"\"\"One admissible piece of run material, addressed by a run-bound id.\"\"\"\n\n    evidence_id: str\n    source: str      # analyst state key the material came from, e.g. \"market_report\"\n    excerpt: str     # short, human-resolvable pointer into the material\n    run_id: str\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ArgumentRecord:\n    \"\"\"An argument accepted only because each cited evidence id resolved in this run.\"\"\"\n\n    argument_id: str\n    speaker: str                  # \"Bull Analyst\" / \"Bear Analyst\"\n    text: str\n    evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass GateOutcome:\n    \"\"\"The single release decision for a run.\"\"\"\n\n    status: str                              # APPROVED | BLOCKED\n    reason: str | None                       # INVALID_RATING | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n    rating: str | None                       # a 5-tier rating only when APPROVED\n    resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)\n    # resolved_chain items: (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n\n    @property\n    def approved(self) -> bool:\n        return self.status == APPROVED\n\n\n# --- the serializable on-state representation -------------------------------\n#\n# The graph state carries the index as plain data so a checkpoint (msgpack) can\n# store it. Shape:\n#   evidence_index = {\n#       \"run_id\": str,\n#       \"evidence\": [ {\"id\", \"source\", \"excerpt\"} , ... ],\n#       \"arguments\": [ {\"id\", \"speaker\", \"text\", \"evidence_ids\"} , ... ],\n#   }\n# Every value is a str / list / dict of primitives.\n\n\ndef index_to_state(index: \"EvidenceIndex\") -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Flatten an EvidenceIndex into msgpack-safe primitives for the graph state.\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": index.run_id,\n        \"evidence\": [\n            {\"id\": e.evidence_id, \"source\": e.source, \"excerpt\": e.excerpt}\n            for e in index.evidence_records\n        ],\n        \"arguments\": [\n            {\"id\": a.argument_id, \"speaker\": a.speaker, \"text\": a.text,\n             \"evidence_ids\": list(a.evidence_ids)}\n            for a in index.argument_records\n        ],\n    }\n\n\nclass EvidenceIndex:\n    \"\"\"Run-scoped evidence and accepted arguments (in-memory helper).\n\n    Built at run start from its own reports; ``accept`` validates submissions.\n    The graph state holds ``index_to_state(...)`` rather than this object, and\n    ``evaluate`` reads either shape via :func:`as_index`.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, run_id: str, evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord]):\n        self.run_id = run_id\n        self._evidence = dict(evidence)\n        self._arguments: dict[str, ArgumentRecord] = {}\n\n    # --- evidence ---\n\n    def has_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool:\n        return evidence_id in self._evidence\n\n    def evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> EvidenceRecord:\n        return self._evidence[evidence_id]\n\n    @property\n    def evidence_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._evidence)\n\n    @property\n    def evidence_records(self) -> tuple[EvidenceRecord, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._evidence.values())\n\n    # --- accepted arguments ---\n\n    def accept(self, argument: ArgumentRecord) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Accept an argument iff every cited evidence id resolves in this run.\n\n        Returns whether it was accepted. Rejection leaves the index unchanged;\n        the caller must not mint an argument id for a rejected submission.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not argument.evidence_ids:\n            return False\n        if any(eid not in self._evidence for eid in argument.evidence_ids):\n            return False\n        self._arguments[argument.argument_id] = argument\n        return True\n\n    def argument(self, argument_id: str) -> ArgumentRecord:\n        return self._arguments[argument_id]\n\n    def has_argument(self, argument_id: str) -> bool:\n        return argument_id in self._arguments\n\n    @property\n    def argument_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._arguments)\n\n    @property\n    def argument_records(self) -> tuple[ArgumentRecord, ...]:\n        return tuple(self._arguments.values())\n\n\ndef as_index(value) -> \"EvidenceIndex\":\n    \"\"\"A read-only EvidenceIndex view of either an object or the state dict.\n\n    ``evaluate`` accepts the graph state's serializable dict or an in-memory\n    index, so the same logic serves tests and resumed checkpoints.\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, EvidenceIndex):\n        return value\n    if value is None:\n        return EvidenceIndex(run_id=\"\", evidence={})\n    run_id = value.get(\"run_id\", \"\")\n    evidence = {\n        item[\"id\"]: EvidenceRecord(\n            evidence_id=item[\"id\"], source=item[\"source\"],\n            excerpt=item.get(\"excerpt\", \"\"), run_id=run_id,\n        )\n        for item in value.get(\"evidence\", [])\n    }\n    index = EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n    for arg in value.get(\"arguments\", []):\n        index._arguments[arg[\"id\"]] = ArgumentRecord(\n            argument_id=arg[\"id\"], speaker=arg.get(\"speaker\", \"\"),\n            text=arg.get(\"text\", \"\"), evidence_ids=tuple(arg.get(\"evidence_ids\", [])),\n        )\n    return index\n\n\ndef build_evidence_index(run_id: str, state) -> EvidenceIndex:\n    \"\"\"Index this run's non-empty analyst reports, one ``evidence_id`` per report.\n\n    Only material actually present in the run is indexed. Deterministic: ids and\n    iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.\n    \"\"\"\n    evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}\n    for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:\n        text = state.get(key)\n        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():\n            continue\n        evidence_id = f\"ev:{run_id}:{key}\"\n        evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n            evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=_excerpt(text), run_id=run_id,\n        )\n    return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n\n\ndef evidence_menu(index) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The evidence IDs and their material, for the researcher prompt.\n\n    The model may cite only these IDs; they are the program-built index for this\n    run, so a cited ID resolves to actual run material.\n    \"\"\"\n    idx = as_index(index)\n    if not idx.evidence_ids:\n        return \"(No evidence is available in this run; you cannot cite any evidence ID.)\"\n    lines = []\n    for record in idx.evidence_records:\n        lines.append(f\"- {record.evidence_id}  [{record.source}] {record.excerpt}\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n    flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n    return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n\n\ndef _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n\n    Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n    ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n    \"\"\"\n    if value is None:\n        return None\n    rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n    if not isinstance(rating, str):\n        return None\n    return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n\n\ndef evaluate(index, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids) -> GateOutcome:\n    \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n\n    ``index`` may be the state dict or an EvidenceIndex. Order matters: an invalid\n    rating is reported before a missing chain, so a candidate that fails both\n    returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is consulted here.\n    \"\"\"\n    idx = as_index(index)\n    rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n    if rating is None:\n        return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n\n    cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n    resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    for argument_id in cited:\n        if not idx.has_argument(argument_id):\n            continue\n        argument = idx.argument(argument_id)\n        for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n            if idx.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n                resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, idx.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n    if not resolved:\n        return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n\n    return GateOutcome(\n        status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n    )\n\n\ndef apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n\n    On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the\n    candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the\n    run carries no official rating and no candidate body in any official field:\n    ``candidate_decision`` is removed from the returned mapping entirely, so the\n    Python API's returned state cannot expose the candidate. ``final_rating``\n    becomes the non-tradeable sentinel ``REVIEW`` for legacy callers; the API's\n    second tuple member is the only other REVIEW use.\n    \"\"\"\n    status = outcome.status\n    final_state[\"publication_status\"] = status\n    final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = outcome.reason\n    final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)\n\n    if outcome.approved:\n        body = final_state.get(\"candidate_decision\") or final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\") or \"\"\n        final_state[\"final_rating\"] = outcome.rating\n        final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = body\n        final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n    else:\n        # No tradeable rating and no candidate body leak into the returned state.\n        final_state[\"final_rating\"] = RATING_REVIEW\n        final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n        final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n    return final_state\n",

          "type": "text",
          "text": "`_new_run_token` uses a random uuid each node invocation — that breaks checkpoint resume because on resume the index node re-runs and mints a new token. Better: derive a stable run token from company+date so that resumed runs get the same token. But cross-run reference must still fail. Since the index is rebuilt on resume from the same reports, a same ticker+date resumed run producing the same token is fine — cross-run means a *different* run, and its index wouldn't contain the argument anyway. Use a deterministic token from company+date. But then two separate runs of same ticker/date share a token — arguments are still validated by presence in the index of *that* state, so cross-run still blocked. Use deterministic."
        },

        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "A concern: the CLI test relies on `cli.display.message_buffer` being the shared singleton, but `display_complete_report` uses the module-level `message_buffer` only for the layout, not for the final report. `display_complete_report` reads `final_state` directly, so it's independent of the buffer. Good.\n\nBut the `_apply_stream_chunk` helper uses its own `MessageBuffer`, which doesn't mutate the singleton. Fine — the assertion is on the panel content.\n\nNow Item 1: the positive-publish test must take the evidence ID **from the actual prompt** the researcher receives, not pre-inject. Let me rewrite `test_fr01_publish_valid.py` so the fake structured model parses the \"Available evidence\" block from the prompt."
        },
        {
          "type": "tool",
          "id": "call_00_b7nYOIAUtdh7gezg8xi05456",
          "name": "write",
          "executed": false,
          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"FR-01 positive test — a valid rating with resolvable evidence is released.\n\nThe normal case: a decision that cites an accepted argument whose evidence id\nexists in this run's index publishes as an official rating, and the chain resolves\nback to the run material. This guards against a gate that blocks everything.\n\nThe fake model does **not** receive a pre-injected evidence id: it reads the\n``Available evidence`` block out of the prompt it is actually given and cites the\nfirst id it finds — so the test proves the prompt wiring, not an injected constant.\n\nIt also proves the argument id is run-bound: an argument id minted under a\ndifferent run token is rejected (see ``test_cross_run_argument_is_rejected``).\n\nDrives the real ``TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()`` path.\nNo network.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun\nfrom langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.schemas import DebateArgument, PortfolioDecision, PortfolioRating\n\nREPORT = \"The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend.\"\n\n# A line in the evidence menu looks like: \"- ev:<run>:market_report  [market_report] <excerpt>\"\n_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r\"^- (ev:\\S+)\\s+\\[\", re.MULTILINE)\n\n\ndef _cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The evidence IDs the researcher is actually offered in this prompt.\"\"\"\n    match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)\n    return [match.group(1)] if match else []\n\n\nclass _EvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):\n    \"\"\"Emits reports; structured calls read the evidence menu from the prompt.\"\"\"\n\n    @property\n    def _llm_type(self) -> str:\n        return \"evidence-fake\"\n\n    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        return self\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        if schema is DebateArgument:\n            return _StructuredArgument()\n        if schema is PortfolioDecision:\n            return _StructuredDecision()\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,\n                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,\n                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:\n        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])\n\n\nclass _StructuredArgument:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # Cite the real run evidence id that appears in the prompt.\n        return DebateArgument(\n            argument=\"bull case\",\n            evidence_ids=_cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt),\n        )\n\n\nclass _StructuredDecision:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # The PM must cite the accepted argument. The argument id is run-bound, so\n        # read it from the 'Accepted arguments' block the PM is actually given.\n        match = re.search(r\"^- (arg:\\S+)\", prompt, re.MULTILINE)\n        argument_ids = [match.group(1)] if match else []\n        return PortfolioDecision(\n            rating=PortfolioRating.BUY,\n            executive_summary=\"add\",\n            investment_thesis=\"breakout\",\n            argument_ids=argument_ids,\n        )\n\n\nclass _FakeClient:\n    def __init__(self, llm):\n        self._llm = llm\n\n    def get_llm(self):\n        return self._llm\n\n\ndef _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg\n    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"create_tier_client\", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_EvidenceModel()))\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"resolve_instrument_identity\", lambda t: {\n        \"company_name\": \"NVIDIA Corporation\", \"sector\": \"Technology\",\n        \"industry\": \"Semiconductors\", \"exchange\": \"NASDAQ\", \"quote_type\": \"EQUITY\",\n    })\n    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)\n    config.update({\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n        \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n        \"memory_log_path\": str(tmp_path / \"memory.md\"),\n        \"checkpoint_enabled\": False,\n    })\n    graph = tg.TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts=(\"market\",), debug=False, config=config)\n    final_state, signal = graph.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-01-05\")\n    return graph, final_state, signal\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_valid_rating_with_resolvable_evidence_is_approved(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    graph, final_state, signal = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n\n    assert final_state.get(\"publication_status\") == \"APPROVED\", final_state.get(\"publication_reason\")\n    assert signal == \"Buy\"\n    assert final_state.get(\"publication_chain\")  # resolves back to run material\n    assert graph.memory_log.load_entries()  # an approved decision is recorded\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_argument_id_is_run_bound(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"The accepted argument id embeds the run id, so it cannot be reused cross-run.\"\"\"\n    _, final_state, _ = _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n    chain = final_state.get(\"publication_chain\") or []\n    assert chain, \"expected a resolved chain\"\n    argument_id = chain[0][0]\n    assert argument_id.startswith(\"arg:bull:\")\n    assert \"NVDA:2026-01-05\" in argument_id\n",
              "path": "[REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/test/offline/test_fr01_publish_valid.py"

At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to\n11:    markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason\n12:    (malformed JSON from a weak model, transient provider issue), fall\n13:    back to a plain ``llm.invoke`` so the pipeline never blocks.\n14: \n15: Centralising the pattern here keeps the agent factories small and ensures\n16: all three agents log the same warnings when fallback fires.\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: import logging\n22: from collections.abc import Callable\n23: from typing import Any, TypeVar\n24: \n25: from pydantic import BaseModel\n26: \n27: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n28: \n29: T = TypeVar(\"T\", bound=BaseModel)\n30: \n31: # Schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool (the schema itself), so a\n32: # model that reaches for a search tool emits an unknown tool call and the whole\n33: # structured attempt is discarded for a free-text retry. Agents on this path\n34: # state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone\n35: # (#1130).\n36: NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (\n37:     \"Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools \"\n38:     \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n39: )\n40: \n41: \n42: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n43:     \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n44: \n45:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n46:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n47:     \"\"\"\n48:     try:\n49:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n50:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n51:         logger.warning(\n52:             \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n53:             \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n54:             agent_name, exc,\n55:         )\n56:         return None\n57: \n58: \n59: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n60:     \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n61: \n62:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n63:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n64:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n65:     \"\"\"\n66:     if structured_llm is None:\n67:         return None\n68:     try:\n69:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n70:         if result is None:\n71:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n72:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n73:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n74:             raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n75:         return result\n76:     except Exception as exc:\n77:         logger.warning(\n78:             \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n79:             agent_name, exc,\n80:         )\n81:         return None\n82: \n83: \n84: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n85:     structured_llm: Any | None,\n86:     plain_llm: Any,\n87:     prompt: Any,\n88:     render: Callable[[T], str],\n89:     agent_name: str,\n90: ) -> str:\n91:     \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n92:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n93:     if result is not None:\n94:         return render(result)\n95:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content"

On blocked, `_report_parts` omits the decision section (empty). Good.\n\nNow Item 3 — add a **resume test** verifying the chain still validates after a checkpoint round-trip. Let me add a unit test that serializes the state dict with msgpack and rebuilds via `as_index`, plus a `test_inv01_resume.py` that simulates resume by re-running `evaluate` on the rehydrated index."

          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"INV-01 checkpoint test — the evidence chain survives a serialization round-trip.\n\nFR-01 / INV-01, requirement 3: a checkpointed run must be resumable, so the graph\nstate's ``evidence_index`` must be plain, msgpack-safe data — not an ``EvidenceIndex``\nobject (the baseline error was ``TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable:\nEvidenceIndex``). After a round-trip through msgpack, ``evaluate`` must still resolve\nthe same chain and reach the same release decision.\n\nAlso proves the run-bound argument id is stable across the round-trip (so a resumed\nrun can still cite the argument the pre-interruption debate accepted).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport msgpack\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tradingagents.graph import publication_gate as gate\n\n\ndef _roundtrip(value):\n    \"\"\"Serialize and deserialize a value the way a checkpoint does (msgpack).\"\"\"\n    return msgpack.unpackb(msgpack.packb(value), raw=False)\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_state_index_is_msgpack_safe():\n    index = gate.build_evidence_index(\"run-1\", {\"market_report\": \"breakout text\"})\n    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]\n    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(\"arg:bull:run-1:1\", \"Bull Analyst\", \"x\", (ev,)))\n\n    state_index = gate.index_to_state(index)\n    # The whole point of requirement 3: this must not raise.\n    restored = _roundtrip(state_index)\n\n    assert restored[\"run_id\"] == \"run-1\"\n    assert restored[\"evidence\"][0][\"id\"] == ev\n    assert restored[\"arguments\"][0][\"evidence_ids\"] == [ev]\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_chain_still_validates_after_roundtrip():\n    index = gate.build_evidence_index(\"run-1\", {\"market_report\": \"breakout text\"})\n    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]\n    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(\"arg:bull:run-1:1\", \"Bull Analyst\", \"x\", (ev,)))\n\n    restored = _roundtrip(gate.index_to_state(index))\n\n    outcome = gate.evaluate(restored, \"Buy\", (\"arg:bull:run-1:1\",))\n    assert outcome.status == gate.APPROVED\n    assert outcome.resolved_chain == ((\"arg:bull:run-1:1\", ev, \"market_report\"),)\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_roundtrip_keeps_the_block_on_a_missing_chain():\n    index = gate.build_evidence_index(\"run-1\", {\"market_report\": \"breakout text\"})\n    restored = _roundtrip(gate.index_to_state(index))\n\n    outcome = gate.evaluate(restored, \"Buy\", (\"arg:bull:run-1:1\",))\n    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED\n    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_state_dict_and_object_read_the_same():\n    index = gate.build_evidence_index(\"run-1\", {\"market_report\": \"breakout text\"})\n    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]\n    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(\"arg:bull:run-1:1\", \"Bull Analyst\", \"x\", (ev,)))\n\n    from_object = gate.evaluate(index, \"Buy\", (\"arg:bull:run-1:1\",))\n    from_dict = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(index), \"Buy\", (\"arg:bull:run-1:1\",))\n    assert from_object == from_dict\n",

          "text": "Now there's still the issue that the fake graph has no `default_report_path`/`save_reports` — but with `flags={\"save\": False}`, `_offer_reports` skips saving. Good.\n\nNow item 2: replace the msgpack test with a real checkpoint-resume test. Let me first look at how to interrupt and resume.           "text": "Now I understand the checkpoint config. Let me write the real resume test. The strategy:\n\n1. Build a fake model that counts Bull turns and raises on the **second** Bull turn... Actually the simplest deterministic interruption is to use `stream_run`, consume steps until we've seen the `Index Evidence` step's effect (state has `run_id` and non-empty `evidence_index`), then `stream.close()` — simulating a process interruption mid-run. This leaves the checkpointer with saved state.\n\n2. Then re-open `begin_checkpoint` for the same ticker/date — it should detect a resume step — and invoke with `None` to resume to completion.\n\nBut `_Graph` control: I'll use the real `TradingAgentsGraph` with a fake model via monkeypatching `create_tier_client` and `resolve_instrument_identity`, as the counterexample does. The fake model must support structured output for `DebateArgument` (cite a real id from the prompt) and `PortfolioDecision` (cite the accepted argument id read from the prompt), and plain invoke for analysts.\n\nProblem: the evidence ids are minted with the run's `run_id` (a uuid). The Bull's prompt shows the real id, so the structured model reads it. The PM's prompt shows the accepted argument id (`arg:bull:<run>:<n>`), so the PM reads that. This mirrors the positive test.\n\nFor the interruption: I'll iterate `graph.stream_run(...)` and stop (close) once I've observed a state where `evidence_index` is present and has evidence. But `stream_run` yields `(messages, chunk)`; the `Index Evidence` step is a top-level `values` chunk. I can detect `chunk.get(\"run_id\")` and a non-empty `evidence_index[\"evidence\"]`. Then break out of the loop without consuming further — but need to avoid the `finally` closing issue; `stream_run` has its own `finally`. If I `break`, the generator is not exhausted; I should call `.close()` on it. Then `graph.end_checkpoint()`.\n\nThen resume: `graph.begin_checkpoint(...)` returns a thread_id, and `graph.checkpoint_input(init)` returns `None` if resuming. Then `graph.graph.invoke(None, config={\"configurable\": {\"thread_id\": ...}})` — but I need the config. Actually `_run_graph` handles this. Simpler: call `graph.propagate(...)` again — but `propagate` builds a *fresh* `create_run_state` and uses `checkpoint_scope` which calls `begin_checkpoint` (resume detected) then `_run_graph` uses `checkpoint_input` → None → resumes. \n\nBut the second `propagate` will use the same `graph` object; `begin_checkpoint` re-enters the checkpointer. Let me just call `propagate` twice, but interrupt the *first* by making the Bull model raise a special exception after Index Evidence, so `propagate` raises and the checkpoint is saved at the last completed node. investment_thesis=\"breakout\",\n84:             argument_ids=argument_ids,\n85:         )\n86: \n87: \n88: class _FakeClient:\n89:     def __init__(self, llm):\n90:         self._llm = llm\n91: \n92:     def get_llm(self):\n93:         return self._llm\n94: \n95: \n96: def _run(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n97:     import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg\n98:     from           "text": "Good, applied. Now let me write the real checkpoint-resume test. Let me check the `propagate` debug=False path with `checkpoint_enabled=True`: it uses `graph.invoke` which runs to completion. Then `propagate` again resumes. Let me verify `stream_run` propagates exceptions — yes, it doesn't catch, only `finally: stream.close`. And `_run_graph` with `debug=False` uses `graph.invoke`, which will propagate the model exception.\n\nBut `propagate` wraps in `checkpoint_scope` (contextmanager) whose `finally` calls `end_checkpoint` — so the SQLite file is closed but persists. The `clear_checkpoint_on_success` in `_run_graph` won't run because the exception propagates before it. Good — checkpoint remains.\n\nOn the second `propagate`, `begin_checkpoint` reads `checkpoint_step(...)` → not None → `_resuming=True`, returns thread_id. `_run_graph` → `checkpoint_input(init)` → None → `graph.invoke(None, config with thread_id)` → resumes. \n\nNow the fake: I need a module-level flag to fail exactly once. Let me write it. I'll make the Bull structured call raise on its first invocation only (class attribute counter). Since both runs share the same model instance settings (monkeypatched factory returns a fresh model per `TradingAgentsGraph`? Actually `create_tier_client` is called to build the llm once per graph. Two `propagate` calls on the same graph reuse the same llm. So a class-level counter works.\n\nLet me also confirm `resolve_instrument_identity` is called each `create_run_state`. It is (in `resolve_instrument_context`). Fine.\n\nNow, the model must handle `DebateArgument` and `PortfolioDecision` structured output, and plain invoke for analysts/managers/researchers. The researchers use `invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, ...)` where `structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, DebateArgument, ...)`. If `with_structured_output(DebateArgument)` returns a failing object, `invoke_structured` catches and falls back to plain `llm.invoke` → report text with no evidence ids → no accepted argument → PM gets no accepted arguments → PM cites nothing → BLOCKED. That would fail the \"legal suggestion passes\" assertion.\n\nSo the crash must happen **after** Index Evidence but I must ensure the resume path produces an accepted argument. The interruption point: if I crash on the Bull's *structured* call, on resume the Bull re-runs (the node didn't complete) and this time succeeds.             "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"INV-01 checkpoint resume — a resumed run keeps its id and its chain verifies.\n\nFR-01 / INV-01, requirement 3: a checkpointed run must be resumable **using the\nproject's own LangGraph checkpointer** (no ``msgpack`` dependency, no disabling the\ncheckpoint to dodge the problem). The evidence index is plain, serializable state,\nso an interrupted run saves and a subsequent invocation on the same ticker+date\nresumes it. The resumed run must:\n\n- keep the **same run id** the interrupted run minted (ids are stable across a\n  resume), so an argument accepted before the interruption is still resolvable;\n- still resolve that argument's evidence, and so a legal decision is approved.\n\nThe interruption is real: the fake model raises inside the first Bull turn, after\nthe ``Index Evidence`` node has completed and saved. The second ``propagate`` call\nresumes from that checkpoint.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun\nfrom langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel\nfrom langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\nfrom langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult\n\nfrom tradingagents.agents.schemas import DebateArgument, PortfolioDecision, PortfolioRating\n\nREPORT = \"The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend.\"\n\n_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r\"^- (ev:\\S+)\\s+\\[\", re.MULTILINE)\n_ARGUMENT_LINE = re.compile(r\"^- (arg:\\S+)\", re.MULTILINE)\n\n\nclass _CrashException(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"Raised from the first Bull turn of the first attempt to interrupt the run.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass _CrashThenSucceedModel(BaseChatModel):\n    \"\"\"Crashes once mid-run; every later call succeeds.\n\n    ``crashes`` is the number of times to raise before behaving normally. It is a\n    plain class attribute so the two ``propagate`` calls share it.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    crashes: int = 0\n\n    @property\n    def _llm_type(self) -> str:\n        return \"crash-then-succeed-fake\"\n\n    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        return self\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        if schema is DebateArgument:\n            return _StructuredArgument()\n        if schema is PortfolioDecision:\n            return _StructuredDecision()\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,\n                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,\n                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:\n        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])\n\n\nclass _StructuredArgument:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # The first Bull turn of the first attempt interrupts the run.\n        if _CrashThenSucceedModel.crashes > 0:\n            _CrashThenSucceedModel.crashes -= 1\n            raise _CrashException(\"simulated interruption after the index was built\")\n        match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)\n        return DebateArgument(\n            argument=\"bull case\",\n            evidence_ids=[match.group(1)] if match else [],\n        )\n\n\nclass _StructuredDecision:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        match = _ARGUMENT_LINE.search(prompt)\n        argument_ids = [match.group(1)] if match else []\n        return PortfolioDecision(\n            rating=PortfolioRating.BUY,\n            executive_summary=\"add\",\n            investment_thesis=\"breakout\",\n            argument_ids=argument_ids,\n        )\n\n\nclass _FakeClient:\n    def __init__(self, llm):\n        self._llm = llm\n\n    def get_llm(self):\n        return self._llm\n\n\ndef _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path, crashes: int):\n    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg\n    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n\n    _CrashThenSucceedModel.crashes = crashes\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"create_tier_client\",\n                        lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_CrashThenSucceedModel()))\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"resolve_instrument_identity\", lambda t: {\n        \"company_name\": \"NVIDIA Corporation\", \"sector\": \"Technology\",\n        \"industry\": \"Semiconductors\", \"exchange\": \"NASDAQ\", \"quote_type\": \"EQUITY\",\n    })\n    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)\n    config.update({\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n        \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n        \"memory_log_path\": str(tmp_path / \"memory.md\"),\n        #           "type": "text",
          "text": "Now create the cross-run isolation test (item 3): two independent runs on the same ticker/date; different run ids; the second citing the first's evidence/argument is BLOCKED. I'll do it at the gate level (deterministic) plus a run-level check via two `propagate` calls capturing run ids."

          "state": {
            "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"INV-01 cross-run isolation — two independent runs cannot cite each other.\n\nFR-01 / INV-01, requirement 3: a run's id is minted fresh per run (not derived from\nticker+date), so two independent runs on the same instrument and date have\ndifferent ids. A decision in the second run that cites the first run's ``evidence_id``\nor ``argument_id`` must be blocked — the reference does not resolve in the second\nrun's index.\n\nPart 1 exercises the gate directly (deterministic). Part 2 checks the same at the\nreal ``propagate()`` level: two runs on the same ticker+date get different run ids.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tradingagents.graph import publication_gate as gate\n\n\ndef _index_with_accepted(run_id: str, report: str):\n    \"\"\"An index for ``run_id`` with one argument accepted against its evidence.\"\"\"\n    index = gate.build_evidence_index(run_id, {\"market_report\": report})\n    ev = index.evidence_ids[0]\n    argument_id = f\"arg:bull:{run_id}:1\"\n    index.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(argument_id, \"Bull Analyst\", \"x\", (ev,)))\n    return index, ev, argument_id\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_citing_another_runs_evidence_id_is_blocked():\n    run_a, ev_a, arg_a = _index_with_accepted(\"run-A\", \"a\")\n    # Run B is a different run: its index has its own evidence and no accepted argument.\n    run_b, _ev_b, _ = _index_with_accepted(\"run-B\", \"b\")\n\n    # Run B cannot claim run A's evidence, even by trying to build an identical arg.\n    assert run_b.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(\n        \"arg:bull:run-B:1\", \"Bull Analyst\", \"x\", (ev_a,),\n    )) is False\n    outcome = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), \"Buy\", (arg_a,))\n    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED\n    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_citing_another_runs_argument_id_is_blocked():\n    _run_a, _ev_a, arg_a = _index_with_accepted(\"run-A\", \"a\")\n    run_b, ev_b, arg_b = _index_with_accepted(\"run-B\", \"b\")\n\n    # Run B resolves its own chain fine.\n    owns = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), \"Buy\", (arg_b,))\n    assert owns.status == gate.APPROVED\n\n    # But run A's argument id is not in run B's index.\n    outcome = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), \"Buy\", (arg_a,))\n    assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED\n    assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_two_propagate_runs_on_same_ticker_and_date_get_different_ids(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"The run id is per-run, so two independent runs of the same ticker+date differ.\"\"\"\n    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg\n    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n\n    from langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun\n    from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel\n    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n    from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult\n\n    class _NoEvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):\n        @property\n        def _llm_type(self):\n            return \"no-evidence-fake\"\n\n        def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n            return self\n\n        def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n            raise NotImplementedError\n\n        def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,\n                      run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None, **kwargs):\n            return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=\"text\"))])\n\n    class _FakeClient:\n        def __init__(self, llm):\n            self._llm = llm\n\n        def get_llm(self):\n            return self._llm\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"create_tier_client\",\n                        lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient(_NoEvidenceModel()))\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"resolve_instrument_identity\", lambda t: {\n        \"company_name\": \"NVIDIA Corporation\", \"sector\": \"Technology\",\n        \"industry\": \"Semiconductors\", \"exchange\": \"NASDAQ\", \"quote_type\": \"EQUITY\",\n    })\n    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)\n    config.update({\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n        \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n        \"memory_log_path\": str(tmp_path / \"memory.md\"),\n        \"checkpoint_enabled\": False,\n    })\n    graph = tg.TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts=(\"market\",), debug=False, config=config)\n\n    state_a, _ = graph.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-01-05\")\n    state_b, _ = graph.propagate(\"NVDA\", \"2026-01-05\")\n\n    assert state_a.get(\"run_id\"), \"first run should carry a run id\"\n    assert state_b.get(\"run_id\"), \"second run should carry a run id\"\n    assert state_a[\"run_id\"] != state_b[\"run_id\"]\n",

investment_thesis=\"breakout\",\n84:             argument_ids=argument_ids,\n85:         )\n86: \n87: \n88: class _FakeClient:\n89:     def __init__(self, llm):\n90:         self._llm = llm\n91: \n92: signal\n115: \n116: \n117: @pytest.mark.unit\n118: def test_valid_rating_with_resolvable_evidence_is_approved(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n119:     graph, final_state, signal = _run(monkeypatch, Run B is a different run: its index has its own evidence and no accepted argument.\n33:     run_b, _ev_b, _ = _index_with_accepted(\"run-B\", \"b\")\n34: \n35:     # Run B cannot claim run A's evidence, even by trying to build an identical arg.\n36:     assert run_b.accept(gate.ArgumentRecord(\n37:         \"arg:bull:run-B:1\", \"Bull Analyst\", \"x\", (ev_a,),\n38:     )) is False\n39:     outcome = gate.evaluate(gate.index_to_state(run_b), \"Buy\", (arg_a,))\n40:     assert outcome.status == gate.BLOCKED\n41:     assert outcome.reason == gate.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n42: \n43: \n44: @pytest.mark.unit\n45: def test_citing_another_runs_argument_id_is_blocked():\n46:     _run_a, _ev_a, arg_a = _index_with_accepted(\"run-A\", \"a\")\n47:     run_b, ev_b, arg_b = _index_with_accepted(\"run-B\", \"b\")\n48: \n49:     #
