                "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/docs/architecture/permission-model.md, lines 1-27\n1: # Permission model\n2: \n3: Default deny for tools, reads and writes. Use three course roles: Plan (read-only), Build (asks on each approved edit), Verify (read-only). The allowlist covers only project governance, the planned implementation seams and course tests. Broad shell/search tools, external directories, MCP and subagents are denied so they cannot replace bounded reads or edits.\n4: \n5: | Requirement | Planned edit seam (further narrowed by human approval) |\n6: | --- | --- |\n7: | FR-01 | Publication gate, researcher outputs, decision graph, CLI and report adapters |\n8: | FR-02 | Verified metric owner, fundamentals analyst, state and report adapters |\n9: | FR-03 | Sentiment coverage owner, sentiment analyst, state and report adapters |\n10: | NFR-01 | Budget owner, model factory and approved graph dispatch seams |\n11: | NFR-02 | Context owner, analyst closure and neutral risk role |\n12: \n13: OpenCode 2.3.0 automatically loads [opencode.jsonc](../../.opencode/opencode.jsonc). It is the source of truth; [permissions.jsonc](../../.opencode/permissions.jsonc) is its identical course-delivery copy, not a second configuration source. Keep them identical (`git diff --no-index .opencode/opencode.jsonc .opencode/permissions.jsonc`). Secrets, project rules, course requirements, existing tests, CI and Git are never agent-editable. Human approves only the exact implementation paths in the plan; do not select an approval that persists beyond the immediate action.\n14: \n15: From the repository root, run `opencode --version`, `opencode debug config` and `opencode debug agents` before starting `opencode`. Verify the project config source, both rule files, and the three course roles. V2 does not use the previous `--pure` workflow: inspect configured plugins and MCP tools separately, and use a clean profile if unrelated integrations or overrides remain.\n16: \n17: In a disposable checkout, check that Plan/Verify can read a whitelisted file but cannot edit it; all three roles must deny shell and external access. Build must ask before editing a designated module and deny a frozen path such as `AGENTS.md`. Decline the probe edit. Confirm the guard outcomes in the actual tool session; config discovery alone is not enforcement evidence. Do not publish config dumps. These are tool-level controls, not an OS sandbox; any failed guard check blocks agent use.\n18: \n19: ## Configuration review items\n20: \n21: The documentation index (`docs/README.md`), product scope (`docs/req/product.yaml`) and review memo (`docs/review-memo.md`) have exact read-only allowlist entries. C0–C5 is covered by the existing architecture Markdown read pattern.\n22: \n23: The AI-use log, bug and debt records, upstream vendor/date adapters and non-Python fixtures are not generally allowlisted. Before a task depends on one, the human maintainer must review its exact path and update both configuration copies consistently if access is needed. Do not add a broad `docs/**`, vendor-tree or repository-wide write rule.\n24: \n25: For FR-03, proposed additional reads to review include `tradingagents/dataflows/date_window.py`, `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/stocktwits.py`, `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/reddit.py` and `tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/news.py`; resolve any further imports in the approved plan. Approve fixture reads/writes by exact filename (or a justified bounded task directory). Read access is not edit approval.\n26: \n27: Configuration changes belong to the human maintainer. Record effective guard-probe outcomes before session use. If a required read is denied, stop the affected operation for exact-path review. Tool boundaries and evidence responsibilities are defined in the [tool manifest](../code-governance/mcp-tool-manifest.md)."

              "content": "\"\"\"FR-01 / INV-01 R8-B — the four official sinks and the report gate.\n\nBaseline: ``712617e25a380197e38d6ee5cc4dcc7ab393cf61``; contracts C0/C1 v1.0.\nCase IDs: T-FR01-SINKS, T-INV01-BYPASS (report/API/memory/CLI exits).\nApproved plan: R8-B §2 rows 1–6 and §6 A-11, supplementary note §2.2–§2.3.\n\nDesign (separate-approval note):\n\n- ``PublicationResult`` is the only release record. A sink reads it and nothing\n  else: a flat legacy ``publication_status`` or an official-looking\n  ``final_rating``/``final_trade_decision`` without a real gate result is not an\n  approval.\n- The four sinks are exercised independently: the Python return value, the saved\n  report tree (Markdown, HTML, ``5_portfolio/decision.md``), decision memory, and\n  the CLI display entry the existing CLI fake-graph test already drives.\n- The positive control shows each sink still publishes a valid run, so a sink\n  that shows or writes nothing is not the fix.\n- ``save_reports()`` refusal must be the typed ``publication_gate`` exception\n  (note §2.3 option A-1). Any other exception counts as a failure and is re-raised.\n\nReading a denied source here is not an approval of that path.\n\nNo implementation exists yet, so this file is expected to fail at import or\ncollection (the v1 owner symbols are absent). That is not behaviour evidence.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom tradingagents.graph import publication_gate as gate\n\nCONTRACT_VERSION = \"1.0\"\nAPPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\nBLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\nRUN_NOT_COMPLETE = \"RUN_NOT_COMPLETE\"\n\nTICKER = \"AAPL\"\nAS_OF_DATE = \"2026-11-10\"\nRUN_ID = \"run-a-0001\"\nBUY = \"Buy\"\n\n# The candidate body marker: any official surface carrying it has leaked the\n# unapproved candidate (INV-01).\nMARKER = \"INV01-UNPUBLISHED-CANDIDATE-BODY-7f3c\"\nCANDIDATE_BODY = (\n    f\"**Rating**: {BUY}\\n\\n\"\n    \"**Executive Summary**: add on the breakout.\\n\\n\"\n    f\"**Investment Thesis**: {MARKER} price holds above the upper band.\"\n)\n\n\ndef _owner():\n    \"\"\"The v1 owner symbols, or a skip that names what the baseline lacks.\"\"\"\n    missing = [\n        name for name in (\"evaluate_publication\", \"PublicationRequiredError\")\n        if not hasattr(gate, name)\n    ]\n    if missing:\n        pytest.skip(\n            \"FR-01 B not implemented at this baseline: publication_gate lacks \"\n            + \", \".join(missing)\n            + \"; the four-sink behaviour below cannot be exercised\"\n        )\n\n\ndef _run(run_id: str = RUN_ID, execution_status: str = \"COMPLETED\") -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"contract_version\": CONTRACT_VERSION,\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"ticker\": TICKER,\n        \"as_of_date\": AS_OF_DATE,\n        \"execution_status\": execution_status,\n        \"request_limit\": 40,\n    }\n\n\ndef _evidence_index(run_id: str = RUN_ID) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"records\": [{\n            \"contract_version\": CONTRACT_VERSION,\n            \"run_id\": run_id,\n            \"evidence_id\": f\"ev:{run_id}:market\",\n            \"source_kind\": \"market_snapshot\",\n            \"vendor\": \"yahoo\",\n            \"source_ref\": (\n                \"tool:get_verified_market_snapshot?tool_call_id=call-1\"\n                \"&curr_date=2026-11-10&look_back_days=7\"\n            ),\n            \"content_ref\": f\"evidence://{run_id}/call-1.md\",\n            \"window_start\": \"2026-11-03\",\n            \"window_end\": \"2026-11-10\",\n        }],\n    }\n\n\ndef _argument_index(run_id: str = RUN_ID) -> dict:\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"records\": [{\n            \"contract_version\": CONTRACT_VERSION,\n            \"run_id\": run_id,\n            \"argument_id\": f\"arg:bull:{run_id}:1\",\n            \"claim\": \"Price holds above the Bollinger upper band.\",\n            \"evidence_ids\": [f\"ev:{run_id}:market\"],\n        }],\n    }\n\n\ndef _candidate(rating=BUY, argument_ids=None) -> dict:\n    if argument_ids is None:\n        argument_ids = [_argument_index()[\"records\"][0][\"argument_id\"]]\n    return {\"rating\": rating, \"argument_ids\": list(argument_ids), \"body\": CANDIDATE_BODY}\n\n\ndef _approved_result():\n    _owner()\n    return gate.evaluate_publication(\n        _candidate(), _argument_index(), _evidence_index(), _run(),\n    )\n\n\ndef _blocked_result():\n    _owner()\n    return gate.evaluate_publication(\n        _candidate(), {}, _evidence_index(), _run(),\n    )\n\n\ndef _run_state(result) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"A finished run state as the four sinks receive it: identity plus the result.\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": RUN_ID,\n        \"course_run\": _run(),\n        \"company_of_interest\": TICKER,\n        \"trade_date\": AS_OF_DATE,\n        \"market_report\": \"AAPL closed at 348.245 USD.\",\n        \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n        \"news_report\": \"\",\n        \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n        \"investment_debate_state\": {},\n        \"risk_debate_state\": {},\n        \"investment_plan\": \"\",\n        \"trader_investment_plan\": \"\",\n        \"publication_result\": result,\n    }\n\n\ndef _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"A real ``TradingAgentsGraph`` with isolated paths and no model calls.\"\"\"\n    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg\n    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n\n    class _UnusedModel:\n        def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):\n            return self\n\n        def invoke(self, *a, **k):\n            raise AssertionError(\"a sink test must not call the model\")\n\n    class _FakeClient:\n        def get_llm(self):\n            return _UnusedModel()\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"create_tier_client\", lambda *a, **k: _FakeClient())\n    monkeypatch.setattr(tg, \"resolve_instrument_identity\", lambda t: {\n        \"company_name\": \"Apple Inc.\", \"sector\": \"Technology\",\n        \"industry\": \"Consumer Electronics\", \"exchange\": \"NASDAQ\", \"quote_type\": \"EQUITY\",\n    })\n    config = dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG)\n    config.update({\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n        \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n        \"memory_log_path\": str(tmp_path / \"memory.md\"),\n        \"checkpoint_enabled\": False,\n    })\n    return tg.TradingAgentsGraph(selected_analysts=(\"market\",), debug=False, config=config)\n\n\ndef _files(root):\n    from pathlib import Path\n\n    root = Path(root)\n    if not root.exists():\n        return []\n    return sorted(p.relative_to(root) for p in root.rglob(\"*\") if p.is_file())\n\n\ndef _text(root, files, suffixes):\n    return \"\\n\".join(\n        (root / p).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        for p in files if p.suffix in suffixes\n    )\n\n\n# --- sink 1: the Python result -------------------------------------------------\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_python_result_is_the_gate_record():\n    \"\"\"APPROVED exposes the rating; BLOCKED exposes none and no body text.\"\"\"\n    approved = _approved_result()\n    assert approved.publication_status == APPROVED\n    assert approved.rating == BUY\n\n    blocked = _blocked_result()\n    assert blocked.publication_status == BLOCKED\n    assert blocked.rating is None\n    assert MARKER not in repr(blocked)\n\n\n# --- sink 2: the saved report tree --------------------------------------------\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_approved_report_publishes_rating_and_body(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n    save_path = tmp_path / \"reports\"\n\n    graph.save_reports(_run_state(_approved_result()), TICKER, save_path=save_path)\n\n    files = _files(save_path)\n    markdown = _text(save_path, files, (\".md\",))\n    html = _text(save_path, files, (\".html\",))\n    assert files, \"an approved run must write the report tree\"\n    assert f\"**Rating**: {BUY}\" in markdown\n    assert MARKER in markdown\n    assert MARKER in html\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_blocked_report_writes_no_official_surface(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"A real BLOCKED result never reaches a formal report or the decision file.\"\"\"\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n    save_path = tmp_path / \"reports\"\n\n    graph.save_reports(_run_state(_blocked_result()), TICKER, save_path=save_path)\n\n    files = _files(save_path)\n    markdown = _text(save_path, files, (\".md\",))\n    html = _text(save_path, files, (\".html\",))\n    assert not ({\"5_portfolio/decision.md\"} & {str(p) for p in files})\n    assert f\"**Rating**: {BUY}\" not in markdown\n    assert MARKER not in markdown\n    assert MARKER not in html\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\[REDACTED_EMAIL](\"without_result\", [True, False], ids=[\"missing-result\", \"legacy-flat-approval\"])\ndef test_ungated_or_legacy_approved_state_is_refused_by_typed_error(\n        monkeypatch, tmp_path, without_result):\n    \"\"\"§6 A-11 / note §2.3: only the typed gate error counts as a refusal.\"\"\"\n    _owner()\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n    state = {\n        \"run_id\": RUN_ID,\n        \"course_run\": _run(),\n        \"company_of_interest\": TICKER,\n        \"trade_date\": AS_OF_DATE,\n        \"market_report\": \"AAPL closed at 348.245 USD.\",\n        \"sentiment_report\": \"\",\n        \"news_report\": \"\",\n        \"fundamentals_report\": \"\",\n        # What the legacy writer used to publish straight from.\n        \"final_rating\": BUY,\n        \"final_trade_decision\": CANDIDATE_BODY,\n    }\n    if not without_result:\n        # A forged flat status with no real gate record.\n        state[\"publication_status\"] = APPROVED\n    save_path = tmp_path / \"reports\"\n\n    try:\n        with pytest.raises(gate.PublicationRequiredError):\n            graph.save_reports(state, TICKER, save_path=save_path)\n    except gate.PublicationRequiredError:\n        pass\n    except BaseException as exc:  # any other failure is not the expected refusal\n        pytest.fail(\n            f\"expected publication_gate.PublicationRequiredError, got {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\",\n            pytrace=False,\n        )\n\n    files = _files(save_path)\n    markdown = _text(save_path, files, (\".md\",))\n    assert not ({\"5_portfolio/decision.md\"} & {str(p) for p in files})\n    assert f\"**Rating**: {BUY}\" not in markdown\n    assert MARKER not in markdown\n\n\n# --- sink 3: decision memory --------------------------------------------------\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_blocked_result_is_not_written_to_decision_memory(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n    state = _run_state(_blocked_result())\n\n    graph.record_decision(TICKER, AS_OF_DATE, state)\n\n    assert graph.memory_log.load_entries() == []\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_approved_result_is_written_to_decision_memory(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n    state = _run_state(_approved_result())\n\n    graph.record_decision(TICKER, AS_OF_DATE, state)\n\n    entries = graph.memory_log.load_entries()\n    assert entries, \"an approved decision must reach decision memory\"\n\n\n# --- sink 4: CLI display ------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _cli_sink(monkeypatch, tmp_path, result):\n    \"\"\"Drive the real CLI entry with a fake graph carrying ``result``; return its text.\"\"\"\n    from rich.console import Console\n\n    import cli.display as display\n    import cli.run as cli_run\n    from cli.models import AnalystType\n\n    state = _run_state(result)\n\n    class _Graph:\n        def publish(self, final_state):\n            return final_state[\"publication_result\"].publication_status\n\n        def create_run_state(self, *a, **k):\n            return {\"messages\": []}\n\n        def record_decision(self, *a, **k):\n            pass\n\n        def get_graph_args(self, callbacks=None):\n            return {}\n\n        def begin_checkpoint(self, *a, **k):\n            return None\n\n        def checkpoint_input(self, s):\n            return s\n\n        def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, *a, **k):\n            pass\n\n        def end_checkpoint(self):\n            pass\n\n        def stream_run(self, *a, **k):\n            yield [], dict(state)\n\n    fake = _Graph()\n    fake.graph = fake\n    fake.propagator = fake\n\n    class _NullLive:\n        def __init__(self, *a, **k):\n            pass\n\n        def __enter__(self):\n            return self\n\n        def __exit__(self, *a):\n            return False\n\n        def update(self, *a, **k):\n            pass\n\n    record = Console(record=True, width=200, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(display, \"console\", record)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"console\", record)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"TradingAgentsGraph\", lambda *a, **k: fake)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"Live\", _NullLive)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run.sys, \"stdin\", type(\"S\", (), {\"isatty\": lambda s: True})())\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"get_user_selections\", lambda flags=None: {\n        \"ticker\": TICKER, \"analysis_date\": AS_OF_DATE,\n        \"analysts\": [AnalystType.MARKET], \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n    })\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"_build_run_config\", lambda s, c: {\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"c\"),\n                 "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/dataflows/date_window.py, lines 1-176\n1: \"\"\"Point-in-time rules shared by every dated path: data is served as of the run's date.\n2: \n3: - ``as_of`` / ``as_of_window`` clamp a date or window the model asks for to the\n4:   trade date, so no tool reaches a vendor with a later one, and always hand it\n5:   over as ``YYYY-MM-DD``: vendors compare dates as text.\n6: - ``in_window`` trims dated items (news, StockTwits, Reddit) to the analysis\n7:   window: timestamps normalized to UTC, the upper bound exclusive at midnight\n8:   after ``end``, and an undated item kept only when the window reaches the\n9:   present, since a backtest cannot prove it is not from the future (#1126, #1220).\n10: - ``coverage_gap`` reports a window a feed cannot reach as unavailable, not empty.\n11: - ``withhold_live_profile`` withholds present-day snapshots from historical runs.\n12: \"\"\"\n13: \n14: from __future__ import annotations\n15: \n16: from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, timedelta\n17: \n18: \n19: def to_utc(dt: datetime) -> datetime:\n20:     \"\"\"Normalize a datetime to UTC-aware; a naive value is assumed to be UTC.\"\"\"\n21:     return dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC) if dt.tzinfo is None else dt.astimezone(UTC)\n22: \n23: \n24: def in_window(pub_dt: datetime | None, start_dt: datetime, end_dt: datetime) -> bool:\n25:     \"\"\"Whether an item belongs in the half-open window ``[start, end + 1 day)``.\n26: \n27:     ``pub_dt`` None means undated: kept only when the window reaches the present.\n28:     \"\"\"\n29:     end = to_utc(end_dt)\n30:     if pub_dt is not None:\n31:         return to_utc(start_dt) <= to_utc(pub_dt) < end + timedelta(days=1)\n32:     return end >= datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1)\n33: \n34: \n35: def get_current_date() -> str:\n36:     \"\"\"Today's date, YYYY-MM-DD.\"\"\"\n37:     return date.today().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n38: \n39: \n40: def is_historical(run_date) -> bool:\n41:     \"\"\"Whether a run is dated before today, so live-only data would come from after it.\"\"\"\n42:     return bool(run_date) and str(run_date) < get_current_date()\n43: \n44: \n45: def coverage_gap(\n46:     dates, start_date: str, end_date: str, source: str, subject: str\n47: ) -> str | None:\n48:     \"\"\"Placeholder for a window a feed did not fully observe, else None.\n49: \n50:     Yahoo news and the Reddit and StockTwits feeds return their latest items\n51:     whatever window is asked for, so \"none found\" over a window they never\n52:     observed would claim an absence nobody saw. A window is observed when\n53:     coverage reaches its first day and it ends by today; an empty result is then\n54:     a real absence and this returns None.\n55: \n56:     ``dates`` are the returned items' timestamps, plus the lookback start for a\n57:     feed with a fixed lookback. The oldest one bounds coverage only for a feed\n58:     returned newest-first and unbroken in time; a merged or relevance-ranked\n59:     result passes no dates, leaving only the present as the bound.\n60:     \"\"\"\n61:     now = datetime.now(UTC)\n62:     oldest = min((to_utc(d) for d in dates if d is not None), default=now)\n63:     if datetime.strptime(end_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date() > now.date():\n64:         reason = \"the window extends past today\"\n65:     elif oldest.date() > datetime.strptime(start_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date():\n66:         reason = \"it only serves recent items\"\n67:     else:\n68:         return None\n69:     return f\"<{source} unavailable for {start_date}..{end_date}: {reason}, so this is not an absence of {subject}>\"\n70: \n71: \n72: def _parse(date: str | None) -> datetime | None:\n73:     try:\n74:         return datetime.strptime(date, \"%Y-%m-%d\")\n75:     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n76:         return None\n77: \n78: \n79: def as_of(requested: str | None, trade_date: str) -> str | None:\n80:     \"\"\"The date a tool serves: the model's date, but never later than the run's.\n81: \n82:     A model can omit the date or pass today's instead of the analysis date, which\n83:     would walk past every point-in-time guard behind the tool. A date is served in\n84:     its canonical form: \"2026-7-3\" compares as later than \"2026-07-23\". An empty\n85:     ``trade_date`` (a direct call outside a graph run) passes the request through.\n86:     \"\"\"\n87:     parsed = _parse(requested)\n88:     if not trade_date:\n89:         return requested if parsed is None else f\"{parsed:%Y-%m-%d}\"\n90:     return f\"{parsed:%Y-%m-%d}\" if parsed is not None and parsed <= _parse(trade_date) else trade_date\n91: \n92: \n93: def as_of_window(start_date: str, end_date: str, trade_date: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n94:     \"\"\"``[start, end]`` with its end clamped to the run date.\n95: \n96:     A window wholly after the run date keeps its length and moves back to end there.\n97:     An unreadable end reads as the run date, but no window can be guessed from an\n98:     unreadable start or from a start after the end, so those raise ValueError for\n99:     the caller to send back (#1476).\n100:     \"\"\"\n101:     start, old_end = _parse(start_date), _parse(end_date)\n102:     if start is None:\n103:         raise ValueError(f\"start_date {start_date!r} is not a date; give it as YYYY-MM-DD\")\n104:     if old_end is not None and start > old_end:\n105:         raise ValueError(f\"start_date {start_date} is after end_date {end_date}; give the earlier date first\")\n106:     end = as_of(end_date, trade_date)\n107:     end_dt = _parse(end)\n108:     if end_dt is None or end_dt == old_end or start <= end_dt:\n109:         return f\"{start:%Y-%m-%d}\", end\n110:     span = (old_end - start) if old_end is not None and old_end >= start else timedelta(0)\n111:     return f\"{end_dt - span:%Y-%m-%d}\", end\n112: \n113: \n114: def withhold_live_profile(as_of_date: str | None, label: str) -> str | None:\n115:     \"\"\"Notice to serve instead of a live-only company profile, or None to serve it.\n116: \n117:     Vendor \"company overview\" endpoints (yfinance ``Ticker.info``, Alpha Vantage\n118:     ``OVERVIEW``) carry no historical vintage — not even name, sector and\n119:     industry, which move when a company renames or is reclassified — so serving\n120:     one into a run dated in the past leaks post-decision information (#1300).\n121:     Every fundamentals vendor withholds on this rule, so switching between them\n122:     cannot reintroduce the leak.\n123:     \"\"\"\n124:     if not is_historical(as_of_date):\n125:         return None\n126:     return (\n127:         f\"# Company Fundamentals for {label}\\n\"\n128:         f\"# Point-in-time as of: {as_of_date}\\n\\n\"\n129:         f\"Profile fundamentals are withheld for this date. This vendor serves \"\n130:         f\"only present-day values with no historical vintage: market \"\n131:         f\"cap, valuation multiples, the 52-week range and TTM income move with \"\n132:         f\"today's quote, and even the name, sector and industry reflect today \"\n133:         f\"rather than {as_of_date} (companies rename and get reclassified). \"\n134:         f\"Serving them would put post-decision information into a {as_of_date} \"\n135:         f\"analysis. Statements filed by {as_of_date} are served as filed where \"\n136:         f\"the filing date is known (SEC EDGAR, for US filers).\"\n137:     )\n138: \n139: \n140: def withhold_undisclosed_trades(as_of_date: str | None, label: str) -> str | None:\n141:     \"\"\"Notice to serve instead of insider trades with no filing date, or None to serve them.\n142: \n143:     A vendor that dates an insider trade by when it happened (Yahoo, Alpha\n144:     Vantage) cannot say when it became public: its Form 4 is filed up to two\n145:     business days later. A past run is told so rather than served trades that\n146:     may not yet have been disclosed.\n147:     \"\"\"\n148:     if not is_historical(as_of_date):\n149:         return None\n150:     return (\n151:         f\"# Insider Transactions for {label}\\n\"\n152:         f\"# Point-in-time as of: {as_of_date}\\n\\n\"\n153:         f\"Insider transactions are withheld for this date. This vendor dates a trade \"\n154:         f\"by when it happened and reports no filing date, so it cannot show which \"\n155:         f\"trades were public on {as_of_date}.\"\n156:     )\n157: \n158: \n159: def withhold_undated_statements(as_of_date: str | None, label: str, title: str) -> str | None:\n160:     \"\"\"Notice to serve instead of a statement with no filing date, or None to serve it.\n161: \n162:     A vendor that dates a statement by the period it covers (Yahoo, Alpha\n163:     Vantage) cannot say when its figures became public: a company files weeks\n164:     after the period ends, so a run dated in that gap would read figures that\n165:     were not yet known. A past run is told so; SEC EDGAR, which dates every\n166:     filing, serves US filers as filed.\n167:     \"\"\"\n168:     if not is_historical(as_of_date):\n169:         return None\n170:     return (\n171:         f\"# {title} for {label}\\n\"\n172:         f\"# Point-in-time as of: {as_of_date}\\n\\n\"\n173:         f\"{title} data is withheld for this date. This vendor dates a statement by \"\n174:         f\"the period it covers and reports no filing date, so it cannot show which \"\n175:         f\"figures were public on {as_of_date}. SEC EDGAR serves US filers as filed.\"\n176:     )"

            "input": {
              "content": "\"\"\"FR-01 R8-B — market snapshot collection: window, retained material, wrap_up.\n\nBaseline: ``712617e25a380197e38d6ee5cc4dcc7ab393cf61``; contracts C0/C1 v1.0.\nApproved plan: R8-B §4, supplementary note §3 (W-A, ``source_ref``, ``content_ref``,\n``effective_as_of``) and the newly readable §5.5 sources:\n\n- ``tradingagents/agents/tools.py`` — ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` is a\n  ``@tool``; its model-facing args are ``curr_date`` and ``look_back_days`` while\n  ``symbol`` and ``trade_date`` are injected from graph state. Vendor failures come\n  back as text placeholders (``vendor_unavailable`` / ``no_data_available``), never\n  as exceptions.\n- ``tradingagents/agents/analysts/market_analyst.py`` — the market analyst offers\n  ``get_stock_data``, ``get_indicators`` and ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` and\n  calls ``take_turn`` once per graph step; ``wrap_up`` re-invokes it after the\n  tool-round limit.\n- ``tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py`` — the verified snapshot\n  renders a \"### Recent verified closes\" ``| Date | Close |`` table whose rows are\n  ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))`` and whose dates are ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\n- ``tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ohlcv.py`` — ``load_ohlcv`` reads\n  ``{data_cache_dir}/{safe_symbol}-YFin-data.csv`` first and only downloads when the\n  cache is missing or stale, so a cache file written today is the fixed frame.\n- ``tradingagents/dataflows/date_window.py`` — ``as_of(curr_date, trade_date)``\n  clamps the model's date to the run's date.\n\nDesign of this file:\n\n* The **real collection chain** runs: the real ``@tool`` closure, the real\n  ``build_verified_market_snapshot`` over a fixed OHLCV frame, the real snapshot\n  ``as_of`` clamp. Only the vendor download is replaced by that cache file, and\n  only the collector is the object under test.\n* Window ``W-A`` (note §3.2) is verified against the rows the retained Markdown\n  actually shows: first and last row date, ISO format, end <= ``effective_as_of``,\n  row count <= ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))``.\n* ``content_ref`` must resolve back to retained material under the retention root\n  (``{results_dir}/{safe_ticker}/{trade_date}/evidence/{run_id}/``).\n* ``wrap_up``: after the tool round, the analyst is asked to write its report; the\n  snapshot tool is still offered but the model answers without calling it.\n* Negative cases: vendor error/no-data placeholders, report-only runs (no tool\n  call), unreadable retained material, and a foreign run's evidence.\n\nBLOCKED dependences, recorded here rather than hidden:\n\n* ``evidence_collection.py`` (the collector the plan allocates to FR-01) does not\n  exist at this baseline. Every test that needs it is ``@pytest.mark.blocked`` and\n  calls ``pytest.skip`` with a reason naming the missing symbol, so a baseline run\n  reports them as **skipped, not passed**; they must execute after implementation.\n* Nothing in the approved plan states the collector's callable name or its return\n  type, and no source defines it yet. This file therefore drives it through one\n  small adapter, :func:`_collect`, which is the single place to update when the\n  implementation fixes the entry point. Every assertion below the adapter is\n  contract text (R8-B / C0 / C1) and does not depend on the adapter's shape.\n* ``tradingagents/dataflows/symbols.py`` (``safe_ticker_component`` /\n  ``normalize_symbol``) and ``tradingagents/dataflows/router.py`` (placeholder\n  text) were denied, so the retention-root path and the exact placeholder strings\n  are derived from the call sites that ARE readable, not restated.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport importlib\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pandas as pd\nimport pytest\n\n# --- fixed run identity (C0) --------------------------------------------------\n\nCONTRACT_VERSION = \"1.0\"\nTICKER = \"AAPL\"\nTRADE_DATE = \"2026-11-10\"\nRUN_A = \"run-a-0001\"\nRUN_B = \"run-b-0002\"\nREQUEST_LIMIT = 40\n\nTOOL_NAME = \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\nSNAPSHOT_HEADING = \"### Recent verified closes\"\nRETENTION_SUFFIX = (\"evidence\", RUN_A)\n\n# The fixed OHLCV frame: five consecutive business days ending on the run date.\n# Business-day rows keep the \"Recent verified closes\" window deterministic.\nFIXED_ROWS = (\n    # (date,        open,    high,    low,     close,   volume)\n    (\"2026-11-04\", 341.10, 344.20, 340.05, 344.02, 51_200_000),\n    (\"2026-11-05\", 344.02, 347.80, 343.10, 347.55, 49_800_000),\n    (\"2026-11-06\", 347.55, 350.10, 346.20, 349.90, 52_500_000),\n    (\"2026-11-09\", 349.90, 352.30, 348.80, 351.60, 47_300_000),\n    (\"2026-11-10\", 351.60, 353.40, 347.90, 348.245, 55_100_000),\n)\nLATEST_CLOSE = \"348.245\"\n\n\ndef _fixed_frame() -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"The fixed OHLCV DataFrame in the column layout ``load_ohlcv`` produces.\"\"\"\n    return pd.DataFrame(\n        [\n            {\n                \"Date\": date,\n                \"Open\": open_,\n                \"High\": high,\n                \"Low\": low,\n                \"Close\": close,\n                \"Volume\": volume,\n            }\n            for date, open_, high, low, close, volume in FIXED_ROWS\n        ],\n        columns=[\"Date\", \"Open\", \"High\", \"Low\", \"Close\", \"Volume\"],\n    )\n\n\ndef _run_context(run_id: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"A complete RunContext as R8-B §1 specifies it.\"\"\"\n    return {\n        \"contract_version\": CONTRACT_VERSION,\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"ticker\": TICKER,\n        \"as_of_date\": TRADE_DATE,\n        \"execution_status\": \"COMPLETED\",\n        \"request_limit\": REQUEST_LIMIT,\n    }\n\n\ndef _graph_state(trade_date: str = TRADE_DATE) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The state ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` reads its injected args from.\"\"\"\n    return {\"company_of_interest\": TICKER, \"trade_date\": trade_date}\n\n\n# --- the real snapshot tool ----------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _pin_ohlcv_cache(monkeypatch, tmp_path, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Make the real ``load_ohlcv`` read ``frame`` from a fresh same-day cache.\n\n    ``load_ohlcv`` reads ``{data_cache_dir}/{safe_symbol}-YFin-data.csv`` and only\n    downloads when that file is missing or stale. Writing the fixed frame as a\n    same-day cache therefore pins the vendor input without a network call; a\n    missing file at a fresh path is the signal that a download was attempted.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n\n    config = get_config()\n    cache_dir = Path(config[\"data_cache_dir\"])\n    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # The upstream cache path derives the symbol through symbols.py, which is not\n    # readable here; the tool is invoked with the same ticker, so the one file the\n    # run looks for is the symbol used below.\n    (frame if frame is not None else _fixed_frame()).to_csv(\n        cache_dir / f\"{TICKER}-YFin-data.csv\", index=False, encoding=\"utf-8\"\n    )\n\n    def _no_download(*a, **k):\n        raise AssertionError(\"the fixed fixture must be served from cache, not downloaded\")\n\n    import tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.ohlcv as ohlcv\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(ohlcv.yf, \"Ticker\", _no_download)\n    return cache_dir\n\n\ndef _snapshot_text(curr_date: str = TRADE_DATE, look_back_days: int = 7,\n                   trade_date: str = TRADE_DATE) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Run close)`` rows of the \"Recent verified closes\" table.\"\"\"\n    rows: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n    in_table = False\n    for line in text.splitlines():\n        if line.strip() == SNAPSHOT_HEADING or line.startswith(SNAPSHOT_HEADING):\n            in_table = True\n            continue\n        if in_table:\n            if not line.startswith(\"|\"):\n                break\n            cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip(\"|\").split(\"|\")]\n            if len(cells) != 2 or cells[0] in (\"Date\", \"---\", \"---:\"):\n                continue\n            if set(cells[0]) <= {\"-\", \":\", \" \"}:\n                continue\n            rows.append((cells[0], cells[1]))\n    return rows\n\n\n# --- the collector under test ``tool_call`` is the paired call as the graph stores it (``id``, ``name``,\n    ``args``); ``tool_response`` is the tool's returned text; ``run`` is the\n    RunContext of the *current* run.\n\n               "newString": "def _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Serve the fixed frame in place of the vendor download.\n\n    ``build_verified_market_snapshot`` calls ``load_ohlcv`` (readable at §5.5).\n    Replacing that one call keeps the real snapshot rendering, real ``as_of``\n    clamp and real ``@tool`` closure, while the vendor input is the fixed frame.\n    ``load_ohlcv`` is imported into ``snapshot`` by name, so the module attribute\n    is what the snapshot reads.\n    \"\"\"\n    import tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.snapshot as snapshot\n\n    data = frame if frame is not None else _fixed_frame()\n    calls: list[tuple] = []\n\n    def _load(symbol, as_of_date, fill_gaps=True):\n        calls.append((symbol, as_of_date, fill_gaps))\n        return data.copy()\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(snapshot, \"load_ohlcv\", _load)\n    return calls",
              "oldString": "def _pin_ohlcv_cache(monkeypatch, tmp_path, frame: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Make the real ``load_ohlcv`` read ``frame`` from a fresh same-day cache.\n\n    ``load_ohlcv`` reads ``{data_cache_dir}/{safe_symbol}-YFin-data.csv`` and only\n    downloads when that file is missing or stale. Writing the fixed frame as a\n    same-day cache therefore pins the vendor input without a network call; a\n    missing file at a fresh path is the signal that a download was attempted.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n\n    config = get_config()\n    cache_dir = Path(config[\"data_cache_dir\"])\n    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    # The upstream cache path derives the symbol through symbols.py, which is not\n    # readable here; the tool is invoked with the same ticker, so the one file the\n    # run looks for is the symbol used below.\n    (frame if frame is not None else _fixed_frame()).to_csv(\n        cache_dir / f\"{TICKER}-YFin-data.csv\", index=False, encoding=\"utf-8\"\n    )\n\n    def _no_download(*a, **k):\n        raise AssertionError(\"the fixed fixture must be served from cache, not downloaded\")",

Vendor failures come\n10:   back as text placeholders (``vendor_unavailable`` / ``no_data_available``), never\n11:   as exceptions.\n12: - ``tradingagents/agents/analysts/market_analyst.py`` — the market analyst offers\n13:   ``get_stock_data``, ``get_indicators`` and ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` and\n14:   calls ``take_turn`` once per graph step; ``wrap_up`` re-invokes it after the\n15:   tool-round limit.\n16: - ``tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py`` — the verified snapshot\n17:   renders a \"### Recent verified closes\" ``| Date | Close |`` table whose rows are\n18:   ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))`` and whose dates are ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\n19: - ``tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ohlcv.py`` — ``load_ohlcv`` reads\n20:   ``{data_cache_dir}/{safe_symbol}-YFin-data.csv`` first and only downloads when the\n21:   cache is missing or stale, so a cache file written today is the fixed frame.\n22: - ``tradingagents/dataflows/date_window.py`` — ``as_of(curr_date, trade_date)``\n23:   clamps the model's date to the run's date.\n24: \n25: Design of this file:\n26: \n27: * The **real collection chain** runs: the real ``@tool`` closure, the real\n28:   ``build_verified_market_snapshot`` over a fixed OHLCV frame, the real snapshot\n29:   ``as_of`` clamp. Only the vendor download is replaced by that cache file, and\n30:   only the collector is the object under test.\n31: * Window ``W-A`` (note §3.2) is verified against the rows the retained Markdown\n32:   actually shows: first and last row date, ISO format, end <= ``effective_as_of``,\n33:   row count <= ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))``.\n34: * ``content_ref`` must resolve back to retained material under the retention root\n35:   (``{results_dir}/{safe_ticker}/{trade_date}/evidence/{run_id}/``).\n36: * ``wrap_up``: after the tool round, the analyst is asked to write its report; the\n37:   snapshot tool is still offered but the model answers without calling it.\n38: * Negative cases: vendor error/no-data placeholders, report-only runs (no tool\n39:   call), unreadable retained material, and a foreign run's evidence.\n40: \n41: BLOCKED dependences, recorded here rather than hidden:\n42: \n43: * ``evidence_collection.py`` (the collector the plan allocates to FR-01) does not\n44:   exist at this baseline. sites that ARE readable, not restated.\n56: \"\"\"\n57: \n58: from __future__ import annotations\n59: \n60: import importlib\n61: from pathlib import Path\n62: \n63: import pandas as pd\n64: import               "newString": "def _snapshot_text(curr_date: str = TRADE_DATE, look_back_days: int = 7,\n                   trade_date: str = TRADE_DATE) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Run the real snapshot tool exactly as the market analyst would.\n\n    ``symbol`` and ``trade_date`` are the tool's ``InjectedState`` arguments, so\n    they are model-invisible in ``args`` and must arrive through ``state``. The\n    graph's tool node injects them; a direct ``invoke`` has to be handed the same\n    state or the call fails on a missing ``symbol``.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.agents.tools import get_verified_market_snapshot\n\n    return get_verified_market_snapshot.invoke(\n        {\"curr_date\": curr_date, \"look_back_days\": look_back_days},\n        state=_graph_state(trade_date),\n    )\n\n\n# --- the real tool node and analyst subgraph -----------------------------------\n#\n# Why these helpers exist: this file must run on its own. The project's own\n# entry order is ``tradingagents.graph.trading_graph`` (``cli/run.py`` imports it\n# first), which in turn imports ``tradingagents.agents`` and only then ``setup``\n# and ``propagation``; importing pieces of the analyser before that order is\n# established is what produced the circular import seen when this file ran\n# alone. Every helper below therefore imports ``trading_graph`` **first**, then\n# the fragment it needs, so the module graph is built in production order\n# whether or not another test file has already loaded it.\n\n\ndef _import_graph_entry():\n    \"\"\"Import the project's normal graph entry first, then return its module.\"\"\"\n    import tradingagents.graph.trading_graph as tg  # noqa: F401  (entry order matters)\n\n    return tg\n\n\ndef _tool_node(spec_tools):\n    \"\"\"A real ``ToolNode`` over the given tools, as ``setup._analyst_graph`` builds.\"\"\"\n    from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode\n\n    return ToolNode(list(spec_tools))\n\n\ndef _market_analyst_subgraph(llm, max_tool_rounds: int):\n    \"\"\"The market analyst as a real analyst subgraph, like ``setup._analyst_graph``.\n\n    Mirrors the production wiring without importing the denied\n    ``analyst_execution`` plan: ``agent -> tools -> (agent | wrap_up)``, and\n    ``wrap_up`` re-calls the analyst once with ``WRAP_UP`` appended. Being a\n    compiled LangGraph, its ``ToolNode`` injects ``symbol``/``trade_date`` from\n    the state, so a model tool call runs the real tool end to end.\n    \"\"\"\n    _import_graph_entry()\n    from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph\n    from typing_extensions import TypedDict\n\n    from tradingagents.agents.analysts.market_analyst import TOOLS, create_market_analyst\n    from tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\n    from tradingagents.agents.state import AgentState\n\n    agent = create_market_analyst(llm)\n\n    def rounds(messages) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n\n    def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n        return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n\n    def wrap_up(state):\n        from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage\n\n        return agent({**state, \"messages\": [*state[\"messages\"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})\n\n    def tools_or_done(state) -> str:\n        return \"tools\" if state[\"messages\"][-1].tool_calls else END\n\n    output = TypedDict(\"MarketReport\", {\"market_report\": str})\n    graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n    graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n    graph.add_node(\"tools\", _tool_node(TOOLS))\n    graph.add_node(\"wrap_up\", wrap_up)\n    graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"agent\", tools_or_done, [\"tools\", END])\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"tools\", more_or_wrap_up, [\"agent\", \"wrap_up\"])\n    graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", END)\n    return graph.compile()",

              "newString": "@pytest.mark.unit\ndef test_real_snapshot_renders_recent_closes_table(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"The real ``@tool`` over the fixed OHLCV frame yields the frozen table.\"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n\n    with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n        _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n        text = _snapshot_text(look_back_days=7)\n\n    rows = _recent_rows(text)\n    assert rows == [(date, close) for date, _o, _h, _l, close, _v in FIXED_ROWS], rows\n    assert LATEST_CLOSE in text\n    assert \"## Verified market data snapshot for AAPL\" in text\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_tool_node_injects_symbol_and_trade_date_from_state(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"The real ``ToolNode`` injects ``symbol``/``trade_date``; the model passes neither.\n\n    This is the path the analyst subgraph uses: the model's ``tool_calls`` carry\n    only ``curr_date`` and ``look_back_days``, and the node fills the injected\n    arguments from the run state. A direct ``invoke`` without that state is what\n    failed before.\n    \"\"\"\n    _import_graph_entry()\n    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n\n    from tradingagents.agents.analysts.market_analyst import TOOLS\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n\n    call = {\"name\": TOOL_NAME, \"args\": _paired_call()[\"args\"], \"id\": \"call-node\"}\n    with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n        calls = _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n        out = _tool_node(TOOLS).invoke({\n            **_graph_state(),\n            \"messages\": [AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[call])],\n        })\n\n    tool_messages = [m for m in out[\"messages\"] if getattr(m, \"tool_call_id\", None) == \"call-node\"]\n    assert len(tool_messages) == 1, f\"the node ran {len(tool_messages)} tools for one call\"\n    text = tool_messages[0].content\n    assert SNAPSHOT_HEADING in text, f\"the node did not return a snapshot: {text!r}\"\n    assert _recent_rows(text)[-1] == (TRADE_DATE, LATEST_CLOSE)\n    # The injected symbol reached the vendor call, not the model's args.\n    assert [c[0] for c in calls] == [TICKER], calls\n    assert [c[1] for c in calls] == [TRADE_DATE], calls",

              "newString": "# --- wrap_up -------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _wheel_model(report: str):\n    \"\"\"A fake model that calls the snapshot tool, then answers with nothing until wrap-up.\n\n    ``bind_tools`` returns a *different* object, so the caller can tell the\n    tool-bound turn from the wrap-up turn: ``take_turn`` binds tools only while\n    tool rounds remain and calls the plain model once ``WRAP_UP`` was appended.\n    \"\"\"\n    _import_graph_entry()\n    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n\n    class _Bound:\n        def __init__(self, owner):\n            self.owner = owner\n\n        def invoke(self, messages):\n            self.owner.bound_calls += 1\n            n = self.owner.bound_calls\n            return AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[{\n                \"name\": TOOL_NAME,\n                \"args\": _paired_call(call_id=f\"call-{n}\")[\"args\"],\n                \"id\": f\"call-{n}\",\n            }])\n\n    class _Model:\n        def __init__(self):\n            self.bound_calls = 0\n            self.plain_calls = 0\n            self.seen_tool_results: list[str] = []\n\n        def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):\n            return _Bound(self)\n\n        def invoke(self, messages):\n            self.plain_calls += 1\n            for message in messages:\n                text = getattr(message, \"content\", \"\")\n                if isinstance(text, str) and SNAPSHOT_HEADING in text:\n                    self.seen_tool_results.append(text)\n            return AIMessage(content=report)\n\n    return _Model()\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_wrap_up_subgraph_calls_the_real_tool_then_writes_the_report(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"R8-B §6 A-10: the analyst subgraph runs real tool rounds, then wraps up.\n\n    The model calls the snapshot tool every round until ``max_tool_rounds`` is\n    spent; the subgraph's real ``ToolNode`` injects ``symbol``/``trade_date``, so\n    each round renders the fixed frame. After the limit the wrap-up turn offers\n    no tools, and the report is produced from the tool results above.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n\n    max_tool_rounds = 2\n    report = f\"AAPL closed at {LATEST_CLOSE} USD on {TRADE_DATE}.\"\n\n    with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n        calls = _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n        model = _wheel_model(report)\n        subgraph = _market_analyst_subgraph(model, max_tool_rounds)\n        out = subgraph.invoke({\n            **_graph_state(),\n            \"messages\": [(\"human\", TICKER)],\n        })\n\n    # Every tool round ran, each against the fixed frame.\n    assert model.bound_calls == max_tool_rounds, (\n        f\"expected {max_tool_rounds} tool-bound turns, got {model.bound_calls}\"\n    )\n    assert len(calls) == max_tool_rounds, f\"tools executed: {calls}\"\n    assert {c[0] for c in calls} == {TICKER}\n    assert {c[1] for c in calls} == {TRADE_DATE}\n\n    # The limit was reached, so the last turn was the wrap-up and produced the report.\n    assert model.plain_calls == 1, \"the wrap-up turn must be the only unbound call\"\n    assert out[\"market_report\"] == report\n    assert model.seen_tool_results, \"the wrap-up turn did not see the tool results\"\n    assert _recent_rows(model.seen_tool_results[-1])[-1] == (TRADE_DATE, LATEST_CLOSE)",

No material is retained for a response that carried no snapshot (the\n650:     # placeholder text itself is returned by the real tool over the failing frame).\n651:     retained = _retained_files(tmp_path / \"results\")\n652:     assert not retained, f\"a placeholder retained market material: {retained}\"\n653: \n654: \n655: @pytest.mark.unit\n656: def test_no_market_data_placeholder_creates_no_record(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n657:     \"\"\"A \"no data\" placeholder is also absent evidence, not a positive snapshot.\"\"\"\n658:     _require_collector()\n659:     import tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.snapshot as snapshot\n660: \n661:     from tradingagents.dataflows.errors import NoMarketDataError\n662: \n663:     def _empty(symbol, as_of_date, fill_gaps=True):\n664:         raise NoMarketDataError(symbol, None, \"no price rows\")\n665: \n666:     monkeypatch.setattr(snapshot, \"load_ohlcv\", _empty)\n667:     placeholder = _snapshot_text(look_back_days=7)\n668: \n669:     result = _collect(\n670:         _paired_call(\"call-empty\"), placeholder, _graph_state(),\n671:         _run_context(RUN_A), tmp_path / \"results\",\n672:     )\n673:     assert _records(result) == [], f\"a no-data placeholder must not become evidence: {placeholder!r}\"\n674: \n675: \n676: @pytest.mark.unit\n677: def test_report_only_run_has_no_snapshot_evidence(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n678:     \"\"\"A run whose analyst only wrote a report must not gain a snapshot record.\n679: \n680:     No ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` call is paired in this run's messages, so\n681:     there is nothing for the collector to bind a record to.\n682:     \"\"\"\n683:     _require_collector()\n684:     report = \"AAPL trended up; I did not check the verified snapshot.\"\n685:     state = {**_graph_state(), \"market_report\": report, \"messages\": []}\n686:     result = _collect({}, \"\", state, _run_context(RUN_A), tmp_path / \"results\")\n687:     assert _records(result) == []\n688: \n689: \n690: # Approved plan: R8-B (§1–§3) plus the supplementary note (§2.3).\n6: \n7: Skipped is not passed\n8: ---------------------\n9: \n10: The v1 owner symbols (``evaluate_publication``, ``PublicationRequiredError``) do\n11: not exist at this baseline. Every case below goes through ``_gate()`` /\n12: ``_owner()``, which calls ``pytest.skip`` with a reason naming the missing\n13: symbol. A baseline run therefore reports them as **skipped**. The\n    live view is replaced by a null context, the console records text, and the\n    graph object the CLI built is kept so the caller can read the gated state.\n    \"\"\"\n    from rich.console import Console\n\n    import cli.display as display\n    import cli.run as cli_run\n    from cli.models import AnalystType\n\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path, models)\n    graph.quick_thinking_llm = models\n    graph.deep_thinking_llm = models\n    graph.graph_setup.quick_thinking_llm = models\n    graph.graph_setup.deep_thinking_llm = models\n    graph.reflector = _NoopReflector()\n\n    # The state the CLI streamed and the gate judged, captured as the CLI goes.\n    runs: list[dict] = []\n    publish = graph.publish\n\n    def _capturing_publish(final_state):\n        result = publish(final_state)\n        runs.append(final_state)\n        return result\n\n    graph.publish = _capturing_publish\n\n    class _NullLive:\n        def __init__(self, *a, **k):\n            pass\n\n        def __enter__(self):\n            return self\n\n        def __exit__(self, *a):\n            return False\n\n        def update(self, *a, **k):\n            pass\n\n    record = Console(record=True, width=200, force_terminal=False, color_system=None)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(display, \"console\", record)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"console\", record)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"TradingAgentsGraph\", lambda *a, **k: graph)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"Live\", _NullLive)\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run.sys, \"stdin\", type(\"S\", (), {\"isatty\": lambda s: True})())\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"get_user_selections\", lambda flags=None: {\n        \"ticker\": TICKER, \"analysis_date\": AS_OF_DATE,\n        \"analysts\": [AnalystType.MARKET], \"asset_type\": \"stock\",\n    })\n    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_run, \"_build_run_config\", lambda s, c: {\n        \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n        \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n        \"memory_log_path\": str(tmp_path / \"memory.md\"),\n        \"checkpoint_enabled\": False,\n    })\n\n    cli_run.run_analysis(flags={\"save\": False, \"show\": True})\n\n    #                 "type": "text",
                "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/agents/rating.py, lines 1-80\n1: \"\"\"Shared 5-tier rating vocabulary and a deterministic heuristic parser.\n2: \n3: The same five-tier scale (Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell) is used by:\n4: - The Research Manager (investment plan recommendation)\n5: - The Portfolio Manager (final position decision; its free-text fallback is read here)\n6: - The memory log (rating tag stored alongside each decision entry)\n7: \n8: Centralising it here avoids drift between those call sites.\n9: \n10: ``extract_rating`` returns ``None`` when no rating can be found, and every\n11: caller turns that into ``REVIEW`` rather than a tradeable position: a decision\n12: nobody can read is not a Hold, and a Hold recorded in its place is quoted back to\n13: the next run as a call that was never made (#1170).\n14: \"\"\"\n15: \n16: from __future__ import annotations\n17: \n18: import re\n19: import unicodedata\n20: \n21: # Canonical, ordered 5-tier scale (most bullish to most bearish).\n22: RATINGS_5_TIER: tuple[str, ...] = (\n23:     \"Buy\", \"Overweight\", \"Hold\", \"Underweight\", \"Sell\",\n24: )\n25: \n26: # Signal emitted when the model's decision has no recognizable rating. It is not\n27: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than\n28: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum\n29: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.\n30: RATING_REVIEW = \"REVIEW\"\n31: \n32: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}\n33: \n34: # Matches \"Rating: X\" / \"rating - X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n35: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. \"rating\"\n36: # must start a word, so \"Operating margin: Sell-side\" is not a label.\n37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<![a-z])rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n38:                               re.IGNORECASE)\n39: \n40: # The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to\n41: # open with (\"- **Rating**: X\", \"**Final Rating**: X\", \"## Our rating - a naive value is assumed to be UTC.\"\"\"\n21:     return dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC) if dt.tzinfo is None else dt.astimezone(UTC)\n22: \n23: \n24: def in_window(pub_dt: datetime | None, start_dt: datetime, end_dt: datetime) -> bool:\n25:     \"\"\"Whether an item belongs in the half-open window ``[start, end + 1 day)``.\n26: \n27:     ``pub_dt`` None means undated: kept only when the window reaches the present.\n28:     \"\"\"\n29:     end = to_utc(end_dt)\n30:     if pub_dt is not None:\n31:         return to_utc(start_dt) <= to_utc(pub_dt) < end + timedelta(days=1)\n32:     return end >= datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1)\n33: \n34: \n35: def get_current_date() -> str:\n36:     \"\"\"Today's date, YYYY-MM-DD.\"\"\"\n37:     return date.today().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n38: \n39: \n40: def is_historical(run_date) -> bool:\n41:     \"\"\"Whether a run is dated before today, so live-only data would come from after it.\"\"\"\n42:     return bool(run_date) and str(run_date) < get_current_date()\n43: \n44: \n45: def coverage_gap(\n46:     dates, start_date: str, end_date: str, source: str, subject: str\n47: ) -> str | None:\n48:     \"\"\"Placeholder for a window a feed did not fully observe, else None.\n49: \n50:     Yahoo news and the Reddit and StockTwits feeds return their latest items\n51:     whatever window is asked for, so \"none found\" over a window they never\n52:     observed would claim an absence nobody saw. A window is observed when\n53:     coverage reaches its first day and it ends by today; an empty result is then\n54:     a real absence and this returns None.\n55: \n56:     ``dates`` are the returned items' timestamps, plus the lookback start for a\n57:     feed with a fixed lookback. The oldest one bounds coverage only for a feed\n58:     returned newest-first and unbroken in time; a merged or relevance-ranked\n59:     result passes no dates, leaving only the present as the bound.\n60:     \"\"\"\n61:     now = datetime.now(UTC)\n62:     oldest = min((to_utc(d) for d in dates if d is not None), default=now)\n63:     if datetime.strptime(end_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date() > now.date():\n64:         reason = \"the window extends past today\"\n65:     elif oldest.date() > datetime.strptime(start_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date():\n66:         reason = \"it only serves recent items\"\n67:     else:\n68:         return None\n69:     return f\"<{source} unavailable for {start_date}..{end_date}: {reason}, so this is not an absence of {subject}>\"\n70: \n71: \n72: def _parse(date: str | None) -> datetime | None:\n73:     try:\n74:         return datetime.strptime(date, \"%Y-%m-%d\")\n75:     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n76:         return None\n77: \n78: \n79: def as_of(requested: str | None, trade_date: str) -> str | None:\n80:     \"\"\"The date a tool serves: the model's date, but never later than the run's.\n81: \n82:     A model can omit the date or pass today's instead of the analysis date, which\n83:     would walk past every point-in-time guard behind the tool. A date is served in\n84:     its canonical form: \"2026-7-3\" compares as later than \"2026-07-23\". An empty\n85:     ``trade_date`` (a direct call outside a graph run) passes the request through.\n86:     \"\"\"\n87:     parsed = _parse(requested)\n88:     if not trade_date:\n89:         return requested if parsed is None else f\"{parsed:%Y-%m-%d}\"\n90:     return f\"{parsed:%Y-%m-%d}\" if parsed is not None and parsed <= _parse(trade_date) else trade_date\n91: \n92: \n93: def as_of_window(start_date: str, end_date: str, trade_date: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n94:     \"\"\"``[start, end]`` with its end clamped to the run date.\n95: \n96:     A window wholly after the run date keeps its length and moves back to end there.\n97:     An unreadable end reads as the run date, but no window can be guessed from an\n98:     unreadable start or from a start after the end, so those raise ValueError for\n99:     the caller to send back (#1476).\n100:     \"\"\"\n101:     start, old_end = _parse(start_date), _parse(end_date)\n102:     if start is None:\n103:         raise ValueError(f\"start_date {start_date!r} is not a date; give it as YYYY-MM-DD\")\n104:     if old_end is not None and start > old_end:\n105:         raise ValueError(f\"start_date {start_date} is after end_date {end_date}; give the earlier date first\")\n106:     end = as_of(end_date, trade_date)\n107:     end_dt = _parse(end)\n108:     if end_dt is None or end_dt == old_end or start <= end_dt:\n109:         return f\"{start:%Y-%m-%d}\", end\n110:     span = (old_end - start) if old_end is not None and old_end >= start else timedelta(0)\n111:     return f\"{end_dt - span:%Y-%m-%d}\", end\n112: \n113: \n114: def withhold_live_profile(as_of_date: str | None, label: str) -> str | None:\n115:     \"\"\"Notice to serve instead of a live-only company profile, or None to serve it.\n116: \n117:     Vendor \"company overview\" endpoints (yfinance ``Ticker.info``, Alpha Vantage\n118:     ``OVERVIEW``) carry no historical vintage — not even name, sector and\n119:     industry, which move when a company renames or is reclassified — so serving\n120:     one into a run dated in the past leaks post-decision information (#1300).\n121:     Every fundamentals vendor withholds on this rule, so switching between them\n122:     cannot reintroduce the leak.\n123:     \"\"\"\n124:     if not is_historical(as_of_date):\n125:         return None\n126:     return (\n127:         f\"# Company Fundamentals for {label}\\n\"\n128:         f\"# Point-in-time as of: {as_of_date}\\n\\n\"\n129:         f\"Profile fundamentals are withheld for this date. This vendor serves \"\n130:         f\"only present-day values with no historical vintage: market \"\n131:         f\"cap, valuation multiples, the 52-week range and TTM income move with \"\n132:         f\"today's quote, and even the name, sector and industry reflect today \"\n133:         f\"rather than {as_of_date} (companies rename and get reclassified). \"\n134:         f\"Serving them would put post-decision information into a {as_of_date} \"\n135:         f\"analysis. Statements filed by {as_of_date} are served as filed where \"\n136:         f\"the filing date is known (SEC EDGAR, for US filers).\"\n137:     )\n138: \n139: \n140: def withhold_undisclosed_trades(as_of_date: str | None, label: str) -> str | None:\n141:     \"\"\"Notice to serve instead of insider trades with no filing date, or None to serve them.\n142: \n143:     A vendor that dates an insider trade by when it happened (Yahoo, Alpha\n144:     Vantage) cannot say when it became public: its Form 4 is filed up to two\n145:     business days later. A past run is told so rather than served trades that\n146:     may not yet have been disclosed.\n147:     \"\"\"\n148:     if not is_historical(as_of_date):\n149:         return None\n150:     return (\n151:         f\"# Insider Transactions for {label}\\n\"\n152:         f\"# Point-in-time as of: {as_of_date}\\n\\n\"\n153:         f\"Insider transactions are withheld for this date. This vendor dates a trade \"\n154:         f\"by when it happened and reports no filing date, so it cannot show which \"\n155:         f\"trades were public on {as_of_date}.\"\n156:     )\n157: \n158: \n159: def withhold_undated_statements(as_of_date: str | None, label: str, title: str) -> str | None:\n160:     \"\"\"Notice to serve instead of a statement with no filing date, or None to serve it.\n161: \n162:     A vendor that dates a statement by the period it covers (Yahoo, Alpha\n163:     Vantage) cannot say when its figures became public: a company files weeks\n164:     after the period ends, so a run dated in that gap would read figures that\n165:     were not yet known. A past run is told so; SEC EDGAR, which dates every\n166:     filing, serves US filers as filed.\n167:     \"\"\"\n168:     if not is_historical(as_of_date):\n169:         return None\n170:     return (\n171:         f\"# {title} for {label}\\n\"\n172:         f\"# Point-in-time as of: {as_of_date}\\n\\n\"\n173:         f\"{title} data is withheld for this date. This vendor dates a statement by \"\n174:         f\"the period it covers and reports no filing date, so it cannot show which \"\n175:         f\"figures were public on {as_of_date}. SEC EDGAR serves US filers as filed.\"\n176:     )"

Every case below goes through ``_gate()`` /\n12: ``_owner()``, which calls ``pytest.skip`` with a reason naming the missing\n13: symbol. A baseline run therefore reports them as **skipped**. A skip is **not**\n14: B acceptance evidence: each case is a post-implementation obligation that must\n15: execute and pass once the implementation lands. Only\n39:   the two model tiers are scripted (:class:`_ScriptedModel`, a deterministic\n40:   fake that answers from the prompt it is given and returns real ``pydantic``\n41:   schema instances for the structured calls); the analyst, the graph's\n42:   ``Index Evidence`` step, the debate, the researchers' evidence validation,\n43:   the gate and every sink are production code, ``checkpoint_enabled`` is off,\n44:   and no vendor is reached.\n45: * The APPROVED runs cite the evidence id the Bull is actually shown in the run's\n46:   evidence menu. The BLOCKED runs use the *same* graph and scripts and differ in\n47:   one thing only: the Portfolio Manager's candidate cites no argument.             "status": "completed",
            "input": {
              "newString": "def _wheel_model(report: str):\n    \"\"\"A fake model whose two branches ``take_turn`` can pipe its prompt into.\n\n    ``take_turn`` does ``(prompt | llm.bind_tools(tools)).invoke(messages)`` on a\n    tool turn and ``(prompt | llm).invoke(_as_text(messages))`` on the wrap-up\n    turn, so both branches receive a ``PromptValue`` from the pipe, not a list.\n    Each branch is therefore a real ``Runnable``: the bound one is a\n    ``RunnableLambda`` that emits the snapshot ``tool_calls``, and the plain one a\n    ``RunnableLambda`` that produces the report. Both convert the prompt to a\n    message list before inspecting it.\n\n    The bound branch also recognises the wrap-up history: ``take_turn`` only\n    skips binding when the last human message is ``WRAP_UP``, but a wiring that\n    bound tools anyway must still end, so a bound turn holding ``WRAP_UP`` answers\n    with the report instead of calling the tool again. That is what leaves the run\n    with two tool results and one closing report.\n    \"\"\"\n    _import_graph_entry()\n    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage\n    from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda\n\n    from tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\n\n    def _as_messages(prompt) -> list:\n        \"\"\"The prompt as a message list, whichever form the caller passed.\"\"\"\n        to_messages = getattr(prompt, \"to_messages\", None)\n        return to_messages() if callable(to_messages) else list(prompt)\n\n    def _is_wrap_up(messages) -> bool:\n        return (\n            bool(messages)\n            and isinstance(messages[-1], HumanMessage)\n            and messages[-1].content == WRAP_UP\n        )\n\n    class _Model:\n        def __init__(self):\n            self.bound_calls = 0\n            self.plain_calls = 0\n            self.turns: list[dict] = []\n            self.seen_tool_results: list[str] = []\n            self.wrap_up_seen: list[str] = []\n\n        def _snapshots(self, messages) -> list[str]:\n            return [\n                text for text in (getattr(m, \"content\", \"\") for m in messages)\n                if isinstance(text, str) and SNAPSHOT_HEADING in text\n            ]\n\n        def _tool_turn(self, prompt):\n            self.bound_calls += 1\n            messages = _as_messages(prompt)\n            if _is_wrap_up(messages):\n                # Bound but told the rounds are spent: answer, don't call again.\n                self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": True, \"tools_bound\": True})\n                self.wrap_up_seen = self._snapshots(messages)\n                self.seen_tool_results.extend(self.wrap_up_seen)\n                return AIMessage(content=report)\n            n = self.bound_calls\n            self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": False, \"tools_bound\": True})\n            return AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[{\n                \"name\": TOOL_NAME,\n                \"args\": _paired_call(call_id=f\"call-{n}\")[\"args\"],\n                \"id\": f\"call-{n}\",\n            }])\n\n        def _plain_turn(self, prompt):\n            self.plain_calls += 1\n            messages = _as_messages(prompt)\n            wrapped = _is_wrap_up(messages)\n            self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": wrapped, \"tools_bound\": False})\n            if wrapped:\n                self.wrap_up_seen = self._snapshots(messages)\n                self.seen_tool_results.extend(self.wrap_up_seen)\n            return AIMessage(content=report)\n\n        def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):\n            return RunnableLambda(self._tool_turn)\n\n        def invoke(self, prompt):\n            return self._plain_turn(prompt)\n\n    return _Model()",

      "text": "FR-01 / INV-01 的 R8-B 和送审补充说明已通过审核。\n实施基线：712617e25a380197e38d6ee5cc4dcc7ab393cf61。\n沿用 C0/C1 v1.0。现在开始获批的 B 实现。\n\n最新改前实测：\n- 市场快照文件收集 14 个用例，7 passed, 7 skipped。\n  生产子图两轮快照工具调用和 wrap_up 已通过。\n- 离线全量排除 integration：36 passed, 2 failed, 42 skipped。\n- 两个失败均按预期复现：运行 B 借用运行 A 的索引仍获 APPROVED；\n  未过闸门直接 save_reports() 会写出含 Buy 和候选正文的正式报告。\n\n按获批文件范围实施：\n1. 接入市场快照采集和留存，按 W-A 建立本次运行的证据。\n2. 接通共享 RunContext 和 argument_index，按 C0/C1 v1.0 校验\n   执行状态、评级、证据和论点的运行归属。\n3. 让 CLI、Python 返回、正式报告和决策记忆使用同一个发布结果。\n   未经过闸门或只有旧 APPROVED 字段时拒绝保存正式报告。\n   真实 BLOCKED 保留诊断报告，报告不含正式评级、候选正文或 decision.md。\n4. 只在获批范围内迁移测试夹具。保留 A 两个反例的行为断言和通过对照。\n   B 接口实现后，原来跳过的验收用例应实际执行。\n\n如果缺少必要的读取或编辑权限，报告确切路径和受影响的步骤，\n继续完成可以独立实施的部分。完成后列出改动、待验证项和复跑命令，\n停下来等我运行。 ",

                "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md, lines 1-175\n1: # Shared interface contracts\n2: \n3: Version: 1.0. Status: Proposed. Shared boundaries use JSON-compatible records. Internal dataclasses, TypedDict or Pydantic models may use adapters that preserve these fields and semantics. ADR-001 records the design decision.\n4: \n5: ## Ownership and integration\n6: \n7: | Contract | Authority | Producers and consumers |\n8: | --- | --- | --- |\n9: | C0 run identity and outcome | Run coordinator | All five owner modules, CLI, Python, report and memory |\n10: | C1 evidence and publication | FR-01 publication gate | Analyst evidence, accepted arguments, candidate, all official sinks |\n11: | C2 verified metrics | FR-02 metric registry | Fundamentals inputs, controlled downstream fields and metric table |\n12: | C3 sentiment coverage | FR-03 coverage component | Existing source adapters, analyst, state, report and downstream agents |\n13: | C4 dispatch budget | NFR-01 request-budget component | Both model tiers and every in-scope transport send |\n14: | C5 prepared context | NFR-02 context component | Analyst closure and neutral risk debater, then C4 |\n15: \n16: Shared-file integration owner: EverForests. Feature owners submit narrow patches for state, schema, graph/client and reporting adapters. Task plans identify exact paths. The integrator preserves approved contracts across patches; shared files must not be independently replaced by feature branches.\n17: \n18: ## C0 — identity, state and errors\n19: \n20: Every authoritative record carries `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and `as_of_date`. Evidence and metric IDs are only resolvable inside that run. Never retrieve a matching-looking ID from a previous run. A restarted run gets a new ID. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.\n21: \n22: Keep three concepts separate:\n23: \n24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.\n25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.\n26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.\n27: \n28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.\n29: \n30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication\n31: \n32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.\n33: \n34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.\n35: \n36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.\n37: \n38: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.\n39: \n40: ## C2 — verified metrics\n41: \n42: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.\n43: \n44: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.\n45: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.\n46: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.\n47: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.\n48: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.\n49: \n50: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.\n51: \n52: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.\n53: \n54: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score\n55: \n56: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.\n57: \n58: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.\n59: \n60: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.\n61: \n62: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. Never claim these statuses prove that no real-world messages/news exist.\n63: \n64: | Valid logical sources | coverage_status | Sentiment output |\n65: | --- | --- | --- |\n66: | 0/3 | NO_DATA | overall_band UNKNOWN; overall_score null |\n67: | 1/3 or 2/3 | PARTIAL_DATA | Coverage remains explicit; any measured score uses valid evidence only |\n68: | 3/3 | AVAILABLE | Coverage available; score still requires a valid assessment |\n69: \n70: Coverage is authoritative data state; the model cannot increase it. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. Count actual outgoing model attempts, not nodes, tool invocations, callbacks or tokens. Historical settlement is excluded. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation.
