Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.\n83: \n84: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context\n85: \n86: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. Use the ChatMessage representation below and freeze byte fixtures before implementation. Do not measure before template expansion or change representation after measuring. Tool schemas and other separately bound fields are excluded from this message metric and must be recorded/bounded separately; this is not a cap on the whole HTTP body.\n89: \n90: Required blocks: role/task identity; standing safety/publication rules; ticker/date/run identity; current required evidence/verified metrics/source coverage; and the active tool-call/result exchange. Text-wrapped tools retain name, arguments and corresponding result. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. Lists have deterministic order; ID-indexed registries are mappings, not unordered output prose.\n104: \n105: | Record | Required shared fields beyond identity | Owner |\n106: | --- | --- | --- |\n107: | RunContext | contract_version, execution_status, request_limit (positive integer) | Existing graph/run entry; integration by coordinator |\n108: | EvidenceRecord | evidence_id, source_kind, vendor, source_ref, content_ref, window_start, window_end | FR-01 collection/index adapter |\n109: | AcceptedArgument | argument_id, claim (nonempty text), evidence_ids (nonempty list) | FR-01 validates against run-local evidence; Centralizing the mapping here means every yfinance\n19: entry point resolves symbols the same way, and new instruments are added by\n20: appending a table row rather than editing call sites.\n21: \"\"\"\n22: \n23: from __future__ import annotations\n24: \n25: import logging\n26: import re\n27: \n28: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n29: \n30: \n31: # ISO-4217 codes common enough to appear in retail forex pairs. A bare\n32: # six-letter symbol whose halves are BOTH in this set is treated as a spot\n33: # forex pair and given Yahoo's ``=X`` suffix.\n34: _FOREX_CURRENCIES = frozenset(\n35:     {\n36:         \"USD\", \"EUR\", \"GBP\", \"JPY\", \"CHF\", \"CAD\", \"AUD\", \"NZD\",\n37:         \"CNY\", \"CNH\", \"HKD\", \"SGD\", \"SEK\", \"NOK\", \"DKK\", \"PLN\",\n38:         \"MXN\", \"ZAR\", \"TRY\", \"INR\", \"KRW\", \"BRL\", \"RUB\", \"THB\",\n39:     }\n40: )\n41: \n42: # Crypto bases that brokers quote against USD without a separator.\n43: _CRYPTO_BASES = frozenset(\n44:     {\"BTC\", \"ETH\", \"SOL\", \"XRP\", \"ADA\", \"DOGE\", \"LTC\", \"BCH\", \"DOT\", \"AVAX\", \"LINK\"}\n45: )\n46: \n47: # Explicit aliases for instruments whose broker symbol does not map to a\n48: # Yahoo symbol by rule. Metals/energy resolve to their front-month future;\n49: # index CFD names resolve to the underlying Yahoo index symbol. Extend by\n50: # adding rows — no call site changes required.\n51: _ALIASES = {\n52:     # Precious metals (spot names -> COMEX/NYMEX futures)\n53:     \"XAUUSD\": \"GC=F\", \"XAU\": \"GC=F\", \"GOLD\": \"GC=F\",\n54:     \"XAGUSD\": \"SI=F\", \"XAG\": \"SI=F\", \"SILVER\": \"SI=F\",\n55:     \"XPTUSD\": \"PL=F\", \"XPDUSD\": \"PA=F\",\n56:     # Energy\n57:     \"WTICOUSD\": \"CL=F\", \"USOIL\": \"CL=F\", \"WTI\": \"CL=F\",\n58:     \"BCOUSD\": \"BZ=F\", \"UKOIL\": \"BZ=F\", \"BRENT\": \"BZ=F\",\n59:     \"NATGAS\": \"NG=F\", \"XNGUSD\": \"NG=F\",\n60:     \"COPPER\": \"HG=F\", \"XCUUSD\": \"HG=F\",\n61:     # Index CFDs -> Yahoo index symbols\n62:     \"SPX500\": \"^GSPC\", \"US500\": \"^GSPC\", \"SPX\": \"^GSPC\",\n63:     \"NAS100\": \"^NDX\", \"US100\": \"^NDX\", \"USTEC\": \"^NDX\",\n64:     \"US30\": \"^DJI\", \"DJI30\": \"^DJI\", \"WS30\": \"^DJI\",\n65:     \"GER40\": \"^GDAXI\", \"GER30\": \"^GDAXI\", \"DE40\": \"^GDAXI\",\n66:     \"UK100\": \"^FTSE\", \"JP225\": \"^N225\", \"JPN225\": \"^N225\",\n67:     \"FRA40\": \"^FCHI\", \"EU50\": \"^STOXX50E\", \"HK50\": \"^HSI\",\n68: }\n69: \n70: # HKEX codes as Yahoo spells them: the number zero-padded to 4 digits (#957).\n71: _HK_CODE = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{1,5})\\.HK$\")\n72: _SHANGHAI_SH = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{6})\\.SH$\")\n73: \n74: \n75: # Crypto quote currencies that all map to Yahoo's USD pair. Yahoo lists only\n76: # ``<BASE>-USD`` (not the USDT/USDC stablecoin pairs), so a broker symbol quoted\n77: # in any of these resolves to ``-USD`` (#982). Longest first so ``USDT``/``USDC``\n78: # match before the ``USD`` substring.\n79: _CRYPTO_QUOTES = (\"USDT\", \"USDC\", \"USD\")\n80: \n81: \n82: def crypto_base(raw: str) -> str | None:\n83:     \"\"\"Return the crypto base (e.g. ``BTC``) for a known USD/USDT/USDC-quoted\n84:     crypto symbol in any form the pipeline may hold — ``BTC-USD``, ``BTCUSD``,\n85:     ``BTC-USDT`` — or None for non-crypto symbols. Purely syntactic.\n86:     \"\"\"\n87:     if not isinstance(raw, str):\n88:         return None\n89:     compact = raw.strip().upper().rstrip(\"+\").replace(\"-\", \"\")\n90:     for quote in _CRYPTO_QUOTES:\n91:         if compact.endswith(quote):\n92:             base = compact[: -len(quote)]\n93:             return base if base in _CRYPTO_BASES else None\n94:     return None\n95: \n96: \n97: def _normalize_crypto(s: str) -> str | None:\n98:     \"\"\"Return ``<BASE>-USD`` for a known USD/USDT/USDC-quoted crypto, else None.\"\"\"\n99:     base = crypto_base(s)\n100:     return f\"{base}-USD\" if base else None\n101: \n102: \n103: def normalize_symbol(raw: str) -> str:\n104:     \"\"\"Map a user/broker symbol to its canonical Yahoo Finance symbol.\n105: \n106:     Resolution order (first match wins):\n107:       1. Explicit alias table (metals, energy, index CFDs).\n108:       2. Crypto rule: a known crypto base quoted in USD/USDT/USDC (dashed or\n109:          not) -> ``BASE-USD``.\n110:       3. Forex rule: six letters that are two ISO currency codes -> ``PAIR=X``.\n111:       4. HK rule: a numeric ``.HK`` code -> Yahoo's 4-digit padding\n112:          (``09992.HK`` -> ``9992.HK``, ``700.HK`` -> ``0700.HK``).\n113:       5. Shanghai rule: ``600519.SH`` -> ``600519.SS``.\n114:       6. Otherwise the upper-cased symbol is returned unchanged (plain\n115:          equities, ETFs, Yahoo-native symbols like ``GC=F`` or ``^GSPC``).\n116: \n117:     A trailing ``+`` (broker CFD marker, e.g. ``XAUUSD+``) is stripped before\n118:     matching. The function is purely syntactic — it performs no network\n119:     calls — so it is safe to apply on every request.\n120:     \"\"\"\n121:     if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():\n122:         return raw\n123: \n124:     s = raw.strip().upper()\n125:     # Broker CFD/qualifier suffixes Yahoo never uses.\n126:     s = s.rstrip(\"+\")\n127: \n128:     crypto = _normalize_crypto(s)\n129:     if s in _ALIASES:\n130:         canonical = _ALIASES[s]\n131:     elif crypto is not None:\n132:         canonical = crypto\n133:     elif len(s) == 6 and s[:3] in _FOREX_CURRENCIES and s[3:] in _FOREX_CURRENCIES:\n134:         canonical = f\"{s}=X\"\n135:     elif hk := _HK_CODE.match(s):\n136:         canonical = f\"{int(hk.group(1)):04d}.HK\"\n137:     elif sh := _SHANGHAI_SH.match(s):\n138:         canonical = f\"{sh.group(1)}.SS\"\n139:     else:\n140:         canonical = s\n141: \n142:     if canonical != raw.strip().upper():\n143:         logger.info(\"Resolved symbol %r to Yahoo symbol %r\", raw, canonical)\n144:     return canonical\n145: \n146: \n147: # Tickers can contain letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, caret\n148: # (index symbols like ^GSPC), equals (futures like GC=F), and plus\n149: # (forex/CFD symbols like XAUUSD+). None of these enable directory\n150: # traversal, so the value never escapes a containing directory when\n151: # interpolated into a path. Anything else is rejected.\n152: _TICKER_PATH_RE = re.compile(r\"^[A-Za-z0-9._\\-\\^=+]+$\")\n153: \n154: \n155: def safe_ticker_component(value: str, *, max_len: int = 32) -> str:\n156:     \"\"\"Validate ``value`` is safe to interpolate into a filesystem path.\n157: \n158:     Tickers come from user CLI input or from LLM tool calls, both of which\n159:     can be influenced by attacker-controlled content (e.g. prompt injection\n160:     embedded in fetched news). Without validation, a value like\n161:     ``\"../../../etc/foo\"`` flows into ``os.path.join`` / ``Path /`` and\n162:     escapes the configured cache, checkpoint, or results directory.\n163: \n164:     Returns ``value`` unchanged when it matches the allowed pattern; raises\n165:     ``ValueError`` otherwise.\n166:     \"\"\"\n167:     if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n168:         raise ValueError(f\"ticker must be a non-empty string, got {value!r}\")\n169:     if len(value) > max_len:\n170:         raise ValueError(f\"ticker exceeds {max_len} chars: {value!r}\")\n171:     if not _TICKER_PATH_RE.fullmatch(value):\n172:         raise ValueError(\n173:             f\"ticker contains characters not allowed in a filesystem path: {value!r}\"\n174:         )\n175:     # The regex above allows '.', so values like '.', '..', '...' would pass,\n176:     # and as a path component they traverse the parent directory. Reject any\n177:     # value that's only dots.\n178:     if set(value) == {\".\"}:\n179:         raise ValueError(f\"ticker cannot consist solely of dots: {value!r}\")\n180:     return value"

Feature owners submit narrow patches for state, schema, graph/client and reporting adapters. Task plans identify exact paths. The integrator preserves approved contracts across patches; shared files must not be independently replaced by feature branches.\n17: \n18: ## C0 — identity, state and errors\n19: \n20: Every authoritative record carries `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and `as_of_date`. Evidence and metric IDs are only resolvable inside that run. Never retrieve a matching-looking ID from a previous run. A restarted run gets a new ID. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.\n21: \n22: Keep three concepts separate:\n23: \n24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.\n25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.\n26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.\n27: \n28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.\n29: \n30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication\n31: \n32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.\n33: \n34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.\n35: \n36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.\n37: \n38: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.\n39: \n40: ## C2 — verified metrics\n41: \n42: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.\n43: \n44: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.\n45: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.\n46: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.\n47: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.\n48: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.\n49: \n50: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.\n51: \n52: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.\n53: \n54: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score\n55: \n56: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.\n57: \n58: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.\n59: \n60: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). AAPL as-of 2026-11-10 therefore covers 2026-11-03 through 2026-11-10. Freeze the clock for date-dependent fixtures. Historical undated content cannot prove window validity. Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.\n61: \n62: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. A genuine measured Neutral/5.0 remains legal.\n71: \n72: Missing scores never become 0 or 5 and never enter a numerical mean. Structured state, analyst message, downstream prompt and persisted/rendered report must agree. Handle nullable scores without numeric-format errors. Apply the contract to structured **and** free-text fallback; model narrative cannot override authoritative coverage. Keep the existing sentiment_report text as a compatibility view; the new sentiment_assessment record below is authoritative. Both must agree. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation. Validate C5 first so context rejection obtains no reservation.\n81: \n82: No slot => BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no request, no official recommendation. Limit 3 allows exactly 3 attempts; the fourth is refused. Concurrent runs do not share counters. Include application fallback/retry attempts separately. C4 does not promise a monetary or token cap. Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.\n83: \n84: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context\n85: \n86: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. Lists have deterministic order; ID-indexed registries are mappings, not unordered output prose.\n104: \n105: | Record | Required shared fields beyond identity | Owner |\n106: | --- | --- | --- |\n107: | RunContext | contract_version, execution_status, request_limit (positive integer) | Existing graph/run entry; integration by coordinator |\n108: | EvidenceRecord | evidence_id, source_kind, vendor, source_ref, content_ref, window_start, window_end | FR-01 collection/index adapter |\n109: | AcceptedArgument | argument_id, claim (nonempty text), evidence_ids (nonempty list) | FR-01 validates against run-local evidence; Do not silently take abs(capex), invent comparable periods or round source values to make a fixture match. refusal is a typed failure, never a Hold/default rating |\n145: \n146: The sender callable accepts the prepared messages and performs exactly one underlying request with SDK retries disabled. Application fallback/retries call dispatch again. Dispatch failure types are BudgetExhausted, ContextTooLarge and ProviderFailure (defined in the responsible owner module); the graph entry maps them to C0 terminal state. Provider failures after an ambiguous attempt remain charged. Snapshot separates charged attempts, known actual sends and unknown-delivery attempts; a connection attempt is not claimed to be a billed model response.\n147: \n148: Publication evaluation first respects C0 terminal failure/incomplete execution (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or RUN_NOT_COMPLETE); then rejects an invalid rating; then rejects insufficient references. APPROVED has an allowed rating, nonempty accepted argument/evidence references and no rejection reasons. BLOCKED always has rating=null. An incomplete workflow cannot publish an earlier candidate.\n149: \n150: ## V1 graph handoff and compatibility\n151: \n152: Add the following keys to the existing AgentState through narrow integration edits: course_run (RunContext), evidence_index, argument_index, verified_metrics, sentiment_assessment and publication_result. These are separate state keys; do not have parallel nodes overwrite an entire common nested dictionary. Existing nodes own their existing report strings. New owner records are not reconstructed from those strings. That is what leaves the run\n768:     with two tool results and one closing report.\n769:     \"\"\"\n770:     _import_graph_entry()\n771:     from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage\n772:     from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda\n773: \n774:     from tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\n775: \n776:     def _as_messages(prompt) -> list:\n777:         \"\"\"The prompt as a message list, whichever form the caller passed.\"\"\"\n778:         to_messages = getattr(prompt, \"to_messages\", None)\n779:         return to_messages() if callable(to_messages) else list(prompt)\n780: \n781:     def _is_wrap_up(messages) -> bool:\n782:         return (\n783:             bool(messages)\n784:             and isinstance(messages[-1], HumanMessage)\n785:             and messages[-1].content == WRAP_UP\n786:         )\n787: \n788:     class _Model:\n789:         def __init__(self):\n790:             self.bound_calls = 0\n791:             self.plain_calls = 0\n792:             self.turns: list[dict] = []\n793:             self.wrap_up_seen: list[str] = []\n794: \n795:         def _snapshots(self, messages) -> list[str]:\n796:             return [\n797:                 text for text in (getattr(m, \"content\", \"\") for m in messages)\n798:                 if isinstance(text, str) and SNAPSHOT_HEADING in text\n799:             ]\n800: \n801:         def _tool_turn(self, prompt):\n802:             self.bound_calls += 1\n803:             messages = _as_messages(prompt)\n804:             if _is_wrap_up(messages):\n805:                 # Bound but told the rounds are spent: answer, don't call again.\n806:                 self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": True, \"tools_bound\": True})\n807:                 self.wrap_up_seen = self._snapshots(messages)\n808:                 return AIMessage(content=report)\n809:             n = self.bound_calls\n810:             self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": False, \"tools_bound\": True})\n811:             return AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[{\n812:                 \"name\": TOOL_NAME,\n813:                 \"args\": _paired_call(call_id=f\"call-{n}\")[\"args\"],\n814:                 \"id\": f\"call-{n}\",\n815:             }])\n816: \n817:         def _plain_turn(self, prompt):\n818:             self.plain_calls += 1\n819:             messages = _as_messages(prompt)\n820:             wrapped = _is_wrap_up(messages)\n821:             self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": wrapped, \"tools_bound\": False})\n822:             if wrapped:\n823:                 self.wrap_up_seen = self._snapshots(messages)\n824:             return AIMessage(content=report)\n825: \n826:         def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):\n827:             return RunnableLambda(self._tool_turn)\n828: \n829:         def invoke(self, prompt):\n830:             return self._plain_turn(prompt)\n831: \n832:     return _Model()\n833: \n834: \n835: @pytest.mark.unit\n836: def test_wrap_up_subgraph_calls_the_real_tool_then_writes_the_report(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n837:     \"\"\"R8-B §6 A-10: the analyst subgraph runs real tool rounds, then wraps up.\n838: \n839:     The model calls the snapshot tool every round until ``max_tool_rounds`` is\n840:     spent on the **production** analyst subgraph (``setup._analyst_graph``); its\n841:     real ``ToolNode`` injects ``symbol``/``trade_date``, so each round renders the\n842:     fixed frame.               "content": "\"\"\"FR-01 evidence collection: the verified market snapshot collector.\n\nOwner module for R8-B §4. It turns one successful ``get_verified_market_snapshot``\ntool response into at most one v1 ``EvidenceRecord`` whose ``content_ref``\nresolves to material this run actually retained on disk.\n\nContract points this module implements (C1 v1.0):\n\n- An ``EvidenceRecord`` carries ``run_id``, ``ticker`` and ``as_of_date`` copied\n  from the ``RunContext`` (never derived from the ID spelling), plus\n  ``evidence_id``, ``source_kind``, ``vendor``, ``source_ref``, ``content_ref``,\n  ``window_start`` and ``window_end``.\n- Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. A\n  vendor-failure or no-data placeholder, a report-only run with no paired tool\n  call, and material that cannot be read back all collect **no** record.\n- ``content_ref`` is ``evidence://{run_id}/{name}`` and names a file under the\n  retention root ``{results_dir}/{ticker}/{as_of_date}/evidence/{run_id}/``.\n- Window W-A is read from the dates the snapshot actually renders (the\n  \"Recent verified closes\" table), not from the model's requested look-back.\n\nRetention is idempotent. Re-collecting the same response under the same run is\na cache hit: the existing material is re-read and the same record is returned,\nso a resume does not rewrite evidence and a deleted file is never claimed back\n(the read fails, so no record is minted).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom tradingagents.dataflows.symbols import safe_ticker_component\n\nCONTRACT_VERSION = \"1.0\"\nSNAPSHOT_TOOL = \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\nSNAPSHOT_SOURCE_KIND = \"market_snapshot\"\nSNAPSHOT_VENDOR = \"yahoo\"\n\n# The heading the verified snapshot renders above its close table.\n_SNAPSHOT_HEADING = \"### Recent verified closes\"\n\n# A markdown table rule / separator cell (\"---\", \"---:\", \":---:\").\n_RULE_RE = re.compile(r\"^[-:\\s|]+$\")\n_DATE_CELL_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$\")\n\n\ndef _run_field(run: dict, key: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One RunContext string field, required for a v1 record.\"\"\"\n    value = run.get(key)\n    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n        raise ValueError(f\"RunContext is missing a required {key!r} field: {run!r}\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef _paired_call(tool_call, state: dict) -> dict | None:\n    \"\"\"The paired call for the response being collected, or ``None``.\n\n    ``tool_call`` is what the graph stored in ``tool_calls[*]``; the run state\n    also keeps the same pair in ``tool_calls`` and agent-facing ``messages``. A\n    report-only run pairs nothing, and the model may invoke other tools, so the\n    call is only accepted when its name is the snapshot tool.\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(tool_call, dict) and tool_call.get(\"name\") == SNAPSHOT_TOOL:\n        return tool_call\n    for call in state.get(\"tool_calls\") or ():\n        if isinstance(call, dict) and call.get(\"name\") == SNAPSHOT_TOOL:\n SNAPSHOT_TOOL:\n                return call\n    return None\n\n\ndef snapshot_window(text: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:\n    \"\"\"The ``(first_date, last_date)`` W-A window of the rendered close Portfolio Manager Decision\", \"5_portfolio\", (\n76:         (\"Portfolio Manager\", \"decision.md\", (\"final_trade_decision\",)),\n77:     )),\n78: )\n79: \n80: \n81: def _report_parts(final_state: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]]]:\n82:     \"\"\"The sections with something to say: (heading, folder, [(agent, file, text)]).\"\"\"\n83:     parts = []\n84:     for heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:\n85:         written = []\n86:         for agent, filename, path in agents:\n87:             value = final_state\n88:             for key in path:\n89:                 value = (value or {}).get(key)\n90:             if value:\n91:                 written.append((agent, filename, value))\n92:         if written:\n93:             parts.append((heading, folder, written))\n94:     return parts\n95: \n96: \n97: def write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,\n98:                       html: bool = True) -> Path:\n99:     \"\"\"Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.\n100: \n101:     ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run\n102:     to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one\n103:     self-contained page of the same report (#1419).\n104:     Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections\n105:     absent from this run and disabled HTML. Other files and directories are kept.\n106:     \"\"\"\n107:     save_path = Path(save_path)\n108:     save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n109:     parts = _report_parts(final_state)\n110:     sections = []\n111:     for heading, folder, written in parts:\n112:         (save_path / folder).mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n113:         for _agent, filename, text in written:\n114:             (save_path / folder / filename).write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n115:         content = \"\\n\\n\".join(f\"### {agent}\\n{text}\" for agent, _filename, text in written)\n116:         sections.append(f\"## {heading}\\n\\n{content}\")\n117: \n118:     (save_path / \"complete_report.md\").write_text(\n119:         _header(ticker, final_state, settings) + \"\\n\\n\".join(sections), encoding=\"utf-8\"\n120:     )\n121:     if html:\n122:         from tradingagents.report_html import render_report\n123: \n124:         (save_path / \"complete_report.html\").write_text(\n125:             render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts), encoding=\"utf-8\"\n126:         )\n127:     else:\n128:         (save_path / \"complete_report.html\").unlink(missing_ok=True)\n129: \n130:     # Reconcile only the filenames owned by this writer; never clear the tree,\n131:     # since callers may keep notes or other artifacts alongside the reports.\n132:     current_files = {\n133:         (folder, filename)\n134:         for _heading, folder, written in parts\n135:         for _agent, filename, _text in written\n136:     }\n137:     for _heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:\n138:         for _agent, filename, _path in agents:\n139:             if (folder, filename) not in current_files:\n140:                 (save_path / folder / filename).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n141:     return save_path / \"complete_report.md\""

              "newString": "        final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n        final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n        final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n    return final_state\n\n\n# --- C1 v1.0: mapping-authoritative evaluation -------------------------------\n#\n# The authoritative indexes are ID -> record mappings: ``argument_index`` keyed by\n# ``argument_id`` and ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The legacy\n# shapes ``index_to_state(...)`` (lists under \"evidence\"/\"arguments\") and\n# ``accepted_arguments`` are a compatibility layer only: an argument that exists\n# solely in that view never resolves a reference.\n\n\ndef _identity(record, run: dict) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:\n    \"\"\"The record's ``(run_id, ticker, as_of_date)`` when they are the run's own.\n\n    A record without identity fields is treated as this run's (legacy in-memory\n    shapes omit them); a record that states identity must state *this* run's.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(record, dict):\n        return None\n    stated = {key: record.get(key) for key in (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"as_of_date\")}\n    for key, value in stated.items():\n        if value is not None and value != run.get(key):\n            return None\n    return (run.get(\"run_id\", \"\"), run.get(\"ticker\", \"\"), run.get(\"as_of_date\", \"\"))\n\n\ndef _evidence_records(evidence_index, run: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    \"\"\"The run's own evidence, keyed by ``evidence_id``.\n\n    Accepts the v1 mapping, the legacy serialized shape and an ``EvidenceIndex``\n    object; every record is identity-checked against the ``RunContext``.\n    \"\"\"\n    if evidence_index is None:\n        return {}\n    run_id = run.get(\"run_id\", \"\")\n    if isinstance(evidence_index, EvidenceIndex):\n        return {\n            eid: {\"evidence_id\": eid, \"source\": rec.source}\n            for eid, rec in evidence_index._evidence.items()\n        }\n    if isinstance(evidence_index, dict):\n        rows = _mapping_rows(evidence_index, \"evidence\", \"id\")\n    else:\n        return {}\n    records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for key, record in rows:\n        if not isinstance(record, dict):\n            continue\n        if _identity(record, run) is None:\n            continue\n        evidence_id = record.get(\"evidence_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n        if not isinstance(evidence_id, str) or not evidence_id:\n            continue\n        if not str(evidence_id).startswith(f\"ev:{run_id}:\"):\n            continue\n        records[evidence_id] = record\n    return records\n\n\ndef _argument_records(argument_index, run: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    \"\"\"The run's accepted arguments, keyed by ``argument_id``.\n\n    Only the authoritative mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which carries\n    the same records) is read. A ``{\"accepted_arguments\": [...]}`` view is *not*\n    unwrapped: the compatibility view is not a release authority.\n    \"\"\"\n    if argument_index is None:\n        return {}\n    run_id = run.get(\"run_id\", \"\")\n    if isinstance(argument_index, EvidenceIndex):\n        return {\n            aid: {\"argument_id\": aid, \"evidence_ids\": list(rec.evidence_ids)}\n            for aid, rec in argument_index._arguments.items()\n        }\n    if isinstance(argument_index, dict):\n        if \"accepted_arguments\" in argument_index and \"arguments\" not in argument_index:\n            return {}\n        rows = _mapping_rows(argument_index, \"arguments\", \"id\")\n    else:\n        return {}\n    records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for key, record in rows:\n        if not isinstance(record, dict):\n            continue\n        if _identity(record, run) is None:\n            continue\n        argument_id = record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n        if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n            continue\n        if f\":{run_id}:\" not in argument_id:\n            continue\n        records[argument_id] = record\n    return records\n\n\ndef _mapping_rows(index: dict, list_key: str, id_key: str):\n    \"\"\"``(key, record)`` pairs of a mapping index or of its legacy serialized form.\n\n    A mapping keyed by ID yields its own items. The legacy shape\n    ``{list_key: [ {...id_key: ...} ]}`` is read from that list. The key a record\n    is found under is a fallback only; the record's own ID field wins.\n    \"\"\"\n    if list_key in index and isinstance(index.get(list_key), list):\n        return [(None, item) for item in index[list_key]]\n    return list(index.items())\n\n\ndef _rating(value) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` when not publishable.\n\n    Only the exact five tiers count. ``REVIEW``, casing variants, surrounding\n    text (\"Buy (small size)\") and null are all invalid: free text is not a call.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(value, str):\n        return None\n    return value if value in _RATING_SET else None\n\n\ndef evaluate_publication(candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run) -> PublicationResult:\n    \"\"\"C1 v1.0: the one deterministic publication result for a run.\n\n    Rows are checked in the approved order, and the first matching row decides:\n\n    1. C0 terminal failure / incomplete execution (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``,\n       ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` keep their own code; anything not ``COMPLETED``,\n       including a missing ``RunContext``, is ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``).\n    2. An invalid rating (``INVALID_RATING``).\n    3. Missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted references\n       (``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``).\n    4. Otherwise APPROVED, with the rating and the validated references.\n\n    References are rechecked here, not taken from the model: a cited argument\n    must exist in this run's ``argument_index``, and each of its evidence ids must\n    resolve in this run's ``evidence_index``. BLOCKED always carries ``rating=None``.\n    \"\"\"\n    run = run if isinstance(run, dict) else {}\n    identity = {\n        \"contract_version\": str(run.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n        \"run_id\": run.get(\"run_id\") or \"\",\n        \"ticker\": run.get(\"ticker\") or \"\",\n        \"as_of_date\": run.get(\"as_of_date\") or \"\",\n    }\n\n    def _blocked(*codes: str) -> PublicationResult:\n        return PublicationResult(\n            **identity, publication_status=BLOCKED, reason_codes=tuple(codes),\n            rating=None, argument_ids=(), evidence_ids=(),\n        )\n\n    # Row 1: C0 execution state.\n    status = run.get(\"execution_status\")\n    if status in _TERMINAL_EXECUTION:\n        return _blocked(status)\n    if status != EXECUTION_COMPLETED:\n        return _blocked(RUN_NOT_COMPLETE)\n\n    # Row 2: the rating must be one of the five tiers.\n    candidate = candidate if isinstance(candidate, dict) else {}\n    rating = _rating(candidate.get(\"rating\"))\n    if rating is None:\n        return _blocked(INVALID_RATING)\n\n    # Row 3: every cited reference must resolve inside this run.\n    arguments = _argument_records(argument_index, run)\n    evidence = _evidence_records(evidence_index, run)\n    cited = [a for a in (candidate.get(\"argument_ids\") or ()) if isinstance(a, str) and a]\n    resolved_arguments: list[str] = []\n    resolved_evidence: list[str] = []\n    chain: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    for argument_id in cited:\n        argument = arguments.get(argument_id)\n        if argument is None:\n            continue\n        evidence_ids = [\n            eid for eid in (argument.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ())\n            if isinstance(eid, str) and eid in evidence\n        ]\n        if not evidence_ids:\n            continue\n        resolved_arguments.append(argument_id)\n        for evidence_id in evidence_ids:\n            if evidence_id not in resolved_evidence:\n                resolved_evidence.append(evidence_id)\n            chain.append((argument_id, evidence_id, str(evidence.get(evidence_id, {}).get(\"source\", \"\"))))\n    if not resolved_arguments or not resolved_evidence:\n        return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n\n    # Row 4: approved, with identity, rating and validated references.\n    return PublicationResult(\n        **identity,\n        publication_status=APPROVED,\n        reason_codes=(),\n        rating=rating,\n        argument_ids=tuple(resolved_arguments),\n        evidence_ids=tuple(resolved_evidence),\n        resolved_chain=tuple(chain),\n    )\n\n\ndef publication_result_from_state(state: dict) -> PublicationResult | None:\n    \"\"\"The run's authoritative ``publication_result``, or ``None`` when it has none.\n\n    A state carrying only the legacy flat ``publication_status`` (or legacy\n    ``publication_chain``) has no publication result: that field is a projection\n    of the gate's verdict, not the verdict, and a caller can set it freely.\n    \"\"\"\n    stored = state.get(\"publication_result\") if isinstance(state, dict) else None\n    if not isinstance(stored, dict):\n        return None\n    if \"publication_status\" not in stored:\n        return None\n    return PublicationResult(\n        contract_version=str(stored.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n        run_id=stored.get(\"run_id\") or \"\",\n        ticker=stored.get(\"ticker\") or \"\",\n        as_of_date=stored.get(\"as_of_date\") or \"\",\n        publication_status=stored.get(\"publication_status\"),\n        reason_codes=tuple(stored.get(\"reason_codes\") or ()),\n        rating=stored.get(\"rating\"),\n        argument_ids=tuple(stored.get(\"argument_ids\") or ()),\n        evidence_ids=tuple(stored.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ()),\n        resolved_chain=tuple(tuple(link) for link in stored.get(\"resolved_chain\") or ()),\n    )\n\n\ndef apply_publication(result: PublicationResult, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Project a v1 ``PublicationResult`` onto the run state every sink reads.\n\n    Writes ``publication_result`` (the authoritative record) plus the legacy\n    projection fields the existing display/report adapters read. On APPROVED the\n    candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision`` and its rating the\n    ``final_rating``. On BLOCKED the state carries no rating, no body, and no\n    candidate fields at all.\n    \"\"\"\n    final_state[\"publication_result\"] = result.as_state()\n    final_state[\"publication_status\"] = result.publication_status\n    final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = result.reason\n    final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = [list(link) for link in result.resolved_chain]\n\n    if result.approved:\n        body = final_state.get(\"candidate_decision\") or final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\") or \"\"\n        final_state[\"final_rating\"] = result.rating\n        final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = body\n    else:\n        final_state[\"final_rating\"] = \"\"\n        final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n    final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n    final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n    final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n    return final_state",

              "newString": "def publication_run(state: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The ``RunContext`` the gate judges a run against (C0).\n\n    The graph state carries ``course_run``; when it is absent (a legacy or\n    hand-built state) the identity is assembled from the state's own ``run_id`` /\n    ``company_of_interest`` / ``trade_date`` so a run still has an identity to be\n    checked against. A state with no identity at all yields ``run_id=\"\"``, and\n    nothing resolves, so such a run cannot publish.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(state, dict):\n        return {}\n    course_run = state.get(\"course_run\")\n    if isinstance(course_run, dict) and course_run.get(\"run_id\"):\n        return dict(course_run)\n    return {\n        \"contract_version\": str((course_run or {}).get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\")\n        if isinstance(course_run, dict) else \"1.0\",\n        \"run_id\": state.get(\"run_id\") or \"\",\n        \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\") or \"\",\n        \"as_of_date\": state.get(\"trade_date\") or \"\",\n        \"execution_status\": (\n            (course_run or {}).get(\"execution_status\") if isinstance(course_run, dict)\n            else None\n        ) or state.get(\"execution_status\") or EXECUTION_COMPLETED,\n        \"request_limit\": (course_run or {}).get(\"request_limit\")\n        if isinstance(course_run, dict) else None,\n    }\n\n\ndef publication_result_from_state(state: dict) -> PublicationResult | None:",
              "oldString": "def publication_result_from_state(state: dict) -> PublicationResult | None:",

Both are read here, so a snapshot record collected\n    as a mapping is visible to the researchers exactly like a report record.\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(value, EvidenceIndex):\n        return value\n    if value is None:\n        return EvidenceIndex(run_id=\"\", evidence={})\n    run_id = value.get(\"run_id\", \"\")\n\n    if isinstance(value.get(\"evidence\"), list):\n        rows = value[\"evidence\"]\n    elif isinstance(value.get(\"evidence\"), dict):\n        rows = list(value[\"evidence\"].values())\n    else:\n        # a naive value is assumed to be UTC.\"\"\"\n21:     return dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC) if dt.tzinfo is None else dt.astimezone(UTC)\n22: \n23: \n24: def in_window(pub_dt: datetime | None, start_dt: datetime, end_dt: datetime) -> bool:\n25:     \"\"\"Whether an item belongs in the half-open window ``[start, end + 1 day)``.\n26: \n27:     ``pub_dt`` None means undated: kept only when the window reaches the present.\n28:     \"\"\"\n29:     end = to_utc(end_dt)\n30:     if pub_dt is not None:\n31:         return to_utc(start_dt) <= to_utc(pub_dt) < end + timedelta(days=1)\n32:     return end >= datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1)\n33: \n34: \n35: def get_current_date() -> str:\n36:     \"\"\"Today's date, YYYY-MM-DD.\"\"\"\n37:     return date.today().strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")\n38: \n39: \n40: def is_historical(run_date) -> bool:\n41:     \"\"\"Whether a run is dated before today, so live-only data would come from after it.\"\"\"\n42:     return bool(run_date) and str(run_date) < get_current_date()\n43: \n44: \n45: def coverage_gap(\n46:     dates, start_date: str, end_date: str, source: str, subject: str\n47: ) -> str | None:\n48:     \"\"\"Placeholder for a window a feed did not fully observe, else None.\n49: \n50:     Yahoo news and the Reddit and StockTwits feeds return their latest items\n51:     whatever window is asked for, so \"none found\" over a window they never\n52:     observed would claim an absence nobody saw. The oldest one bounds coverage only for a feed\n58:     returned newest-first and unbroken in time; a merged or relevance-ranked\n59:     result passes no dates, leaving only the present as the bound.\n60:     \"\"\"\n61:     now = datetime.now(UTC)\n62:     oldest = min((to_utc(d) for d in dates if d is not None), default=now)\n63:     if datetime.strptime(end_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date() > now.date():\n64:         reason = \"the window extends past today\"\n65:     elif oldest.date() > datetime.strptime(start_date, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date():\n66:         reason = \"it only serves recent items\"\n67:     else:\n68:         return None\n69:     return f\"<{source} unavailable for {start_date}..{end_date}: {reason}, so this is not an absence of {subject}>\"\n70: \n71: \n72: def _parse(date: str | None) -> datetime | None:\n73:     try:\n74:         return datetime.strptime(date, \"%Y-%m-%d\")\n75:     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n76:         return None\n77: \n78: \n79: def as_of(requested: str | None, trade_date: str) -> str | None:\n80:     \"\"\"The date a tool serves: the model's date, but never later than the run's.\n81: \n82:     A model can omit the date or pass today's instead of the analysis date, which\n83:     would walk past every point-in-time guard behind the tool.               "newString": "def _analyst_graph(spec, agent, max_tool_rounds: int):\n    \"\"\"One analyst as a graph of its own: the model and its tools, on a private message history.\n\n    It returns its report, so analysts running side by side never write the same\n    key, and its tool calls never reach the other analysts' messages. After\n    ``max_tool_rounds`` rounds of tool calls it is told to write its report, and\n    that turn ends it whatever it answers, so a model that keeps calling tools\n    cannot run the graph into its recursion limit (#1420).\n\n    R8-B §4: a successful verified snapshot this analyst actually called is\n    retained and returned as ``market_evidence`` — the evidence records the Index\n    Evidence step folds into the run's index. The subgraph owns the tool calls and\n    their results, so only this graph can hand them on; a run with no call, or one\n    whose material cannot be retained, returns no receipts.\n    \"\"\"\n    output = TypedDict(\n        f\"{spec.key.capitalize()}Report\", {spec.report_key: str, \"market_evidence\": list}\n    )\n    graph = StateGraph(AgentState, output_schema=output)\n    graph.add_node(\"agent\", agent)\n    graph.add_edge(START, \"agent\")\n    if not spec.tools:\n        graph.add_edge(\"agent\", END)\n        return graph.compile()\n\n    def calls(messages):\n        return [call[\"name\"] for m in messages for call in (getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None) or [])]\n\n    def rounds(messages) -> int:\n        return sum(1 for m in messages if getattr(m, \"tool_calls\", None))\n\n    def more_or_wrap_up(state) -> str:\n        return \"wrap_up\" if rounds(state[\"messages\"]) >= max_tool_rounds else \"agent\"\n\n    def wrap_up(state):\n        repeated = \", \".join(f\"{name} x{n}\" for name, n in Counter(calls(state[\"messages\"])).most_common())\n        logger.warning(\"%s used its %d tool rounds (%s); asking for its report\",\n                       spec.agent_node, max_tool_rounds, repeated)\n        return agent({**state, \"messages\": [*state[\"messages\"], HumanMessage(WRAP_UP)]})\n\n    def collect(state):\n        \"\"\"Hand this analyst's retained snapshot evidence to the parent graph.\"\"\"\n        return {\"market_evidence\": collect_snapshot_evidence(state)}\n\n    graph.add_node(\"tools\", ToolNode(list(spec.tools)))\n    graph.add_node(\"wrap_up\", wrap_up)\n    graph.add_node(\"collect\", collect)\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"agent\", _tools_or_done, [\"tools\", END])\n    graph.add_conditional_edges(\"tools\", more_or_wrap_up, [\"agent\", \"wrap_up\"])\n    graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", END)\n    if spec.key == \"market\":\n        # The closing step of the market analyst: it has seen every tool result,\n        # so it is where the run's verified snapshots are retained.\n        graph.add_edge(\"wrap_up\", \"collect\")\n        graph.add_edge(\"collect\", END)\n    return graph.compile()\n\n\ndef collect_snapshot_evidence(state) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Retain this analyst's verified-snapshot results and return their records.\n\n    Reads the ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` calls and their paired results from\n    the analyst's own ``messages`` — the only place they exist, because the\n    subgraph does not pass its message history to the parent. Every record is\n    bound to this run's ``RunContext``; without one nothing is collected, and a\n    response that is a placeholder or whose material cannot be retained yields no\n    record rather than an unresolvable reference.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection import record_market_snapshot\n\n    run = state.get(\"course_run\")\n    if not isinstance(run, dict) or not run.get(\"run_id\"):\n        return []\n    try:\n        from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n\n        results_dir = get_config().get(\"results_dir\")\n    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — collection is optional, never fatal\n        return []\n    if not results_dir:\n        return []\n\n    by_id = {\n        call.get(\"id\"): call\n        for message in state.get(\"messages\") or ()\n        for call in (getattr(message, \"tool_calls\", None) or ())\n        if isinstance(call, dict) and call.get(\"name\") == \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\n    }\n    records: list[dict] = []\n    for message in state.get(\"messages\") or ():\n        call_id = getattr(message, \"tool_call_id\", None)\n        if call_id not in by_id or getattr(message, \"name\", None) != \"get_verified_market_snapshot\":\n            continue\n        try:\n            collected = record_market_snapshot(\n                tool_call=by_id[call_id], tool_response=getattr(message, \"content\", \"\"),\n                state=state, run=run, results_dir=results_dir,\n            )\n        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a bad response is not evidence, not a crash\n            continue\n        records.extend((collected or {}).get(\"records\") or ())\n    seen: set[str] = set()\n    unique: list[dict] = []\n    for record in records:\n        evidence_id = record.get(\"evidence_id\")\n        if evidence_id in seen:\n            continue\n        seen.add(evidence_id)\n        unique.append(record)\n    return unique",

              "newString": "def _material_resolves(record: dict, run: dict, results_dir) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether the record's referenced material actually exists for this run.\n\n    A record that names retained material (``content_ref``) counts only when that\n    material is re-read successfully from this run's retention root: a reference\n    whose file is expired, deleted or foreign does not resolve. A record with no\n    ``content_ref`` (an analyst report indexed in memory, whose material is the\n    report itself and is present in the run) has nothing on disk to check.\n    \"\"\"\n    content_ref = record.get(\"content_ref\")\n    if content_ref is None:\n        return True\n    if not isinstance(results_dir, (str, Path)) or not str(results_dir):\n        return False\n    from tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection import resolve_content_ref\n\n    try:\n        return resolve_content_ref(content_ref, results_dir, run) is not None\n    except (OSError, ValueError):\n        return False\n\n\ndef _evidence_records(evidence_index, run: dict, results_dir=None) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    \"\"\"The run's own evidence, keyed by ``evidence_id``.\n\n    Accepts the v1 mapping, the legacy serialized shape and an ``EvidenceIndex``\n    object. A record is this run's only when its **full identity** matches the\n    ``RunContext``; the ID's spelling is irrelevant. A record whose referenced\n    material cannot be resolved no longer counts as evidence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if evidence_index is None:\n        return {}\n    if isinstance(evidence_index, EvidenceIndex):\n        return {\n            eid: {\"evidence_id\": eid, \"source\": rec.source}\n            for eid, rec in evidence_index._evidence.items()\n        }\n    if isinstance(evidence_index, dict):\n        rows = _mapping_rows(evidence_index, \"evidence\", \"id\")\n    else:\n        return {}\n    records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for key, record in rows:\n        if not isinstance(record, dict):\n            continue\n        if _identity(record, run) is None:\n            continue\n        evidence_id = record.get(\"evidence_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n        if not isinstance(evidence_id, str) or not evidence_id:\n            continue\n        if not _material_resolves(record, run, results_dir):\n            continue\n        records[evidence_id] = record\n    return records",

              "newString": "def _argument_records(argument_index, run: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:\n    \"\"\"The run's accepted arguments, keyed by ``argument_id``.\n\n    Only the authoritative mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which carries\n    the same records) is read. A ``{\"accepted_arguments\": [...]}`` view is *not*\n    unwrapped: the compatibility view is not a release authority.\n\n    Ownership is the record's own identity, not the ID's spelling: an ID needs no\n    prefix and must not contain the run id. A record that states an identity must\n    state *this* run's; a record with no identity at all is not owned by any run\n    and is not accepted.\n    \"\"\"\n    if argument_index is None:\n        return {}\n    if isinstance(argument_index, EvidenceIndex):\n        return {\n            aid: {\"argument_id\": aid, \"evidence_ids\": list(rec.evidence_ids)}\n            for aid, rec in argument_index._arguments.items()\n        }\n    if isinstance(argument_index, dict):\n        if \"accepted_arguments\" in argument_index and \"arguments\" not in argument_index:\n            return {}\n        rows = _mapping_rows(argument_index, \"arguments\", \"id\")\n    else:\n        return {}\n    records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    for key, record in rows:\n        if not isinstance(record, dict):\n            continue\n        argument_id = record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n        if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n            continue\n        stated = [record.get(key) for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS]\n        if any(record.get(key) is not None for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS):\n            if _identity(record, run) is None:\n                continue\n        elif any(value is None for value in stated):\n            # No stated identity: an in-memory argument of the indexing step, which\n            # only counts when there is a real run to own it.\n            if not run.get(\"run_id\"):\n                continue\n        records[argument_id] = record\n    return records",

              "newString": "def publication_run(state: dict) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The ``RunContext`` the gate judges a run against (C0).\n\n    The graph state carries one complete ``course_run``, created once at the shared\n    run entry. When it is absent the run has no identity to be checked against and\n    no execution state to prove it finished, so ``execution_status`` is left unset\n    and the gate blocks with ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``. Every field is\n    copied from the run itself, never derived from an ID's spelling. The execution\n    state starts at ``COMPLETED``; a terminal C0 failure recorded later on the state\n    outranks it, and ``publish()`` refuses to treat a run without this context as\n    complete.\n\n    ``request_limit`` is the run's positive-integer request budget, defaulting to\n    the approved value of 40. A non-positive or non-integer setting is a\n    configuration error, not something to silently clamp.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n\n    run_id = state.get(\"run_id\") or _new_run_id()\n    limit = state.get(\"request_limit\")\n    if limit is None:\n        limit = DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"request_limit\")\n    if limit is None:\n        limit = DEFAULT_REQUEST_LIMIT\n    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int) or limit <= 0:\n        raise ValueError(f\"request_limit must be a positive integer, got {limit!r}\")\n    return {\n        \"contract_version\": \"1.0\",\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\", \"\"),\n        # The effective cutoff is as_of()'s own result, not the requested date.\n        \"as_of_date\": _effective_as_of(state),\n        \"execution_status\": state.get(\"execution_status\") or \"COMPLETED\",\n        \"request_limit\": limit,\n    }\n\n\ndef _effective_as_of(state) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The run's effective cutoff date: ``as_of()``'s actual result.\n\n    The window checks and the snapshot retention paths use this same date, so a\n    record dated by ``as_of()`` is the record the run's identity names.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import as_of\n\n    return as_of(state.get(\"trade_date\"), state.get(\"trade_date\"))\n\n\ndef _index_evidence_node(state) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"FR-01: build this run's evidence index before the debate starts.\n\n    The run identity is minted here once and stored on the state as the one\n    complete ``course_run``; a resumed run reuses the id already present instead of\n    minting a new one, so ids stay stable across an interruption. Receipts handed up from the analyst subgraphs, deduplicated by evidence_id\n    # and kept only when their identity is this run's.\n    rows = list(evidence_state.get(\"evidence\") or [])\n    seen = {row.get(\"id\") for row in rows}\n    for record in state.get(\"market_evidence\") or ():\n        if not isinstance(record, dict):\n            continue\n        if record.get(\"run_id\") != run_id:\n            continue\n        evidence_id = record.get(\"evidence_id\")\n        if not evidence_id or evidence_id in seen:\n            continue\n        seen.add(evidence_id)\n        rows.append({**record, \"id\": evidence_id})\n    # Parent-level tool results (a non-subgraph caller) are collected here too.\n    for record in _collect_snapshots(state, course_run):\n        evidence_id = record.get(\"evidence_id\")\n        if not evidence_id or evidence_id in seen:\n            continue\n        seen.add(evidence_id)\n        rows.append({**record, \"id\": evidence_id})\n    evidence_state = {**evidence_state, \"evidence\": rows}\n\n    return {\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"course_run\": course_run,\n        \"evidence_index\": evidence_state,\n        \"argument_index\": {},\n        \"accepted_arguments\": [],\n    }\n\n\ndef _collect_snapshots(state, course_run: dict) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Retain verified snapshots whose calls and results are on the parent state.\n\n    The market analyst runs in a graph of its own and hands its receipts up as\n    ``market_evidence`` (see ``collect_snapshot_evidence``); this path serves a\n    caller whose tool messages are already on the run state. Only\n39:   the two model tiers are scripted (:class:`_ScriptedModel`, a deterministic\n40:   fake that answers from the prompt it is given and returns real ``pydantic``\n41:   schema instances for the structured calls); the analyst, the graph's\n42:   ``Index Evidence`` step, the debate, the researchers' evidence validation,\n43:   the gate and every sink are production code, ``checkpoint_enabled`` is off,\n44:   and no vendor is reached.\n45: * The APPROVED runs cite the evidence id the Bull is actually shown in the run's\n46:   evidence menu. The BLOCKED runs use the *same* graph and scripts and differ in\n47:   one thing only: the Portfolio Manager's candidate cites no argument. Vendor failures come\n10:   back as text placeholders (``vendor_unavailable`` / ``no_data_available``), never\n11:   as exceptions.\n12: - ``tradingagents/agents/analysts/market_analyst.py`` — the market analyst offers\n13:   ``get_stock_data``, ``get_indicators`` and ``get_verified_market_snapshot`` and\n14:   calls ``take_turn`` once per graph step; ``wrap_up`` re-invokes it after the\n15:   tool-round limit.\n16: - ``tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/snapshot.py`` — the verified snapshot\n17:   renders a \"### Recent verified closes\" ``| Date | Close |`` table whose rows are\n18:   ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))`` and whose dates are ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\n19: - ``tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/ohlcv.py`` — ``load_ohlcv`` returns a\n20:   ``Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Volume`` frame for one symbol no later than the\n21:   requested date; the snapshot calls it with ``fill_gaps=False``.\n22: - ``tradingagents/dataflows/date_window.py`` — ``as_of(curr_date, trade_date)``\n23:   clamps the model's date to the run's date.\n24: \n25: Design of this file:\n26: \n27: * The **real collection chain** runs: the real ``@tool`` closure, the real\n28:   ``build_verified_market_snapshot`` over a fixed OHLCV frame, the real snapshot\n29:   ``as_of`` clamp. Only the ``load_ohlcv`` call inside ``snapshot`` is replaced by\n30:   that fixed frame, and only the collector is the object under test.\n31: * The tool is driven two ways: a direct ``invoke`` for helper calls that states\n32:   every argument (``symbol`` and ``trade_date`` included, because a bare tool has\n33:   no graph to inject them), and a real ``ToolNode`` inside a compiled graph, which\n34:   injects them the way the analyst subgraph does. The model never sends\n35:   ``symbol``. ``look_back_days`` is typed ``int`` on the tool, so the tests pass\n36:   an int, never a string.\n37: * The snapshot's rows are read from the ``| Date | Close |`` table under its\n38:   heading, skipping the blank line and header block first, and every close is\n39:   normalised to one canonical decimal string, so a row, the latest close, the\n40:   fixture and the window assertions all compare the same representation.\n41: * Window ``W-A`` (note §3.2) is verified against the rows the snapshot actually\n42:   shows: first and last row date, ISO format, end <= the run date, row count\n43:   ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))``.\n44: * ``content_ref`` must resolve back to retained material under the retention root\n45:   (``{results_dir}/{safe_ticker}/{trade_date}/evidence/{run_id}/``).\n46: * ``wrap_up`` is exercised on the **production analyst subgraph**: the case builds\n47:   it with ``tradingagents.graph.setup._analyst_graph`` plus the production analyst\n48:   plan and ``create_market_analyst``. The fake model's two branches are\n49:   ``Runnable``s, so the production prompt can pipe its ``PromptValue`` into\n50:   either; the bound branch emits the snapshot ``tool_calls`` and the unbound one\n51:   produces the report. After ``max_tool_rounds`` the production wrap-up turn runs\n52:   unbound, produces ``market_report`` and passes both tool results to it. If that\n53:   wiring cannot be imported, the case names it and skips rather than substituting\n54:   a copy.\n55: * Negative cases: vendor error/no-data placeholders, report-only runs (no tool\n56:   call), unreadable retained material, and a foreign run's evidence.\n57: * The unreadable-material case begins with the positive control the acceptance\n58:   needs: a usable snapshot **must** mint a record, so an implementation that\n59:   refuses every snapshot fails the case instead of passing it vacuously. Only\n60:   then is the retained material deleted.\n61: \n62: Running this file on its own:\n63: \n64: * Every helper imports ``tradingagents.graph.trading_graph`` **before** the\n65:   agent or graph fragment it needs, and ``_snapshot_text`` does the same before\n66:   importing the tool. That is the project's own entry order (``cli/run.py``\n67:   imports it first, and it imports ``tradingagents.agents`` before\n68:   ``setup``/``propagation``), so the module graph is built in production order\n69:   whether or not another test file has already loaded it. Importing\n70:   ``tradingagents.graph.setup`` or ``tradingagents.agents`` first produced the\n71:   circular import seen when this file ran alone.\n72: \n73: BLOCKED dependences, recorded here rather than hidden:\n74: \n75: * A baseline **skip is not B acceptance**. ``evidence_collection.py`` (the\n76:   collector the plan allocates to FR-01) does not exist at this baseline, so the\n77:   collection cases call ``pytest.skip`` with a reason naming the missing symbol\n78:   and a baseline run reports them as **skipped, not passed**. They are\n79:   post-implementation obligations that must execute.\n80: * The cases that do NOT need the collector (the fixed frame, the direct tool\n81:   call, the real ``ToolNode`` injection inside a compiled graph, the window clamp,\n82:   the date clamp and the wrap-up subgraph) collect and run at the baseline, so the\n83:   real snapshot chain and the analyst subgraph are verified even before\n84:   implementation. Those cases never skip: an import, config or fake-model error in\n85:   them fails the run instead. Nothing is marked ``blocked``: the marker would hide\n86:   those runnable cases.\n87: * Nothing in the approved plan states the collector's callable name or its return\n88:   type, and no source defines it yet. This file therefore drives it through one\n89:   small adapter, :func:`_collect`, the single place to update when the\n90:   implementation fixes the entry point. Every assertion below the adapter is\n91:   contract text (R8-B / C0 / C1) and does not depend on the adapter's shape.\n92: * ``tradingagents/dataflows/symbols.py`` (``normalize_symbol`` /\n93:   ``safe_ticker_component``), ``router.py`` (placeholder text) and ``errors.py``\n94:   were denied, so the vendor input is pinned at ``load_ohlcv`` (readable, §5.5)\n95:   rather than at the cache file whose name needs ``safe_ticker_component``, and\n96:   the expectation is \"no record, no retained material\" rather than the router's\n97:   exact wording. The vendor-failure cases need the error types the tool itself\n98:   catches (``tradingagents.dataflows.errors``), which were denied to the agent;\n99:   each of those cases attempts that import inside its body and, if the import is\n100:   the failing step, reports as a collection/import error rather than a pass.\n101: * Paths still denied to the agent, so not read or cited directly:\n102:   ``tradingagents/dataflows/symbols.py``, ``tradingagents/dataflows/router.py``,\n103:   ``tradingagents/dataflows/errors.py``, ``tradingagents/graph/__init__.py``,\n104:   ``tradingagents/graph/analyst_execution.py``, ``tradingagents/reporting/`` and\n105:   ``tradingagents/memory/{reflection,settlement,store}.py``.\n106:   ``setup.py`` and ``trading_graph.py`` (which this file relies on) are readable.\n107:   If ``setup._analyst_graph`` or ``analyst_execution`` cannot be imported at run\n108:   time, the wrap_up case skips with a reason naming the missing production wiring\n109:   — production wiring verification is then still outstanding.\n110: \"\"\"\n111: \n112: from __future__ import annotations\n113: \n114: import importlib\n115: from pathlib import Path\n116: \n117: import pandas as pd\n118: import pytest\n119: \n120: # --- fixed run identity (C0) --------------------------------------------------\n121: \n122: CONTRACT_VERSION = \"1.0\"\n123: TICKER = \"AAPL\"\n124: TRADE_DATE = \"2026-11-10\"\n125: RUN_A = \"run-a-0001\"\n126: RUN_B = \"run-b-0002\"\n127: REQUEST_LIMIT = 40\n128: \n129: TOOL_NAME = \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\n130: # The heading line the snapshot renders, without its row count; rows are read\n131: # from the ``| Date | Close |`` table under it.\n132: SNAPSHOT_HEADING = \"### Recent verified closes\"\n133: \n134: # The fixed OHLCV frame: five consecutive business days ending on the run date.\n135: # Business-day rows keep the \"Recent verified closes\" window deterministic.\n136: # Closes are written as the canonical decimal strings the snapshot renders, so a\n137: # row, the latest close and this fixture can all be compared as parsed.\n138: FIXED_ROWS = (\n139:     # (date,        open,    high,    low,     close,   volume)\n140:     (\"2026-11-04\", \"341.10\", \"344.20\", \"340.05\", \"344.02\", 51_200_000),\n[Output truncated.               "newString": "def test_accepted_arguments_view_is_not_a_release_authority(results):\n    \"\"\"§3: an ``accepted_arguments`` view alone never resolves a reference.\n\n    The same argument passes when it is in ``argument_index`` and fails when the\n    only copy is the compatibility view handed to the gate as extra state.\n    \"\"\"\n    evaluate = _gate()\n    argument_id = _argument_id(RUN_A)\n    candidate = _candidate(BUY, (argument_id,))\n    evidence_index = _evidence_index(RUN_A)\n\n    authoritative = evaluate(\n        candidate, _argument_index(RUN_A), evidence_index, _run(RUN_A),\n        results_dir=results,\n    )\n    assert authoritative.publication_status == APPROVED, authoritative.reason_codes\n\n    view_only = {\"accepted_arguments\": list(_argument_index(RUN_A).values())}\n    without_index = evaluate(\n        candidate, view_only, evidence_index, _run(RUN_A),\n        results_dir=results,\n    )\n    assert without_index.publication_status == BLOCKED\n    assert INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE in without_index.reason_codes\n\n\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\ndef test_foreign_evidence_index_never_resolves(results):\n    \"\"\"A complete run A index on run B: identity comes from course_run (§1).\n\n    Only the RunContext changes — the candidate, the argument index and the\n    evidence index are byte-identical to the same-run control that APPROVES in\n    ``test_valid_run_approves_with_identity_and_resolved_references``.\n    \"\"\"\n    result = _evaluate(\n        run=_run(RUN_B),\n        argument_ids=(_argument_id(RUN_A),),\n        evidence_index=_evidence_index(RUN_A),\n        argument_index=_argument_index(RUN_A),\n        results_dir=results,\n    )\n    assert result.publication_status == BLOCKED\n    assert INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE in result.reason_codes\n    assert result.rating is None",

\"\"\"\n    _owner()\n    _pin_snapshot(monkeypatch)\n    models = _ScriptedModel(call_snapshot=True, cite_snapshot_only=True)\n    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path, models)\n\n    final_state, signal = _propagate(graph, models, APPROVED)\n\n    assert models.snapshot_calls >= 1, \"the market analyst never called the snapshot tool\"\n    receipts =    if (r.get(\"source_kind\") or \"\") == \"market_snapshot\"]\n    assert snapshot_ids, f\"the snapshot was not indexed: {evidence_rows}\"\n    for record in evidence_rows:\n        if               "newString": "def _run_context(state) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"R8-B §2 / C0: the one complete ``RunContext`` for this run.\n\n    Written once, at the Index Evidence step, from the id minted at the shared run\n    entry and reused verbatim on resume. Every field is copied from the run\n    itself, never derived from an ID's spelling.\n\n    ``execution_status`` starts at ``RUNNING``: the run has not finished yet, and\n    only a normal finish sets ``COMPLETED`` (see ``TradingAgentsGraph.publish``).\n    A terminal C0 failure keeps its own code, and a run still ``RUNNING`` when the\n    gate judges it is ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``.\n\n    ``request_limit`` is the run's positive-integer request budget, defaulting to\n    the approved value of 40. A non-positive or non-integer setting is a\n    configuration error, not something to silently clamp.\n    \"\"\"\n    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n\n    run_id = state.get(\"run_id\") or _new_run_id()\n    limit = state.get(\"request_limit\")\n    if limit is None:\n        limit = DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"request_limit\")\n    if limit is None:\n        limit = DEFAULT_REQUEST_LIMIT\n    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int) or limit <= 0:\n        raise ValueError(f\"request_limit must be a positive integer, got {limit!r}\")\n    return {\n        \"contract_version\": \"1.0\",\n        \"run_id\": run_id,\n        \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\", \"\"),\n        # The effective cutoff is as_of()'s own result, not the requested date.\n        \"as_of_date\": _effective_as_of(state),\n        \"execution_status\": state.get(\"execution_status\") or RUNNING,\n        \"request_limit\": limit,\n    }",

            "input": {
              "newString": "    def complete_run(self, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Mark a run that finished normally as ``COMPLETED`` (C0).\n\n        The only place a run becomes ``COMPLETED``: ``_run_graph`` and the CLI\n        call it after the graph returns normally, right before the gate judges the\n        candidate. A terminal C0 failure already recorded (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`` /\n        ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE``) keeps its own code and is never overwritten, and a\n        state with no ``course_run`` stays without one, so the gate refuses it.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not isinstance(final_state, dict):\n            return final_state\n        current = final_state.get(\"execution_status\")\n        if current in (\"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED\", \"CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE\"):\n            return final_state\n        final_state[\"execution_status\"] = \"COMPLETED\"\n        course_run = final_state.get(\"course_run\")\n        if isinstance(course_run, dict):\n            final_state[\"course_run\"] = {**course_run, \"execution_status\": \"COMPLETED\"}\n        return final_state\n\n    def publish(self, final_state: dict) -> str:\n        \"\"\"FR-01 / INV-01: decide whether this run's candidate may publish.\n\n        Single deterministic gate, called once per run before any sink reads it\n        (CLI display, API return, report save, memory write). At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to\n11:    markdown. Agents on this path\n34: # state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone\n35: # (#1130).\n36: NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (\n37:     \"Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools \"\n38:     \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n39: )\n40: \n41: \n42: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n43:     \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n44: \n45:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n46:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n47:     \"\"\"\n48:     try:\n49:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n50:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n51:         logger.warning(\n52:             \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n53:             \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n54:             agent_name, exc,\n55:         )\n56:         return None\n57: \n58: \n59: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n60:     \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n61: \n62:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n63:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n64:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n65:     \"\"\"\n66:     if structured_llm is None:\n67:         return None\n68:     try:\n69:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n70:         if result is None:\n71:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n72:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n73:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n74:             raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n75:         return result\n76:     except Exception as exc:\n77:         logger.warning(\n78:             \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n79:             agent_name, exc,\n80:         )\n81:         return None\n82: \n83: \n84: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n85:     structured_llm: Any | None,\n86:     plain_llm: Any,\n87:     prompt: Any,\n88:     render: Callable[[T], str],\n89:     agent_name: str,\n90: ) -> str:\n91:     \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n92:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n93:     if result is not None:\n94:         return render(result)\n95:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content"
