run: dict,\n471:              results_dir: Path) -> dict:\n472:     \"\"\"Collect one snapshot response into a v1 EvidenceRecord (or a receipt).\n473: \n474:     ``tool_call`` is the paired call as the graph stores it (``id``, ``name``,\n475:     ``args``); ``tool_response`` is the tool's returned text; ``run`` is the\n476:     RunContext of the *current* run.\n477: \n478:     Fails through to the caller when the collector is missing so the caller's\n479:     ``pytest.skip`` can name the gap; never fabricates a record.\n480:     \"\"\"\n481:     collector = _collector_callable()\n482:     if collector is None:\n483:         raise _CollectorMissing(\"record_market_snapshot\")\n484: \n485:     return collector(\n486:         tool_call=tool_call,\n487:         tool_response=tool_response,\n488:         state=state,\n489:         run=run,\n490:         results_dir=str(results_dir),\n491:     )\n492: \n493: \n494: class _CollectorMissing(Exception):\n495:     \"\"\"Raised when the collector the plan allocates has not been implemented.\"\"\"\n496: \n497: \n498: def _require_collector():\n499:     if _collector_callable() is None:\n500:         pytest.skip(_BLOCKED_REASON.format(\n501:             missing=\"tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection.record_market_snapshot\"))\n502: \n503: \n504: def _paired_call(call_id: str = \"call-1\", curr_date: str = TRADE_DATE,\n505:                  look_back_days: int = 7) -> dict:\n506:     \"\"\"A tool call as ``tool_calls[*]`` carries it: the args the model sent.\"\"\"\n507:     return {\n508:         \"id\": call_id,\n509:         \"type\": \"tool_call\",\n510:         \"name\": TOOL_NAME,\n511:         \"args\": {\"curr_date\": curr_date, \"look_back_days\": look_back_days},\n512:     }\n513: \n514: \n515: def _paired_tool_result(text: str, call: dict) -> dict:\n516:     \"\"\"The tool result as the graph history pairs it with its call (``ToolMessage``).\"\"\"\n517:     return {\"tool_call_id\": call[\"id\"], \"name\": call[\"name\"], \"content\": text}\n518: \n519: \n520: def _paired_state(text: str, call: dict | None = None) -> dict:\n521:     \"\"\"The run state carrying the snapshot call and its response, as the graph keeps them.\n522: \n523:     The collector binds a record to the call it came from, so the run state it is\n524:     given must hold that pair. ``tool_calls`` / ``tool_results`` are the pairing\n525:     surfaced in plain form; the agent-facing ``messages`` hold the same pair as\n526:     ``AIMessage``/``ToolMessage``, so a collector reading either shape finds it.\n527:     A report-only run pairs nothing and passes no pair.\n528:     \"\"\"\n529:     call = call if call is not None else _paired_call()\n530:     return {\n531:         **_graph_state(),\n532:         **_paired_pair(text, call),\n533:     }\n534: \n535: \n536: def _paired_pair(text: str, call: dict) -> dict:\n537:     \"\"\"The paired call and result in both the plain and the message shapes.\"\"\"\n538:     from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, ToolMessage\n539: \n540:     return {\n541:         \"tool_calls\": [call],\n542:         \"tool_results\": [_paired_tool_result(text, call)],\n543:         \"messages\": [\n544:             AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[call]),\n545:             ToolMessage(content=text, name=call[\"name\"], tool_call_id=call[\"id\"]),\n546:         ],\n547:     }\n548: \n549: \n550: def _record_or_receipt(result) -> dict:\n551:     \"\"\"The single evidence-like record the collector returns.\"\"\"\n552:     assert result is not None, \"the collector returned nothing for a usable snapshot\"\n553:     if isinstance(result, dict) and \"record\" in result:\n554:         return result[\"record\"]\n555:     assert isinstance(result, dict), f\"unexpected collector result: {type(result).__name__}\"\n556:     return result\n557: \n558: \n559: def _records(result) -> list[dict]:\n560:     if result is None:\n561:         return []\n562:     if isinstance(result, dict):\n563:         if \"records\" in result:\n564:             return list(result[\"records\"])\n565:         return [result]\n566:     return list(result)\n567: \n568: \n569: # --- positive: the window and the retained material ---------------------------\n570: \n571: \n572: def _run_config(tmp_path) -> dict:\n573:     \"\"\"An config.update({\n578:         \"data_cache_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"cache\"),\n579:         \"results_dir\": str(tmp_path / \"results\"),\n580:     })\n581:     return config\n582: \n583: \n584: @pytest.mark.unit\n585: def test_fixed_frame_matches_the_ohlcv_column_layout():\n586:     \"\"\"The fixture has the columns ``load_ohlcv`` produces, one row per session.\"\"\"\n587:     frame = The node runs inside a compiled graph, because\n616:     that is where the graph runtime supplies the state ``InjectedState`` reads; a\n617:     bare ``ToolNode.invoke`` never reaches the tool.\n618:     \"\"\"\n619:     _import_graph_entry()\n620:     from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage\n621: \n622:     from tradingagents.agents.analysts.market_analyst import TOOLS\n623:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n624: \n625:     call = {\"name\": TOOL_NAME, \"args\": _paired_call()[\"args\"], \"id\": \"call-node\"}\n626:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n627:         calls = _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n628:         out = _tool_graph(TOOLS).invoke({\n629:             **_graph_state(),\n630:             \"messages\": [AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[call])],\n631:         })\n632: \n633:     tool_messages = [m for m in out[\"messages\"] if getattr(m, \"tool_call_id\", None) == \"call-node\"]\n634:     assert len(tool_messages) == 1, f\"the node ran {len(tool_messages)} tools for one call\"\n635:     text = tool_messages[0].content\n636:     assert SNAPSHOT_HEADING in text, f\"the node did not return a snapshot: {text!r}\"\n637:     assert _recent_rows(text)[-1] == (TRADE_DATE, LATEST_CLOSE)\n638:     # The injected symbol reached the vendor call, not the model's args.\n639:     assert [c[0] for c in calls] == [TICKER], calls\n640:     assert [c[1] for c in calls] == [TRADE_DATE], calls\n641: \n642: \n643: @pytest.mark.unit\n644: def test_snapshot_window_is_clamped_to_look_back_days(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n645:     \"\"\"W-A row bound: ``max(1, min(int(look_back_days), 30))``, at least one row.\"\"\"\n646:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n647: \n648:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n649:         _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n650:         two_rows = _recent_rows(_snapshot_text(look_back_days=2))\n651:         capped = _recent_rows(_snapshot_text(look_back_days=99))\n652:         zero_rows = _recent_rows(_snapshot_text(look_back_days=0))\n653: \n654:     assert len(two_rows) == 2\n655:     assert [r[0] for r in two_rows] == [r[0] for r in FIXED_ROWS[-2:]]\n656:     assert len(capped) <= 30\n657:     assert len(capped) == len(FIXED_ROWS)\n658:     assert len(zero_rows) == 1, \"a look-back of 0 must still show one row\"\n659: \n660: \n661: @pytest.mark.unit\n662: def test_collector_creates_one_record_with_window_and_retained_material(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n663:     \"\"\"W-A + §4: one record, window from the shown rows, ``content_ref`` resolvable.\"\"\"\n664:     _require_collector()\n665:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n666: \n667:     results_dir = tmp_path / \"results\"\n668:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n669:         _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n670:         text = _snapshot_text(look_back_days=7)\n671:         result = _collect(\n672:             _paired_call(), text, _paired_state(text), _run_context(RUN_A), results_dir,\n673:         )\n674: \n675:     record = _record_or_receipt(result)\n676:     rows = _recent_rows(text)\n677: \n678:     # Identity is copied from the RunContext, never derived from the ID spelling.\n679:     assert record[\"run_id\"] == RUN_A\n680:     assert record[\"ticker\"] == TICKER\n681:     assert record[\"as_of_date\"] == TRADE_DATE\n682:     assert record[\"contract_version\"] == CONTRACT_VERSION\n683: \n684:     # Window W-A (note §3.2) is computed from the dates the snapshot shows, and\n685:     # the snapshot's dates are the fixed frame's.\n686:     assert rows and rows[-1][0] == TRADE_DATE\n687:     assert record[\"window_start\"] == rows[0][0]\n688:     assert record[\"window_end\"] == rows[-1][0]\n689:     assert record[\"window_start\"] <= record[\"window_end\"]\n690:     assert record[\"window_end\"] <= TRADE_DATE\n691:     assert len(rows) <= max(1, min(7, 30))\n692: \n693:     # §3.3 source_ref locates the paired call and its effective arguments.\n694:     assert \"get_verified_market_snapshot\" in record[\"source_ref\"]\n695:     assert \"call-1\" in record[\"source_ref\"]\n696:     assert TRADE_DATE in record[\"source_ref\"]\n697:     assert \"look_back_days=7\" in (record[\"source_ref\"] or \"\")\n698: \n699:     # §4.3 content_ref resolves to retained material under the run's root.\n700:     assert record[\"content_ref\"].startswith(f\"evidence://{RUN_A}/\")\n701:     retained = _retained_files(results_dir)\n702:     assert retained, \"the collector retained no material for a usable snapshot\"\n703:     named = record[\"content_ref\"].rsplit(\"/\", 1)[-1]\n704:     assert any(p.name == named for p in retained), (\n705:         f\"content_ref names {named!r}, which the run did not retain: {[p.name for p in retained]}\"\n706:     )\n707:     material = \"\\n\".join(p.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") for p in retained)\n708:     assert SNAPSHOT_HEADING in material\n709:     assert LATEST_CLOSE in material\n710: \n711: \n712: @pytest.mark.unit\n713: def test_tool_clamps_a_future_curr_date_to_the_trade_date(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n714:     \"\"\"``date_window.as_of``: a model asking for a later date gets no later row.\"\"\"\n715:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n716: \n717:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n718:         # The stale-frame guard would refuse a frame whose latest row is far from\n719:         # the requested date, which is a different concern; the clamp is what is\n720:         # under test here, so ``load_ohlcv`` is already replaced by ``_pin_ohlcv``.\n721:         calls = _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n722:         text = _snapshot_text(curr_date=\"2026-12-31\", look_back_days=7)\n723: \n724:     assert [c[1] for c in calls] == [TRADE_DATE], calls\n725:     assert _recent_rows(text)[-1][0] == TRADE_DATE\n726:     assert \"2026-12-31\" not in text\n727: \n728: \n729: @pytest.mark.unit\n730: def test_past_curr_date_is_served_as_requested(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n731:     \"\"\"The clamp only bounds the future: an earlier model date is served as-is.\"\"\"\n732:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n733: \n734:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n735:         calls = _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n736:         text = _snapshot_text(curr_date=\"2026-11-06\", look_back_days=7)\n737: \n738:     assert [c[1] for c in calls] == [\"2026-11-06\"], calls\n739:     assert _recent_rows(text)[-1][0] == \"2026-11-06\"\n740: \n741: \n742: def _retained_files(results_dir: Path, run_id: str = RUN_A) -> list[Path]:\n743:     \"\"\"Retained material for ``run_id`` under the §4.3 retention root.\"\"\"\n744:     root = results_dir / TICKER / TRADE_DATE / \"evidence\" / run_id\n745:     if not root.exists():\n746:         return []\n747:     return sorted(p for p in root.rglob(\"*\") if p.is_file())\n748: \n749: \n750: # --- wrap_up -------------------------------------------------------------------\n751: \n752: \n753: def _wheel_model(report: str):\n754:     \"\"\"A fake model whose two branches ``take_turn`` can pipe its prompt into.\n755: \n756:     ``take_turn`` does ``(prompt | llm.bind_tools(tools)).invoke(messages)`` on a\n757:     tool turn and ``(prompt | llm).invoke(_as_text(messages))`` on the wrap-up\n758:     turn, so both branches receive a ``PromptValue`` from the pipe, not a list.\n759:     Each branch is therefore a real ``Runnable``: the bound one is a\n760:     ``RunnableLambda`` that emits the snapshot ``tool_calls``, and the plain one a\n761:     ``RunnableLambda`` that produces the report. Both convert the prompt to a\n762:     message list before inspecting it.\n763: \n764:     The bound branch also recognises the wrap-up history: ``take_turn`` only\n765:     skips binding when the last human message is ``WRAP_UP``, but a wiring that\n766:     bound tools anyway must still end, so a bound turn holding ``WRAP_UP`` answers\n767:     with the report instead of calling the tool again. That is what leaves the run\n768:     with two tool results and one closing report.\n769:     \"\"\"\n770:     _import_graph_entry()\n771:     from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage\n772:     from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableLambda\n773: \n774:     from tradingagents.agents.analysts.turn import WRAP_UP\n775: \n776:     def _as_messages(prompt) -> list:\n777:         \"\"\"The prompt as a message list, whichever form the caller passed.\"\"\"\n778:         to_messages = getattr(prompt, \"to_messages\", None)\n779:         return to_messages() if callable(to_messages) else list(prompt)\n780: \n781:     def _is_wrap_up(messages) -> bool:\n782:         return (\n783:             bool(messages)\n784:             and isinstance(messages[-1], HumanMessage)\n785:             and messages[-1].content == WRAP_UP\n786:         )\n787: \n788:     class _Model:\n789:         def __init__(self):\n790:             self.bound_calls = 0\n791:             self.plain_calls = 0\n792:             self.turns: list[dict] = []\n793:             self.wrap_up_seen: list[str] = []\n794: \n795:         def _snapshots(self, messages) -> list[str]:\n796:             return [\n797:                 text for text in (getattr(m, \"content\", \"\") for m in messages)\n798:                 if isinstance(text, str) and SNAPSHOT_HEADING in text\n799:             ]\n800: \n801:         def _tool_turn(self, prompt):\n802:             self.bound_calls += 1\n803:             messages = _as_messages(prompt)\n804:             if _is_wrap_up(messages):\n805:                 # Bound but told the rounds are spent: answer, don't call again.\n806:                 self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": True, \"tools_bound\": True})\n807:                 self.wrap_up_seen = self._snapshots(messages)\n808:                 return AIMessage(content=report)\n809:             n = self.bound_calls\n810:             self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": False, \"tools_bound\": True})\n811:             return AIMessage(content=\"\", tool_calls=[{\n812:                 \"name\": TOOL_NAME,\n813:                 \"args\": _paired_call(call_id=f\"call-{n}\")[\"args\"],\n814:                 \"id\": f\"call-{n}\",\n815:             }])\n816: \n817:         def _plain_turn(self, prompt):\n818:             self.plain_calls += 1\n819:             messages = _as_messages(prompt)\n820:             wrapped = _is_wrap_up(messages)\n821:             self.turns.append({\"wrap_up\": wrapped, \"tools_bound\": False})\n822:             if wrapped:\n823:                 self.wrap_up_seen = self._snapshots(messages)\n824:             return AIMessage(content=report)\n825: \n826:         def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):\n827:             return RunnableLambda(self._tool_turn)\n828: \n829:         def invoke(self, prompt):\n830:             return self._plain_turn(prompt)\n831: \n832:     return _Model()\n833: \n834: \n835: @pytest.mark.unit\n836: def test_wrap_up_subgraph_calls_the_real_tool_then_writes_the_report(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n837:     \"\"\"R8-B §6 A-10: the analyst subgraph runs real tool rounds, then wraps up.\n838: \n839:     The model calls the snapshot tool every round until ``max_tool_rounds`` is\n840:     spent on the **production** analyst subgraph (``setup._analyst_graph``); its\n841:     real ``ToolNode`` injects ``symbol``/``trade_date``, so each round renders the\n842:     fixed frame. The production wrap-up turn then appends ``WRAP_UP`` and asks for\n843:     the report; the fake model answers it with the report instead of calling a\n844:     third tool, so the run ends with two tool results and one closing turn that\n845:     saw both of them.\n846:     \"\"\"\n847:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n848: \n849:     max_tool_rounds = 2\n850:     report = f\"AAPL closed at {LATEST_CLOSE} USD on {TRADE_DATE}.\"\n851: \n852:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n853:         calls = _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n854:         model = _wheel_model(report)\n855:         subgraph, marker = _market_analyst_subgraph(model, max_tool_rounds)\n856:         out = subgraph.invoke({\n857:             **_graph_state(),\n858:             \"messages\": [(\"human\", TICKER)],\n859:         })\n860: \n861:     # The real tool ran in the real subgraph for every round, against the fixed frame.\n862:     assert model.bound_calls == max_tool_rounds, (\n863:         f\"expected {max_tool_rounds} tool-bound turns, got {model.bound_calls}\"\n864:     )\n865:     assert marker.bound_turns == max_tool_rounds\n866:     assert len(calls) == max_tool_rounds, f\"tools executed: {calls}\"\n867:     assert {c[0] for c in calls} == {TICKER}\n868:     assert {c[1] for c in calls} == {TRADE_DATE}\n869:     assert {c[2] for c in calls} == {False}, (\n870:         f\"the snapshot must read the raw session rows (fill_gaps=False): {calls}\"\n871:     )\n872: \n873:     # Two tool rounds, then exactly one closing turn on the production wrap-up\n874:     # history; the fake model does not call a third tool when it is wrapped up.\n875:     assert model.turns == [\n876:         {\"wrap_up\": False, \"tools_bound\": True},\n877:         {\"wrap_up\": False, \"tools_bound\": True},\n878:         {\"wrap_up\": True, \"tools_bound\": False},\n879:     ], f\"unexpected turn sequence: {model.turns}\"\n880:     assert marker.turns == model.turns, (\n881:         f\"the production wiring's turn sequence differs from the model's: {marker.turns}\"\n882:     )\n883:     assert model.plain_calls == 1, \"the wrap-up turn must be the only unbound call\"\n884:     assert out[\"market_report\"] == report\n885: \n886:     # The closing turn saw both tool results, each carrying the verified snapshot.\n887:     assert len(model.wrap_up_seen) == max_tool_rounds, (\n888:         f\"the wrap-up turn saw {len(model.wrap_up_seen)} snapshot results, \"\n889:         f\"expected {max_tool_rounds}\"\n890:     )\n891:     for result in model.wrap_up_seen:\n892:         assert _recent_rows(result)[-1] == (TRADE_DATE, LATEST_CLOSE)\n893: \n894: \n895: @pytest.mark.unit\n896: def test_subgraph_hands_retained_snapshots_up_as_market_evidence(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n897:     \"\"\"R8-B §4: the market subgraph returns its retained receipts to the parent.\n898: \n899:     The subgraph's tool calls and results never leave it, so it must retain the\n900:     snapshots itself and expose them under ``market_evidence``; the Index Evidence\n901:     step folds that key into the run's index. Without the key the parent graph\n902:     would only ever see the report and the run could not cite verified data.\n903:     \"\"\"\n904:     from tradingagents.dataflows.config import run_config\n905: \n906:     max_tool_rounds = 2\n907:     report = f\"AAPL closed at {LATEST_CLOSE} USD on {TRADE_DATE}.\"\n908: \n909:     with run_config(_run_config(tmp_path)):\n910:         _pin_ohlcv(monkeypatch)\n911:         model = _wheel_model(report)\n912:         subgraph, _marker = _market_analyst_subgraph(model, max_tool_rounds)\n913:         out = subgraph.invoke({\n914:             **_graph_state(),\n915:             \"run_id\": RUN_A,\n916:             \"messages\": [(\"human\", TICKER)],\n917:         })\n918: \n919:     receipts = out.get(\"market_evidence\")\n920:     assert receipts, (\n921:         \"the market subgraph returned no market_evidence: the parent graph cannot \"\n922:         f\"index a snapshot the run really took (output keys: {sorted(out)})\"\n923:     )\n924:     assert len(receipts) == max_tool_rounds, f\"one receipt per tool round expected: {receipts}\"\n925:     for record in receipts:\n926:         assert record[\"run_id\"] == RUN_A\n927:         assert record[\"ticker\"] == TICKER\n928:         assert record[\"as_of_date\"] == TRADE_DATE\n929:         assert record[\"source_kind\"] == \"market_snapshot\"\n930:         assert (record.get(\"content_ref\") or \"\").startswith(f\"evidence://{RUN_A}/\")\n931:         # The reference names material this run really retained.\n932:         named = record[\"content_ref\"].rsplit(\"/\", 1)[-1]\n933:         retained = _retained_files(Path(_run_config(tmp_path)[\"results_dir\"]))\n934:         assert any(p.name == named for p in retained), (\n935:             f\"content_ref names {named!r}, which the subgraph did not retain: \"\n936:             f\"{[p.name for p in retained]}\"\n937:         )\n938: \n939: \n940: # --- negative: Metals/energy resolve to their front-month future;\n49: # index CFD names resolve to the underlying Yahoo index symbol. Extend by\n50: # adding rows — no call site changes required.\n51: _ALIASES = {\n52:     # Precious metals (spot names -> COMEX/NYMEX futures)\n53:     \"XAUUSD\": \"GC=F\", \"XAU\": \"GC=F\", \"GOLD\": \"GC=F\",\n54:     \"XAGUSD\": \"SI=F\", \"XAG\": \"SI=F\", \"SILVER\": \"SI=F\",\n55:     \"XPTUSD\": \"PL=F\", \"XPDUSD\": \"PA=F\",\n56:     # Energy\n57:     \"WTICOUSD\": \"CL=F\", \"USOIL\": \"CL=F\", \"WTI\": \"CL=F\",\n58:     \"BCOUSD\": \"BZ=F\", \"UKOIL\": \"BZ=F\", \"BRENT\": \"BZ=F\",\n59:     \"NATGAS\": \"NG=F\", \"XNGUSD\": \"NG=F\",\n60:     \"COPPER\": \"HG=F\", \"XCUUSD\": \"HG=F\",\n61:     # Index CFDs -> Yahoo index symbols\n62:     \"SPX500\": \"^GSPC\", \"US500\": \"^GSPC\", \"SPX\": \"^GSPC\",\n63:     \"NAS100\": \"^NDX\", \"US100\": \"^NDX\", \"USTEC\": \"^NDX\",\n64:     \"US30\": \"^DJI\", \"DJI30\": \"^DJI\", \"WS30\": \"^DJI\",\n65:     \"GER40\": \"^GDAXI\", \"GER30\": \"^GDAXI\", \"DE40\": \"^GDAXI\",\n66:     \"UK100\": \"^FTSE\", \"JP225\": \"^N225\", \"JPN225\": \"^N225\",\n67:     \"FRA40\": \"^FCHI\", \"EU50\": \"^STOXX50E\", \"HK50\": \"^HSI\",\n68: }\n69: \n70: # HKEX codes as Yahoo spells them: the number zero-padded to 4 digits (#957).\n71: _HK_CODE = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{1,5})\\.HK$\")\n72: _SHANGHAI_SH = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{6})\\.SH$\")\n73: \n74: \n75: # Crypto quote currencies that all map to Yahoo's USD pair. Explicit alias table (metals, energy, index CFDs).\n108:       2. Crypto rule: a known crypto base quoted in USD/USDT/USDC (dashed or\n109:          not) -> ``BASE-USD``.\n110:       3. Forex rule: six letters that are two ISO currency codes -> ``PAIR=X``.\n111:       4. HK rule: a numeric ``.HK`` code -> Yahoo's 4-digit padding\n112:          (``09992.HK`` -> ``9992.HK``, ``700.HK`` -> ``0700.HK``).\n113:       5. Shanghai rule: ``600519.SH`` -> ``600519.SS``.\n114:       6. Otherwise the upper-cased symbol is returned unchanged (plain\n115:          equities, ETFs, Yahoo-native symbols like ``GC=F`` or ``^GSPC``).\n116: \n117:     A trailing ``+`` (broker CFD marker, e.g. ``XAUUSD+``) is stripped before\n118:     matching. None of these enable directory\n150: # traversal, so the value never escapes a containing directory when\n151: # interpolated into a path. Structured output is layered onto the\n6: three decision-making agents (Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager)\n7: so that:\n8: \n9: - Their outputs follow consistent section headers across runs and providers\n10: - Each provider's native structured-output mode is used (json_schema for\n11:   OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic)\n12: - Schema field descriptions become the model's output instructions, freeing\n13:   the prompt body to focus on context and the rating-scale guidance\n14: - A render helper turns the parsed Pydantic instance back into the same\n15:   markdown shape the rest of the system already consumes, so display,\n16:   memory log, and saved reports keep working unchanged\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: from enum import StrEnum\n22: from typing import Literal\n23: \n24: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator\n25: \n26: # LLMs sometimes write a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\", ...) into an optional\n27: # numeric field instead of omitting it. Coerce those to None so the structured\n28: # call validates instead of erroring (#1058). Pydantic still parses real numeric\n29: # strings (\"189.5\") to float.\n30: _NULLISH_FLOAT = {\"\", \"none\", \"n/a\", \"na\", \"null\", \"nil\", \"-\", \"tbd\", \"unknown\"}\n31: \n32: \n33: def _coerce_optional_float(value):\n34:     \"\"\"Normalise an LLM-written optional numeric field before validation.\n35: \n36:     Three shapes show up in practice: a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\") in\n37:     place of an omitted value (#1058); a percentage where a price was asked for\n38:     (\"15%\", #1288); and a human-formatted price (\"$1,234.50\"). A percentage\n39:     cannot be salvaged into an absolute level -- reading \"15%\" as 15 would put a\n40:     stop at $15 on a $600 stock -- so it is dropped like a placeholder, leaving\n41:     one bad field to null out instead of failing the whole proposal. A formatted\n42:     price is reduced to its number.\n43: \n44:     Anything that is not a single number is dropped the same way. A range\n45:     (\"150-160\") or a hedge (\"around 150\") would otherwise reach pydantic, fail\n46:     validation, and discard the whole decision, losing every field the model got\n47:     right along with the price.\n48:     \"\"\"\n49:     if not isinstance(value, str):\n50:         return value\n51:     text = value.strip()\n52:     if text.lower() in _NULLISH_FLOAT or text.endswith(\"%\"):\n53:         return None\n54:     cleaned = text.replace(\",\", \"\").lstrip(\"$€£¥\").strip()\n55:     try:\n56:         return float(cleaned)\n57:     except ValueError:\n58:         return None\n59: \n60: \n61: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n62: # Shared rating types\n63: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n64: \n65: \n66: class PortfolioRating(StrEnum):\n67:     \"\"\"5-tier rating used by the Research Manager and Portfolio Manager.\"\"\"\n68: \n69:     BUY = \"Buy\"\n70:     OVERWEIGHT = \"Overweight\"\n71:     HOLD = \"Hold\"\n72:     UNDERWEIGHT = \"Underweight\"\n73:     SELL = \"Sell\"\n74: \n75: \n76: class TraderAction(StrEnum):\n77:     \"\"\"3-tier transaction direction used by the Trader.\n78: \n79:     The Trader's job is to translate the Research Manager's investment plan\n80:     into a concrete transaction proposal: should the desk execute a Buy, a\n81:     Sell, or sit on Hold this round.  Position sizing and the nuanced\n82:     Overweight / Underweight calls happen later at the Portfolio Manager.\n83:     \"\"\"\n84: \n85:     BUY = \"Buy\"\n86:     HOLD = \"Hold\"\n87:     SELL = \"Sell\"\n88: \n89: \n90: class DebateArgument(BaseModel):\n91:     \"\"\"A Bull or Bear argument with structured evidence references.\n92: \n93:     FR-01: the researcher may only cite evidence IDs that exist in this run's\n94:     program-built index. Copy exact IDs from the \"\n108:             \"'Available evidence' list; do not invent IDs. It is not\n27: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than\n28: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum\n29: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.\n30: RATING_REVIEW = \"REVIEW\"\n31: \n32: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}\n33: \n34: # Matches \"Rating: X\" / \"rating - X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n35: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. \"rating\"\n36: # must start a word, so \"Operating margin: Sell-side\" is not a label.\n37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<![a-z])rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n38:                               re.IGNORECASE)\n39: \n40: # The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to\n41: # open with (\"- **Rating**: X\", \"**Final Rating**: X\", \"## Our rating - X\"): an\n42: # optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the\n43: # decision itself before \"rating\". \"Consensus rating: Buy\" or \"Trader's rating:\n44: # Buy\" is someone else's rating.\n45: _OWN_QUALIFIER = r\"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\\s+)*\"\n46: _RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(\n47:     r\"\\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\\u2022]|\\d+[.)])\\s+)?[\\s*_#]*\" + _OWN_QUALIFIER\n48:     + r\"rating[^\\w:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(?P<value>\\w+)\",\n49:     re.IGNORECASE,\n50: )\n51: \n52: # A line presenting the scale rather than a decision (\"Rating Scale: Buy, ...\").\n53: _RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\s*(scale|options|legend)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n54: \n55: def extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:\n56:     \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.\n57: \n58:     Reads an explicit \"Rating: X\" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the\n59:     NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``\n60:     matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own\n61:     rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.\n62:     \"\"\"\n63:     if not text:\n64:         return None\n65:     norm = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", text)\n66: \n67:     # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any\n68:     # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote\n69:     # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's\n70:     # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label\n71:     # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing\n72:     # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the\n73:     # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.\n74:     lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]\n75:     first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"#\")\n76:                   or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), \"\")\n77:     m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)\n78:     opening = m if m and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET else None\n79:     if opening and not opening.group(\"item\"):\n80:         return opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()\n81: \n82:     own = [opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()] if opening else []\n83:     labels = []\n84:     for line in lines:\n85:         m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)\n86:         if m and not m.group(\"item\") and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET:\n87:             own.append(m.group(\"value\").capitalize())\n88:         labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]\n89:     # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be\n90:     # one the text argues against (\"not a Sell\"), and reading it reports a\n91:     # direction nobody decided.\n92:     found = own or labels\n93:     return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None\n94: \n95: \n96: def parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:\n97:     \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.\n98: \n99:     For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's\n100:     entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.\n101:     \"\"\"\n102:     rating = extract_rating(text)\n103:     return rating if rating is not None else default\n104: \n105: \n106: def run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:\n107:     \"\"\"A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.\n108: \n109:     The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older\n110:     version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.\n111:     \"\"\"\n112:     return final_state.get(\"final_rating\") or parse_rating(final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\", \"\"))\n113: \n114: \n115: def is_review(signal: str) -> bool:\n116:     \"\"\"Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170).\"\"\"\n117:     return signal == RATING_REVIEW"

A block that came from the fixture would\n+    have blocked the first judgement too.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n+    run_id = f\"course-run-f1-{tmp_path.name}\"\n+    _write_material(graph, run_id)\n+\n+    # Same-run positive control: the state's own identity approves and saves.\n+    same_run = _candidate_state(run_id)\n+    assert graph.publish(same_run) == APPROVED, same_run.get(\"publication_reason\")\n+    assert same_run.get(\"final_rating\") == BUY\n+    save_path = tmp_path / \"reports\"\n+    graph.save_reports(same_run, TICKER, save_path=save_path)\n+    assert DECISION_FILE in _relative_files(save_path), \"the positive control wrote no decision\"\n+\n+    # Cross-run: identical records, only the current run identity changes.\n+    foreign_run = _candidate_state(run_id)\n+    foreign_run[\"course_run\"] = _run_context(f\"{run_id}-other\")\n+    status = graph.publish(foreign_run)\n+\n+    assert status == BLOCKED, (\n+        \"a run citing another run's evidence must not publish, but the gate \"\n+        f\"returned {status!r}\"\n+    )\n+    assert foreign_run.get(\"publication_reason\") == INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n+    assert foreign_run.get(\"final_rating\") in (None, \"\")\n+    assert CANDIDATE_MARKER not in repr(foreign_run.get(\"publication_result\"))\n+\n+\[REDACTED_EMAIL]\n def test_blocked_diagnostic_report_shows_blocked_without_official_rating(monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n     \"\"\"A real BLOCKED run still saves the diagnostic report, free of the candidate.\"\"\"\n     graph = _make_graph(monkeypatch, tmp_path)\n     run_id = f\"course-run-blocked-{tmp_path.name}\"\n",

              "newString": "REPORT = \"The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend.\"\n\n# A line in the evidence menu looks like: \"- ev:<run>:market_snapshot:<call>  [market_snapshot] <excerpt>\"\n_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r\"^- (ev:\\S+)\\s+\\[\", re.MULTILINE)\n_SNAPSHOT_TOOL = \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\n\n\ndef _cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The evidence IDs the researcher is actually offered in this prompt.\"\"\"\n    match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)\n    return [match.group(1)] if match else []\n\n\ndef _prompt_text(prompt) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The flattened text a structured call is given (a string or a PromptValue).\"\"\"\n    to_messages = getattr(prompt, \"to_messages\", None)\n    if callable(to_messages):\n        prompt = to_messages()\n    elif isinstance(prompt, str):\n        return prompt\n    parts = []\n    for message in prompt:\n        if isinstance(message, str):\n            parts.append(message)\n            continue\n        content = getattr(message, \"content\", \"\")\n        parts.append(content if isinstance(content, str) else \"\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _pin_snapshot(monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"Serve a fixed OHLCV frame in place of the vendor download.\n\n    Only ``load_ohlcv`` is replaced; the real tool closure, rendering and\n    ``as_of`` clamp still run, so the tool call retains genuine snapshot text.\n    \"\"\"\n    import pandas as pd\n\n    import tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.snapshot as snapshot\n\n    frame = pd.DataFrame(\n        [\n            {\"Date\": d, \"Open\": o, \"High\": h, \"Low\": low, \"Close\": c, \"Volume\": v}\n            for d, o, h, low, c, v in (\n                (\"2025-12-30\", 138.10, 140.20, 137.05, 139.80, 51_200_000),\n                (\"2025-12-31\", 139.80, 142.40, 139.10, 141.95, 49_800_000),\n                (\"2026-01-02\", 141.95, 144.10, 141.20, 143.60, 52_500_000),\n                (\"2026-01-05\", 143.60, 145.30, 142.80, 144.90, 55_100_000),\n            )\n        ],\n        columns=[\"Date\", \"Open\", \"High\", \"Low\", \"Close\", \"Volume\"],\n    )\n    monkeypatch.setattr(snapshot, \"load_ohlcv\", lambda *a, **k: frame.copy())\n\n\nclass _EvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):\n    \"\"\"Emits reports; the market analyst first calls the snapshot tool.\n\n    The Bull then reads the evidence menu out of the prompt it is actually given\n    and cites that id, so the test proves the prompt wiring and the retained\n    material read-back rather than an injected constant.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    snapshot_calls: int = 0\n\n    @property\n    def _llm_type(self) -> str:\n        return \"evidence-fake\"\n\n    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        return self\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        if schema is DebateArgument:\n            return _StructuredArgument()\n        if schema is PortfolioDecision:\n            return _StructuredDecision()\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,\n                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,\n                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:\n        text = _prompt_text(messages).lower()\n        # The market analyst's prompt opens \"You are a trading assistant\" and\n        # lists its tools. Its first turn is a real tool call, so the subgraph\n        # retains the snapshot and hands the receipt up to the parent graph.\n        is_analyst = \"you are a trading assistant\" in text or \"ohlcv\" in text\n        if is_analyst and self.snapshot_calls == 0:\n            self.snapshot_calls += 1\n            return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(\n                content=\"\",\n                tool_calls=[{\n                    \"name\": _SNAPSHOT_TOOL,\n                    \"args\": {\"curr_date\": \"2026-01-05\", \"look_back_days\": 7},\n                    \"id\": \"call-1\",\n                }],\n            ))])\n        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])\n\n\nclass _StructuredArgument:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # Cite the real run evidence id that appears in the prompt.\n        return DebateArgument(\n            argument=\"bull case\",\n            evidence_ids=_cited_evidence_from_prompt(_prompt_text(prompt)),\n        )\n\n\nclass _StructuredDecision:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # The PM must cite the accepted argument. The argument id is run-bound, so\n        # read it from the 'Accepted arguments' block the PM is actually given.\n        text = _prompt_text(prompt)\n        match = re.search(r\"^- (arg:\\S+)\", text, re.MULTILINE)\n        argument_ids = [match.group(1)] if match else []\n        return PortfolioDecision(\n            rating=PortfolioRating.BUY,\n            executive_summary=\"add\",\n            investment_thesis=\"breakout\",\n            argument_ids=argument_ids,\n        )",
              "oldString": "REPORT = \"The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend.\"\n\n# A line in the evidence menu looks like: \"- ev:<run>:market_report  [market_report] <excerpt>\"\n_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r\"^- (ev:\\S+)\\s+\\[\", re.MULTILINE)\n\n\ndef _cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The evidence IDs the researcher is actually offered in this prompt.\"\"\"\n    match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)\n    return [match.group(1)] if match else []\n\n\nclass _EvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):\n    \"\"\"Emits reports; structured calls read the evidence menu from the prompt.\"\"\"\n\n    @property\n    def _llm_type(self) -> str:\n        return \"evidence-fake\"\n\n    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        return self\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        if schema is DebateArgument:\n            return _StructuredArgument()\n        if schema is PortfolioDecision:\n            return _StructuredDecision()\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,\n                  run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,\n                  **kwargs) -> ChatResult:\n        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])\n\n\nclass _StructuredArgument:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # Cite the real run evidence id that appears in the prompt.\n        return DebateArgument(\n            argument=\"bull case\",\n            evidence_ids=_cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt),\n        )\n\n\nclass _StructuredDecision:\n    def invoke(self, prompt):\n        # The PM must cite the accepted argument.                   "patch": "Index: test/offline/test_fr01_publish_valid.py\n===================================================================\n--- test/offline/test_fr01_publish_valid.py\n+++ test/offline/test_fr01_publish_valid.py\n@@ -28,21 +28,71 @@\n from tradingagents.agents.schemas import DebateArgument, PortfolioDecision, PortfolioRating\n \n REPORT = \"The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend.\"\n \n-# A line in the evidence menu looks like: \"- ev:<run>:market_report  [market_report] <excerpt>\"\n+# A line in the evidence menu looks like: \"- ev:<run>:market_snapshot:<call>  [market_snapshot] <excerpt>\"\n _EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r\"^- (ev:\\S+)\\s+\\[\", re.MULTILINE)\n+_SNAPSHOT_TOOL = \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\n \n \n def _cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt: str) -> list[str]:\n     \"\"\"The evidence IDs the researcher is actually offered in this prompt.\"\"\"\n     match = _EVIDENCE_LINE.search(prompt)\n     return [match.group(1)] if match else []\n \n \n+def _prompt_text(prompt) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"The flattened text a structured call is given (a string or a PromptValue).\"\"\"\n+    to_messages = getattr(prompt, \"to_messages\", None)\n+    if callable(to_messages):\n+        prompt = to_messages()\n+    elif isinstance(prompt, str):\n+        return prompt\n+    parts = []\n+    for message in prompt:\n+        if isinstance(message, str):\n+            parts.append(message)\n+            continue\n+        content = getattr(message, \"content\", \"\")\n+        parts.append(content if isinstance(content, str) else \"\")\n+    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n+\n+\n+def _pin_snapshot(monkeypatch):\n+    \"\"\"Serve a fixed OHLCV frame in place of the vendor download.\n+\n+    Only ``load_ohlcv`` is replaced; the real tool closure, rendering and\n+    ``as_of`` clamp still run, so the tool call retains genuine snapshot text.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    import pandas as pd\n+\n+    import tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.snapshot as snapshot\n+\n+    frame = pd.DataFrame(\n+        [\n+            {\"Date\": d, \"Open\": o, \"High\": h, \"Low\": low, \"Close\": c, \"Volume\": v}\n+            for d, o, h, low, c, v in (\n+                (\"2025-12-30\", 138.10, 140.20, 137.05, 139.80, 51_200_000),\n+                (\"2025-12-31\", 139.80, 142.40, 139.10, 141.95, 49_800_000),\n+                (\"2026-01-02\", 141.95, 144.10, 141.20, 143.60, 52_500_000),\n+                (\"2026-01-05\", 143.60, 145.30, 142.80, 144.90, 55_100_000),\n+            )\n+        ],\n+        columns=[\"Date\", \"Open\", \"High\", \"Low\", \"Close\", \"Volume\"],\n+    )\n+    monkeypatch.setattr(snapshot, \"load_ohlcv\", lambda *a, **k: frame.copy())\n+\n+\n class _EvidenceModel(BaseChatModel):\n-    \"\"\"Emits reports; structured calls read the evidence menu from the prompt.\"\"\"\n+    \"\"\"Emits reports; the market analyst first calls the snapshot tool.\n \n+    The Bull then reads the evidence menu out of the prompt it is actually given\n+    and cites that id, so the test proves the prompt wiring and the retained\n+    material read-back rather than an injected constant.\n+    \"\"\"\n+\n+    snapshot_calls: int = 0\n+\n     @property\n     def _llm_type(self) -> str:\n         return \"evidence-fake\"\n \n@@ -58,25 +108,41 @@\n \n     def _generate(self, messages, stop=None,\n                   run_manager: CallbackManagerForLLMRun | None = None,\n                   **kwargs) -> ChatResult:\n+        text = _prompt_text(messages).lower()\n+        # The market analyst's prompt opens \"You are a trading assistant\" and\n+        # lists its tools. Its first turn is a real tool call, so the subgraph\n+        # retains the snapshot and hands the receipt up to the parent graph.\n+        is_analyst = \"you are a trading assistant\" in text or \"ohlcv\" in text\n+        if is_analyst and self.snapshot_calls == 0:\n+            self.snapshot_calls += 1\n+            return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(\n+                content=\"\",\n+                tool_calls=[{\n+                    \"name\": _SNAPSHOT_TOOL,\n+                    \"args\": {\"curr_date\": \"2026-01-05\", \"look_back_days\": 7},\n+                    \"id\": \"call-1\",\n+                }],\n+            ))])\n         return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(content=REPORT))])\n \n \n class _StructuredArgument:\n     def invoke(self, prompt):\n         # Cite the real run evidence id that appears in the prompt.\n         return DebateArgument(\n             argument=\"bull case\",\n-            evidence_ids=_cited_evidence_from_prompt(prompt),\n+            evidence_ids=_cited_evidence_from_prompt(_prompt_text(prompt)),\n         )\n \n \n class _StructuredDecision:\n     def invoke(self, prompt):\n         # The PM must cite the accepted argument. The argument id is run-bound, so\n         # read it from the 'Accepted arguments' block the PM is actually given.\n-        match = re.search(r\"^- (arg:\\S+)\", prompt, re.MULTILINE)\n+        text = _prompt_text(prompt)\n+        match = re.search(r\"^- (arg:\\S+)\", text, re.MULTILINE)\n         argument_ids = [match.group(1)] if match else []\n         return PortfolioDecision(\n             rating=PortfolioRating.BUY,\n             executive_summary=\"add\",\n",

The gate is the single authority for whether a candidate recommendation\n6: becomes an official decision. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the\n7: program itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating\n8: fallback is honoured around the gate.\n9: \n10: Design (plan revision 1, superseded by the R8-B C1 v1.0 section below):\n11: - The run's evidence index is built *before* the first debate turn from material\n12:   the run actually retained (the market analyst's verified snapshots), so every\n13:   accepted argument cites material that exists in this run. An analyst report is\n14:   **not** evidence: prose alone has no traceable retained source. The index is\n15:   carried on the graph state as **plain, msgpack-safe data** (``evidence_index`` =\n16:   an ``evidence_id`` -> record mapping), never as an object, so checkpointed runs\n17:   can be saved and resumed.\n18: - Bull/Bear submit structured ``evidence_ids``; the program validates each against\n19:   the run index and only then mints a run-bound ``argument_id``.\n20: - The Portfolio Manager selects from those accepted ``argument_ids``.\n21: - ``evaluate_publication`` checks the whole chain (recommendation -> accepted\n22:   argument -> this run's retained material) and returns one ``PublicationResult``.\n23:   ``apply_publication`` projects that result onto the run state used by the sinks\n24:   (CLI, API, reports, memory).\n25: \n26: Only two outward rejection reasons exist: ``INVALID_RATING`` and\n27: ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references\n28: all map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,\n29: ``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.\n30: \n31: C1 v1.0 (``evaluate_publication`` / ``PublicationResult``):\n32: - The authoritative indexes are ID -> record **mappings**: ``argument_index``\n33:   keyed by ``argument_id``, ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The old\n34:   ``index_to_state`` lists and ``accepted_arguments`` stay as a compatibility\n35:   layer and are never a release authority.\n36: - Rows are applied in order: C0 terminal/incomplete execution, then an invalid\n37:   rating, then insufficient references; APPROVED is the only state with a rating.\n38: - Every record is identity-checked against the ``RunContext`` (a foreign run's\n39:   material never resolves) and every reference is rechecked from the candidate,\n40:   never trusted from the model.\n41: - ``PublicationResult`` is the one result all four sinks (CLI, Python return,\n42:   saved report, decision memory) consume; ``PublicationRequiredError`` refuses an\n43:   official write when a state carries no real result.\n44: \"\"\"\n45: \n46: from __future__ import annotations\n47: \n48: from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n49: from pathlib import Path\n50: \n51: from tradingagents.agents.rating import RATINGS_5_TIER\n52: \n53: # The analyst state keys whose non-empty text is admissible as run material.\n54: _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS = (\n55:     \"market_report\",\n56:     \"sentiment_report\",\n57:     \"news_report\",\n58:     \"fundamentals_report\",\n59: )\n60: \n61: # Outward rejection reasons (D1 / runtime-policy-catalog.md).\n62: INVALID_RATING = \"INVALID_RATING\"\n63: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE = \"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\"\n64: \n65: # The five-tier scale as a set of canonical strings, for O(1) membership tests.\n66: _RATING_SET = frozenset(RATINGS_5_TIER)\n67: \n68: # Publication status values carried on the run state.\n69: APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n70: BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n71: \n72: # C0 execution states. Only COMPLETED may publish; each terminal failure keeps its\n73: # own reason code, and any other non-completed state is RUN_NOT_COMPLETE.\n74: EXECUTION_COMPLETED = \"COMPLETED\"\n75: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = \"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED\"\n76: CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE = \"CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE\"\n77: RUN_NOT_COMPLETE = \"RUN_NOT_COMPLETE\"\n78: _TERMINAL_EXECUTION = (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE)\n79: \n80: \n81: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n82: class EvidenceRecord:\n83:     \"\"\"One admissible piece of run material, addressed by a run-bound id.\"\"\"\n84: \n85:     evidence_id: str\n86:     source: str      # analyst state key the material came from, e.g. \"market_report\"\n87:     excerpt: str     # short, human-resolvable pointer into the material\n88:     run_id: str\n89: \n90: \n91: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n92: class ArgumentRecord:\n93:     \"\"\"An argument accepted only because each cited evidence id resolved in this run.\"\"\"\n94: \n95:     argument_id: str\n96:     speaker: str                  # \"Bull Analyst\" / \"Bear Analyst\"\n97:     text: str\n98:     evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n99: \n100: \n101: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n102: class GateOutcome:\n103:     \"\"\"The single release decision for a run.\"\"\"\n104: \n105:     status: str                              # APPROVED | BLOCKED\n106:     reason: str | None                       # INVALID_RATING | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n107:     rating: str | None                       # a 5-tier rating only when APPROVED\n108:     resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)\n109:     # resolved_chain items: (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n110: \n111:     @property\n112:     def approved(self) -> bool:\n113:         return self.status == APPROVED\n114: \n115: \n116: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n117: class PublicationResult:\n118:     \"\"\"The one authoritative C1 v1.0 publication result, shared by all four sinks.\n119: \n120:     Identity is copied from the ``RunContext``;                 "type": "text",
                "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md, lines 1-175\n1: # Shared interface contracts\n2: \n3: Version: 1.0. Status: Proposed. Shared boundaries use JSON-compatible records. Internal dataclasses, TypedDict or Pydantic models may use adapters that preserve these fields and semantics. ADR-001 records the design decision.\n4: \n5: ## Ownership and integration\n6: \n7: | Contract | Authority | Producers and consumers |\n8: | --- | --- | --- |\n9: | C0 run identity and outcome | Run coordinator | All five owner modules, CLI, Python, report and memory |\n10: | C1 evidence and publication | FR-01 publication gate | Analyst evidence, accepted arguments, candidate, all official sinks |\n11: | C2 verified metrics | FR-02 metric registry | Fundamentals inputs, controlled downstream fields and metric table |\n12: | C3 sentiment coverage | FR-03 coverage component | Existing source adapters, analyst, state, report and downstream agents |\n13: | C4 dispatch budget | NFR-01 request-budget component | Both model tiers and every in-scope transport send |\n14: | C5 prepared context | NFR-02 context component | Analyst closure and neutral risk debater, then C4 |\n15: \n16: Shared-file integration owner: EverForests. Feature owners submit narrow patches for state, schema, graph/client and reporting adapters. Task plans identify exact paths. The integrator preserves approved contracts across patches; shared files must not be independently replaced by feature branches.\n17: \n18: ## C0 — identity, state and errors\n19: \n20: Every authoritative record carries `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and `as_of_date`. Evidence and metric IDs are only resolvable inside that run. Never retrieve a matching-looking ID from a previous run. A restarted run gets a new ID. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.\n21: \n22: Keep three concepts separate:\n23: \n24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.\n25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.\n26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.\n27: \n28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.\n29: \n30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication\n31: \n32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.\n33: \n34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.\n35: \n36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.\n37: \n38: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.\n39: \n40: ## C2 — verified metrics\n41: \n42: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.\n43: \n44: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.\n45: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.\n46: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.\n47: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.\n48: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.\n49: \n50: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.\n51: \n52: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.\n53: \n54: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score\n55: \n56: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.\n57: \n58: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.\n59: \n60: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). AAPL as-of 2026-11-10 therefore covers 2026-11-03 through 2026-11-10. Freeze the clock for date-dependent fixtures. Historical undated content cannot prove window validity. Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.\n61: \n62: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. Never claim these statuses prove that no real-world messages/news exist.\n63: \n64: | Valid logical sources | coverage_status | Sentiment output |\n65: | --- | --- | --- |\n66: | 0/3 | NO_DATA | overall_band UNKNOWN; overall_score null |\n67: | 1/3 or 2/3 | PARTIAL_DATA | Coverage remains explicit; any measured score uses valid evidence only |\n68: | 3/3 | AVAILABLE | Coverage available; score still requires a valid assessment |\n69: \n70: Coverage is authoritative data state; the model cannot increase it. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. A genuine measured Neutral/5.0 remains legal.\n71: \n72: Missing scores never become 0 or 5 and never enter a numerical mean. Structured state, analyst message, downstream prompt and persisted/rendered report must agree. Handle nullable scores without numeric-format errors. Apply the contract to structured **and** free-text fallback; model narrative cannot override authoritative coverage. Keep the existing sentiment_report text as a compatibility view; the new sentiment_assessment record below is authoritative. Both must agree. Internal schema adaptation may change, but the v1 shared record does not drift silently.\n73: \n74: The original baseline stores `sentiment_report` as text and requires a nonnull numeric SentimentReport score. Updating only the prompt cannot establish this contract. No raw social bodies or credentials belong in public evidence. Missing optional sentiment does not stop otherwise valid market/fundamental analysis; C1 still decides publication.\n75: \n76: ## C4 — atomic per-run model dispatch\n77: \n78: Supported scope: one single-stock main analysis, both model tiers, structured/fallback requests and application retries. Count actual outgoing model attempts, not nodes, tool invocations, callbacks or tokens. Historical settlement is excluded. Disable SDK/transport implicit retries in supported course runs; unsupported hidden-retry modes are outside the verified configuration, not silently compliant.\n79: \n80: Budget state: positive integer `limit`, charged sends, active reservations and exhaustion. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation. Validate C5 first so context rejection obtains no reservation.\n81: \n82: No slot => BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no request, no official recommendation. Limit 3 allows exactly 3 attempts; the fourth is refused. Concurrent runs do not share counters. Include application fallback/retry attempts separately. C4 does not promise a monetary or token cap. Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.\n83: \n84: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context\n85: \n86: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. Other analyst turns and risk roles are not implicitly covered. Before reserving C4, fully expand/convert the scoped final message sequence into one agreed provider-facing representation.\n87: \n88: Canonical v1 measurement: the final provider-facing message array encoded as JSON with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon) without optional whitespace, allow_nan=False, then UTF-8. Use the ChatMessage representation below and freeze byte fixtures before implementation. Do not measure before template expansion or change representation after measuring. Tool schemas and other separately bound fields are excluded from this message metric and must be recorded/bounded separately; this is not a cap on the whole HTTP body.\n89: \n90: Required blocks: role/task identity; standing safety/publication rules; ticker/date/run identity; current required evidence/verified metrics/source coverage; and the active tool-call/result exchange. Optional blocks: explicitly marked older discussion/history. A tool-call/result pair is indivisible; if a member is required, preserve the whole pair. Text-wrapped tools retain name, arguments and corresponding result. Removing context cannot delete authoritative evidence/state from storage.\n91: \n92: At the configured 65536-byte acceptance cap: short input passes unchanged. If oversized, remove optional groups oldest first (stable original index for ties), reassemble, reinject critical constraints and remeasure. Do not summarize required evidence with another unmetered model call. If required blocks cannot fit or pairing cannot be preserved, return CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE; zero send, reservation and debit. Same normalized input/config produces identical prepared output. Run final retention/pairing checks before C4.\n93: \n94: This byte cap does not implement the separate D2 token-budget requirement. ADR-001 records that architecture design and the remaining tokenizer/model-capacity validation. Do not infer token counts from bytes/4 or claim provider safety from 64 KiB alone.\n95: \n96: ## Contract-change and approval record\n97: \n98: Before implementation, record requirement IDs, contract revision, baseline SHA, exact read/edit paths, fixture/case revision, reviewer and approval time. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Feature PRs link the approved plan and actual evidence; the coordinator runs integrated regressions before release.\n99: \n100: \n101: ## V1 shared record layout\n102: \n103: Version field: `contract_version = \"1.0\"`. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. opaque to other features | NFR-01 |\n122: \n123: `Operand.period` is `{kind, start, end, label}`: kind is quarter/year/instant, start/end are ISO dates, and label records the source's fiscal period or quote timestamp. Currency and scale are part of unit (for example USD vs USD_millions); conversion must be explicit and preserve original operands. Do not silently take abs(capex), invent comparable periods or round source values to make a fixture match. An EvidenceRecord source_ref identifies the source, while content_ref locates the retained shareable material/fixture; an ID with no resolvable retained material is insufficient.\n124: \n125: For SentimentAssessment, overall_band is one existing measured band or UNKNOWN. overall_score is a finite float in [0,10] for MEASURED, otherwise null. confidence keeps the existing low/medium/high vocabulary; UNKNOWN uses low and is not a measured weak-neutral signal. Returns the\n    **accepted record** — the argument's full identity plus its claim and the\n    resolved evidence ids — or ``None`` when the submission is not acceptable.\n\n    An argument is accepted only when every part of C1 holds:\n\n    * it carries the run's **full identity** (``run_id``, ``ticker``,\n      ``as_of_date`` all equal the ``RunContext``'s), so a foreign or\n      identity-less submission is not this run's argument;\n    * it has an ``argument_id`` and a nonempty ``claim``;\n    * ``evidence_ids`` is a nonempty list, and **every** cited id resolves to\n      admissible evidence in this run: present in the index, complete, and\n      backed by retained material that exists and has content.\n\n    A model flag is not acceptance, and a partially resolvable citation is not a\n    partial acceptance: one unresolvable id refuses the argument. No more \"skip what doesn't resolve\".\n- Added `EXECUTION_FAILED = \"FAILED\"`. Row 1 keeps `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` / `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE` as their own codes; `FAILED` (and `RUNNING`/missing) → `RUN_NOT_COMPLETE`.\n- `publication_run` carries a recorded terminal state (`FAILED` included) forward.\n\n**2. `tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py`**\n- `complete_run` no longer promotes `FAILED` (or the budget codes) to `COMPLETED`, whether recorded on the flat field or inside `course_run`.\n\n**3. `tradingagents/graph/propagation.py`**\n- `create_initial_state` now mints `run_id` and creates the one complete `course_run` (`contract_version`, `run_id`, `ticker`, `as_of_date`, `RUNNING`, `request_limit` → `DEFAULT_REQUEST_LIMIT`), seeding both onto state.\n\n**4. `tradingagents/graph/setup.py`**\n- `_run_context` reuses a seeded `course_run` verbatim (with validation), preserving resume identity; a recorded terminal failure outranks the `RUNNING` default.\n- `_pending_run_context` prefers the seeded context.\n- Added `_results_dir()` helper.\n\n**5. / 6. `bull_researcher.py` / `bear_researcher.py`**\n- Both now call `validate_argument` with the seeded run identity and store the **returned** accepted record.
