you cannot cite any evidence ID.)\"\n356:     lines = []\n357:     for record in idx.evidence_records:\n358:         lines.append(f\"- {record.evidence_id}  [{record.source}] {record.excerpt}\")\n359:     return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n360: \n361: \n362: def _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n363:     \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n364:     flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n365:     return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n366: \n367: \n368: def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n369:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n370: \n371:     Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n372:     ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n373:     \"\"\"\n374:     if value is None:\n375:         return None\n376:     rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n377:     if not isinstance(rating, str):\n378:         return None\n379:     return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n380: \n381: \n382: def evaluate(index, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids) -> GateOutcome:\n383:     \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n384: \n385:     ``index`` may be the state dict or an EvidenceIndex. Order matters: an invalid\n386:     rating is reported before a missing chain, so a candidate that fails both\n387:     returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is consulted here.\n388:     \"\"\"\n389:     idx = as_index(index)\n390:     rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n391:     if rating is None:\n392:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n393: \n394:     cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n395:     resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n396:     for argument_id in cited:\n397:         if not idx.has_argument(argument_id):\n398:             continue\n399:         argument = idx.argument(argument_id)\n400:         for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n401:             if idx.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n402:                 resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, idx.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n403:     if not resolved:\n404:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n405: \n406:     return GateOutcome(\n407:         status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n408:     )\n409: \n410: \n411: def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n412:     \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n413: \n414:     On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the\n415:     candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the\n416:     returned state carries no candidate material at all — the candidate body,\n417:     candidate rating and candidate argument ids are removed from the mapping, so\n418:     the Python API's returned state cannot expose or re-derive the candidate. The\n419:     only place ``REVIEW`` appears is the API's second tuple member (computed by the\n420:     caller via ``run_rating``); ``final_rating`` is emptied here, not set to REVIEW.\n421:     \"\"\"\n422:     status = outcome.status\n423:     final_state[\"publication_status\"] = status\n424:     final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = outcome.reason\n425:     final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)\n426: \n427:     if outcome.approved:\n428:         body = final_state.get(\"candidate_decision\") or final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\") or \"\"\n429:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = outcome.rating\n430:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = body\n431:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n432:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n433:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n434:     else:\n435:         # No candidate material leaks into the returned state: the body, its rating\n436:         # and the ids it cited are all removed. ``final_rating`` is emptied rather\n437:         # than set to REVIEW; REVIEW is the API's second tuple member only.\n438:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = \"\"\n439:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n440:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n441:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n442:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n443:     return final_state\n444: \n445: \n446: # --- C1 v1.0: mapping-authoritative evaluation -------------------------------\n447: #\n448: # The authoritative indexes are ID -> record mappings: ``argument_index`` keyed by\n449: # ``argument_id`` and ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The legacy\n450: # shapes ``index_to_state(...)`` (lists under \"evidence\"/\"arguments\") and\n451: # ``accepted_arguments`` are a compatibility layer only: an argument that exists\n452: # solely in that view never resolves a reference.\n453: \n454: \n455: _IDENTITY_KEYS = (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"as_of_date\")\n456: \n457: # C1 v1.0 required shared fields, beyond identity. \"A missing required field is an\n458: # invalid record\": a record without one is not admissible evidence/acceptance.\n459: _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED = (\n460:     \"evidence_id\", \"source_kind\", \"vendor\", \"source_ref\",\n461:     \"content_ref\", \"window_start\", \"window_end\",\n462: )\n463: _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED = (\"argument_id\", \"claim\")\n464: \n465: \n466: def _field_present(record: dict, key: str) -> bool:\n467:     \"\"\"Whether a required field is present and non-empty.\n468: \n469:     A missing value, ``None``, an empty string and a whitespace-only string are\n470:     all the same thing here: no value. A list is present when it is non-empty.\n471:     \"\"\"\n472:     value = record.get(key)\n473:     if isinstance(value, str):\n474:         return bool(value.strip())\n475:     if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):\n476:         return len(value) > 0\n477:     return value is not None\n478: \n479: \n480: def _required_fields_ok(record, required) -> bool:\n481:     \"\"\"Whether every C1 required field of ``record`` is present and non-empty.\"\"\"\n482:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n483:         return False\n484:     return all(_field_present(record, key) for key in required)\n485: \n486: \n487: def _identity(record, run: dict) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:\n488:     \"\"\"The record's ``(run_id, ticker, as_of_date)`` when it *fully* matches the run.\n489: \n490:     Ownership is checked on the record's full identity, never on how its ID is\n491:     spelled: an ID needs no prefix and must not contain the run id. All three\n492:     fields are required and must equal the ``RunContext``'s, so a record with a\n493:     missing identity, a partial identity or a foreign run's identity is not this\n494:     run's material and never resolves.\n495:     \"\"\"\n496:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n497:         return None\n498:     if not all(isinstance(run.get(key), str) and run.get(key) for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS):\n499:         return None\n500:     for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS:\n501:         if record.get(key) != run.get(key):\n502:             return None\n503:     return tuple(run[key] for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS)\n504: \n505: \n506: def _material_resolves(record: dict, run: dict, results_dir) -> bool:\n507:     \"\"\"Whether the record's referenced retained material exists **and has content**.\n508: \n509:     Only a record that names retained material (``content_ref``) and whose material\n510:     can be re-read from this run's retention root counts. A record with no\n511:     ``content_ref`` — an analyst report indexed only in memory — has no traceable\n512:     source material, so it is **not** admissible evidence: the prose itself is not\n513:     a retained source. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``\n7:    so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. If the provider does\n8:    not support structured output (rare; mostly older Ollama models), the\n9:    wrap is skipped and the agent uses free-text generation instead.\n10: 2. At invocation, run the structured call and render the result back to\n11:    markdown. If the structured call itself fails for any reason\n12:    (malformed JSON from a weak model, transient provider issue), fall\n13:    back to a plain ``llm.invoke`` so the pipeline never blocks.\n14: \n15: Centralising the pattern here keeps the agent factories small and ensures\n16: all three agents log the same warnings when fallback fires.\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: import logging\n22: from collections.abc import Callable\n23: from typing import Any, TypeVar\n24: \n25: from pydantic import BaseModel\n26: \n27: from tradingagents.llm_clients.budget_transport import terminal_request_status\n28: \n29: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n30: \n31: T = TypeVar(\"T\", bound=BaseModel)\n32: \n33: # Schema-only structured output binds exactly one tool (the schema itself), so a\n34: # model that reaches for a search tool emits an unknown tool call and the whole\n35: # structured attempt is discarded for a free-text retry. Agents on this path\n36: # state the constraint explicitly rather than relying on the binding alone\n37: # (#1130).\n38: NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS = (\n39:     \"Use only the evidence provided in this prompt. Do not call external tools \"\n40:     \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n41: )\n42: \n43: \n44: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n45:     \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n46: \n47:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n48:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n49:     \"\"\"\n50:     try:\n51:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n52:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n53:         logger.warning(\n54:             \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n55:             \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n56:             agent_name, exc,\n57:         )\n58:         return None\n59: \n60: \n61: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n62:     \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n63: \n64:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n65:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n66:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n67: \n68:     A terminal C0 failure (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``, ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` or\n69:     ``FAILED``) is re-raised instead of falling back: the fallback is a second\n70:     model turn, and on a metered run it must not become an unbudgeted send\n71:     (NFR-01 / INV-02). Only ordinary structured-output misses fall through to\n72:     ``None`` for the caller's free-text fallback.\n73:     \"\"\"\n74:     if structured_llm is None:\n75:         return None\n76:     try:\n77:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n78:         if result is None:\n79:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n80:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n81:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n82:             raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n83:         return result\n84:     except Exception as exc:\n85:         # The transport owner module is the single authority on which\n86:         # exceptions are terminal and on unwrapping wrapped causes. Fail closed:\n87:         # if the classifier itself cannot run, treat the failure as terminal\n88:         # rather than risk an unbudgeted free-text retry.\n89:         try:\n90:             terminal = terminal_request_status(exc) is not None\n91:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed on an unusable classifier\n92:             terminal = True\n93:         if terminal:\n94:             # Re-raise the original failure (not a wrapper) so the graph keeps\n95:             # its terminal status and the run ends without retrying.\n96:             raise\n97:         logger.warning(\n98:             \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n99:             agent_name, exc,\n100:         )\n101:         return None\n102: \n103: \n104: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n105:     structured_llm: Any | None,\n106:     plain_llm: Any,\n107:     prompt: Any,\n108:     render: Callable[[T], str],\n109:     agent_name: str,\n110: ) -> str:\n111:     \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n112:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n113:     if result is not None:\n114:         return render(result)\n115:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content"

Extend TradingAgents at `upstream-baseline` (`9fa1196fffbcfd9de5146d2dd2869df84ab99838`); retain the single-stock graph, providers, CLI and Python entry points. No brokerage execution, arbitrary prose arithmetic, or new external provider is in scope.\n4: \n5: | Requirement | Planned owner module | Contract and authority |\n6: | --- | --- | --- |\n7: | FR-01 / INV-01 | `tradingagents/graph/publication_gate.py` | Build run-local evidence index, validate candidate rating and argument references, and return an approved decision or blocked status/reason. Model text is advisory. Apply the same outcome before CLI/API/report/memory publication. No free-text fallback around the gate. |\n8: | FR-02 | `tradingagents/agents/verified_metrics.py` | Validate provenance, comparable periods, units and operands; produce immutable verified records keyed by metric ID. Resolve controlled fields by ID, not model-supplied values. |\n9: | FR-03 | `tradingagents/agents/sentiment_coverage.py` | Normalize three tool results to coverage, source reasons and nullable score. Report and downstream consume the same state. |\n10: | NFR-01 / INV-02 | `tradingagents/llm_clients/request_budget.py` | Atomically reserve one slot for each in-scope actual send; scope counters per run, including both model tiers. Disable implicit retry for supported course runs. |\n11: | NFR-02 | `tradingagents/llm_clients/context_limit.py` | Prepare final messages for analyst closure and the neutral risk debater; preserve mandatory blocks and reject requests that cannot fit. |\n12: \n13: Integrate at existing graph and client seams. At dispatch: prepare final messages → apply context limit where scoped → reserve budget → send. Load existing market and sentiment inputs; attach verified metrics and coverage; run debate and candidate generation; gate candidate before official sinks. Treat any display of intermediate model text as unverified and keep candidate text out of official output on refusal. Historical settlement is outside the metered analysis scope.\n14: \n15: Use fixed fixtures and fake transports for deterministic tests, then separately smoke-test configured live integration. Emit run ID, publication status/reason, verified metric counts, sentiment coverage, request count and message byte size without credentials or raw prompts. See [trace matrix](docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md) and [runtime policies](docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md).\n16: \n17: Plan is read-only. A human approves scope, interface and tests before Build starts. A separate reviewer runs verification and records a verdict. Amend D1/D2, tests and governance together when a contract changes; changes to safety enforcement require an ADR and explicit human approval.\n18: \n19: ## Integration and change control\n20: \n21: [C0–C5](docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md) defines shared records, function boundaries, state keys and failure precedence. Each component owns its authoritative records; legacy report strings remain compatible views. Shared-file changes are integrated by the designated coordinator.\n22: \n23: The application retains the upstream package layout. Verify the final submission mapping to the required `src/` and `test/` layout before packaging. Approval and outstanding verification items are recorded in [review records](docs/review-memo.md)."

The blueprint assigns exactly one owner module to each new design element. Existing modules remain integration adapters; do not duplicate business rules across CLI, API and reports.\n4: \n5: | Requirement | Owner and boundary |\n6: | --- | --- |\n7: | FR-01 / INV-01 | Publication gate owns the official outcome; pass its result to all sinks, including memory. |\n8: | FR-02 | Verified metrics owns arithmetic and reference resolution. Downstream renders resolved values. |\n9: | FR-03 | Sentiment coverage owns missingness and reasons. Consumers do not invent numeric defaults. |\n10: | NFR-01 / INV-02 | Request budget owns the atomic run counter. Only a reserved dispatch may send. |\n11: | NFR-02 | Context limit owns payload sizing and deterministic reduction; it cannot bypass the budget or remove mandatory content. |\n12: \n13: For each new or modified module and function, document the associated requirement, ADR and invariant where applicable in a short comment or docstring. Integration code may orchestrate but cannot override an authoritative rejection. The team must name a shared-file integration owner and exact paths for state/schema, reporting and dispatch changes. Each feature may use an approved fake producer/consumer for independent tests; integration tests must later replace those doubles with real connected components. CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE means no send or budget debit for that rejected request.\n16: 2. If context is ready but C4 has no slot, return BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Both terminal paths suppress any earlier candidate as an official final recommendation.\n17: 3. Invalid financial records are excluded; optional sentiment failures preserve per-source reasons and UNKNOWN/null where appropriate. Continue usable analysis rather than treating absent sentiment as a neutral signal or unconditional publication failure.\n18: 4. On nonzero source coverage but failed assessment, keep PARTIAL_DATA/AVAILABLE and record assessment failure with UNKNOWN/null. Coverage is collection state, not model confidence.\n19: 5. Gate any resulting candidate at every official sink. A source placeholder is not substantive evidence. Publication passes only when C1 succeeds, regardless of a model's requested rating.\n20: \n21: A user retry after a terminal failure is a new run with a new identity; do not resume the same metered identity with a fresh counter. Invalid configuration or unknown contract version blocks the affected task before live dispatch. Record implementation and case evidence for each failure path.\n22: \n23: Each enforcing component emits the specified receipt fields. Verification records identify the producing path, implementation revision and observed result."

Air-gapped tests use fixed inputs, fake transports and isolated state; a live smoke run is separate and cannot replace offline coverage. Problem statement\n\nShortened-ID copying happens in a place a prompt cannot fully control: the model must copy an opaque long ID. Two corrections are available:\n- **prompt asking again** — cannot enforce only at the model level; ruled out by the evaluation table (\"prompts and settings only\" → Reject);\n- **deterministic alias resolution in the program** — enforcement stays at the model level: shorter, stable per-invocation tokens (`E1`, `A1`) that the program maps to the canonical record.\n\nThe proposed design therefore sits at the existing seams, and **nothing about acceptance, release, or sinks changes**.\n\n### 1.1 What \"plain `E1` is only a selection in the current menu\" means\nIn the menu the model sees during one call, `E1` is a **positional label**. The same `E1` in a different invocation or a different run may point to different evidence. The program cannot know which run a bare `E1` \"belongs to\" unless it resolves it against **that invocation's** menu. Inside the run that produced the menu, `E1` is not \"evidence with ID E1\"; it is \"the first entry of the menu I was given\". So resolving it requires (a) the frozen menu for the run and (b) the model call itself. Once resolved, only the canonical full ID is stored (C1: \"consumers must not infer meaning from ID spelling\").\n\n### 1.2 The mapping is frozen per invocation\nThe alias -> canonical mapping is a read-only mapping built from that call's actual (already-rendered) menu, then bound in the node closure for that invocation:\n- it is built **after** the menu text is rendered, from the **exact** list rendered;\n- it is immutable (read-only) and never rebuilt from state during resolution;\n- it never changes within the invocation; a model call after state changes cannot resolve against a different menu (see case O-FR01-ALIAS-MAP-FREEZE).\n\n## 2. Interface contracts\n\n### 3.1 Minimal change (owner: FR-01; integrator approval required)\n\n**A. `tradingagents/graph/publication_gate.py` — private helper, no public signature change**\n```\nmake_evidence_aliases(index) -> Mapping[str, str]        # read-only {\"E1\": canonical, \"E2\": ...} in menu order\nmake_argument_aliases(argument_index, run=None) -> Mapping[str, str]\nresolve_evidence_alias(refs, aliases) -> (canonical_list | None, invalid_pairs)\nresolve_argument_alias(refs, aliases)  -> (canonical_list | None, invalid_pairs)\n```\nBehavior:\n- **Input**: `refs` is the model-supplied list; `aliases` is the frozen read-only mapping from one invocation.\n- **Output**: a list of canonical full IDs, or `None` (plus diagnostic pairs). `None` is returned if any `ref` does not exactly match an alias, an exact canonical full ID, or (for evidence) is `''`/whitespace/truncated.\n- **Resolution order (all-or-nothing):** exact alias key, then exact canonical value already in the mapping. Anything else is **invalid**; there is **no fuzzy matching, no prefix/suffix repair, no case folding, no partial acceptance**.\n- **Unknown:** `\"E9\"`, `\"ev:short\"`, empty string, non-str.\n- **Truncated:** `\"E1->\"`? no — the test suite asserts `\"E\"` and `\"E1.\"` and `\"ev:<run>:market\"`-style truncated full IDs are rejected.\n- **Read-only:** returned `MappingProxyType`; mutation raises `TypeError`. Mapping keys and values are the **full menu IDs in menu order**.\n- **Empty menu:** `{}`; any ref is invalid; the menu line says nothing is available (statement already in `evidence_menu`).\n- **Diagnostics helper:** `log_reference_rejection(role, invalid_pairs, reason, logger)` writes **role, the invalid reference string (sanitized: first 64 chars, no raw body, no secrets) and a fixed reason** to a module logger only. It is never part of `PublicationResult`, state, reports, CLI or memory.\n- Public names listed in §2.3 of verification-constraints stay as-is. `EvidenceIndex`, `evaluate_publication`, `validate_argument`, `apply_publication`, `PublicationResult` are unchanged.\n- Documented in the docstring: \"A private adapter. Resolution may 'guess' nothing: the only accepted spellings are the menu's own alias and its own canonical ID.\"\n\n**B. `researchers/bull_researcher.py` and `bear_researcher.py`**\nPer invocation (inside `bull_node`/`bear_node`, after `evidence_block` is built):\n1. Build `alias_map = make_evidence_aliases(state.get(\"evidence_index\"))` as a frozen, read-only mapping and keep it in the node closure's `_invocation_aliases` variable (local, one per call — never a module global, never cached across calls).\n2. Render `evidence_menu` **as before** (legacy canonical line kept for established callers/tests) and **add the alias prefix** to each line:\n   ```\n   - E1  -> <canonical>\n   ```\n3. Prompt instruction: cite **either** the exact alias `E1` **or** the exact full ID from the menu (unchanged sentence plus the alias sentence).\n4. After the structured call, `evidence_ids = tuple(resolve_evidence_alias(structured.evidence_ids, alias_map))`; on `None`, **pass the raw list** to `validate_argument` — the existing validator already returns `None` and the argument is likely rejected, but the safe path is whatever it does: it returns `None`. The node still emits `pending_argument` and the debate state exactly as today.\n5. On rejection, `log_reference_rejection(\"Bull Analyst\", invalid_pairs, \"no exact match for a menu alias or canonical evidence ID\")`.\n6. `pending_argument.evidence_ids` carries **canonical IDs only** (C1 record compatibility).\n- No new API calls; no retries; no fallback path changed (plain free text still mints no argument).\n\n**C. `managers/portfolio_manager.py`**\n- Build `alias_map = make_argument_aliases(state.get(\"argument_index\"), run)` from the **same** accepted list already used to render the `accepted_line` block.\n- Add `A1`, `A2`, … to that block: `- A1 -> <argument_id> (<speaker>; evidence <full ids>)`.\n- After `invoke_structured`, `argument_ids = list(resolve_argument_alias(decision.argument_ids, alias_map))`; on no match, pass the raw list (gate blocks it). All-or-nothing: one unknown ref in a mixed list rejects the PM selection.\n- On rejection: `log_reference_rejection(\"Portfolio Manager\", invalid_pairs, \"no exact match for an accepted-argument alias or canonical argument ID\")`.\n- **No extra model call.** `portfolio_verified_metrics` stays unchanged.\n- `candidate_argument_ids` becomes **canonical IDs only**; the stored candidate is still gated identically.\n\n**D. `agents/schemas.py`** — field descriptions explain the aliases (no model call, no extra field):\n- `DebateArgument.evidence_ids`: mention \"the short `E<n>` alias listed beside each evidence item, or the exact full ID printed next to it\".\n- `PortfolioDecision.argument_ids`: mention \"the short `A<n>` alias listed beside each accepted argument, or its exact full ID\".\n- No validation, no pydantic coercion; invalid output still reaches the validator/gate unchanged.\n\n**Decision ownership:** the gate still decides acceptance and publication. The alias layer only normalizes model input; it never decides acceptance and never registers anything.\n\n### 3.2 The frozen closure (per call)\n```\ndef bull_node(state):\n    menu = evidence_menu(state.get(\"evidence_index\"))      # existing text\n    aliases = make_evidence_aliases(state.get(\"evidence_index\"))  # read-only, built from THAT render\n    ...\n    evidence_ids = resolve_evidence_alias(structured.evidence_ids, aliases)\n```\nThe mapping is built **from the same `EvidenceIndex`/list used to render the menu** and is used only inside this call. `state` is not mutated to hold it.\n\n### 3.3 What is explicitly *not* done\n- No new dependency, provider, model call, retry or fallback.\n- No public reason-code change: only `INVALID_RATING` / `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` can be emitted; the diagnostic logger never touches `publication_result`.\n- No change to gate order, `PublicationResult` fields, `as_state()`/`apply_publication`, sinks or memory.\n- No new state key; `argument_index`, `evidence_index`, `pending_argument` are unchanged in shape.\n\n## 4. Scope\n\n### 4.1 Exact edit paths (all that may be written)\n1. `tradingagents/graph/publication_gate.py`\n2. `tradingagents/agents/researchers/bull_researcher.py`\n3. `tradingagents/agents/researchers/bear_researcher.py`\n4. `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py`\n5. `tradingagents/agents/schemas.py`\n6. **new** `test/offline/test_fr01_reference_aliases.py`\n\nNo `__init__.py` / `__all__` / config / workflow / docs edits. If a new name needs export and export is required, this is a **test design change → stop for approval**.\n\n### 4.2 Baseline code that must remain intact\nAll of `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `tests/`, `test/offline/*` (existing files) and any existing keys/signatures in the six files above. The existing files are preserved; this plan is additive only in the new test file.\n\n### 4.3 Explicit exclusions\n- FR-02, FR-03, NFR-01, NFR-02.\n- Changing *why* the model shortens IDs (that is prompt/model behavior); no prompt change outside the five listed files.\n- Any public API surface or exported symbol change; any allowlist or permission change.\n- Raw receipts or live transcripts committed.\n- Resolving `E<n>` against a menu from a *different* call or run (would be a wrong acceptance path; forbidden).\n\n### 4.4 Frozen fixtures (must exist before the test file is approved)\nPrivate, under a temp dir created by the test; not committed as data:\n- one `RunContext` `A`: `run_id=\"run-a\"`, `ticker=\"AAPL\"`, `as_of_date=\"2026-11-10\"`, `execution_status=\"COMPLETED\"`;\n- one **foreign** `RunContext` `B`: `run_id=\"run-b\"`, same ticker/date;\n- one real retained market snapshot file on disk (reuse the existing `record_market_snapshot` writer with a minimal W-A table) or, if simpler, the existing fixture pattern in `test_fr01_publish_valid.py`; **exact source object to be frozen by the human before approval**;\n- two evidence rows: `E1 -> ev:<run-a>:market_snapshot:call-a`, `E2 -> ev:<run-a>:…:call-b`, each complete (all C1 required fields) with a `content_ref` readable through `resolve_content_ref`;\n- one native argument record for A keyed `arg:bull:run-a:2`;\n- one native argument record for B, only for the cross-run case.\n\n### 4.5 Prompt-change dependency\nThe PM/researcher prompts change, so the **existing test inventory must be checked before Build**: tests that assert on the accepted-arguments block (e.g. `test_fr01_publish_valid.py`, menu-line format regex) require a **full regression**. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.\n21: \n22: Keep three concepts separate:\n23: \n24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.\n25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.\n26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.\n27: \n28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.\n29: \n30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication\n31: \n32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.\n33: \n34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.\n35: \n36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.\n37: \n38: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.\n39: \n40: ## C2 — verified metrics\n41: \n42: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.\n43: \n44: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.\n45: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.\n46: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.\n47: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.\n48: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.\n49: \n50: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.\n51: \n52: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.\n53: \n54: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score\n55: \n56: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.\n57: \n58: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.\n59: \n60: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). AAPL as-of 2026-11-10 therefore covers 2026-11-03 through 2026-11-10. Freeze the clock for date-dependent fixtures. Historical undated content cannot prove window validity. Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.\n61: \n62: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. Never claim these statuses prove that no real-world messages/news exist.\n63: \n64: | Valid logical sources | coverage_status | Sentiment output |\n65: | --- | --- | --- |\n66: | 0/3 | NO_DATA | overall_band UNKNOWN; overall_score null |\n67: | 1/3 or 2/3 | PARTIAL_DATA | Coverage remains explicit; any measured score uses valid evidence only |\n68: | 3/3 | AVAILABLE | Coverage available; score still requires a valid assessment |\n69: \n70: Coverage is authoritative data state; the model cannot increase it. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. A genuine measured Neutral/5.0 remains legal.\n71: \n72: Missing scores never become 0 or 5 and never enter a numerical mean. Structured state, analyst message, downstream prompt and persisted/rendered report must agree. Handle nullable scores without numeric-format errors. Apply the contract to structured **and** free-text fallback; model narrative cannot override authoritative coverage. Keep the existing sentiment_report text as a compatibility view; the new sentiment_assessment record below is authoritative. Both must agree. Internal schema adaptation may change, but the v1 shared record does not drift silently.\n73: \n74: The original baseline stores `sentiment_report` as text and requires a nonnull numeric SentimentReport score. Updating only the prompt cannot establish this contract. No raw social bodies or credentials belong in public evidence. Missing optional sentiment does not stop otherwise valid market/fundamental analysis; C1 still decides publication.\n75: \n76: ## C4 — atomic per-run model dispatch\n77: \n78: Supported scope: one single-stock main analysis, both model tiers, structured/fallback requests and application retries. Count actual outgoing model attempts, not nodes, tool invocations, callbacks or tokens. Historical settlement is excluded. Disable SDK/transport implicit retries in supported course runs; unsupported hidden-retry modes are outside the verified configuration, not silently compliant.\n79: \n80: Budget state: positive integer `limit`, charged sends, active reservations and exhaustion. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation. Validate C5 first so context rejection obtains no reservation.\n81: \n82: No slot => BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no request, no official recommendation. Limit 3 allows exactly 3 attempts; the fourth is refused. Concurrent runs do not share counters. Include application fallback/retry attempts separately. C4 does not promise a monetary or token cap. Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.\n83: \n84: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context\n85: \n86: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. Other analyst turns and risk roles are not implicitly covered. Before reserving C4, fully expand/convert the scoped final message sequence into one agreed provider-facing representation.\n87: \n88: Canonical v1 measurement: the final provider-facing message array encoded as JSON with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon) without optional whitespace, allow_nan=False, then UTF-8. Use the ChatMessage representation below and freeze byte fixtures before implementation. Do not measure before template expansion or change representation after measuring. Tool schemas and other separately bound fields are excluded from this message metric and must be recorded/bounded separately; this is not a cap on the whole HTTP body.\n89: \n90: Required blocks: role/task identity; standing safety/publication rules; ticker/date/run identity; current required evidence/verified metrics/source coverage; and the active tool-call/result exchange. Optional blocks: explicitly marked older discussion/history. A tool-call/result pair is indivisible; if a member is required, preserve the whole pair. Text-wrapped tools retain name, arguments and corresponding result. Removing context cannot delete authoritative evidence/state from storage.\n91: \n92: At the configured 65536-byte acceptance cap: short input passes unchanged. If oversized, remove optional groups oldest first (stable original index for ties), reassemble, reinject critical constraints and remeasure. Do not summarize required evidence with another unmetered model call. If required blocks cannot fit or pairing cannot be preserved, return CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE; zero send, reservation and debit. Same normalized input/config produces identical prepared output. Run final retention/pairing checks before C4.\n93: \n94: This byte cap does not implement the separate D2 token-budget requirement. ADR-001 records that architecture design and the remaining tokenizer/model-capacity validation. Do not infer token counts from bytes/4 or claim provider safety from 64 KiB alone.\n95: \n96: ## Contract-change and approval record\n97: \n98: Before implementation, record requirement IDs, contract revision, baseline SHA, exact read/edit paths, fixture/case revision, reviewer and approval time. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Feature PRs link the approved plan and actual evidence; the coordinator runs integrated regressions before release.\n99: \n100: \n101: ## V1 shared record layout\n102: \n103: Version field: `contract_version = \"1.0\"`. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. Lists have deterministic order; ID-indexed registries are mappings, not unordered output prose.\n104: \n105: | Record | Required shared fields beyond identity | Owner |\n106: | --- | --- | --- |\n107: | RunContext | contract_version, execution_status, request_limit (positive integer) | Existing graph/run entry; integration by coordinator |\n108: | EvidenceRecord | evidence_id, source_kind, vendor, source_ref, content_ref, window_start, window_end | FR-01 collection/index adapter |\n109: | AcceptedArgument | argument_id, claim (nonempty text), evidence_ids (nonempty list) | FR-01 validates against run-local evidence; a model flag is not acceptance |\n110: | CandidateDecision | rating (untrusted string or null), argument_ids | Model/adapters produce; C1 decides |\n111: | PublicationResult | publication_status, reason_codes, rating (allowed string or null), argument_ids, evidence_ids | FR-01 |\n112: | Operand | role, value (finite decimal string), unit, period, source_ref, field_ref | FR-02 input adapter; roles current/prior/numerator/denominator/reference |\n113: | MetricRequest | kind (yoy/ratio/price_delta), operands | FR-02 input |\n114: | VerifiedMetric | metric_id, kind, operands, result_value (decimal string), result_unit, formula, source_refs | FR-02 immutable run-local registry |\n115: | MetricResult | status (VERIFIED/UNVERIFIABLE), metric (VerifiedMetric or null), reason_codes | FR-02 |\n116: | SourceOutcome | source_id, window_start, window_end, available (bool), valid_record_count, reason_codes, evidence_refs | FR-03 normalization adapter |\n117: | SentimentCoverage | coverage_status, valid_sources, total_sources (=3), sources (mapping keyed news/stocktwits/reddit) | FR-03 deterministic coverage |\n118: | SentimentAssessment | all SentimentCoverage fields, assessment_status (MEASURED/UNKNOWN), overall_band, overall_score, confidence, assessment_reason_codes, narrative | FR-03 deterministic finalization |\n119: | ContextBlock | group_id, required (bool), messages (list of ChatMessage); grouping metadata is never sent to the model | NFR-02 scoped adapter |\n120: | PreparedRequest | status (READY/CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE), messages (list or null), message_bytes, original_message_bytes, dropped_group_ids, required_groups_ok | NFR-02 or nonreducing adapter |\n121: | Reservation | reservation_id, run_id, state (reserved/charged/cancelled); opaque to other features | NFR-01 |\n122: \n123: `Operand.period` is `{kind, start, end, label}`: kind is quarter/year/instant, start/end are ISO dates, and label records the source's fiscal period or quote timestamp. Currency and scale are part of unit (for example USD vs USD_millions); conversion must be explicit and preserve original operands. Do not silently take abs(capex), invent comparable periods or round source values to make a fixture match. An EvidenceRecord source_ref identifies the source, while content_ref locates the retained shareable material/fixture; an ID with no resolvable retained material is insufficient.\n124: \n125: For SentimentAssessment, overall_band is one existing measured band or UNKNOWN. overall_score is a finite float in [0,10] for MEASURED, otherwise null. confidence keeps the existing low/medium/high vocabulary; UNKNOWN uses low and is not a measured weak-neutral signal. Missing sources are unavailable with reasons; valid sources have valid_record_count >=1. Missing uncollected source entries are normalized as unavailable with NOT_COLLECTED rather than increasing the denominator or silently disappearing. Extra providers do not count as fourth sources. Source order is news, stocktwits, reddit.\n126: \n127: `ChatMessage` contains provider-facing role, content and, when present, name/tool_call_id/tool_calls/reasoning_content. Preserve content strings or JSON-compatible content blocks without paraphrasing. Preserve each tool call's id, type, function name and arguments plus the paired tool result. Reasoning fields required by the selected provider's tool round-trip are mandatory if present. Do not add ContextBlock metadata to ChatMessage. The cap measures the agreed canonical message representation, not HTTP whitespace, the whole body, output tokens or hidden provider overhead.\n128: \n129: ## V1 callable boundaries (specification signatures, no implementation)\n130: \n131: Inputs are read-only to consumers. Return the declared records; do not attach extra authoritative fields through prose. Signatures below describe Python-callable boundaries; they do not create five network services.\n132: \n133: | Planned owner | Public v1 call | Behavior |\n134: | --- | --- | --- |\n135: | publication_gate.py | validate_argument(argument, evidence_index, run) -> AcceptedArgument or validation failure | Check current-run references before acceptance |\n136: | publication_gate.py | evaluate_publication(candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run) -> PublicationResult | Recheck accepted references and rating; one result for all official sinks |\n137: | verified_metrics.py | verify_metric(request, run) -> MetricResult | Compute from validated operands, register only verified records |\n138: | verified_metrics.py | resolve_metric(metric_id, registry, run) -> VerifiedMetric or null | Resolve trusted ID; never accept a caller-supplied replacement value |\n139: | sentiment_coverage.py | normalize_source(raw_result, source_id, run, window_start, window_end) -> SourceOutcome | Derive availability from collection receipts and approved metadata rules |\n140: | sentiment_coverage.py | build_sentiment_coverage(sources, run) -> SentimentCoverage | Count three logical sources once each |\n141: | sentiment_coverage.py | finalize_sentiment(coverage, model_assessment_or_null, run) -> SentimentAssessment | Coverage is authoritative; validate score/band; no imputation |\n142: | context_limit.py | prepare_context(blocks, max_message_bytes=65536) -> PreparedRequest | Only the two scoped sites reduce; reject irreducible context |\n143: | request_budget.py | RequestBudget(run_id, limit); try_reserve() -> Reservation or null; charge_attempt(ticket); cancel_before_send(ticket); snapshot() | Atomic lifecycle; cancellation only when transport is known not to have started |\n144: | request_budget.py | dispatch(prepared, budget, send) -> sender's normal response type | Require READY, reserve, charge at attempt boundary, invoke send exactly once; refusal is a typed failure, never a Hold/default rating |\n145: \n146: The sender callable accepts the prepared messages and performs exactly one underlying request with SDK retries disabled. Application fallback/retries call dispatch again. Dispatch failure types are BudgetExhausted, ContextTooLarge and ProviderFailure (defined in the responsible owner module); the graph entry maps them to C0 terminal state. Provider failures after an ambiguous attempt remain charged. Snapshot separates charged attempts, known actual sends and unknown-delivery attempts; a connection attempt is not claimed to be a billed model response.\n147: \n148: Publication evaluation first respects C0 terminal failure/incomplete execution (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or RUN_NOT_COMPLETE); then rejects an invalid rating; then rejects insufficient references. APPROVED has an allowed rating, nonempty accepted argument/evidence references and no rejection reasons. BLOCKED always has rating=null. An incomplete workflow cannot publish an earlier candidate.\n149: \n150: ## V1 graph handoff and compatibility\n151: \n152: Add the following keys to the existing AgentState through narrow integration edits: course_run (RunContext), evidence_index, argument_index, verified_metrics, sentiment_assessment and publication_result. These are separate state keys; do not have parallel nodes overwrite an entire common nested dictionary. Existing nodes own their existing report strings. New owner records are not reconstructed from those strings. Avoid new dependencies or replacement of the orchestrator.\n153: \n154: For sentiment, the analyst emits sentiment_assessment and renders its legacy sentiment_report from that same record, including the model-message/report views. At 0/3, the selected v1 path skips the sentiment model call and creates a deterministic missing-data narrative with UNKNOWN/null. With data, finalize the model assessment while preserving coverage; provider/free-text fallback cannot restore a made-up default score. The FR-03 task plan tests schema/renderer compatibility before selecting the internal Pydantic adaptation. FR-01 can publish from valid non-sentiment evidence when its own gate passes.\n155: \n156: The shared model client receives PreparedRequest. At the two NFR-02 sites use prepare_context; elsewhere use a nonreducing READY adapter so NFR-01 covers all sends without accidentally applying a 64 KiB cap to every call. All branches then use the same C4 dispatch boundary. Tests can use fixed fake producers/consumers until integration, but combined graph acceptance needs the real connected owner modules.\n157: \n158: ## Working defaults and limits with different purposes\n159: \n160: | Setting | V1 choice / purpose | Change rule |\n161: | --- | --- | --- |\n162: | Application baseline | 9fa1196; retain existing package layout | New baseline needs explicit rationale and regressions |\n163: | Local environment | Reuse verified Python 3.11 environment; record exact patch/dependencies | Align a team-approved baseline when needed, no automatic reinstall |\n164: | Course profile model | School CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash for both tiers; explicit thinking-disabled request after compatibility check | Record actual settings; do not infer backend revision from alias |\n165: | Course profile output allowance | 4096 tokens as initial run-profile choice, not an acceptance threshold | Raise only with a truncation reason and recorded configuration |\n166: | Product request_limit | 40 per single-stock run as initial configurable profile | Revisit against completed baseline; D1 hard rule is actual requests <= configured limit |\n167: | NFR-01 boundary fixture | limit 3, exactly-three succeeds, fourth refuses | Fixed test condition; not the normal application's default |\n168: | NFR-02 message cap | 65536 bytes at analyst closure and neutral risk role | Normal configurable setting; changes update the affected fixtures/contracts |\n169: | Token architecture proposal | 16384 input tokens, 80% trigger remains unactivated design pending counting/capacity evidence | Not an automatic global gate or an extra feature |\n170: \n171: Production metered resume remains disabled until counter restoration is implemented and verified.\n172: \n173: ## Change control\n174: \n175: Internal class and function organization may vary while preserving shared record names, types, authority and failure semantics. Changes to public fields, source-validity rules, thresholds or shared dispatch/publication paths require a versioned contract/test revision and affected-owner review. FR-01 / INV-01: the manager\n5: writes **only** the internal candidate (``candidate_decision``,\n6: ``candidate_rating``, ``candidate_argument_ids``); the publication gate promotes\n7: it to the official ``final_trade_decision`` / ``final_rating`` on approval, so a\n8: refused candidate never reaches the memory log, CLI display or saved reports.\n9: When a provider does not expose structured output, the agent falls back to\n10: free-text generation and the rating is read from that text — but with no\n11: argument ids, so the gate blocks it.\n12: \n13: Both decision paths meet before the node returns. Order follows the registry's own key order\n38:     and is the same on both decision paths. The passed state is only read.\n39:     \"\"\"\n40:     run = state.get(\"course_run\") if isinstance(state, dict) else None\n41:     registry = state.get(\"verified_metrics\") if isinstance(state, dict) else None\n42:     if not isinstance(run, dict) or not isinstance(registry, dict) or not registry:\n43:         return []\n44:     resolved = []\n45:     for metric_id in registry:\n46:         record = resolve_metric(metric_id, registry, run)\n47:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n48:             continue\n49:         if record.get(\"metric_id\") != metric_id:\n50:             continue\n51:         resolved.append({\n52:             \"metric_id\": metric_id,\n53:             \"result_value\": record.get(\"result_value\"),\n54:             \"result_unit\": record.get(\"result_unit\"),\n55:         })\n56:     return resolved\n57: \n58: \n59: def create_portfolio_manager(llm):\n60:     structured_llm = bind_structured(llm, PortfolioDecision, \"Portfolio Manager\")\n61: \n62:     def portfolio_manager_node(state) -> dict:\n63:         instrument_context = get_instrument_context_from_state(state)\n64:         portfolio_context = get_portfolio_context_from_state(state)\n65: \n66:         history = state[\"risk_debate_state\"][\"history\"]\n67:         risk_debate_state = state[\"risk_debate_state\"]\n68:         research_plan = state[\"investment_plan\"]\n69:         trader_plan = state[\"trader_investment_plan\"]\n70: \n71:         past_context = state.get(\"past_context\", \"\")\n72:         lessons_line = (\n73:             f\"- Lessons from prior decisions and outcomes:\\n{past_context}\\n\"\n74:             if past_context\n75:             else \"\"\n76:         )\n77: \n78:         # FR-01: the decision must rest on arguments the program accepted. The\n79:         # accepted argument IDs are injected here so the manager can cite them.\n80:         accepted = state.get(\"accepted_arguments\") or []\n81:         accepted_line = \"\"\n82:         if accepted:\n83:             listed = \"\\n\".join(\n84:                 f\"- {a['argument_id']} ({a['speaker']}; evidence {', '.join(a['evidence_ids'])})\"\n85:                 for a in accepted\n86:             )\n87:             accepted_line = f\"\\n**Accepted arguments** (cite their IDs in argument_ids):\\n{listed}\\n\"\n88: \n89:         prompt = f\"\"\"As the Portfolio Manager, synthesize the risk analysts' debate and deliver the final trading decision.\n90: \n91: {instrument_context}\n92: \n93: {portfolio_context}\n94: \n95: ---\n96: \n97: **Rating Scale** (use exactly one):\n98: - **Buy**: Strong conviction to enter or add to position\n99: - **Overweight**: Favorable outlook, gradually increase exposure\n100: - **Hold**: Maintain current position, no action needed\n101: - **Underweight**: Reduce exposure, take partial profits\n102: - **Sell**: Exit position or avoid entry\n103: \n104: **Context:**\n105: - Research Manager's investment plan: **{research_plan}**\n106: - Trader's transaction proposal: **{trader_plan}**\n107: {lessons_line}\n108: **Risk Analysts Debate History:**\n109: {history}\n110: {accepted_line}\n111: \n112: ---\n113: \n114: Ground every conclusion in specific evidence from the analysts. The risk debate always contains conflicting stances; deciding which is stronger is the job, so conflict alone is not a reason to Hold. Commit to the stronger case, sized by how decisively it wins. Choose Hold only when the evidence is still balanced after that weighing, or too thin to support a call; do not force a direction to appear decisive. Weigh the analysts on their merits, independent of speaking order.\n115: \n116: ## Output\n117: \n118: Write these sections, in this order, starting with the rating on its own line:\n119: \n120: - **Rating**: exactly one of Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell\n121: - **Executive Summary**: the call and how to act on it\n122: - **Investment Thesis**: the evidence that decided it, and what would change it\n123: \n124: {NO_EXTERNAL_TOOLS}{get_language_instruction()}\"\"\"\n125: \n126:         # The typed rating is the decision; the rendered text only carries it.\n127:         # Read back from text, a rating the thesis quotes could replace it.\n128:         decision = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, \"Portfolio Manager\")\n129:         if decision is not None:\n130:             candidate_body = render_pm_decision(decision)\n131:             candidate_rating = decision.rating.value\n132:             argument_ids = list(decision.argument_ids or [])\n133:         else:\n134:             # FR-01: no free-text rating fallback around the gate. A free-text\n135:             # answer carries no structured argument_ids, so the candidate decision\n136:             # is kept but cannot publish — the gate blocks it for lack of evidence.\n137:             candidate_body = llm.invoke(prompt).content\n138:             candidate_rating = parse_rating(candidate_body)\n139:             argument_ids = []\n140: \n141:         # Both paths meet here: re-read this run's verified metrics by ID.\n142:         portfolio_verified_metrics = _resolved_metrics(state)\n143: \n144:         new_risk_debate_state = {\n145:             \"history\": risk_debate_state[\"history\"],\n146:             \"aggressive_history\": risk_debate_state[\"aggressive_history\"],\n147:             \"conservative_history\": risk_debate_state[\"conservative_history\"],\n148:             \"neutral_history\": risk_debate_state[\"neutral_history\"],\n149:             \"latest_speaker\": \"Judge\",\n150:             \"current_aggressive_response\": risk_debate_state[\"current_aggressive_response\"],\n151:             \"current_conservative_response\": risk_debate_state[\"current_conservative_response\"],\n152:             \"current_neutral_response\": risk_debate_state[\"current_neutral_response\"],\n153:             \"count\": risk_debate_state[\"count\"],\n154:         }\n155: \n156:         # FR-01 / INV-01: the Portfolio Manager writes only the internal candidate.\n157:         # The publication gate promotes it to the official fields on approval; on\n158:         # refusal nothing here can reach an official sink.\n159:         return {\n160:             \"risk_debate_state\": new_risk_debate_state,\n161:             \"candidate_decision\": candidate_body,\n162:             \"candidate_rating\": candidate_rating,\n163:             \"candidate_argument_ids\": argument_ids,\n164:             \"portfolio_verified_metrics\": portfolio_verified_metrics,\n165:         }\n166: \n167:     return portfolio_manager_node"

                "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/graph/publication_gate.py, lines 1-920\n1: \"\"\"Deterministic publication gate for FR-01 / INV-01.\n2: \n3: Owner module for the release decision described in\n4: ``architecture-blueprint.md`` (FR-01 row) and ``docs/architecture/invariants.md``\n5: (INV-01). The gate is the single authority for whether a candidate recommendation\n6: becomes an official decision. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the\n7: program itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating\n8: fallback is honoured around the gate.\n9: \n10: Design (plan revision 1, superseded by the R8-B C1 v1.0 section below):\n11: - The run's evidence index is built *before* the first debate turn from material\n12:   the run actually retained (the market analyst's verified snapshots), so every\n13:   accepted argument cites material that exists in this run. An analyst report is\n14:   **not** evidence: prose alone has no traceable retained source. The index is\n15:   carried on the graph state as **plain, msgpack-safe data** (``evidence_index`` =\n16:   an ``evidence_id`` -> record mapping), never as an object, so checkpointed runs\n17:   can be saved and resumed.\n18: - Bull/Bear submit structured ``evidence_ids``; the program validates each against\n19:   the run index and only then mints a run-bound ``argument_id``.\n20: - The Portfolio Manager selects from those accepted ``argument_ids``.\n21: - ``evaluate_publication`` checks the whole chain (recommendation -> accepted\n22:   argument -> this run's retained material) and returns one ``PublicationResult``.\n23:   ``apply_publication`` projects that result onto the run state used by the sinks\n24:   (CLI, API, reports, memory).\n25: \n26: Only two outward rejection reasons exist: ``INVALID_RATING`` and\n27: ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references\n28: all map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,\n29: ``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.\n30: \n31: C1 v1.0 (``evaluate_publication`` / ``PublicationResult``):\n32: - The authoritative indexes are ID -> record **mappings**: ``argument_index``\n33:   keyed by ``argument_id``, ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The old\n34:   ``index_to_state`` lists and ``accepted_arguments`` stay as a compatibility\n35:   layer and are never a release authority.\n36: - Rows are applied in order: C0 terminal/incomplete execution, then an invalid\n37:   rating, then insufficient references; APPROVED is the only state with a rating.\n38: - Every record is identity-checked against the ``RunContext`` (a foreign run's\n39:   material never resolves) and every reference is rechecked from the candidate,\n40:   never trusted from the model.\n41: - ``PublicationResult`` is the one result all four sinks (CLI, Python return,\n42:   saved report, decision memory) consume; ``PublicationRequiredError`` refuses an\n43:   official write when a state carries no real result.\n44: \"\"\"\n45: \n46: from __future__ import annotations\n47: \n48: from dataclasses import dataclass, field\n49: from pathlib import Path\n50: \n51: from tradingagents.agents.rating import RATINGS_5_TIER\n52: \n53: # The analyst state keys whose non-empty text is admissible as run material.\n54: _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS = (\n55:     \"market_report\",\n56:     \"sentiment_report\",\n57:     \"news_report\",\n58:     \"fundamentals_report\",\n59: )\n60: \n61: # Outward rejection reasons (D1 / runtime-policy-catalog.md).\n62: INVALID_RATING = \"INVALID_RATING\"\n63: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE = \"INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\"\n64: \n65: # The five-tier scale as a set of canonical strings, for O(1) membership tests.\n66: _RATING_SET = frozenset(RATINGS_5_TIER)\n67: \n68: # Publication status values carried on the run state.\n69: APPROVED = \"APPROVED\"\n70: BLOCKED = \"BLOCKED\"\n71: \n72: # C0 execution states. Only COMPLETED may publish; each terminal failure keeps its\n73: # own reason code, and any other non-completed state is RUN_NOT_COMPLETE.\n74: EXECUTION_COMPLETED = \"COMPLETED\"\n75: EXECUTION_FAILED = \"FAILED\"\n76: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = \"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED\"\n77: CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE = \"CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE\"\n78: RUN_NOT_COMPLETE = \"RUN_NOT_COMPLETE\"\n79: # Terminal failures that keep their own code. FAILED is terminal too, but its\n80: # outward reason is RUN_NOT_COMPLETE (see ``evaluate_publication``).\n81: _TERMINAL_EXECUTION = (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE, EXECUTION_FAILED)\n82: # Terminal states whose reason code is its own name.\n83: _TERMINAL_EXECUTION_NAMED = (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE)\n84: \n85: \n86: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n87: class EvidenceRecord:\n88:     \"\"\"One admissible piece of run material, addressed by a run-bound id.\"\"\"\n89: \n90:     evidence_id: str\n91:     source: str      # analyst state key the material came from, e.g. \"market_report\"\n92:     excerpt: str     # short, human-resolvable pointer into the material\n93:     run_id: str\n94: \n95: \n96: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n97: class ArgumentRecord:\n98:     \"\"\"An argument accepted only because each cited evidence id resolved in this run.\"\"\"\n99: \n100:     argument_id: str\n101:     speaker: str                  # \"Bull Analyst\" / \"Bear Analyst\"\n102:     text: str\n103:     evidence_ids: tuple[str, ...]\n104: \n105: \n106: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n107: class GateOutcome:\n108:     \"\"\"The single release decision for a run.\"\"\"\n109: \n110:     status: str                              # APPROVED | BLOCKED\n111:     reason: str | None                       # INVALID_RATING | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\n112:     rating: str | None                       # a 5-tier rating only when APPROVED\n113:     resolved_chain: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)\n114:     # resolved_chain items: (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n115: \n116:     @property\n117:     def approved(self) -> bool:\n118:         return self.status == APPROVED\n119: \n120: \n121: @dataclass(frozen=True)\n122: class PublicationResult:\n123:     \"\"\"The one authoritative C1 v1.0 publication result, shared by all four sinks.\n124: \n125:     Identity is copied from the ``RunContext``; it is never inferred from the\n126:     spelling of an ID. ``rating`` is a 5-tier rating only on APPROVED and is\n127:     ``None`` on BLOCKED, so a refused candidate's rating can never be read from\n128:     this record. The candidate's prose is deliberately not a field here: the\n129:     result carries the verdict and the validated references, never the body.\n130:     \"\"\"\n131: \n132:     contract_version: str          # \"1.0\"\n133:     run_id: str\n134:     ticker: str\n135:     as_of_date: str\n136:     publication_status: str        # APPROVED | BLOCKED\n137:     reason_codes: tuple[str, ...]  # rejection reasons, empty on APPROVED\n138:     rating: str | None             # resolved_chain items: (argument_id, evidence_id, source)\n143: \n144:     @property\n145:     def approved(self) -> bool:\n146:         return self.publication_status == APPROVED\n147: \n148:     @property\n149:     def reason(self) -> str | None:\n150:         \"\"\"The first rejection reason, for the legacy single-reason state fields.\"\"\"\n151:         return self.reason_codes[0] if self.reason_codes else None\n152: \n153:     def as_state(self) -> dict:\n154:         \"\"\"Plain, msgpack-safe primitives for the graph state (``publication_result``).\"\"\"\n155:         return {\n156:             \"contract_version\": self.contract_version,\n157:             \"run_id\": self.run_id,\n158:             \"ticker\": self.ticker,\n159:             \"as_of_date\": self.as_of_date,\n160:             \"publication_status\": self.publication_status,\n161:             \"reason_codes\": list(self.reason_codes),\n162:             \"rating\": self.rating,\n163:             \"argument_ids\": list(self.argument_ids),\n164:             \"evidence_ids\": list(self.evidence_ids),\n165:             \"resolved_chain\": [list(link) for link in self.resolved_chain],\n166:         }\n167: \n168: \n169: class PublicationRequiredError(RuntimeError):\n170:     \"\"\"An official surface was asked to publish without a real gate result.\n171: \n172:     Raised instead of writing an official report or decision when the run state\n173:     carries no ``publication_result``, or carries only the legacy flat\n174:     ``publication_status`` field. The flat field is not a release authority: a\n175:     caller could set it to ``APPROVED`` without any gate ever running.\n176:     \"\"\"\n177: \n178: \n179: \n180: \n181: # --- the serializable on-state representation -------------------------------\n182: #\n183: # The graph state carries the index as plain data so a checkpoint (msgpack) can\n184: # store it. Shape:\n185: #   evidence_index = {\n186: #       \"run_id\": str,\n187: #       \"evidence\": [ {\"id\", \"source\", \"excerpt\"} , ... ],\n188: #       \"arguments\": [ {\"id\", \"speaker\", \"text\", \"evidence_ids\"} , ... ],\n189: #   }\n190: # Every value is a str / list / dict of primitives.\n191: \n192: \n193: def index_to_state(index: EvidenceIndex) -> dict:\n194:     \"\"\"Flatten an EvidenceIndex into msgpack-safe primitives for the graph state.\"\"\"\n195:     return {\n196:         \"run_id\": index.run_id,\n197:         \"evidence\": [\n198:             {\"id\": e.evidence_id, \"source\": e.source, \"excerpt\": e.excerpt}\n199:             for e in index.evidence_records\n200:         ],\n201:         \"arguments\": [\n202:             {\"id\": a.argument_id, \"speaker\": a.speaker, \"text\": a.text,\n203:              \"evidence_ids\": list(a.evidence_ids)}\n204:             for a in index.argument_records\n205:         ],\n206:     }\n207: \n208: \n209: class EvidenceIndex:\n210:     \"\"\"Run-scoped evidence and accepted arguments (in-memory helper).\n211: \n212:     Built at run start from its own reports; ``accept`` validates submissions.\n213:     The graph state holds ``index_to_state(...)`` rather than this object, and\n214:     ``evaluate`` reads either shape via :func:`as_index`.\n215:     \"\"\"\n216: \n217:     def __init__(self, run_id: str, evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord]):\n218:         self.run_id = run_id\n219:         self._evidence = dict(evidence)\n220:         self._arguments: dict[str, ArgumentRecord] = {}\n221: \n222:     # --- evidence ---\n223: \n224:     def has_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool:\n225:         return evidence_id in self._evidence\n226: \n227:     def evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> EvidenceRecord:\n228:         return self._evidence[evidence_id]\n229: \n230:     @property\n231:     def evidence_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n232:         return tuple(self._evidence)\n233: \n234:     @property\n235:     def evidence_records(self) -> tuple[EvidenceRecord, ...]:\n236:         return tuple(self._evidence.values())\n237: \n238:     # --- accepted arguments ---\n239: \n240:     def accept(self, argument: ArgumentRecord) -> bool:\n241:         \"\"\"Accept an argument iff every cited evidence id resolves in this run.\n242: \n243:         Returns whether it was accepted. Rejection leaves the index unchanged;\n244:         the caller must not mint an argument id for a rejected submission.\n245:         \"\"\"\n246:         if not argument.evidence_ids:\n247:             return False\n248:         if any(eid not in self._evidence for eid in argument.evidence_ids):\n249:             return False\n250:         self._arguments[argument.argument_id] = argument\n251:         return True\n252: \n253:     def argument(self, argument_id: str) -> ArgumentRecord:\n254:         return self._arguments[argument_id]\n255: \n256:     def has_argument(self, argument_id: str) -> bool:\n257:         return argument_id in self._arguments\n258: \n259:     @property\n260:     def argument_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n261:         return tuple(self._arguments)\n262: \n263:     @property\n264:     def argument_records(self) -> tuple[ArgumentRecord, ...]:\n265:         return tuple(self._arguments.values())\n266: \n267: \n268: def as_index(value) -> EvidenceIndex:\n269:     \"\"\"A read-only EvidenceIndex view of an object, the legacy state dict, or a mapping.\n270: \n271:     ``evaluate``/``evidence_menu`` accept the graph state's serializable dict or\n272:     an in-memory index, so the same logic serves tests and resumed checkpoints.\n273:     A legacy serialized index stores its rows in lists; the C1 v1.0 shape stores\n274:     them in ID-keyed mappings. Both are read here, so a snapshot record collected\n275:     as a mapping is visible to the researchers exactly like a report record.\n276:     \"\"\"\n277:     if isinstance(value, EvidenceIndex):\n278:         return value\n279:     if value is None:\n280:         return EvidenceIndex(run_id=\"\", evidence={})\n281:     run_id = value.get(\"run_id\", \"\")\n282: \n283:     if isinstance(value.get(\"evidence\"), list):\n284:         rows = value[\"evidence\"]\n285:     elif isinstance(value.get(\"evidence\"), dict):\n286:         rows = list(value[\"evidence\"].values())\n287:     else:\n288:         # A bare ID -> record mapping: everything that is not metadata is a row.\n289:         rows = [\n290:             record for key, record in value.items()\n291:             if isinstance(record, dict) and (record.get(\"evidence_id\") or record.get(\"id\"))\n292:         ]\n293:     evidence = {}\n294:     for item in rows:\n295:         if not isinstance(item, dict):\n296:             continue\n297:         evidence_id = item.get(\"evidence_id\") or item.get(\"id\")\n298:         if not evidence_id:\n299:             continue\n300:         evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n301:             evidence_id=evidence_id,\n302:             source=item.get(\"source\") or item.get(\"source_kind\", \"\"),\n303:             excerpt=item.get(\"excerpt\") or _excerpt(item.get(\"source_ref\", \"\")),\n304:             run_id=item.get(\"run_id\") or run_id,\n305:         )\n306: \n307:     index = EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n308:     if isinstance(value.get(\"arguments\"), list):\n309:         argument_rows = value[\"arguments\"]\n310:     else:\n311:         argument_rows = [\n312:             record for key, record in value.items()\n313:             if isinstance(record, dict) and (record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\"))\n314:         ]\n315:     for arg in argument_rows:\n316:         if not isinstance(arg, dict):\n317:             continue\n318:         argument_id = arg.get(\"argument_id\") or arg.get(\"id\")\n319:         if not argument_id:\n320:
