or arg.get(\"claim\", \"\"),\n324:             evidence_ids=tuple(arg.get(\"evidence_ids\", [])),\n325:         )\n326:     return index\n327: \n328: \n329: def build_evidence_index(run_id: str, state) -> EvidenceIndex:\n330:     \"\"\"Index this run's non-empty analyst reports, one ``evidence_id`` per report.\n331: \n332:     Only material actually present in the run is indexed. Deterministic: ids and\n333:     iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.\n334:     \"\"\"\n335:     evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}\n336:     for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:\n337:         text = state.get(key)\n338:         if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():\n339:             continue\n340:         evidence_id = f\"ev:{run_id}:{key}\"\n341:         evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n342:             evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=_excerpt(text), run_id=run_id,\n343:         )\n344:     return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n345: \n346: \n347: def evidence_menu(index) -> str:\n348:     \"\"\"The evidence IDs and their material, for the researcher prompt.\n349: \n350:     The model may cite only these IDs; they are the program-built index for this\n351:     run, so a cited ID resolves to actual run material.\n352:     \"\"\"\n353:     idx = as_index(index)\n354:     if not idx.evidence_ids:\n355:         return \"(No evidence is available in this run; you cannot cite any evidence ID.)\"\n356:     lines = []\n357:     for record in idx.evidence_records:\n358:         lines.append(f\"- {record.evidence_id}  [{record.source}] {record.excerpt}\")\n359:     return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n360: \n361: \n362: def _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n363:     \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n364:     flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n365:     return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n366: \n367: \n368: def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n369:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n370: \n371:     Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n372:     ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n373:     \"\"\"\n374:     if value is None:\n375:         return None\n376:     rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n377:     if not isinstance(rating, str):\n378:         return None\n379:     return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n380: \n381: \n382: def evaluate(index, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids) -> GateOutcome:\n383:     \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n384: \n385:     ``index`` may be the state dict or an EvidenceIndex. Order matters: an invalid\n386:     rating is reported before a missing chain, so a candidate that fails both\n387:     returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is consulted here.\n388:     \"\"\"\n389:     idx = as_index(index)\n390:     rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n391:     if rating is None:\n392:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n393: \n394:     cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n395:     resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n396:     for argument_id in cited:\n397:         if not idx.has_argument(argument_id):\n398:             continue\n399:         argument = idx.argument(argument_id)\n400:         for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n401:             if idx.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n402:                 resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, idx.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n403:     if not resolved:\n404:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n405: \n406:     return GateOutcome(\n407:         status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n408:     )\n409: \n410: \n411: def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n412:     \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n413: \n414:     On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the\n415:     candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the\n416:     returned state carries no candidate material at all — the candidate body,\n417:     candidate rating and candidate argument ids are removed from the mapping, so\n418:     the Python API's returned state cannot expose or re-derive the candidate. The\n419:     only place ``REVIEW`` appears is the API's second tuple member (computed by the\n420:     caller via ``run_rating``); ``final_rating`` is emptied here, not set to REVIEW.\n421:     \"\"\"\n422:     status = outcome.status\n423:     final_state[\"publication_status\"] = status\n424:     final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = outcome.reason\n425:     final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)\n426: \n427:     if outcome.approved:\n428:         body = final_state.get(\"candidate_decision\") or final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\") or \"\"\n429:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = outcome.rating\n430:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = body\n431:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n432:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n433:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n434:     else:\n435:         # No candidate material leaks into the returned state: the body, its rating\n436:         # and the ids it cited are all removed. ``final_rating`` is emptied rather\n437:         # than set to REVIEW; REVIEW is the API's second tuple member only.\n438:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = \"\"\n439:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n440:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n441:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n442:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n443:     return final_state\n444: \n445: \n446: # --- C1 v1.0: mapping-authoritative evaluation -------------------------------\n447: #\n448: # The authoritative indexes are ID -> record mappings: ``argument_index`` keyed by\n449: # ``argument_id`` and ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The legacy\n450: # shapes ``index_to_state(...)`` (lists under \"evidence\"/\"arguments\") and\n451: # ``accepted_arguments`` are a compatibility layer only: an argument that exists\n452: # solely in that view never resolves a reference.\n453: \n454: \n455: _IDENTITY_KEYS = (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"as_of_date\")\n456: \n457: # C1 v1.0 required shared fields, beyond identity. \"A missing required field is an\n458: # invalid record\": a record without one is not admissible evidence/acceptance.\n459: _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED = (\n460:     \"evidence_id\", \"source_kind\", \"vendor\", \"source_ref\",\n461:     \"content_ref\", \"window_start\", \"window_end\",\n462: )\n463: _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED = (\"argument_id\", \"claim\")\n464: \n465: \n466: def _field_present(record: dict, key: str) -> bool:\n467:     \"\"\"Whether a required field is present and non-empty.\n468: \n469:     A missing value, ``None``, an empty string and a whitespace-only string are\n470:     all the same thing here: no value. A list is present when it is non-empty.\n471:     \"\"\"\n472:     value = record.get(key)\n473:     if isinstance(value, str):\n474:         return bool(value.strip())\n475:     if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):\n476:         return len(value) > 0\n477:     return value is not None\n478: \n479: \n480: def _required_fields_ok(record, required) -> bool:\n481:     \"\"\"Whether every C1 required field of ``record`` is present and non-empty.\"\"\"\n482:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n483:         return False\n484:     return all(_field_present(record, key) for key in required)\n485: \n486: \n487: def _identity(record, run: dict) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:\n488:     \"\"\"The record's ``(run_id, ticker, as_of_date)`` when it *fully* matches the run.\n489: \n490:     Ownership is checked on the record's full identity, never on how its ID is\n491:     spelled: an ID needs no prefix and must not contain the run id. All three\n492:     fields are required and must equal the ``RunContext``'s, so a record with a\n493:     missing identity, a partial identity or a foreign run's identity is not this\n494:     run's material and never resolves.\n495:     \"\"\"\n496:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n497:         return None\n498:     if not all(isinstance(run.get(key), str) and run.get(key) for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS):\n499:         return None\n500:     for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS:\n501:         if record.get(key) != run.get(key):\n502:             return None\n503:     return tuple(run[key] for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS)\n504: \n505: \n506: def _material_resolves(record: dict, run: dict, results_dir) -> bool:\n507:     \"\"\"Whether the record's referenced retained material exists **and has content**.\n508: \n509:     Only a record that names retained material (``content_ref``) and whose material\n510:     can be re-read from this run's retention root counts. A record with no\n511:     ``content_ref`` — an analyst report indexed only in memory — has no traceable\n512:     source material, so it is **not** admissible evidence: the prose itself is not\n513:     a retained source. A reference whose file is expired, deleted or foreign does\n514:     not resolve either.\n515: \n516:     C1 v1.0: \"assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content\n517:     valid\". A retained file that resolves but holds only whitespace has no\n518:     substance, so it is not evidence.\n519:     \"\"\"\n520:     content_ref = record.get(\"content_ref\")\n521:     if not isinstance(content_ref, str) or not content_ref:\n522:         return False\n523:     if not isinstance(results_dir, (str, Path)) or not str(results_dir):\n524:         return False\n525:     from tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection import resolve_content_ref\n526: \n527:     try:\n528:         material = resolve_content_ref(content_ref, results_dir, run)\n529:     except (OSError, ValueError):\n530:         return False\n531:     if not isinstance(material, str):\n532:         return False\n533:     # A retained file that exists but holds only whitespace has no substance.\n534:     return bool(material.strip())\n535: \n536: \n537: def _evidence_records(evidence_index, run: dict, results_dir=None) -> dict[str, dict]:\n538:     \"\"\"The run's own evidence, keyed by ``evidence_id``.\n539: \n540:     Only the authoritative v1 mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which\n541:     carries the same records) is read; an in-memory ``EvidenceIndex`` object is\n542:     the compatibility layer and is refused here, because an object carries no\n543:     per-record ``content_ref`` and would therefore skip the material read-back.\n544: \n545:     A record counts only when its **full identity** matches the ``RunContext``;\n546:     the ID's spelling is irrelevant. A record whose referenced retained material\n547:     cannot be resolved is not evidence, so a report record with no ``content_ref``\n548:     never backs a release.\n549:     \"\"\"\n550:     if not isinstance(evidence_index, dict):\n551:         return {}\n552:     rows = _mapping_rows(evidence_index, \"evidence\", \"id\")\n553:     records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n554:     for _key, record in rows:\n555:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n556:             continue\n557:         # C1: \"a missing required field is an invalid record\". The *record* is\n558:         # judged, never its mapping key or a legacy ``id`` alias: an index entry\n559:         # that supplies ``evidence_id`` only by being keyed under it still has no\n560:         # ``evidence_id`` of its own, so it is not evidence.\n561:         if not _required_fields_ok(record, _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED):\n562:             continue\n563:         evidence_id = record[\"evidence_id\"]\n564:         if not isinstance(evidence_id, str) or not evidence_id:\n565:             continue\n566:         # Ownership is the record's full identity, never the ID's spelling.\n567:         if _identity(record, run) is None:\n568:             continue\n569:         if not _material_resolves(record, run, results_dir):\n570:             continue\n571:         records[evidence_id] = record\n572:     return records\n573: \n574: \n575: def _argument_records(argument_index, run: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:\n576:     \"\"\"The run's accepted arguments, keyed by ``argument_id``.\n577: \n578:     Only the authoritative v1 mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which\n579:     carries the same records) is read; an ``EvidenceIndex`` object or a\n580:     ``{\"accepted_arguments\": [...]}`` view is the compatibility layer and is not\n581:     a release authority, so it yields nothing here.\n582: \n583:     A record counts only when its **full identity** matches the ``RunContext``\n584:     (``run_id``, ``ticker`` and ``as_of_date`` all equal). An ID needs no prefix\n585:     and must not contain the run id. A record that states no identity at all is\n586:     not owned by any run and is refused, whether or not a run id is available.\n587:     \"\"\"\n588:     if not isinstance(argument_index, dict):\n589:         return {}\n590:     if \"accepted_arguments\" in argument_index and \"arguments\" not in argument_index:\n591:         return {}\n592:     rows = _mapping_rows(argument_index, \"arguments\", \"id\")\n593:     records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n594:     for key, record in rows:\n595:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n596:             continue\n597:         argument_id = record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n598:         if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n599:             continue\n600:         if _identity(record, run) is None:\n601:             # No identity, a partial identity, or another run's identity.\n602:             continue\n603:         # C1: an AcceptedArgument needs a nonempty claim and a nonempty\n604:         # ``evidence_ids`` list. ``text`` is the legacy spelling of the claim.\n605:         normalised = {\n606:             **record,\n607:             \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n608:             \"claim\": record.get(\"claim\") or record.get(\"text\") or \"\",\n609:         }\n610:         if not _required_fields_ok(normalised, _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED):\n611:             continue\n612:         if not _field_present(normalised, \"evidence_ids\"):\n613:             continue\n614:         records[argument_id] = record\n615:     return records\n616: \n617: \n618: def validate_argument(argument, evidence_index, run, results_dir=None) -> dict | None:\n619:     \"\"\"C1 v1.0: check current-run references before accepting an argument.\n620: \n621:     The v1 callable boundary from ``interface-contracts.md``. Returns the\n622:     **accepted record** — the argument's full identity plus its claim and the\n623:     resolved evidence ids — or ``None`` when the submission is not acceptable.\n624: \n625:     An argument is accepted only when every part of C1 holds:\n626: \n627:     * it carries the run's **full identity** (``run_id``, ``ticker``,\n628:       ``as_of_date`` all equal the ``RunContext``'s), so a foreign or\n629:       identity-less submission is not this run's argument;\n630:     * it has an ``argument_id`` and a nonempty ``claim``;\n631:     * ``evidence_ids`` is a nonempty list, and **every** cited id resolves to\n632:       admissible evidence in this run: present in the index, complete, and\n633:       backed by retained material that exists and has content.\n634: \n635:     A model flag is not acceptance, and a partially resolvable citation is not a\n636:     partial acceptance: one unresolvable id refuses the argument. This is the\n637:     validation layer; ``evaluate_publication`` rechecks the whole chain again,\n638:     because a record can reach the index without passing through here.\n639:     \"\"\"\n640:     if not isinstance(argument, dict):\n641:         return None\n642:     if _identity(argument, run) is None:\n643:         return None\n644:     argument_id = argument.get(\"argument_id\") or argument.get(\"id\")\n645:     if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n646:         return None\n647:     claim = argument.get(\"claim\") or argument.get(\"text\") or \"\"\n648:     if not isinstance(claim, str) or not claim.strip():\n649:         return None\n650:     evidence_ids = argument.get(\"evidence_ids\")\n651:     if not isinstance(evidence_ids, (list, tuple)) or not evidence_ids:\n652:         return None\n653:     if any(not isinstance(eid, str) or not eid for eid in evidence_ids):\n654:         return None\n655: \n656:     available = _evidence_records(evidence_index, run, results_dir)\n657:     if any(eid not in available for eid in evidence_ids):\n658:         return None\n659: \n660:     return {\n661:         \"contract_version\": str(argument.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n662:         \"run_id\": run[\"run_id\"],\n663:         \"ticker\": run[\"ticker\"],\n664:         \"as_of_date\": run[\"as_of_date\"],\n665:         \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n666:         \"claim\": claim,\n667:         \"speaker\": argument.get(\"speaker\", \"\"),\n668:         \"evidence_ids\": list(evidence_ids),\n669:     }\n670: \n671: \n672: def _mapping_rows(index: dict, list_key: str, id_key: str):\n673:     \"\"\"``(key, record)`` pairs of a mapping index or of its legacy serialized form.\n674: \n675:     Three shapes are read:\n676: \n677:     * a bare ID -> record mapping yields its own items;\n678:     * the authoritative v1 wrapper ``{\"run_id\": ..., list_key: {id: record}}``\n679:       yields the wrapped mapping's items, so metadata is never mistaken for a\n680:       record;\n681:     * the legacy serialized form ``{list_key: [ {...id_key: ...} ]}`` is read\n682:       from that list.\n683: \n684:     The key a record is found under is a fallback only; the record's own ID field\n685:     wins.\n686:     \"\"\"\n687:     if list_key in index:\n688:         wrapped = index[list_key]\n689:         if isinstance(wrapped, dict):\n690:             return list(wrapped.items())\n691:         if isinstance(wrapped, list):\n692:             return [(None, item) for item in wrapped]\n693:     return list(index.items())\n694: \n695: \n696: def _rating(value) -> str | None:\n697:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` when not publishable.\n698: \n699:     Only the exact five tiers count. ``REVIEW``, casing variants, surrounding\n700:     text (\"Buy (small size)\") and null are all invalid: free text is not a call.\n701:     \"\"\"\n702:     if not isinstance(value, str):\n703:         return None\n704:     return value if value in _RATING_SET else None\n705: \n706: \n707: def evaluate_publication(\n708:     candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run, results_dir=None\n709: ) -> PublicationResult:\n710:     \"\"\"C1 v1.0: the one deterministic publication result for a run.\n711: \n712:     Rows are checked in the approved order, and the first matching row decides:\n713: \n714:     1. C0 terminal failure / incomplete execution (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``,\n715:        ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` keep their own code; anything not ``COMPLETED``,\n716:        including a missing ``RunContext``, is ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``).\n717:     2. An invalid rating (``INVALID_RATING``).\n718:     3. Missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted references\n719:        (``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``).\n720:     4. Otherwise APPROVED, with the rating and the validated references.\n721: \n722:     References are rechecked here, not taken from the model: a cited argument\n723:     must exist in this run's ``argument_index``, ownership is decided by each\n724:     record's full identity (never by an ID prefix), and each of its evidence ids\n725:     must resolve in this run's ``evidence_index`` with its retained material still\n726:     readable under ``results_dir``. A record with no retained material never\n727:     resolves. BLOCKED always carries ``rating=None``.\n728:     \"\"\"\n729:     run = run if isinstance(run, dict) else {}\n730:     identity = {\n731:         \"contract_version\": str(run.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n732:         \"run_id\": run.get(\"run_id\") or \"\",\n733:         \"ticker\": run.get(\"ticker\") or \"\",\n734:         \"as_of_date\": run.get(\"as_of_date\") or \"\",\n735:     }\n736: \n737:     def _blocked(*codes: str) -> PublicationResult:\n738:         return PublicationResult(\n739:             **identity, publication_status=BLOCKED, reason_codes=tuple(codes),\n740:             rating=None, argument_ids=(), evidence_ids=(),\n741:         )\n742: \n743:     # Row 1: C0 execution state.\n744:     status = run.get(\"execution_status\")\n745:     if status in _TERMINAL_EXECUTION_NAMED:\n746:         return _blocked(status)\n747:     if status != EXECUTION_COMPLETED:\n748:         # FAILED, RUNNING and a missing RunContext: the workflow did not finish\n749:         # normally, so nothing it produced may publish.\n750:         return _blocked(RUN_NOT_COMPLETE)\n751: \n752:     # Row 2: the rating must be one of the five tiers.\n753:     candidate = candidate if isinstance(candidate, dict) else {}\n754:     rating = _rating(candidate.get(\"rating\"))\n755:     if rating is None:\n756:         return _blocked(INVALID_RATING)\n757: \n758:     # Row 3: every cited reference must resolve inside this run.\n759:     #\n760:     # Fail-closed: a candidate is one recommendation, so an unresolvable cited\n761:     # reference makes it unverifiable and the **whole** candidate is refused.\n762:     # Skipping the references that happened to resolve would release a decision\n763:     # whose stated basis is partly unverified (C1: \"missing, unknown, cross-run or\n764:     # unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\").\n765:     arguments = _argument_records(argument_index, run)\n766:     evidence = _evidence_records(evidence_index, run, results_dir)\n767:     cited = [a for a in (candidate.get(\"argument_ids\") or ()) if isinstance(a, str) and a]\n768:     if not cited:\n769:         return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n770:     resolved_arguments: list[str] = []\n771:     resolved_evidence: list[str] = []\n772:     chain: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n773:     for argument_id in cited:\n774:         argument = arguments.get(argument_id)\n775:         if argument is None:\n776:             return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n777:         evidence_ids = [\n778:             eid for eid in (argument.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ())\n779:             if isinstance(eid, str) and eid in evidence\n780:         ]\n781:         if not evidence_ids:\n782:             return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n783:         if len(evidence_ids) != len(argument.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ()):\n784:             # The argument cites something that is not this run's admissible\n785:             # evidence, even though its other references resolve.\n786:             return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n787:         resolved_arguments.append(argument_id)\n788:         for evidence_id in evidence_ids:\n789:             if evidence_id not in resolved_evidence:\n790:                 resolved_evidence.append(evidence_id)\n791:             chain.append((argument_id, evidence_id, str(evidence.get(evidence_id, {}).get(\"source\", \"\"))))\n792:     if not resolved_arguments or not resolved_evidence:\n793:         return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n794: \n795:     # Row 4: approved, with identity, rating and validated references.\n796:     return PublicationResult(\n797:         **identity,\n798:         publication_status=APPROVED,\n799:         reason_codes=(),\n800:         rating=rating,\n801:         argument_ids=tuple(resolved_arguments),\n802:         evidence_ids=tuple(resolved_evidence),\n803:         resolved_chain=tuple(chain),\n804:     )\n805: \n806: \n807: def run_as_of_date(state: dict) -> str:\n808:     \"\"\"The run's effective cutoff date, as the ``RunContext`` records it.\n809: \n810:     A researcher records an argument's identity with the same date the evidence\n811:     records and the gate use — ``as_of()``'s own result — not the raw trade date,\n812:     so the argument's identity and the evidence's identity agree.\n813:     \"\"\"\n814:     course_run = state.get(\"course_run\") if isinstance(state, dict) else None\n815:     if isinstance(course_run, dict) and course_run.get(\"as_of_date\"):\n816:         return str(course_run[\"as_of_date\"])\n817:     from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import as_of\n818: \n819:     trade_date = state.get(\"trade_date\") if isinstance(state, dict) else \"\"\n820:     return as_of(trade_date, trade_date)\n821: \n822: \n823: def accepted_arguments_view(argument_index: dict) -> list[dict]:\n824:     \"\"\"The legacy ``accepted_arguments`` list, derived from the authoritative mapping.\n825: \n826:     The Portfolio Manager's prompt still lists accepted arguments in the old\n827:     shape. It is built from ``argument_index`` on every write, so it cannot drift\n828:     from the mapping, and the gate never reads it back as authority.\n829:     \"\"\"\n830:     view = []\n831:     for argument_id, record in (argument_index or {}).items():\n832:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n833:             continue\n834:         view.append({\n835:             \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n836:             \"speaker\": record.get(\"speaker\", \"\"),\n837:             \"evidence_ids\": list(record.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ()),\n838:         })\n839:     return view\n840: \n841: \n842: def publication_run(state: dict) -> dict:\n843:     \"\"\"The ``RunContext`` the gate judges a run against (C0).\n844: \n845:     The graph state carries one complete ``course_run``, created once at the shared\n846:     run entry. When it is absent the run has no identity to be checked against and\n847:     no execution state to prove it finished, so ``execution_status`` is left unset\n848:     and the gate blocks with ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``. A terminal failure recorded on\n849:     the state (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`` / ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE``) is carried through so\n850:     it keeps its own reason code.\n851:     \"\"\"\n852:     if not isinstance(state, dict):\n853:         return {}\n854:     course_run = state.get(\"course_run\")\n855:     if isinstance(course_run, dict) and course_run.get(\"run_id\"):\n856:         return dict(course_run)\n857:     recorded = state.get(\"execution_status\")\n858:     return {\n859:         \"contract_version\": \"1.0\",\n860:         \"run_id\": \"\",\n861:         \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\") or \"\",\n862:         \"as_of_date\": state.get(\"trade_date\") or \"\",\n863:         # No RunContext, no proof of completion: never assume COMPLETED. At agent creation, wrap the LLM with ``with_structured_output(Schema)``\n7:    so the model returns a typed Pydantic instance. Do not call external tools \"\n40:     \"or search the web; if something is missing, say so explicitly.\"\n41: )\n42: \n43: \n44: def bind_structured(llm: Any, schema: type[T], agent_name: str) -> Any | None:\n45:     \"\"\"Return ``llm.with_structured_output(schema)`` or ``None`` if unsupported.\n46: \n47:     Logs a warning when the binding fails so the user understands the agent\n48:     will use free-text generation for every call instead of one-shot fallback.\n49:     \"\"\"\n50:     try:\n51:         return llm.with_structured_output(schema)\n52:     except (NotImplementedError, AttributeError) as exc:\n53:         logger.warning(\n54:             \"%s: provider does not support with_structured_output (%s); \"\n55:             \"falling back to free-text generation\",\n56:             agent_name, exc,\n57:         )\n58:         return None\n59: \n60: \n61: def invoke_structured(structured_llm: Any | None, prompt: Any, agent_name: str) -> T | None:\n62:     \"\"\"Run the structured call; ``None`` when there is none or it fails.\n63: \n64:     ``prompt`` is whatever the underlying LLM accepts (a string for chat\n65:     invocations, a list of message dicts for chat models that take that\n66:     shape), so a caller can forward the same value to its free-text fallback.\n67: \n68:     A terminal C0 failure (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``, ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` or\n69:     ``FAILED``) is re-raised instead of falling back: the fallback is a second\n70:     model turn, and on a metered run it must not become an unbudgeted send\n71:     (NFR-01 / INV-02). Only ordinary structured-output misses fall through to\n72:     ``None`` for the caller's free-text fallback.\n73:     \"\"\"\n74:     if structured_llm is None:\n75:         return None\n76:     try:\n77:         result = structured_llm.invoke(prompt)\n78:         if result is None:\n79:             # A thinking model can answer in plain text instead of calling\n80:             # the tool, leaving the parser with nothing to return. Treat it\n81:             # as a structured miss and fall back, with a clear reason.\n82:             raise ValueError(\"structured output returned no parsed result\")\n83:         return result\n84:     except Exception as exc:\n85:         # The transport owner module is the single authority on which\n86:         # exceptions are terminal and on unwrapping wrapped causes. Fail closed:\n87:         # if the classifier itself cannot run, treat the failure as terminal\n88:         # rather than risk an unbudgeted free-text retry.\n89:         try:\n90:             terminal = terminal_request_status(exc) is not None\n91:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed on an unusable classifier\n92:             terminal = True\n93:         if terminal:\n94:             # Re-raise the original failure (not a wrapper) so the graph keeps\n95:             # its terminal status and the run ends without retrying.\n96:             raise\n97:         logger.warning(\n98:             \"%s: structured-output invocation failed (%s); retrying once as free text\",\n99:             agent_name, exc,\n100:         )\n101:         return None\n102: \n103: \n104: def invoke_structured_or_freetext(\n105:     structured_llm: Any | None,\n106:     plain_llm: Any,\n107:     prompt: Any,\n108:     render: Callable[[T], str],\n109:     agent_name: str,\n110: ) -> str:\n111:     \"\"\"Run the structured call and render to markdown; fall back to free-text on any failure.\"\"\"\n112:     result = invoke_structured(structured_llm, prompt, agent_name)\n113:     if result is not None:\n114:         return render(result)\n115:     return plain_llm.invoke(prompt).content"

Structured output is layered onto the\n6: three decision-making agents (Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager)\n7: so that:\n8: \n9: - Their outputs follow consistent section headers across runs and providers\n10: - Each provider's native structured-output mode is used (json_schema for\n11:   OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic)\n12: - Schema field descriptions become the model's output instructions, freeing\n13:   the prompt body to focus on context and the rating-scale guidance\n14: - A render helper turns the parsed Pydantic instance back into the same\n15:   markdown shape the rest of the system already consumes, so display,\n16:   memory log, and saved reports keep working unchanged\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: from enum import StrEnum\n22: from typing import Literal\n23: \n24: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n25: \n26: # LLMs sometimes write a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\", ...) into an optional\n27: # numeric field instead of omitting it. Coerce those to None so the structured\n28: # call validates instead of erroring (#1058). Pydantic still parses real numeric\n29: # strings (\"189.5\") to float.\n30: _NULLISH_FLOAT = {\"\", \"none\", \"n/a\", \"na\", \"null\", \"nil\", \"-\", \"tbd\", \"unknown\"}\n31: \n32: \n33: def _coerce_optional_float(value):\n34:     \"\"\"Normalise an LLM-written optional numeric field before validation.\n35: \n36:     Three shapes show up in practice: a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\") in\n37:     place of an omitted value (#1058); a percentage where a price was asked for\n38:     (\"15%\", #1288); and a human-formatted price (\"$1,234.50\"). It is\n75:     generated with ``uuid4`` and stored in the serializable graph state, then\n76:     reused verbatim on resume (see ``_index_evidence_node``), so a resumed run keeps\n77:     the same id.\n78:     \"\"\"\n79:     import uuid\n80: \n81:     return uuid.uuid4().hex\n82: \n83: \n84: def _run_context(state) -> dict:\n85:     \"\"\"R8-B §2 / C0: the one complete ``RunContext`` for this run.\n86: \n87:     Written once, at the Index Evidence step, from the id minted at the shared run\n88:     entry and reused verbatim on resume. Every field is copied from the run\n89:     itself, never derived from an ID's spelling.\n90: \n91:     ``execution_status`` starts at ``RUNNING``: the run has not finished yet, and\n92:     only a normal finish sets ``COMPLETED`` (see ``TradingAgentsGraph.publish``).\n93:     A terminal C0 failure keeps its own code, and a run still ``RUNNING`` when the\n94:     gate judges it is ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``.\n95: \n96:     ``request_limit`` is the run's positive-integer request budget, defaulting to\n97:     the approved value of 40. A non-positive or non-integer setting is a\n98:     configuration error, not something to silently clamp.\n99:     \"\"\"\n100:     from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG\n101: \n102:     # C0/C1: the shared run entry already created the one complete RunContext.\n103:     # Reuse it verbatim — including on resume — so the identity the material was\n104:     # stamped with is the identity the gate judges.\n105:     seeded = state.get(\"course_run\")\n106:     if isinstance(seeded, dict) and seeded.get(\"run_id\"):\n107:         context = dict(seeded)\n108:         context.setdefault(\"contract_version\", \"1.0\")\n109:         context[\"ticker\"] = context.get(\"ticker\") or state.get(\"company_of_interest\", \"\")\n110:         context[\"as_of_date\"] = context.get(\"as_of_date\") or _effective_as_of(state)\n111:         context[\"execution_status\"] = context.get(\"execution_status\") or RUNNING\n112:         limit = context.get(\"request_limit\")\n113:         if limit is None:\n114:             limit = DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"request_limit\")\n115:         if limit is None:\n116:             limit = DEFAULT_REQUEST_LIMIT\n117:         if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int) or limit <= 0:\n118:             raise ValueError(f\"request_limit must be a positive integer, got {limit!r}\")\n119:         context[\"request_limit\"] = limit\n120:         # A recorded terminal failure outranks the RUNNING default.\n121:         if state.get(\"execution_status\") in (\"FAILED\", \"BUDGET_EXHAUSTED\", \"CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE\"):\n122:             context[\"execution_status\"] = state[\"execution_status\"]\n123:         return context\n124: \n125:     run_id = state.get(\"run_id\") or _new_run_id()\n126:     limit = state.get(\"request_limit\")\n127:     if limit is None:\n128:         limit = DEFAULT_CONFIG.get(\"request_limit\")\n129:     if limit is None:\n130:         limit = DEFAULT_REQUEST_LIMIT\n131:     if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int) or limit <= 0:\n132:         raise ValueError(f\"request_limit must be a positive integer, got {limit!r}\")\n133:     return {\n134:         \"contract_version\": \"1.0\",\n135:         \"run_id\": run_id,\n136:         \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\", \"\"),\n137:         # The effective cutoff is as_of()'s own result, not the requested date.\n138:         \"as_of_date\": _effective_as_of(state),\n139:         \"execution_status\": state.get(\"execution_status\") or RUNNING,\n140:         \"request_limit\": limit,\n141:     }\n142: \n143: \n144: def _effective_as_of(state) -> str:\n145:     \"\"\"The run's effective cutoff date: ``as_of()``'s actual result.\n146: \n147:     The window checks and the snapshot retention paths use this same date, so a\n148:     record dated by ``as_of()`` is the record the run's identity names.\n149:     \"\"\"\n150:     from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import as_of\n151: \n152:     return as_of(state.get(\"trade_date\"), state.get(\"trade_date\"))\n153: \n154: \n155: def _index_evidence_node(state) -> dict:\n156:     \"\"\"FR-01 / R8-B §4: build this run's authoritative evidence mapping.\n157: \n158:     The run id was minted at the shared run entry, so the one complete\n159:     ``course_run`` written here reuses it and a resumed run never mints a new one.\n160: \n161:     The evidence index is an **ID -> record mapping built from retained\n162:     material**: the market analyst's verified snapshots, which the subgraph\n163:     retained and handed up as ``market_evidence``. A record carries its full\n164:     identity and a ``content_ref`` naming its retained file, so the gate can\n165:     re-read the material before publishing. Analyst reports are **not** evidence:\n166:     prose alone has no traceable retained source, so indexing it would let a\n167:     candidate publish without any verified data.\n168: \n169:     The mapping is keyed by ``evidence_id`` (C1 v1.0), not a list the gate has to\n170:     search. ``\"run_id\"`` rides alongside as compatibility metadata only; no\n171:     record's ownership is ever read from it.\n172: \n173:     ``argument_index`` starts empty and is filled by the researchers as they cite\n174:     validated evidence.\n175:     \"\"\"\n176:     course_run = _run_context(state)\n177:     run_id = course_run[\"run_id\"]\n178: \n179:     evidence: dict[str, dict] = {}\n180: \n181:     def add(record) -> None:\n182:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n183:             return\n184:         if record.get(\"run_id\") != run_id:\n185:             return\n186:         evidence_id = record.get(\"evidence_id\")\n187:         if not evidence_id or evidence_id in evidence:\n188:             return\n189:         evidence[evidence_id] = {**record, \"id\": evidence_id}\n190: \n191:     # Retained snapshot receipts handed up by the market analyst's subgraph.\n192:     for record in state.get(\"market_evidence\") or ():\n193:         add(record)\n194:     # A caller whose tool messages are on the parent state (no subgraph).\n195:     for record in _collect_snapshots(state, course_run):\n196:         add(record)\n197: \n198:     return {\n199:         \"run_id\": run_id,\n200:         \"course_run\": course_run,\n201:         \"evidence_index\": {\"run_id\": run_id, \"evidence\": evidence},\n202:         \"argument_index\": {},\n203:         \"accepted_arguments\": [],\n204:     }\n205: \n206: \n207: def _collect_snapshots(state, course_run: dict) -> list[dict]:\n208:     \"\"\"Retain verified snapshots whose calls and results are on the parent state.\n209: \n210:     The market analyst runs in a graph of its own and hands its receipts up as\n211:     ``market_evidence`` (see ``collect_snapshot_evidence``); this path serves a\n212:     caller whose tool messages are already on the run state. A run with no such\n213:     call (a report-only run) or one whose material cannot be retained contributes\n214:     nothing, and never an unresolvable reference.\n215:     \"\"\"\n216:     from tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection import record_market_snapshot\n217: \n218:     try:\n219:         from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n220: \n221:         results_dir = get_config().get(\"results_dir\")\n222:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — collection is optional, never fatal\n223:         results_dir = None\n224:     if not results_dir:\n225:         return []\n226: \n227:     calls = [\n228:         call for message in state.get(\"messages\") or ()\n229:         for call in (getattr(message, \"tool_calls\", None) or ())\n230:         if isinstance(call, dict) and call.get(\"name\") == \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\n231:     ]\n232:     by_id = {call.get(\"id\"): call for call in calls}\n233:     results = []\n234:     for message in state.get(\"messages\") or ():\n235:         call_id = getattr(message, \"tool_call_id\", None)\n236:         if call_id not in by_id or getattr(message, \"name\", None) != \"get_verified_market_snapshot\":\n237:             continue\n238:         try:\n239:             collected = record_market_snapshot(\n240:                 tool_call=by_id[call_id], tool_response=getattr(message, \"content\", \"\"),\n241:                 state=state, run=course_run, results_dir=results_dir,\n242:             )\n243:         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a bad response is not evidence, not a crash\n244:             continue\n245:         results.extend((collected or {}).get(\"records\") or ())\n246:     return results\n247: \n248: \n249: def _results_dir():\n250:     \"\"\"The run's results root, where retained material lives (never fatal).\n251: \n252:     The gate re-reads each record's retained material from here, so the argument\n253:     validation layer must judge against the same root.\n254:     \"\"\"\n255:     try:\n256:         from tradingagents.dataflows.config import get_config\n257: \n258:         return get_config().get(\"results_dir\")\n259:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — an absent config means no material to read\n260:         return None\n261: \n262: \n263: def _pending_run_context(state) -> dict | None:\n264:     \"\"\"The run's identity as an analyst subgraph sees it, before Index Evidence.\n265: \n266:     ``RunContext`` is created once at the shared run entry. An analyst subgraph\n267:     receives that context on its input state, so it reuses it verbatim — the same\n268:     id, ticker, cutoff date and budget the parent will judge. A caller whose state\n269:     carries only a ``run_id`` (an older checkpoint) still gets the same fields\n270:     derived, and a state with no identity at all returns ``None`` so no receipt is\n271:     stamped with an identity the parent does not share.\n272:     \"\"\"\n273:     seeded = state.get(\"course_run\")\n274:     if isinstance(seeded, dict) and seeded.get(\"run_id\"):\n275:         return dict(seeded)\n276:     run_id = state.get(\"run_id\")\n277:     if not run_id:\n278:         return None\n279:     return {\n280:         \"contract_version\": \"1.0\",\n281:         \"run_id\": run_id,\n282:         \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\", \"\"),\n283:         \"as_of_date\": _effective_as_of(state),\n284:         \"execution_status\": state.get(\"execution_status\") or RUNNING,\n285:         \"request_limit\": state.get(\"request_limit\") or DEFAULT_REQUEST_LIMIT,\n286:     }\n287: \n288: \n289: # --- The market snapshot's quote source -------------------------------------\n290: \n291: \n292: def _quote_source_line(text):\n293:     \"\"\"The quote source on the reply's own last line, or None.\n294: \n295:     Only the final nonblank line is considered, and it must carry exactly the\n296:     source prefix. Numbers are parsed with ``Decimal`` so the vendor's precision\n297:     survives the trip through JSON.\n298:     \"\"\"\n299:     lines = [line for line in str(text if text is not None else \"\").splitlines() if line.strip()]\n300:     if not lines or not lines[-1].startswith(_QUOTE_SOURCE_PREFIX):\n301:         return None\n302:     try:\n303:         payload = json.loads(lines[-1][len(_QUOTE_SOURCE_PREFIX):], parse_float=Decimal)\n304:     except (ValueError, TypeError):\n305:         return None\n306:     return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None\n307: \n308: \n309: def _decimal(value):\n310:     \"\"\"An exact finite Decimal from a JSON number or numeric string, or None.\"\"\"\n311:     if isinstance(value, bool) or value is None:\n312:         return None\n313:     if isinstance(value, Decimal):\n314:         number = value\n315:     elif isinstance(value, int):\n316:         number = Decimal(value)\n317:     elif isinstance(value, float):\n318:         number = Decimal(repr(value))\n319:     elif isinstance(value, str):\n320:         try:\n321:             number = Decimal(value.strip())\n322:         except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):\n323:             return None\n324:     else:\n325:         return None\n326:     return number if number.is_finite() else None\n327: \n328: \n329: def _is_quote_currency(unit) -> bool:\n330:     \"\"\"Whether a unit is a three-letter uppercase currency code.\"\"\"\n331:     return (isinstance(unit, str) and len(unit) == 3\n332:             and unit.isascii() and unit.isalpha() and unit.isupper())\n333: \n334: \n335: def _calendar_date(value):\n336:     \"\"\"A date built from an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string, or None.\"\"\"\n337:     import datetime\n338: \n339:     text = value.strip() if isinstance(value, str) else \"\"\n340:     if len(text) != 10 or text[4] != \"-\" or text[7] != \"-\":\n341:         return None\n342:     try:\n343:         parsed = datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n344:     except ValueError:\n345:         return None\n346:     return parsed if parsed.isoformat() == text else None\n347: \n348: \n349: def _valid_run(state):\n350:     \"\"\"This invocation's course_run, or None when there is none to scope a record to.\"\"\"\n351:     run = state.get(\"course_run\") if isinstance(state, dict) else None\n352:     if not isinstance(run, dict):\n353:         return None\n354:     if not all(isinstance(run.get(field), str) and run.get(field).strip()\n355:                for field in (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"as_of_date\")):\n356:         return None\n357:     return run\n358: \n359: \n360: def _effective_cutoff(state, call, run):\n361:     \"\"\"The effective as-of date for this call, or None when it is not this run's.\n362: \n363:     The state's own company and analysis date must be the ones the run records,\n364:     and the run's date must itself be a real calendar date: an invalid one is a\n365:     missing source, not something to raise out of a tool node. The cutoff then\n366:     follows the data layer's own rule for the call's requested day — a missing\n367:     ``curr_date`` falls back to the analysis date there — and it may never run\n368:     past the analysis date.\n369:     \"\"\"\n370:     if not isinstance(state, dict):\n371:         return None\n372:     company = state.get(\"company_of_interest\")\n373:     trade_date = state.get(\"trade_date\")\n374:     if not isinstance(company, str) or company.strip().upper() != run[\"ticker\"].strip().upper():\n375:         return None\n376:     if not isinstance(trade_date, str) or trade_date.strip() != run[\"as_of_date\"].strip():\n377:         return None\n378:     analysis = _calendar_date(run[\"as_of_date\"])\n379:     if analysis is None:\n380:         return None\n381:     args = call.get(\"args\") or {}\n382:     requested = args.get(\"curr_date\") if isinstance(args, dict) else None\n383:     try:\n384:         cutoff = _calendar_date(str(as_of(requested, trade_date)))\n385:     except (TypeError, ValueError):\n386:         return None\n387:     if cutoff is None or cutoff > analysis:\n388:         return None\n389:     return cutoff\n390: \n391: \n392: def _quote_request(payload, run, cutoff):\n393:     \"\"\"The C2 price gap the snapshot states, or None when it is not verifiable here.\n394: \n395:     The stock must be this run's, the reply's stated cutoff the effective one,\n396:     the trading day a real date that is not later than that cutoff (a weekend or\n397:     holiday is served by the last trading day before it, and an explicitly\n398:     earlier query is allowed too), the currency a plain code, and both figures\n399:     finite. Field, day and currency are the ones the Yahoo snapshot reported.\n400:     \"\"\"\n401:     if payload.get(\"as_of_date\") != cutoff.isoformat():\n402:         return None\n403:     symbol = payload.get(\"symbol\")\n404:     if not isinstance(symbol, str) or symbol.strip().upper() != run[\"ticker\"].strip().upper():\n405:         return None\n406:     trading_day = _calendar_date(payload.get(\"trading_date\"))\n407:     if trading_day is None or trading_day > cutoff:\n408:         return None\n409:     currency = payload.get(\"currency\")\n410:     if not _is_quote_currency(currency):\n411:         return None\n412:     close = _decimal(payload.get(\"close\"))\n413:     upper = _decimal(payload.get(\"boll_ub\"))\n414:     if close is None or upper is None:\n415:         return None\n416: \n417:     instant = {\"kind\": \"instant\", \"start\": trading_day.isoformat(),\n418:                \"end\": trading_day.isoformat(), \"label\": f\"{trading_day.isoformat()} quote\"}\n419:     source = f\"quote:{run['ticker'].strip().upper()}:{trading_day.isoformat()}\"\n420:     return {\"kind\": \"price_delta\", \"operands\": [\n421:         {\"role\": \"current\", \"value\": str(upper), \"unit\": currency,\n422:          \"period\": dict(instant), \"source_ref\": source, \"field_ref\": \"boll_ub\"},\n423:         {\"role\": \"reference\", \"value\": str(close), \"unit\": currency,\n424:          \"period\": dict(instant), \"source_ref\": source, \"field_ref\": \"Close\"},\n425:     ]}\n426: \n427: \n428: def _quote_outcome(request, reply):\n429:     \"\"\"The reply unchanged, or a Command that also hands over the verified price gap.\n430: \n431:     Only the market tool's own successful reply is read, matched to its call by\n432:     name and ID and by the reply carrying that ID. A reply with no usable source,\n433:     a run that is not this invocation's, or a metric the module refuses all\n434:     return the reply exactly as it was: nothing is invented and no run is made.\n435:     \"\"\"\n436:     call = getattr(request, \"tool_call\", None) or {}\n437:     if not isinstance(call, dict) or call.get(\"name\") != _QUOTE_TOOL:\n438:         return reply\n439:     call_id = call.get(\"id\")\n440:     if not isinstance(reply, ToolMessage):\n441:         return reply\n442:     if not call_id or reply.tool_call_id != call_id or reply.name != call[\"name\"]:\n443:         return reply\n444:     if getattr(reply, \"status\", \"success\") == \"error\":\n445:         return reply\n446:     state = getattr(request, \"state\", None) or {}\n447:     run = _valid_run(state)\n448:     if run is None:\n449:         return reply\n450:     cutoff = _effective_cutoff(state, call, run)\n451:     if cutoff is None:\n452:         return reply\n453:     payload = _quote_source_line(reply.content)\n454:     if payload is None:\n455:         return reply\n456:     request_body = _quote_request(payload, run, cutoff)\n457:     if request_body is None:\n458:         return reply\n459: \n460:     result = verify_metric(request_body, run)\n461:     if not isinstance(result, dict) or result.get(\"status\") != VERIFIED:\n462:         return reply\n463:     metric = result.get(\"metric\")\n464:     if not isinstance(metric, dict) or not metric.get(\"metric_id\"):\n465:         return reply\n466:     return Command(update={\n467:         \"messages\": [reply],\n468:         \"verified_metrics\": {metric[\"metric_id\"]: metric},\n469:     })\n470: \n471: \n472: # --- The statement tools' filed facts ----------------------------------------\n473: #\n474: # The two statement replies end in a source array, one entry per printed cell.\n475: # Only a successful reply of the tool that was actually called is read, and\n476: # only through the same name, ID, run and effective cutoff the quote path uses.\n477: # A fact is cited only when its own record is complete and its period, unit and\n478: # scale can be stated exactly; the metric module then decides whether the pair\n479: # it forms is comparable.\n480: \n481: _STATEMENT_SOURCE_PREFIX = \"# FR02_SEC_SOURCE \"\n482: _INCOME_TOOL = \"get_income_statement\"\n483: _CASHFLOW_TOOL = \"get_cashflow\"\n484: _YOY_ITEMS = (\"Revenue\", \"Cost of Revenue\")\n485: _FREQUENCIES = (\"quarterly\", \"annual\")\n486: \n487: _MILLIONS = Decimal(1000000)\n488: _YEAR_DAYS = (300, 400)\n489: _QUARTER_DAYS = (60, 115)\n490: \n491: \n492: def _statement_source_array(text):\n493:     \"\"\"The statement's source array on the reply's own last line, or None.\n494: \n495:     Only the final nonblank line is considered and it must carry exactly the\n496:     prefix; numbers keep their precision through ``Decimal``. A missing prefix,\n497:     unreadable JSON or a payload that is not a list reads as no source.\n498:     \"\"\"\n499:     lines = [line for line in str(text if text is not None else \"\").splitlines() if line.strip()]\n500:     if not lines or not lines[-1].startswith(_STATEMENT_SOURCE_PREFIX):\n501:         return None\n502:     try:\n503:         payload = json.loads(lines[-1][len(_STATEMENT_SOURCE_PREFIX):], parse_float=Decimal)\n504:     except (ValueError, TypeError):\n505:         return None\n506:     return payload if isinstance(payload, list) else None\n507: \n508: \n509: def _stated_fact(entry, run, cutoff, freq):\n510:     \"\"\"(fact, period) for one citable source entry, or None.\n511: \n512:     The entry must name this run's stock and the effective cutoff; carry the\n513:     filer's CIK, tag, accession, item, period and span; have a period equal to\n514:     the fact's own end and a span of integer 0 (the quarter or year itself, not\n515:     a year-to-date column); state real dates with start not after end, and neither\n516:     the period end nor the filing date after the cutoff; and carry a finite\n517:     non-boolean value whose scale is the one its unit uses — USD printed in\n518:     millions divides by 1,000,000, any other unit is kept only at exactly 1.\n519:     The period must also cover one span of the call's own frequency.\n520:     \"\"\"\n521:     if not isinstance(entry, dict):\n522:         return None\n523:     ticker = entry.get(\"ticker\")\n524:     if not isinstance(ticker, str) or ticker.strip().upper() != run[\"ticker\"].strip().upper():\n525:         return None\n526:     if entry.get(\"as_of\") != cutoff.isoformat():\n527:         return None\n528:     for field in (\"cik\", \"tag\", \"accn\", \"item\", \"period\"):\n529:         if not isinstance(entry.get(field), str) or not entry.get(field).strip():\n530:             return None\n531: \n532:     span = entry.get(\"span\")\n533:     if isinstance(span, bool) or not isinstance(span, int) or span != 0:\n534:         return None\n535: \n536:     start = _calendar_date(entry.get(\"start\"))\n537:     end = _calendar_date(entry.get(\"end\"))\n538:     filed = _calendar_date(entry.get(\"filed\"))\n539:     if start is None or end is None or filed is None:\n540:         return None\n541:     if start > end or end > filed or filed > cutoff:\n542:         return None\n543:     if _calendar_date(entry.get(\"period\")) != end:\n544:         return None\n545: \n546:     days = (end - start).days + 1\n547:     low, high = _QUARTER_DAYS if freq == \"quarterly\" else _YEAR_DAYS\n548:     if not low <= days <= high:\n549:         return None\n550: \n551:     raw = _decimal(entry.get(\"value\"))\n552:     if raw is None:\n553:         return None\n554:     unit = entry.get(\"unit\")\n555:     if not isinstance(unit, str) or not unit.strip():\n556:         return None\n557:     divisor = _decimal(entry.get(\"display_divisor\"))\n558:     if divisor is None:\n559:         return None\n560:     if unit.strip() == \"USD\":\n561:         if divisor != _MILLIONS:\n562:             return None\n563:         value, scaled = raw / divisor, \"USD_millions\"\n564:     else:\n565:         if divisor != Decimal(1):\n566:             return None\n567:         value, scaled = raw, unit.strip()\n568: \n569:     fact = {\n570:         \"item\": entry[\"item\"].strip(),\n571:         \"tag\": entry[\"tag\"].strip(),\n572:         \"accn\": entry[\"accn\"].strip(),\n573:         \"cik\": entry[\"cik\"].strip(),\n574:         \"start\": start,\n575:         \"end\": end,\n576:         \"filed\": filed,\n577:         \"value\":
