None,\n62:     ):\n63:         \"\"\"Initialize the trading agents graph and components.\n64: \n65:         Args:\n66:             selected_analysts: List of analyst types to include\n67:             debug: Whether to run in debug mode\n68:             config: Configuration dictionary. If None, uses default config\n69:             callbacks: Optional list of callback handlers (e.g., for tracking LLM/tool stats)\n70:         \"\"\"\n71:         self.debug = debug\n72:         self.config = config or DEFAULT_CONFIG\n73:         self.callbacks = callbacks or []\n74: \n75:         set_config(self.config)\n76: \n77:         os.makedirs(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n78:         os.makedirs(self.config[\"results_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n79: \n80:         extra = {\"callbacks\": self.callbacks} if self.callbacks else {}\n81:         self.deep_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"deep\", **extra).get_llm()\n82:         self.quick_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"quick\", **extra).get_llm()\n83: \n84:         self.memory_log = TradingMemoryLog(self.config)\n85: \n86:         self.conditional_logic = ConditionalLogic(\n87:             max_debate_rounds=self.config[\"max_debate_rounds\"],\n88:             max_risk_discuss_rounds=self.config[\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"],\n89:         )\n90:         # An analyst takes two graph steps per tool round, plus its first turn\n91:         # and its wrap-up; a limit past the recursion limit would end the run\n92:         # there instead.\n93:         max_tool_rounds, max_recur_limit = self.config[\"max_tool_rounds\"], self.config[\"max_recur_limit\"]\n94:         if 2 * max_tool_rounds + 2 >= max_recur_limit:\n95:             raise ValueError(\n96:                 f\"max_tool_rounds={max_tool_rounds} needs max_recur_limit above {2 * max_tool_rounds + 2}\"\n97:             )\n98:         self.graph_setup = GraphSetup(\n99:             self.quick_thinking_llm,\n100:             self.deep_thinking_llm,\n101:             self.conditional_logic,\n102:             max_tool_rounds,\n103:         )\n104: \n105:         self.propagator = Propagator(\n106:             max_recur_limit=max_recur_limit,\n107:         )\n108:         self.reflector = Reflector(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n109: \n110:         # Graph-shape-affecting run choices, kept for the checkpoint signature.\n111:         self.selected_analysts = tuple(selected_analysts)\n112: \n113:         # Set up the graph: keep the workflow for recompilation with a checkpointer.\n114:         self.workflow = self.graph_setup.setup_graph(selected_analysts, memory_node=self._memory_step)\n115:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n116:         self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n117:         self._resuming = False\n118: \n119:     def resolve_instrument_context(self, ticker: str, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n120:                                    trade_date: str | None = None) -> str:\n121:         \"\"\"Resolve ticker identity once and return the full instrument context.\n122: \n123:         Deterministic yfinance lookup (cached, fail-open) injected into a\n124:         context string so every agent anchors to the real company instead of\n125:         hallucinating one from the price chart (#814). Both the propagate()\n126:         path and the CLI call this so the resolved identity reaches the whole\n127:         graph regardless of entry point.\n128:         \"\"\"\n129:         identity = resolve_instrument_identity(ticker)\n130:         return build_instrument_context(ticker, asset_type, identity, trade_date)\n131: \n132:     def _memory_as_of(self, trade_date) -> str | None:\n133:         \"\"\"Point-in-time cutoff for past-context lessons (#1251).\n134: \n135:         A historical/backtest run (trade date before today) filters lessons to\n136:         those already resolved by the trade date. A current-date run returns\n137:         None, disabling the filter so live behavior and pre-migration entries\n138:         (which have no stored resolution date) are unaffected.\n139:         \"\"\"\n140:         return str(trade_date) if is_historical(trade_date) else None\n141: \n142:     def _run_signature(self, asset_type: str, portfolio=None) -> str:\n143:         \"\"\"Run inputs that must invalidate a checkpoint if changed.\n144: \n145:         Keyed into the checkpoint thread ID so a resume under a different analyst\n146:         selection, debate/risk depth, or asset mode starts fresh instead of\n147:         silently continuing the previous graph (#1089). The rest of the config\n148:         counts too (provider, models, endpoint, language, vendors, limits): a\n149:         resume must not carry reports that other settings produced. Only where\n150:         the run keeps its files and how it retries are left out.\n151:         \"\"\"\n152:         settings = {k: v for k, v in self.config.items() if k not in _NOT_IN_SIGNATURE}\n153:         digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(settings, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]\n154:         return \"|\".join([\n155:             \"analysts=\" + \",\".join(self.selected_analysts),\n156:             f\"debate={self.config['max_debate_rounds']}\",\n157:             f\"risk={self.config['max_risk_discuss_rounds']}\",\n158:             f\"asset={asset_type}\",\n159:             # None, an empty book and a changed book are three different runs.\n160:             f\"portfolio={portfolio.fingerprint() if portfolio is not None else 'none'}\",\n161:             # The layout itself: a checkpoint saved when analysts ran one after\n162:             # another has pending nodes this graph no longer has, and one saved\n163:             # before the Memory Log step would resume without the lessons.\n164:             \"analysts=parallel\",\n165:             \"memory=parallel\",\n166:             f\"settings={digest}\",\n167:         ])\n168: \n169:     def propagate(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n170:         \"\"\"Run the trading agents graph for a company on a specific date.\n171: \n172:         ``asset_type`` selects between the stock pipeline (default) and the\n173:         crypto pipeline (``\"crypto\"``) shipped in #567 — the CLI auto-detects\n174:         from the ticker; programmatic callers pass it explicitly. When\n175:         ``checkpoint_enabled`` is set in config, the graph is recompiled with\n176:         a per-ticker SqliteSaver so a crashed run can resume from the last\n177:         successful node on a subsequent invocation with the same ticker+date.\n178: \n179:         Returns ``(final_state, signal)`` where ``signal`` is one of the 5-tier\n180:         ratings (Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) or ``\"REVIEW\"``\n181:         when the decision had no parseable rating (#1170); guard with\n182:         ``tradingagents.agents.rating.is_review`` before mapping it to the\n183:         PortfolioRating enum.\n184:         \"\"\"\n185:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n186: \n187:         with run_config(self.config), \\\n188:                 self.checkpoint_scope(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio) as thread_id_value:\n189:             return self._run_graph(\n190:                 company_name, trade_date, asset_type=asset_type,\n191:                 checkpoint_thread_id=thread_id_value, portfolio=portfolio,\n192:             )\n193: \n194:     def begin_checkpoint(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None) -> str | None:\n195:         \"\"\"Recompile the graph with a per-ticker checkpointer and return the\n196:         ``thread_id`` to inject into the stream/invoke ``config`` (or ``None``\n197:         when checkpointing is disabled).\n198: \n199:         Pair every call with :meth:`end_checkpoint` in a ``finally``. Both\n200:         ``propagate`` (via :meth:`checkpoint_scope`) and the CLI stream path use\n201:         this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup\n202:         lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less\n203:         graph, making the flag a no-op.\n204:         \"\"\"\n205:         self._resuming = False\n206:         if not self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n207:             return None\n208:         signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)\n209:         self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name)\n210:         saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()\n211:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)\n212: \n213:         step = checkpoint_step(\n214:             self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature\n215:         )\n216:         self._resuming = step is not None\n217:         if step is not None:\n218:             logger.info(\"Resuming from step %d for %s on %s\", step, company_name, trade_date)\n219:         else:\n220:             logger.info(\"Starting fresh for %s on %s\", company_name, trade_date)\n221:         return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)\n222: \n223:     def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):\n224:         \"\"\"The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,\n225:         else the initial state for a fresh run.\n226: \n227:         LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;\n228:         re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message\n229:         reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).\n230:         \"\"\"\n231:         return None if self._resuming else init_state\n232: \n233:     def end_checkpoint(self):\n234:         \"\"\"Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run.\"\"\"\n235:         if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:\n236:             self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)\n237:             self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n238:             self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n239:         self._resuming = False\n240: \n241:     @contextmanager\n242:     def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n243:         \"\"\"Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path.\"\"\"\n244:         try:\n245:             yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n246:         finally:\n247:             self.end_checkpoint()\n248: \n249:     def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n250:         \"\"\"Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249).\"\"\"\n251:         if self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n252:             clear_checkpoint(\n253:                 self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date),\n254:                 self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),\n255:             )\n256: \n257:     def run_settings(self) -> dict:\n258:         \"\"\"What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.\n259: \n260:         An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and\n261:         local paths are never recorded.\n262:         \"\"\"\n263:         cfg = self.config\n264:         return {\n265:             \"version\": tradingagents.__version__,\n266:             \"llm_provider\": cfg.get(\"llm_provider\"),\n267:             \"deep_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"deep\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n268:             \"deep_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"deep_think_llm\"),\n269:             \"quick_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"quick\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n270:             \"quick_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"quick_think_llm\"),\n271:             \"analysts\": list(self.selected_analysts),\n272:             \"max_debate_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_debate_rounds\"),\n273:             \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"),\n274:             \"output_language\": cfg.get(\"output_language\"),\n275:             \"data_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"data_vendors\") or {}),\n276:             \"tool_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"tool_vendors\") or {}),\n277:         }\n278: \n279:     def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:\n280:         \"\"\"Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.\n281: \n282:         Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass\n283:         an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the\n284:         report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.\n285: \n286:         FR-01 / INV-01: an official report is written only from the publication\n287:         gate's own ``publication_result``. A state that never passed the gate — no\n288:         result, or only a flat ``publication_status`` someone set — raises\n289:         ``PublicationRequiredError`` and writes nothing, so a candidate can never\n290:         be saved as an official decision. A real BLOCKED result still writes a\n291:         diagnostic report: the same tree without an official rating, without the\n292:         candidate body and without ``5_portfolio/decision.md``.\n293:         \"\"\"\n294:         from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import (\n295:             PublicationRequiredError,\n296:             publication_result_from_state,\n297:         )\n298: \n299:         result = publication_result_from_state(final_state)\n300:         if result is None:\n301:             raise PublicationRequiredError(\n302:                 \"save_reports() needs the publication gate's publication_result; this \"\n303:                 \"state has none (a flat publication_status is not a gate result), so no \"\n304:                 \"official report was written\"\n305:             )\n306:         if save_path is None:\n307:             save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)\n308:         return write_report_tree(\n309:             final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html,\n310:         )\n311: \n312:     def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:\n313:         \"\"\"Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now.\"\"\"\n314:         stamp = datetime.now().strftime(\"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S\")\n315:         return Path(self.config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"reports\" / f\"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}\"\n316: \n317:     def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n318:         \"\"\"Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.\n319: \n320:         Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The\n321:         memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles\n322:         and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).\n323:         \"\"\"\n324:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n325:         # The initial state mints this run's one ``course_run`` identity, so the\n326:         # propagator call must read this graph's config on every entry path\n327:         # (propagate(), the CLI stream, a bare create_run_state()): inside its own\n328:         # ``run_config`` block the identity no longer depends on whatever happened\n329:         # to be serving config at call time. Nested blocks restore the outer one on\n330:         # exit, so propagating callers see the config they set.\n331:         with run_config(self.config):\n332:             return self.propagator.create_initial_state(\n333:                 company_name,\n334:                 trade_date,\n335:                 asset_type=asset_type,\n336:                 instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),\n337:                 portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else \"\",\n338:             )\n339: \n340:     def _run_budget(self, init_agent_state) -> RequestBudget | None:\n341:         \"\"\"The metered budget for this run, or ``None`` when metering is off.\n342: \n343:         One ``RequestBudget`` per main analysis flow (NFR-01 / INV-02, C4), keyed\n344:         by the run identity the initial state already minted, with the limit\n345:         recorded on its ``course_run``. ``None`` outside ``request_budget_enabled``\n346:         (no budget is fabricated). Under it, a run with no usable identity refuses\n347:         rather than running unlimited: a missing or malformed ``course_run`` raises\n348:         ``ValueError``, and :class:`RequestBudget` refuses a missing or non-positive\n349:         limit.\n350:         \"\"\"\n351:         if not self.config.get(\"request_budget_enabled\"):\n352:             return None\n353:         course_run = init_agent_state.get(\"course_run\") if isinstance(init_agent_state, dict) else None\n354:         if not isinstance(course_run, dict):\n355:             raise ValueError(\n356:                 \"request metering is enabled but the initial state carries no course_run; \"\n357:                 \"refusing to run unmetered\"\n358:             )\n359:         return RequestBudget(course_run.get(\"run_id\"), course_run.get(\"request_limit\"))\n360: \n361:     def _terminal_state(self, graph_input, init_agent_state, exc: BaseException, latest=None) -> dict | None:\n362:         \"\"\"The one final state of a run that ended on a recognized C4/C5 failure.\n363: \n364:         Built from ``init_agent_state`` — so a resumed run that streamed ``None``\n365:         still has the identity the gate needs — then overlaid with whatever the run\n366:         had produced (``latest``) and the terminal C0 code in the flat\n367:         ``execution_status`` and on its ``course_run``. ``None`` when the failure is\n368:         not a recognized budget/context/provider refusal: the caller re-raises.\n369:         \"\"\"\n370:         if latest is None:\n371:             latest = graph_input if graph_input is not None else init_agent_state\n372:         terminal = terminal_request_status(exc)\n373:         if terminal is None:\n374:             return None\n375:         # Actual latest values win over the initial state; a partial state never\n376:         # removes an identity field it did not see.\n377:         final_state = {}\n378:         for source in (init_agent_state, latest):\n379:             if isinstance(source, dict):\n380:                 final_state.update(source)\n381:         final_state[\"execution_status\"] = terminal\n382:         course_run = final_state.get(\"course_run\")\n383:         if isinstance(course_run, dict):\n384:             final_state[\"course_run\"] = {**course_run, \"execution_status\": terminal}\n385:         return final_state\n386: \n387:     def _memory_step(self, state):\n388:         \"\"\"The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every\n389:         ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the\n390:         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).\n391: \n392:         Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,\n393:         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here\n394:         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in\n395:         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.\n396:         \"\"\"\n397:         note = \"\"\n398:         try:\n399:             # Settlement and reflection are historical work, not part of the run's\n400:             # model flow (NFR-01 / INV-02, C4): their requests are made outside the\n401:             # run's budget scope, so they never consume a slot from it. An explicit\n402:             # ``None`` scope keeps that true even when a caller has one published.\n403:             with request_budget_scope(None):\n404:                 # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.\n405:                 done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)\n406:             if done.failed:\n407:                 note = (f\"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run \"\n408:                         \"and stay pending.\")\n409:         except Exception as exc:\n410:             logger.warning(\"Settling past decisions failed: %s\", exc)\n411:             note = f\"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending.\"\n412:         try:\n413:             past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(\n414:                 state[\"company_of_interest\"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state[\"trade_date\"]))\n415:         except Exception as exc:\n416:             logger.warning(\"Reading the memory log failed: %s\", exc)\n417:             past_context = \"\"\n418:             note = note or f\"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__}).\"\n419:         return {\"past_context\": past_context, \"memory_note\": note}\n420: \n421:     def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:\n422:         \"\"\"Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.\n423: \n424:         A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own\n425:         decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done\n426:         analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to\n427:         settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.\n428:         \"\"\"\n429:         with run_config(self.config):\n430:             return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)\n431: \n432:     def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:\n433:         \"\"\"Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).\n434: \n435:         For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would\n436:         otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.\n437:         With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.\n438:         \"\"\"\n439:         with run_config(self.config):\n440:             return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)\n441: \n442:     def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):\n443:         \"\"\"Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log\n444:         for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here.\n445: \n446:         FR-01 / INV-01: a run the publication gate blocked writes nothing to\n447:         decision memory — not a rating, not even a REVIEW entry — and its state log\n448:         omits the candidate body.\n449:         \"\"\"\n450:         self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)\n451:         from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import publication_result_from_state\n452: \n453:         result = publication_result_from_state(final_state)\n454:         if result is None or not result.approved:\n455:             logger.warning(\n456:                 \"Publication blocked for %s on %s (%s); nothing added to the memory log\",\n457:                 company_name, trade_date,\n458:                 result.reason if result is not None else \"no gate result\",\n459:             )\n460:             return\n461:         decision = final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\")\n462:         if not decision:\n463:             logger.warning(\"No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log\",\n464:                            company_name, trade_date)\n465:             return\n466:         self.memory_log.store_decision(\n467:             ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,\n468:             rating=run_rating(final_state),\n469:         )\n470: \n471:     def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n472:                    checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):\n473:         \"\"\"Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log.\"\"\"\n474:         init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n475:         args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()\n476: \n477:         # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same\n478:         # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).\n479:         if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:\n480:             args.setdefault(\"config\", {}).setdefault(\"configurable\", {})[\"thread_id\"] = checkpoint_thread_id\n481: \n482:         # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).\n483:         graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)\n484:         if self.debug:\n485:             # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).\n486:             final_state, printed = {}, set()\n487:             for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):\n488:                 for msg in messages:\n489:                     key = getattr(msg, \"id\", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, \"content\", None))\n490:                     if key not in printed:\n491:                         printed.add(key)\n492:                         msg.pretty_print()\n493:                 if state is not None:\n494:                     final_state.update(state)\n495:         else:\n496:             # NFR-01 / INV-02 (C4): one budget for this run, published for the\n497:             # whole invoke so every outbound request of the flow is metered. A\n498:             # recognized refusal ends the run with a terminal state instead of\n499:             # propagating a half-finished graph — recording the terminal code on a\n500:             # final state whose normal tail still runs (the gate then blocks it),\n501:             # so the API and CLI end the same way; any other error re-raises.\n502:             budget = self._run_budget(init_agent_state)\n503:             try:\n504:                 with request_budget_scope(budget):\n505:                     final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)\n506:             except Exception as exc:\n507:                 terminal_state = self._terminal_state(graph_input, init_agent_state, exc)\n508:                 if terminal_state is None:\n509:                     raise\n510:                 run_id = (init_agent_state.get(\"course_run\") or {}).get(\"run_id\")\n511:                 logger.warning(\n512:                     \"Run %s for %s on %s ended as %s\",\n513:                     run_id, company_name, trade_date, terminal_state[\"execution_status\"],\n514:                 )\n515:                 final_state = terminal_state\n516: \n517:         # The graph returned normally, so the run finished: only now does its\n518:         # execution state become COMPLETED. A run that raised above never reaches\n519:         # this line and stays RUNNING, which the gate refuses as RUN_NOT_COMPLETE.\n520:         # complete_run() keeps a terminal code already recorded (C0).\n521:         self.complete_run(final_state)\n522: \n523:         self.publish(final_state)\n524: \n525:         self.record_decision(company_name, trade_date, final_state)\n526: \n527:         # Clear checkpoint on successful completion to avoid stale state. A run\n528:         # that ended on a terminal failure keeps its checkpoint, as before.\n529:         if final_state.get(\"execution_status\") == \"COMPLETED\":\n530:             self.clear_checkpoint_on_success(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n531: \n532:         return final_state, run_rating(final_state)\n533: \n534:     def complete_run(self, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n535:         \"\"\"Mark a run that finished normally as ``COMPLETED`` (C0).\n536: \n537:         The only place a run becomes ``COMPLETED``: ``_run_graph`` and the CLI\n538:         call it after the graph returns normally, right before the gate judges the\n539:         candidate. It is not\n27: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than\n28: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum\n29: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.\n30: RATING_REVIEW = \"REVIEW\"\n31: \n32: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}\n33: \n34: # Matches \"Rating: X\" / \"rating - X\" / \"Rating — **X**\" — tolerates markdown\n35: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. \"rating\"\n36: # must start a word, so \"Operating margin: Sell-side\" is not a label.\n37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r\"(?<![a-z])rating\\b[^:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(\\w+)\",\n38:                               re.IGNORECASE)\n39: \n40: # The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to\n41: # open with (\"- **Rating**: X\", \"**Final Rating**: X\", \"## Our rating - X\"): an\n42: # optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the\n43: # decision itself before \"rating\". \"Consensus rating: Buy\" or \"Trader's rating:\n44: # Buy\" is someone else's rating.\n45: _OWN_QUALIFIER = r\"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\\s+)*\"\n46: _RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(\n47:     r\"\\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\\u2022]|\\d+[.)])\\s+)?[\\s*_#]*\" + _OWN_QUALIFIER\n48:     + r\"rating[^\\w:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015]*[:\\-\\u2010-\\u2015][\\s*]*(?P<value>\\w+)\",\n49:     re.IGNORECASE,\n50: )\n51: \n52: # A line presenting the scale rather than a decision (\"Rating Scale: Buy, ...\").\n53: _RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r\"rating\\s*(scale|options|legend)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n54: \n55: def extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:\n56:     \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.\n57: \n58:     Reads an explicit \"Rating: X\" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the\n59:     NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``\n60:     matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own\n61:     rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.\n62:     \"\"\"\n63:     if not text:\n64:         return None\n65:     norm = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", text)\n66: \n67:     # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any\n68:     # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote\n69:     # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's\n70:     # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label\n71:     # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing\n72:     # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the\n73:     # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.\n74:     lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]\n75:     first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith(\"#\")\n76:                   or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), \"\")\n77:     m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)\n78:     opening = m if m and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET else None\n79:     if opening and not opening.group(\"item\"):\n80:         return opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()\n81: \n82:     own = [opening.group(\"value\").capitalize()] if opening else []\n83:     labels = []\n84:     for line in lines:\n85:         m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)\n86:         if m and not m.group(\"item\") and m.group(\"value\").lower() in _RATING_SET:\n87:             own.append(m.group(\"value\").capitalize())\n88:         labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]\n89:     # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be\n90:     # one the text argues against (\"not a Sell\"), and reading it reports a\n91:     # direction nobody decided.\n92:     found = own or labels\n93:     return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None\n94: \n95: \n96: def parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:\n97:     \"\"\"Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.\n98: \n99:     For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's\n100:     entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.\n101:     \"\"\"\n102:     rating = extract_rating(text)\n103:     return rating if rating is not None else default\n104: \n105: \n106: def run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:\n107:     \"\"\"A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.\n108: \n109:     The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older\n110:     version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.\n111:     \"\"\"\n112:     return final_state.get(\"final_rating\") or parse_rating(final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\", \"\"))\n113: \n114: \n115: def is_review(signal: str) -> bool:\n116:     \"\"\"Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170).\"\"\"\n117:     return signal == RATING_REVIEW"

                "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/docs/architecture/adr/001-choice-tbd.md, lines 1-51\n1: # ADR-001 — Deterministic extensions at existing application boundaries\n2: \n3: Status: Proposed. Interface version: 1.0.\n4: \n5: ## Context and drivers\n6: \n7: The extension preserves the existing single-stock graph, model clients, data providers and publication paths. Architectural drivers are verifiable outputs, explicit degraded behavior, bounded dispatch, limited baseline changes and independent offline acceptance tests.\n8: \n9: ## Decision process and alternatives\n10: \n11: Trace the existing dispatch and publication paths, compare the candidates in the [evaluation table](../evaluation-table.md), define shared contracts and review adverse cases before implementation.\n12: \n13: | Option | Assessment |\n14: |---|---|\n15: | Prompt and configuration changes only | Insufficient enforcement of publication, arithmetic, missing-data state and total request limits |\n16: | Deterministic components at existing boundaries | Selected; supports the five acceptance contracts with localized integration |\n17: | Replacement orchestration | Deferred; increases migration and regression scope without an identified requirement |\n18: \n19: ## Component decisions\n20: \n21: | Requirement | Decision |\n22: |---|---|\n23: | FR-01 | Resolve current-run evidence and apply one publication result at every official sink |\n24: | FR-02 | Compute from validated operands; resolve immutable verified records by ID |\n25: | FR-03 | Separate source coverage, assessment and execution state; 0/3 yields UNKNOWN/null without a sentiment-model call |\n26: | NFR-01 | Atomically reserve capacity at a common outbound boundary |\n27: | NFR-02 | Reduce optional history at the two scoped sites; reject irreducible messages before budget reservation |\n28: \n29: Use [C0–C5](../interface-contracts.md) JSON-compatible shared records. Internal types may use adapters. Add separate owner keys to AgentState and retain legacy report strings as views of authoritative records.\n30: \n31: ## Layered model context\n32: \n33: Context layers are role/task identity, standing constraints, typed evidence and run state, active tool exchanges, optional discussion history and the current request. Mark required blocks explicitly.\n34: \n35: Assembly order: prioritize and deduplicate optional history; measure the final representation; remove optional groups oldest first; reassemble; re-inject critical constraints; verify required blocks and tool pairs; recount before dispatch. Preserve authoritative stored evidence when reducing a request. Refuse a scoped request when mandatory content cannot fit.\n36: \n37: NFR-02 uses a configurable 65536-byte message cap at analyst closure and the neutral risk role. It excludes separately bound tool schemas and is independent of token measurement.\n38: \n39: ## Token-budget design\n40: \n41: The input-token design uses a proposed cap of 16384 tokens and a compaction trigger above 13107 tokens (floor of 80% of the cap). Configure output allowance and provider-envelope reserve independently. Validate the selected model capacity, counting method, schema overhead and provider conversion before enabling this policy. Until then, token enforcement remains unverified. Byte counts are not a substitute for token counts.\n42: \n43: ## Run profile\n44: \n45: The initial product profile uses a configurable request limit of 40, both tiers on the school model alias, explicit thinking-disabled requests and an output allowance of 4096 tokens. NFR-01 boundary fixtures use limit 3. Configuration evidence accompanies baseline comparisons; changes to public semantics require a contract revision.\n46: \n47: ## Consequences and review triggers\n48: \n49: Benefits are localized changes and explicit failure states. Costs are shared dispatch/publication integration and nullable-state compatibility across existing consumers. Review this decision when provider retries become opaque, a sink bypasses publication checks, required context routinely cannot fit, or requirements need different orchestration.\n50: \n51: Changes to shared fields, date semantics, thresholds, safety behavior or dependencies require affected-owner review and synchronized requirements, interfaces and tests. Record the human decision and supporting evidence."

Runtime diagnostic outputs must not masquerade as official recommendations.\n12: \n13: ## Combined-path precedence (C0–C5)\n14: \n15: 1. Validate/reduce scoped context before reserving a model slot. CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE means no send or budget debit for that rejected request.\n16: 2. If context is ready but C4 has no slot, return BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Both terminal paths suppress any earlier candidate as an official final recommendation.\n17: 3. Invalid financial records are excluded; optional sentiment failures preserve per-source reasons and UNKNOWN/null where appropriate. Continue usable analysis rather than treating absent sentiment as a neutral signal or unconditional publication failure.\n18: 4. On nonzero source coverage but failed assessment, keep PARTIAL_DATA/AVAILABLE and record assessment failure with UNKNOWN/null. Coverage is collection state, not model confidence.\n19: 5. Gate any resulting candidate at every official sink. A source placeholder is not substantive evidence. Publication passes only when C1 succeeds, regardless of a model's requested rating.\n20: \n21: A user retry after a terminal failure is a new run with a new identity; do not resume the same metered identity with a fresh counter. Invalid configuration or unknown contract version blocks the affected task before live dispatch. Record implementation and case evidence for each failure path.\n22: \n23: Each enforcing component emits the specified receipt fields. Verification records identify the producing path, implementation revision and observed result."

Centralizing the mapping here means every yfinance\n19: entry point resolves symbols the same way, and new instruments are added by\n20: appending a table row rather than editing call sites.\n21: \"\"\"\n22: \n23: from __future__ import annotations\n24: \n25: import logging\n26: import re\n27: \n28: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n29: \n30: \n31: # ISO-4217 codes common enough to appear in retail forex pairs. A bare\n32: # six-letter symbol whose halves are BOTH in this set is treated as a spot\n33: # forex pair and given Yahoo's ``=X`` suffix.\n34: _FOREX_CURRENCIES = frozenset(\n35:     {\n36:         \"USD\", \"EUR\", \"GBP\", \"JPY\", \"CHF\", \"CAD\", \"AUD\", \"NZD\",\n37:         \"CNY\", \"CNH\", \"HKD\", \"SGD\", \"SEK\", \"NOK\", \"DKK\", \"PLN\",\n38:         \"MXN\", \"ZAR\", \"TRY\", \"INR\", \"KRW\", \"BRL\", \"RUB\", \"THB\",\n39:     }\n40: )\n41: \n42: # Crypto bases that brokers quote against USD without a separator.\n43: _CRYPTO_BASES = frozenset(\n44:     {\"BTC\", \"ETH\", \"SOL\", \"XRP\", \"ADA\", \"DOGE\", \"LTC\", \"BCH\", \"DOT\", \"AVAX\", \"LINK\"}\n45: )\n46: \n47: # Explicit aliases for instruments whose broker symbol does not map to a\n48: # Yahoo symbol by rule. Metals/energy resolve to their front-month future;\n49: # index CFD names resolve to the underlying Yahoo index symbol. Extend by\n50: # adding rows — no call site changes required.\n51: _ALIASES = {\n52:     # Precious metals (spot names -> COMEX/NYMEX futures)\n53:     \"XAUUSD\": \"GC=F\", \"XAU\": \"GC=F\", \"GOLD\": \"GC=F\",\n54:     \"XAGUSD\": \"SI=F\", \"XAG\": \"SI=F\", \"SILVER\": \"SI=F\",\n55:     \"XPTUSD\": \"PL=F\", \"XPDUSD\": \"PA=F\",\n56:     # Energy\n57:     \"WTICOUSD\": \"CL=F\", \"USOIL\": \"CL=F\", \"WTI\": \"CL=F\",\n58:     \"BCOUSD\": \"BZ=F\", \"UKOIL\": \"BZ=F\", \"BRENT\": \"BZ=F\",\n59:     \"NATGAS\": \"NG=F\", \"XNGUSD\": \"NG=F\",\n60:     \"COPPER\": \"HG=F\", \"XCUUSD\": \"HG=F\",\n61:     # Index CFDs -> Yahoo index symbols\n62:     \"SPX500\": \"^GSPC\", \"US500\": \"^GSPC\", \"SPX\": \"^GSPC\",\n63:     \"NAS100\": \"^NDX\", \"US100\": \"^NDX\", \"USTEC\": \"^NDX\",\n64:     \"US30\": \"^DJI\", \"DJI30\": \"^DJI\", \"WS30\": \"^DJI\",\n65:     \"GER40\": \"^GDAXI\", \"GER30\": \"^GDAXI\", \"DE40\": \"^GDAXI\",\n66:     \"UK100\": \"^FTSE\", \"JP225\": \"^N225\", \"JPN225\": \"^N225\",\n67:     \"FRA40\": \"^FCHI\", \"EU50\": \"^STOXX50E\", \"HK50\": \"^HSI\",\n68: }\n69: \n70: # HKEX codes as Yahoo spells them: the number zero-padded to 4 digits (#957).\n71: _HK_CODE = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{1,5})\\.HK$\")\n72: _SHANGHAI_SH = re.compile(r\"^(\\d{6})\\.SH$\")\n73: \n74: \n75: # Crypto quote currencies that all map to Yahoo's USD pair. Yahoo lists only\n76: # ``<BASE>-USD`` (not the USDT/USDC stablecoin pairs), so a broker symbol quoted\n77: # in any of these resolves to ``-USD`` (#982). Longest first so ``USDT``/``USDC``\n78: # match before the ``USD`` substring.\n79: _CRYPTO_QUOTES = (\"USDT\", \"USDC\", \"USD\")\n80: \n81: \n82: def crypto_base(raw: str) -> str | None:\n83:     \"\"\"Return the crypto base (e.g. ``BTC``) for a known USD/USDT/USDC-quoted\n84:     crypto symbol in any form the pipeline may hold — ``BTC-USD``, ``BTCUSD``,\n85:     ``BTC-USDT`` — or None for non-crypto symbols. Purely syntactic.\n86:     \"\"\"\n87:     if not isinstance(raw, str):\n88:         return None\n89:     compact = raw.strip().upper().rstrip(\"+\").replace(\"-\", \"\")\n90:     for quote in _CRYPTO_QUOTES:\n91:         if compact.endswith(quote):\n92:             base = compact[: -len(quote)]\n93:             return base if base in _CRYPTO_BASES else None\n94:     return None\n95: \n96: \n97: def _normalize_crypto(s: str) -> str | None:\n98:     \"\"\"Return ``<BASE>-USD`` for a known USD/USDT/USDC-quoted crypto, else None.\"\"\"\n99:     base = crypto_base(s)\n100:     return f\"{base}-USD\" if base else None\n101: \n102: \n103: def normalize_symbol(raw: str) -> str:\n104:     \"\"\"Map a user/broker symbol to its canonical Yahoo Finance symbol.\n105: \n106:     Resolution order (first match wins):\n107:       1. Explicit alias table (metals, energy, index CFDs).\n108:       2. Crypto rule: a known crypto base quoted in USD/USDT/USDC (dashed or\n109:          not) -> ``BASE-USD``.\n110:       3. Forex rule: six letters that are two ISO currency codes -> ``PAIR=X``.\n111:       4. HK rule: a numeric ``.HK`` code -> Yahoo's 4-digit padding\n112:          (``09992.HK`` -> ``9992.HK``, ``700.HK`` -> ``0700.HK``).\n113:       5. Shanghai rule: ``600519.SH`` -> ``600519.SS``.\n114:       6. Otherwise the upper-cased symbol is returned unchanged (plain\n115:          equities, ETFs, Yahoo-native symbols like ``GC=F`` or ``^GSPC``).\n116: \n117:     A trailing ``+`` (broker CFD marker, e.g. ``XAUUSD+``) is stripped before\n118:     matching. The function is purely syntactic — it performs no network\n119:     calls — so it is safe to apply on every request.\n120:     \"\"\"\n121:     if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():\n122:         return raw\n123: \n124:     s = raw.strip().upper()\n125:     # Broker CFD/qualifier suffixes Yahoo never uses.\n126:     s = s.rstrip(\"+\")\n127: \n128:     crypto = _normalize_crypto(s)\n129:     if s in _ALIASES:\n130:         canonical = _ALIASES[s]\n131:     elif crypto is not None:\n132:         canonical = crypto\n133:     elif len(s) == 6 and s[:3] in _FOREX_CURRENCIES and s[3:] in _FOREX_CURRENCIES:\n134:         canonical = f\"{s}=X\"\n135:     elif hk := _HK_CODE.match(s):\n136:         canonical = f\"{int(hk.group(1)):04d}.HK\"\n137:     elif sh := _SHANGHAI_SH.match(s):\n138:         canonical = f\"{sh.group(1)}.SS\"\n139:     else:\n140:         canonical = s\n141: \n142:     if canonical != raw.strip().upper():\n143:         logger.info(\"Resolved symbol %r to Yahoo symbol %r\", raw, canonical)\n144:     return canonical\n145: \n146: \n147: # Tickers can contain letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, caret\n148: # (index symbols like ^GSPC), equals (futures like GC=F), and plus\n149: # (forex/CFD symbols like XAUUSD+). None of these enable directory\n150: # traversal, so the value never escapes a containing directory when\n151: # interpolated into a path. Anything else is rejected.\n152: _TICKER_PATH_RE = re.compile(r\"^[A-Za-z0-9._\\-\\^=+]+$\")\n153: \n154: \n155: def safe_ticker_component(value: str, *, max_len: int = 32) -> str:\n156:     \"\"\"Validate ``value`` is safe to interpolate into a filesystem path.\n157: \n158:     Tickers come from user CLI input or from LLM tool calls, both of which\n159:     can be influenced by attacker-controlled content (e.g. prompt injection\n160:     embedded in fetched news). Without validation, a value like\n161:     ``\"../../../etc/foo\"`` flows into ``os.path.join`` / ``Path /`` and\n162:     escapes the configured cache, checkpoint, or results directory.\n163: \n164:     Returns ``value`` unchanged when it matches the allowed pattern; raises\n165:     ``ValueError`` otherwise.\n166:     \"\"\"\n167:     if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:\n168:         raise ValueError(f\"ticker must be a non-empty string, got {value!r}\")\n169:     if len(value) > max_len:\n170:         raise ValueError(f\"ticker exceeds {max_len} chars: {value!r}\")\n171:     if not _TICKER_PATH_RE.fullmatch(value):\n172:         raise ValueError(\n173:             f\"ticker contains characters not allowed in a filesystem path: {value!r}\"\n174:         )\n175:     # The regex above allows '.', so values like '.', '..', '...' would pass,\n176:     # and as a path component they traverse the parent directory. Reject any\n177:     # value that's only dots.\n178:     if set(value) == {\".\"}:\n179:         raise ValueError(f\"ticker cannot consist solely of dots: {value!r}\")\n180:     return value"

Do not resolve references from a prior run. |\n6: | FR-02 | Verified records are immutable within a run; report may retain source references and immutable calculation records. No user-wide metric cache in first release. |\n7: | FR-03 | Coverage and reasons are run-local; avoid persisting raw social responses. |\n8: | NFR-01 | Counter is run-local; a resumed metered run must not reset spent slots. Disable upstream checkpoint resume for metered course runs until counters can be restored atomically; restart is a distinct run. |\n9: | NFR-02 | Reduction is per request; optional context may be dropped from the sent payload only, not silently erased from approved evidence records. |\n10: \n11: Reuse the upstream user-owned decision log for approved decisions only and retain its configured rotation/deletion behavior. Keep course fixtures isolated from users' local caches and memory. Reports may contain nonsecret source metadata; users control local retention. No credentials, raw model sessions or student identifiers belong in public logs. Repeatability claims require a new run or an explicitly versioned snapshot, not a retained LLM answer.\n12: \n13: ## Shared state contract\n14: \n15: Use C0 identity and C1–C3 authoritative records from [interface-contracts.md](interface-contracts.md). Add coverage/assessment state beside existing sentiment text; downstream readers use authoritative fields rather than reparsing a Neutral placeholder. Keep data coverage, assessment failure, execution completion and publication approval separate. New runs never inherit prior scores, references or counters.\n16: \n17: Raw prompts, account details, personal API keys and complete vendor/social responses stay out of public logs and repository fixtures. Keep original private run receipts separately from shareable, synthetic test fixtures; record only approved references/hashes in public artifacts. Determine the team's actual retention duration before collecting new live payloads; no indefinite retention is implied."

evidence line, in either accepted shape: a bare \"E1\" beside\n# the full id on the same line, or an \"= E1\"-style tag appended to the line.\n_ALIAS_ON_EVIDENCE_LINE = re.compile(r\"^(?:- \"get_verified_market_snapshot\"\n\n\ndef _prompt_text(prompt) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The flattened text a structured call is given (a string or a PromptValue).\"\"\"\n    to_messages = getattr(prompt, isinstance(message, str):\n            parts.append(message)\n            continue\n        content = getattr(message, \"content\", \"\")\n        parts.append(content if isinstance(content, str) else \"\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\n\n\ndef _pin_snapshot(monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"Serve a fixed OHLCV frame in place of the vendor download.\"\"\"\n    import pandas as pd\n\n    import tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.snapshot as snapshot\n\n    frame = pd.DataFrame(\n        [\n            {\"Date\": d, \"Open\": o, \"High\": h, \"Low\": low, \"Close\": c, \"Volume\": v}\n m.group(2))\n        for m in _ALIAS_ON_EVIDENCE_LINE.finditer(prompt)\n    ]\n    return [alias for _pos, alias in sorted(found)]\n\n\nclass _ScriptedModel(BaseChatModel):\n    \"\"\"Emits fixed @property\n    def _llm_type(self) -> str:\n        return \"reference-alias-fake\"\n\n    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        return self\n\n    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):  # type: ignore[override]\n        if schema is DebateArgument:\n            return _StructuredArgument(self)\n        if schema is PortfolioDecision:\n tool_calls=[{\n                    \"name\": _SNAPSHOT_TOOL,\n                    \"args\": {\"curr_date\": TRADE_DATE, \"look_back_days\": 7},\n                    \"id\": \"call-1\",\n                }],\n            ))])\n        return ChatResult(generations=[ChatGeneration(message=AIMessage(\n            content=\"The 50-day breakout and volume confirm the uptrend.\"\n        ))])\n\n\nclass [aliases[0]]\n\n\ndef _cite_canonical_evidence(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    ids = _evidence_ids_in_prompt(text)\n    assert ids, \"the researcher prompt offered no canonical evidence ID\"\n    return Status: Proposed. Shared boundaries use JSON-compatible records. Internal dataclasses, TypedDict or Pydantic models may use adapters that preserve these fields and semantics. ADR-001 records the design decision.\n4: \n5: ## Ownership and integration\n6: \n7: | Contract | Authority | Producers and consumers |\n8: | --- | --- | --- |\n9: | C0 run identity and outcome | Run coordinator | All five owner modules, CLI, Python, report and memory |\n10: | C1 evidence and publication | FR-01 publication gate | Analyst evidence, accepted arguments, candidate, all official sinks |\n11: | C2 verified metrics | FR-02 metric registry | Fundamentals inputs, controlled downstream fields and metric table |\n12: | C3 sentiment coverage | FR-03 coverage component | Existing source adapters, analyst, state, report and downstream agents |\n13: | C4 dispatch budget | NFR-01 request-budget component | Both model tiers and every in-scope transport send |\n14: | C5 prepared context | NFR-02 context component | Analyst closure and neutral risk debater, then C4 |\n15: \n16: Shared-file integration owner: EverForests. Feature owners submit narrow patches for state, schema, graph/client and reporting adapters. Task plans identify exact paths. The integrator preserves approved contracts across patches; shared files must not be independently replaced by feature branches.\n17: \n18: ## C0 — identity, state and errors\n19: \n20: Every authoritative record carries `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and `as_of_date`. Evidence and metric IDs are only resolvable inside that run. Never retrieve a matching-looking ID from a previous run. A restarted run gets a new ID. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.\n21: \n22: Keep three concepts separate:\n23: \n24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.\n25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.\n26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.\n27: \n28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.\n29: \n30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication\n31: \n32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.\n33: \n34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.\n35: \n36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.\n37: \n38: The FR-01 model adapter may offer invocation-local `E1` evidence selections and `A1` accepted-argument selections. Freeze the mapping from that invocation's actual menu and resolve selections before C1 validation. Existing canonical IDs remain supported. Persist canonical IDs in evidence, accepted arguments, candidates and publication results. Unknown selections and truncated canonical IDs remain subject to rejection. Each short selection refers only to the current menu; the full records establish run ownership. See the [ADR reference-selection amendment](adr/001-choice-tbd.md#fr-01-reference-selection-adapter--19-november-2026).\n39: \n40: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.\n41: \n42: ## C2 — verified metrics\n43: \n44: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.\n45: \n46: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.\n47: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.\n48: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.\n49: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.\n50: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.\n51: \n52: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.\n53: \n54: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.\n55: \n56: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score\n57: \n58: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.\n59: \n60: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.\n61: \n62: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). AAPL as-of 2026-11-10 therefore covers 2026-11-03 through 2026-11-10. Freeze the clock for date-dependent fixtures. Historical undated content cannot prove window validity. Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.\n63: \n64: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. Never claim these statuses prove that no real-world messages/news exist.\n65: \n66: | Valid logical sources | coverage_status | Sentiment output |\n67: | --- | --- | --- |\n68: | 0/3 | NO_DATA | overall_band UNKNOWN; overall_score null |\n69: | 1/3 or 2/3 | PARTIAL_DATA | Coverage remains explicit; any measured score uses valid evidence only |\n70: | 3/3 | AVAILABLE | Coverage available; score still requires a valid assessment |\n71: \n72: Coverage is authoritative data state; the model cannot increase it. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. A genuine measured Neutral/5.0 remains legal.\n73: \n74: Missing scores never become 0 or 5 and never enter a numerical mean. Structured state, analyst message, downstream prompt and persisted/rendered report must agree. Handle nullable scores without numeric-format errors. Apply the contract to structured **and** free-text fallback; model narrative cannot override authoritative coverage. Keep the existing sentiment_report text as a compatibility view; the new sentiment_assessment record below is authoritative. Both must agree. Internal schema adaptation may change, but the v1 shared record does not drift silently.\n75: \n76: The original baseline stores `sentiment_report` as text and requires a nonnull numeric SentimentReport score. Updating only the prompt cannot establish this contract. No raw social bodies or credentials belong in public evidence. Missing optional sentiment does not stop otherwise valid market/fundamental analysis; C1 still decides publication.\n77: \n78: ## C4 — atomic per-run model dispatch\n79: \n80: Supported scope: one single-stock main analysis, both model tiers, structured/fallback requests and application retries. Count actual outgoing model attempts, not nodes, tool invocations, callbacks or tokens. Historical settlement is excluded. Disable SDK/transport implicit retries in supported course runs; unsupported hidden-retry modes are outside the verified configuration, not silently compliant.\n81: \n82: Budget state: positive integer `limit`, charged sends, active reservations and exhaustion. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation. Validate C5 first so context rejection obtains no reservation.\n83: \n84: No slot => BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no request, no official recommendation. Limit 3 allows exactly 3 attempts; the fourth is refused. Concurrent runs do not share counters. Include application fallback/retry attempts separately. C4 does not promise a monetary or token cap. Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.\n85: \n86: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context\n87: \n88: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. Other analyst turns and risk roles are not implicitly covered. Before reserving C4, fully expand/convert the scoped final message sequence into one agreed provider-facing representation.\n89: \n90: Canonical v1 measurement: the final provider-facing message array encoded as JSON with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon) without optional whitespace, allow_nan=False, then UTF-8. Use the ChatMessage representation below and freeze byte fixtures before implementation. Do not measure before template expansion or change representation after measuring. Tool schemas and other separately bound fields are excluded from this message metric and must be recorded/bounded separately; this is not a cap on the whole HTTP body.\n91: \n92: Required blocks: role/task identity; standing safety/publication rules; ticker/date/run identity; current required evidence/verified metrics/source coverage; and the active tool-call/result exchange. Optional blocks: explicitly marked older discussion/history. A tool-call/result pair is indivisible; if a member is required, preserve the whole pair. Text-wrapped tools retain name, arguments and corresponding result. Removing context cannot delete authoritative evidence/state from storage.\n93: \n94: At the configured 65536-byte acceptance cap: short input passes unchanged. If oversized, remove optional groups oldest first (stable original index for ties), reassemble, reinject critical constraints and remeasure. Do not summarize required evidence with another unmetered model call. If required blocks cannot fit or pairing cannot be preserved, return CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE; zero send, reservation and debit. Same normalized input/config produces identical prepared output. Run final retention/pairing checks before C4.\n95: \n96: This byte cap does not implement the separate D2 token-budget requirement. ADR-001 records that architecture design and the remaining tokenizer/model-capacity validation. Do not infer token counts from bytes/4 or claim provider safety from 64 KiB alone.\n97: \n98: ## Contract-change and approval record\n99: \n100: Before implementation, record requirement IDs, contract revision, baseline SHA, exact read/edit paths, fixture/case revision, reviewer and approval time. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Feature PRs link the approved plan and actual evidence; the coordinator runs integrated regressions before release.\n101: \n102: \n103: ## V1 shared record layout\n104: \n105: Version field: `contract_version = \"1.0\"`. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. Lists have deterministic order; ID-indexed registries are mappings, not unordered output prose.\n106: \n107: | Record | Required shared fields beyond identity | Owner |\n108: | --- | --- | --- |\n109: | RunContext | contract_version, execution_status, request_limit (positive integer) | Existing graph/run entry; integration by coordinator |\n110: | EvidenceRecord | evidence_id, source_kind, vendor, source_ref, content_ref, window_start, window_end | FR-01 collection/index adapter |\n111: | AcceptedArgument | argument_id, claim (nonempty text), evidence_ids (nonempty list) | FR-01 validates against run-local evidence; a model flag is not acceptance |\n112: | CandidateDecision | rating (untrusted string or null), argument_ids | Model/adapters produce; C1 decides |\n113: | PublicationResult | publication_status, reason_codes, rating (allowed string or null), argument_ids, evidence_ids | FR-01 |\n114: | Operand | role, value (finite decimal string), unit, period, source_ref, field_ref | FR-02 input adapter; roles current/prior/numerator/denominator/reference |\n115: | MetricRequest | kind (yoy/ratio/price_delta), operands | FR-02 input |\n116: | VerifiedMetric | metric_id, kind, operands, result_value (decimal string), result_unit, formula, source_refs | FR-02 immutable run-local registry |\n117: | MetricResult | status (VERIFIED/UNVERIFIABLE), metric (VerifiedMetric or null), reason_codes | FR-02 |\n118: | SourceOutcome | source_id, window_start, window_end, available (bool), valid_record_count, reason_codes, evidence_refs | FR-03 normalization adapter |\n119: | SentimentCoverage | coverage_status, valid_sources, total_sources (=3), sources (mapping keyed news/stocktwits/reddit) | FR-03 deterministic coverage |\n120: | SentimentAssessment | all SentimentCoverage fields, assessment_status (MEASURED/UNKNOWN), overall_band, overall_score, confidence, assessment_reason_codes, narrative | FR-03 deterministic finalization |\n121: | ContextBlock | group_id, required (bool), messages (list of ChatMessage); grouping metadata is never sent to the model | NFR-02 scoped adapter |\n122: | PreparedRequest | status (READY/CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE), messages (list or null), message_bytes, original_message_bytes, dropped_group_ids, required_groups_ok | NFR-02 or nonreducing adapter |\n123: | Reservation | reservation_id, run_id, state (reserved/charged/cancelled); opaque to other features | NFR-01 |\n124: \n125: `Operand.period` is `{kind, start, end, label}`: kind is quarter/year/instant, start/end are ISO dates, and label records the source's fiscal period or quote timestamp. Currency and scale are part of unit (for example USD vs USD_millions); conversion must be explicit and preserve original operands. Do not silently take abs(capex), invent comparable periods or round source values to make a fixture match. An EvidenceRecord source_ref identifies the source, while content_ref locates the retained shareable material/fixture; an ID with no resolvable retained material is insufficient.\n126: \n127: For SentimentAssessment, overall_band is one existing measured band or UNKNOWN. overall_score is a finite float in [0,10] for MEASURED, otherwise null. confidence keeps the existing low/medium/high vocabulary; UNKNOWN uses low and is not a measured weak-neutral signal. Missing sources are unavailable with reasons; valid sources have valid_record_count >=1. Missing uncollected source entries are normalized as unavailable with NOT_COLLECTED rather than increasing the denominator or silently disappearing. Extra providers do not count as fourth sources. Source order is news, stocktwits, reddit.\n128: \n129: `ChatMessage` contains provider-facing role, content and, when present, name/tool_call_id/tool_calls/reasoning_content. Preserve content strings or JSON-compatible content blocks without paraphrasing. Preserve each tool call's id, type, function name and arguments plus the paired tool result. Reasoning fields required by the selected provider's tool round-trip are mandatory if present. Do not add ContextBlock metadata to ChatMessage. The cap measures the agreed canonical message representation, not HTTP whitespace, the whole body, output tokens or hidden provider overhead.\n130: \n131: ## V1 callable boundaries (specification signatures, no implementation)\n132: \n133: Inputs are read-only to consumers. Return the declared records; do not attach extra authoritative fields through prose.
