you cannot cite any evidence ID.)\"\n356:     lines = []\n357:     for record in idx.evidence_records:\n358:         lines.append(f\"- {record.evidence_id}  [{record.source}] {record.excerpt}\")\n359:     return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n360: \n361: \n362: def _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n363:     \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n364:     flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n365:     return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n366: \n367: \n368: def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n369:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n370: \n371:     Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n372:     ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n373:     \"\"\"\n374:     if value is None:\n375:         return None\n376:     rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n377:     if not isinstance(rating, str):\n378:         return None\n379:     return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n380: \n381: \n382: def evaluate(index, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids) -> GateOutcome:\n383:     \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n384: \n385:     ``index`` may be the state dict or an EvidenceIndex. Order matters: an invalid\n386:     rating is reported before a missing chain, so a candidate that fails both\n387:     returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is consulted here.\n388:     \"\"\"\n389:     idx = as_index(index)\n390:     rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n391:     if rating is None:\n392:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n393: \n394:     cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n395:     resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n396:     for argument_id in cited:\n397:         if not idx.has_argument(argument_id):\n398:             continue\n399:         argument = idx.argument(argument_id)\n400:         for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n401:             if idx.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n402:                 resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, idx.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n403:     if not resolved:\n404:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n405: \n406:     return GateOutcome(\n407:         status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n408:     )\n409: \n410: \n411: def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n412:     \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n413: \n414:     On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the\n415:     candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the\n416:     returned state carries no candidate material at all — the candidate body,\n417:     candidate rating and candidate argument ids are removed from the mapping, so\n418:     the Python API's returned state cannot expose or re-derive the candidate. The\n419:     only place ``REVIEW`` appears is the API's second tuple member (computed by the\n420:     caller via ``run_rating``); ``final_rating`` is emptied here, not set to REVIEW.\n421:     \"\"\"\n422:     status = outcome.status\n423:     final_state[\"publication_status\"] = status\n424:     final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = outcome.reason\n425:     final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)\n426: \n427:     if outcome.approved:\n428:         body = final_state.get(\"candidate_decision\") or final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\") or \"\"\n429:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = outcome.rating\n430:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = body\n431:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n432:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n433:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n434:     else:\n435:         # No candidate material leaks into the returned state: the body, its rating\n436:         # and the ids it cited are all removed. ``final_rating`` is emptied rather\n437:         # than set to REVIEW; REVIEW is the API's second tuple member only.\n438:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = \"\"\n439:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n440:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n441:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n442:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n443:     return final_state\n444: \n445: \n446: # --- C1 v1.0: mapping-authoritative evaluation -------------------------------\n447: #\n448: # The authoritative indexes are ID -> record mappings: ``argument_index`` keyed by\n449: # ``argument_id`` and ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The legacy\n450: # shapes ``index_to_state(...)`` (lists under \"evidence\"/\"arguments\") and\n451: # ``accepted_arguments`` are a compatibility layer only: an argument that exists\n452: # solely in that view never resolves a reference.\n453: \n454: \n455: _IDENTITY_KEYS = (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"as_of_date\")\n456: \n457: # C1 v1.0 required shared fields, beyond identity. \"A missing required field is an\n458: # invalid record\": a record without one is not admissible evidence/acceptance.\n459: _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED = (\n460:     \"evidence_id\", \"source_kind\", \"vendor\", \"source_ref\",\n461:     \"content_ref\", \"window_start\", \"window_end\",\n462: )\n463: _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED = (\"argument_id\", \"claim\")\n464: \n465: \n466: def _field_present(record: dict, key: str) -> bool:\n467:     \"\"\"Whether a required field is present and non-empty.\n468: \n469:     A missing value, ``None``, an empty string and a whitespace-only string are\n470:     all the same thing here: no value. A list is present when it is non-empty.\n471:     \"\"\"\n472:     value = record.get(key)\n473:     if isinstance(value, str):\n474:         return bool(value.strip())\n475:     if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):\n476:         return len(value) > 0\n477:     return value is not None\n478: \n479: \n480: def _required_fields_ok(record, required) -> bool:\n481:     \"\"\"Whether every C1 required field of ``record`` is present and non-empty.\"\"\"\n482:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n483:         return False\n484:     return all(_field_present(record, key) for key in required)\n485: \n486: \n487: def _identity(record, run: dict) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:\n488:     \"\"\"The record's ``(run_id, ticker, as_of_date)`` when it *fully* matches the run.\n489: \n490:     Ownership is checked on the record's full identity, never on how its ID is\n491:     spelled: an ID needs no prefix and must not contain the run id. All three\n492:     fields are required and must equal the ``RunContext``'s, so a record with a\n493:     missing identity, a partial identity or a foreign run's identity is not this\n494:     run's material and never resolves.\n495:     \"\"\"\n496:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n497:         return None\n498:     if not all(isinstance(run.get(key), str) and run.get(key) for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS):\n499:         return None\n500:     for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS:\n501:         if record.get(key) != run.get(key):\n502:             return None\n503:     return tuple(run[key] for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS)\n504: \n505: \n506: def _material_resolves(record: dict, run: dict, results_dir) -> bool:\n507:     \"\"\"Whether the record's referenced retained material exists **and has content**.\n508: \n509:     Only a record that names retained material (``content_ref``) and whose material\n510:     can be re-read from this run's retention root counts. A record with no\n511:     ``content_ref`` — an analyst report indexed only in memory — has no traceable\n512:     source material, so it is **not** admissible evidence: the prose itself is not\n513:     a retained source. A reference whose file is expired, deleted or foreign does\n514:     not resolve either.\n515: \n516:     C1 v1.0: \"assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content\n517:     valid\". A retained file that resolves but holds only whitespace has no\n518:     substance, so it is not evidence.\n519:     \"\"\"\n520:     content_ref = record.get(\"content_ref\")\n521:     if not isinstance(content_ref, str) or not content_ref:\n522:         return False\n523:     if not isinstance(results_dir, (str, Path)) or not str(results_dir):\n524:         return False\n525:     from tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection import resolve_content_ref\n526: \n527:     try:\n528:         material = resolve_content_ref(content_ref, results_dir, run)\n529:     except (OSError, ValueError):\n530:         return False\n531:     if not isinstance(material, str):\n532:         return False\n533:     # A retained file that exists but holds only whitespace has no substance.\n534:     return bool(material.strip())\n535: \n536: \n537: def _evidence_records(evidence_index, run: dict, results_dir=None) -> dict[str, dict]:\n538:     \"\"\"The run's own evidence, keyed by ``evidence_id``.\n539: \n540:     Only the authoritative v1 mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which\n541:     carries the same records) is read; an in-memory ``EvidenceIndex`` object is\n542:     the compatibility layer and is refused here, because an object carries no\n543:     per-record ``content_ref`` and would therefore skip the material read-back.\n544: \n545:     A record counts only when its **full identity** matches the ``RunContext``;\n546:     the ID's spelling is irrelevant. A record whose referenced retained material\n547:     cannot be resolved is not evidence, so a report record with no ``content_ref``\n548:     never backs a release.\n549:     \"\"\"\n550:     if not isinstance(evidence_index, dict):\n551:         return {}\n552:     rows = _mapping_rows(evidence_index, \"evidence\", \"id\")\n553:     records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n554:     for _key, record in rows:\n555:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n556:             continue\n557:         # C1: \"a missing required field is an invalid record\". The *record* is\n558:         # judged, never its mapping key or a legacy ``id`` alias: an index entry\n559:         # that supplies ``evidence_id`` only by being keyed under it still has no\n560:         # ``evidence_id`` of its own, so it is not evidence.\n561:         if not _required_fields_ok(record, _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED):\n562:             continue\n563:         evidence_id = record[\"evidence_id\"]\n564:         if not isinstance(evidence_id, str) or not evidence_id:\n565:             continue\n566:         # Ownership is the record's full identity, never the ID's spelling.\n567:         if _identity(record, run) is None:\n568:             continue\n569:         if not _material_resolves(record, run, results_dir):\n570:             continue\n571:         records[evidence_id] = record\n572:     return records\n573: \n574: \n575: def _argument_records(argument_index, run: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:\n576:     \"\"\"The run's accepted arguments, keyed by ``argument_id``.\n577: \n578:     Only the authoritative v1 mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which\n579:     carries the same records) is read; an ``EvidenceIndex`` object or a\n580:     ``{\"accepted_arguments\": [...]}`` view is the compatibility layer and is not\n581:     a release authority, so it yields nothing here.\n582: \n583:     A record counts only when its **full identity** matches the ``RunContext``\n584:     (``run_id``, ``ticker`` and ``as_of_date`` all equal). An ID needs no prefix\n585:     and must not contain the run id. A record that states no identity at all is\n586:     not owned by any run and is refused, whether or not a run id is available.\n587:     \"\"\"\n588:     if not isinstance(argument_index, dict):\n589:         return {}\n590:     if \"accepted_arguments\" in argument_index and \"arguments\" not in argument_index:\n591:         return {}\n592:     rows = _mapping_rows(argument_index, \"arguments\", \"id\")\n593:     records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n594:     for key, record in rows:\n595:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n596:             continue\n597:         argument_id = record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n598:         if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n599:             continue\n600:         if _identity(record, run) is None:\n601:             # No identity, a partial identity, or another run's identity.\n602:             continue\n603:         # C1: an AcceptedArgument needs a nonempty claim and a nonempty\n604:         # ``evidence_ids`` list. ``text`` is the legacy spelling of the claim.\n605:         normalised = {\n606:             **record,\n607:             \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n608:             \"claim\": record.get(\"claim\") or record.get(\"text\") or \"\",\n609:         }\n610:         if not _required_fields_ok(normalised, _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED):\n611:             continue\n612:         if not _field_present(normalised, \"evidence_ids\"):\n613:             continue\n614:         records[argument_id] = record\n615:     return records\n616: \n617: \n618: def validate_argument(argument, evidence_index, run, results_dir=None) -> dict | None:\n619:     \"\"\"C1 v1.0: check current-run references before accepting an argument.\n620: \n621:     The v1 callable boundary from ``interface-contracts.md``. Returns the\n622:     **accepted record** — the argument's full identity plus its claim and the\n623:     resolved evidence ids — or ``None`` when the submission is not acceptable.\n624: \n625:     An argument is accepted only when every part of C1 holds:\n626: \n627:     * it carries the run's **full identity** (``run_id``, ``ticker``,\n628:       ``as_of_date`` all equal the ``RunContext``'s), so a foreign or\n629:       identity-less submission is not this run's argument;\n630:     * it has an ``argument_id`` and a nonempty ``claim``;\n631:     * ``evidence_ids`` is a nonempty list, and **every** cited id resolves to\n632:       admissible evidence in this run: present in the index, complete, and\n633:       backed by retained material that exists and has content.\n634: \n635:     A model flag is not acceptance, and a partially resolvable citation is not a\n636:     partial acceptance: one unresolvable id refuses the argument. This is the\n637:     validation layer; ``evaluate_publication`` rechecks the whole chain again,\n638:     because a record can reach the index without passing through here.\n639:     \"\"\"\n640:     if not isinstance(argument, dict):\n641:         return None\n642:     if _identity(argument, run) is None:\n643:         return None\n644:     argument_id = argument.get(\"argument_id\") or argument.get(\"id\")\n645:     if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n646:         return None\n647:     claim = argument.get(\"claim\") or argument.get(\"text\") or \"\"\n648:     if not isinstance(claim, str) or not claim.strip():\n649:         return None\n650:     evidence_ids = argument.get(\"evidence_ids\")\n651:     if not isinstance(evidence_ids, (list, tuple)) or not evidence_ids:\n652:         return None\n653:     if any(not isinstance(eid, str) or not eid for eid in evidence_ids):\n654:         return None\n655: \n656:     available = _evidence_records(evidence_index, run, results_dir)\n657:     if any(eid not in available for eid in evidence_ids):\n658:         return None\n659: \n660:     return {\n661:         \"contract_version\": str(argument.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n662:         \"run_id\": run[\"run_id\"],\n663:         \"ticker\": run[\"ticker\"],\n664:         \"as_of_date\": run[\"as_of_date\"],\n665:         \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n666:         \"claim\": claim,\n667:         \"speaker\": argument.get(\"speaker\", \"\"),\n668:         \"evidence_ids\": list(evidence_ids),\n669:     }\n670: \n671: \n672: def _mapping_rows(index: dict, list_key: str, id_key: str):\n673:     \"\"\"``(key, record)`` pairs of a mapping index or of its legacy serialized form.\n674: \n675:     Three shapes are read:\n676: \n677:     * a bare ID -> record mapping yields its own items;\n678:     * the authoritative v1 wrapper ``{\"run_id\": ..., list_key: {id: record}}``\n679:       yields the wrapped mapping's items, so metadata is never mistaken for a\n680:       record;\n681:     * the legacy serialized form ``{list_key: [ {...id_key: ...} ]}`` is read\n682:       from that list.\n683: \n684:     The key a record is found under is a fallback only; the record's own ID field\n685:     wins.\n686:     \"\"\"\n687:     if list_key in index:\n688:         wrapped = index[list_key]\n689:         if isinstance(wrapped, dict):\n690:             return list(wrapped.items())\n691:         if isinstance(wrapped, list):\n692:             return [(None, item) for item in wrapped]\n693:     return list(index.items())\n694: \n695: \n696: def _rating(value) -> str | None:\n697:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` when not publishable.\n698: \n699:     Only the exact five tiers count. ``REVIEW``, casing variants, surrounding\n700:     text (\"Buy (small size)\") and null are all invalid: free text is not a call.\n701:     \"\"\"\n702:     if not isinstance(value, str):\n703:         return None\n704:     return value if value in _RATING_SET else None\n705: \n706: \n707: def evaluate_publication(\n708:     candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run, results_dir=None\n709: ) -> PublicationResult:\n710:     \"\"\"C1 v1.0: the one deterministic publication result for a run.\n711: \n712:     Rows are checked in the approved order, and the first matching row decides:\n713: \n714:     1. C0 terminal failure / incomplete execution (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``,\n715:        ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` keep their own code; anything not ``COMPLETED``,\n716:        including a missing ``RunContext``, is ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``).\n717:     2. An invalid rating (``INVALID_RATING``).\n718:     3. Missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted references\n719:        (``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``).\n720:     4. Otherwise APPROVED, with the rating and the validated references.\n721: \n722:     References are rechecked here, not taken from the model: a cited argument\n723:     must exist in this run's ``argument_index``, ownership is decided by each\n724:     record's full identity (never by an ID prefix), and each of its evidence ids\n725:     must resolve in this run's ``evidence_index`` with its retained material still\n726:     readable under ``results_dir``. A record with no retained material never\n727:     resolves. BLOCKED always carries ``rating=None``.\n728:     \"\"\"\n729:     run = run if isinstance(run, dict) else {}\n730:     identity = {\n731:         \"contract_version\": str(run.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n732:         \"run_id\": run.get(\"run_id\") or \"\",\n733:         \"ticker\": run.get(\"ticker\") or \"\",\n734:         \"as_of_date\": run.get(\"as_of_date\") or \"\",\n735:     }\n736: \n737:     def _blocked(*codes: str) -> PublicationResult:\n738:         return PublicationResult(\n739:             **identity, publication_status=BLOCKED, reason_codes=tuple(codes),\n740:             rating=None, argument_ids=(), evidence_ids=(),\n741:         )\n742: \n743:     # Row 1: C0 execution state.\n744:     status = run.get(\"execution_status\")\n745:     if status in _TERMINAL_EXECUTION_NAMED:\n746:         return _blocked(status)\n747:     if status != EXECUTION_COMPLETED:\n748:         # FAILED, RUNNING and a missing RunContext: the workflow did not finish\n749:         # normally, so nothing it produced may publish.\n750:         return _blocked(RUN_NOT_COMPLETE)\n751: \n752:     # Row 2: the rating must be one of the five tiers.\n753:     candidate = candidate if isinstance(candidate, dict) else {}\n754:     rating = _rating(candidate.get(\"rating\"))\n755:     if rating is None:\n756:         return _blocked(INVALID_RATING)\n757: \n758:     # Row 3: every cited reference must resolve inside this run.\n759:     #\n760:     # Fail-closed: a candidate is one recommendation, so an unresolvable cited\n761:     # reference makes it unverifiable and the **whole** candidate is refused.\n762:     # Skipping the references that happened to resolve would release a decision\n763:     # whose stated basis is partly unverified (C1: \"missing, unknown, cross-run or\n764:     # unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE\").\n765:     arguments = _argument_records(argument_index, run)\n766:     evidence = _evidence_records(evidence_index, run, results_dir)\n767:     cited = [a for a in (candidate.get(\"argument_ids\") or ()) if isinstance(a, str) and a]\n768:     if not cited:\n769:         return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n770:     resolved_arguments: list[str] = []\n771:     resolved_evidence: list[str] = []\n772:     chain: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n773:     for argument_id in cited:\n774:         argument = arguments.get(argument_id)\n775:         if argument is None:\n776:             return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n777:         evidence_ids = [\n778:             eid for eid in (argument.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ())\n779:             if isinstance(eid, str) and eid in evidence\n780:         ]\n781:         if not evidence_ids:\n782:             return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n783:         if len(evidence_ids) != len(argument.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ()):\n784:             # The argument cites something that is not this run's admissible\n785:             # evidence, even though its other references resolve.\n786:             return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n787:         resolved_arguments.append(argument_id)\n788:         for evidence_id in evidence_ids:\n789:             if evidence_id not in resolved_evidence:\n790:                 resolved_evidence.append(evidence_id)\n791:             chain.append((argument_id, evidence_id, str(evidence.get(evidence_id, {}).get(\"source\", \"\"))))\n792:     if not resolved_arguments or not resolved_evidence:\n793:         return _blocked(INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)\n794: \n795:     # Row 4: approved, with identity, rating and validated references.\n796:     return PublicationResult(\n797:         **identity,\n798:         publication_status=APPROVED,\n799:         reason_codes=(),\n800:         rating=rating,\n801:         argument_ids=tuple(resolved_arguments),\n802:         evidence_ids=tuple(resolved_evidence),\n803:         resolved_chain=tuple(chain),\n804:     )\n805: \n806: \n807: def run_as_of_date(state: dict) -> str:\n808:     \"\"\"The run's effective cutoff date, as the ``RunContext`` records it.\n809: \n810:     A researcher records an argument's identity with the same date the evidence\n811:     records and the gate use — ``as_of()``'s own result — not the raw trade date,\n812:     so the argument's identity and the evidence's identity agree.\n813:     \"\"\"\n814:     course_run = state.get(\"course_run\") if isinstance(state, dict) else None\n815:     if isinstance(course_run, dict) and course_run.get(\"as_of_date\"):\n816:         return str(course_run[\"as_of_date\"])\n817:     from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import as_of\n818: \n819:     trade_date = state.get(\"trade_date\") if isinstance(state, dict) else \"\"\n820:     return as_of(trade_date, trade_date)\n821: \n822: \n823: def accepted_arguments_view(argument_index: dict) -> list[dict]:\n824:     \"\"\"The legacy ``accepted_arguments`` list, derived from the authoritative mapping.\n825: \n826:     The Portfolio Manager's prompt still lists accepted arguments in the old\n827:     shape. It is built from ``argument_index`` on every write, so it cannot drift\n828:     from the mapping, and the gate never reads it back as authority.\n829:     \"\"\"\n830:     view = []\n831:     for argument_id, record in (argument_index or {}).items():\n832:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n833:             continue\n834:         view.append({\n835:             \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n836:             \"speaker\": record.get(\"speaker\", \"\"),\n837:             \"evidence_ids\": list(record.get(\"evidence_ids\") or ()),\n838:         })\n839:     return view\n840: \n841: \n842: def publication_run(state: dict) -> dict:\n843:     \"\"\"The ``RunContext`` the gate judges a run against (C0).\n844: \n845:     The graph state carries one complete ``course_run``, created once at the shared\n846:     run entry. When it is absent the run has no identity to be checked against and\n847:     no execution state to prove it finished, so ``execution_status`` is left unset\n848:     and the gate blocks with ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``. A terminal failure recorded on\n849:     the state (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`` / ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE``) is carried through so\n850:     it keeps its own reason code.\n851:     \"\"\"\n852:     if not isinstance(state, dict):\n853:         return {}\n854:     course_run = state.get(\"course_run\")\n855:     if isinstance(course_run, dict) and course_run.get(\"run_id\"):\n856:         return dict(course_run)\n857:     recorded = state.get(\"execution_status\")\n858:     return {\n859:         \"contract_version\": \"1.0\",\n860:         \"run_id\": \"\",\n861:         \"ticker\": state.get(\"company_of_interest\") or \"\",\n862:         \"as_of_date\": state.get(\"trade_date\") or \"\",\n863:         # No RunContext, no proof of completion: never assume COMPLETED. Field, day and currency are the ones the Yahoo snapshot reported.\n400:     \"\"\"\n401:     if payload.get(\"as_of_date\") != cutoff.isoformat():\n402:         return None\n403:     symbol = payload.get(\"symbol\")\n404:     if not isinstance(symbol, str) or symbol.strip().upper() != run[\"ticker\"].strip().upper():\n405:         return None\n406:     trading_day = _calendar_date(payload.get(\"trading_date\"))\n407:     if trading_day is None or trading_day > cutoff:\n408:         return None\n409:     currency = payload.get(\"currency\")\n410:     if not _is_quote_currency(currency):\n411:         return None\n412:     close = _decimal(payload.get(\"close\"))\n413:     upper = _decimal(payload.get(\"boll_ub\"))\n414:     if close is None or upper is None:\n415:         return None\n416: \n417:     instant = {\"kind\": \"instant\", \"start\": trading_day.isoformat(),\n418:                \"end\": trading_day.isoformat(), \"label\": f\"{trading_day.isoformat()} quote\"}\n419:     source = f\"quote:{run['ticker'].strip().upper()}:{trading_day.isoformat()}\"\n420:     return {\"kind\": \"price_delta\", \"operands\": [\n421:         {\"role\": \"current\", \"value\": str(upper), \"unit\": currency,\n422:          \"period\": dict(instant), \"source_ref\": source, \"field_ref\": \"boll_ub\"},\n423:         {\"role\": \"reference\", \"value\": str(close), \"unit\": currency,\n424:          \"period\": dict(instant), \"source_ref\": source, \"field_ref\": \"Close\"},\n425:     ]}\n426: \n427: \n428: def _quote_outcome(request, reply):\n429:     \"\"\"The reply unchanged, or a Command that also hands over the verified price gap.\n430: \n431:     Only the market tool's own successful reply is read, matched to its call by\n432:     name and ID and by the reply carrying that ID. A reply with no usable source,\n433:     a run that is not this invocation's, or a metric the module refuses all\n434:     return the reply exactly as it was: nothing is invented and no run is made.\n435:     \"\"\"\n436:     call = getattr(request, \"tool_call\", None) or {}\n437:     if not isinstance(call, dict) or call.get(\"name\") != _QUOTE_TOOL:\n438:         return reply\n439:     call_id = call.get(\"id\")\n440:     if not isinstance(reply, ToolMessage):\n441:         return reply\n442:     if not call_id or reply.tool_call_id != call_id or reply.name != call[\"name\"]:\n443:         return reply\n444:     if getattr(reply, \"status\", \"success\") == \"error\":\n445:         return reply\n446:     state = getattr(request, \"state\", None) or {}\n447:     run = _valid_run(state)\n448:     if run is None:\n449:         return reply\n450:     cutoff = _effective_cutoff(state, call, run)\n451:     if cutoff is None:\n452:         return reply\n453:     payload = _quote_source_line(reply.content)\n454:     if payload is None:\n455:         return reply\n456:     request_body = _quote_request(payload, run, cutoff)\n457:     if request_body is None:\n458:         return reply\n459: \n460:     result = verify_metric(request_body, run)\n461:     if not isinstance(result, dict) or result.get(\"status\") != VERIFIED:\n462:         return reply\n463:     metric = result.get(\"metric\")\n464:     if not isinstance(metric, dict) or not metric.get(\"metric_id\"):\n465:         return reply\n466:     return Command(update={\n467:         \"messages\": [reply],\n468:         \"verified_metrics\": {metric[\"metric_id\"]: metric},\n469:     })\n470: \n471: \n472: # it forms is comparable.\n480: \n481: _STATEMENT_SOURCE_PREFIX = \"# FR02_SEC_SOURCE \"\n482: _INCOME_TOOL = \"get_income_statement\"\n483: _CASHFLOW_TOOL = \"get_cashflow\"\n484: _YOY_ITEMS = (\"Revenue\", \"Cost of Revenue\")\n485: _FREQUENCIES = (\"quarterly\", \"annual\")\n486: \n487: _MILLIONS = Decimal(1000000)\n488: _YEAR_DAYS = (300, 400)\n489: _QUARTER_DAYS = (60, 115)\n490: \n491: \n492: def _statement_source_array(text):\n493:     \"\"\"The statement's source array on the reply's own last line, or None.\n494: \n495:     Only the final nonblank line is considered and it must carry exactly the\n496:     prefix; numbers keep their precision through ``Decimal``. return abs((current_end - anniversary).days) <= 7\n607: \n608: \n609: def _attempt_yoy(attempt, rows):\n610:     \"\"\"Try each current period against the newest comparable one a year earlier.\n611: \n612:     Rows are newest first. Stops at the first pair the module signs; a current\n613:     row with no candidate, or one whose candidates are all refused, leaves the\n614:     search to the next row.\n615:     \"\"\"\n616:     for index, (current, current_period) in enumerate(rows):\n617:         current_end = current[\"end\"]\n618:         if index and rows[index - 1][0][\"end\"] == current_end:\n619:             continue                        # the same end already tried\n620:         for prior, prior_period in rows[index + 1:]:\n621:             if prior[\"end\"] >= current_end:\n622:                 continue\n623:             if prior[\"unit\"] != current[\"unit\"] or prior[\"cik\"] != current[\"cik\"]:\n624:                 continue\n625:             if prior_period[\"kind\"] != current_period[\"kind\"]:\n626:                 continue\n627:             if not _year_apart(prior[\"end\"], current_end):\n628:                 continue\n629:             if attempt(\"yoy\", [\n630:                 _fact_operand(\"current\", current, current_period),\n631:                 _fact_operand(\"prior\", prior, prior_period),\n632:             ]):\n633:                 return True\n634:     return False\n635: \n636: \n637: def _signed_statement_requests(payload, run, cutoff, freq, tool_name):\n638:     \"\"\"The records this reply's own facts sign, by ID.\n639: \n640:     Each pair is formed from cited facts and offered to ``verify_metric`` as it\n641:     is found, so a refusal moves on to the next candidate rather than ending the\n642:     search. canonical = False\n39:     if not canonical:\n40:         raise ValueError(f\"trade_date must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format, got {trade_date!r}\")\n41:     if value > get_current_date():\n42:         raise ValueError(f\"trade_date cannot be in the future: {value}\")\n43:     return value\n44: \n45: \n46: # Config keys that do not change what a run writes: where it keeps its files,\n47: # whether it checkpoints, and how often it retries a provider.\n48: _NOT_IN_SIGNATURE = frozenset({\n49:     \"results_dir\", \"data_cache_dir\", \"memory_log_path\", \"checkpoint_enabled\", \"llm_max_retries\",\n50: })\n51: \n52: \n53: class TradingAgentsGraph:\n54:     \"\"\"Main class that orchestrates the trading agents framework.\"\"\"\n55: \n56:     def __init__(\n57:         self,\n58:         selected_analysts=(\"market\", \"social\", \"news\", \"fundamentals\"),\n59:         debug=False,\n60:         config: dict[str, Any] = None,\n61:         callbacks: list | None = None,\n62:     ):\n63:         \"\"\"Initialize the trading agents graph and components.\n64: \n65:         Args:\n66:             selected_analysts: List of analyst types to include\n67:             debug: Whether to run in debug mode\n68:             config: Configuration dictionary. If None, uses default config\n69:             callbacks: Optional list of callback handlers (e.g., for tracking LLM/tool stats)\n70:         \"\"\"\n71:         self.debug = debug\n72:         self.config = config or DEFAULT_CONFIG\n73:         self.callbacks = callbacks or []\n74: \n75:         set_config(self.config)\n76: \n77:         os.makedirs(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n78:         os.makedirs(self.config[\"results_dir\"], exist_ok=True)\n79: \n80:         extra = {\"callbacks\": self.callbacks} if self.callbacks else {}\n81:         self.deep_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"deep\", **extra).get_llm()\n82:         self.quick_thinking_llm = create_tier_client(self.config, \"quick\", **extra).get_llm()\n83: \n84:         self.memory_log = TradingMemoryLog(self.config)\n85: \n86:         self.conditional_logic = ConditionalLogic(\n87:             max_debate_rounds=self.config[\"max_debate_rounds\"],\n88:             max_risk_discuss_rounds=self.config[\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"],\n89:         )\n90:         # An analyst takes two graph steps per tool round, plus its first turn\n91:         # and its wrap-up; a limit past the recursion limit would end the run\n92:         # there instead.\n93:         max_tool_rounds, max_recur_limit = self.config[\"max_tool_rounds\"], self.config[\"max_recur_limit\"]\n94:         if 2 * max_tool_rounds + 2 >= max_recur_limit:\n95:             raise ValueError(\n96:                 f\"max_tool_rounds={max_tool_rounds} needs max_recur_limit above {2 * max_tool_rounds + 2}\"\n97:             )\n98:         self.graph_setup = GraphSetup(\n99:             self.quick_thinking_llm,\n100:             self.deep_thinking_llm,\n101:             self.conditional_logic,\n102:             max_tool_rounds,\n103:         )\n104: \n105:         self.propagator = Propagator(\n106:             max_recur_limit=max_recur_limit,\n107:         )\n108:         self.reflector = Reflector(self.quick_thinking_llm)\n109: \n110:         # Graph-shape-affecting run choices, kept for the checkpoint signature.\n111:         self.selected_analysts = tuple(selected_analysts)\n112: \n113:         # Set up the graph: keep the workflow for recompilation with a checkpointer.\n114:         self.workflow = self.graph_setup.setup_graph(selected_analysts, memory_node=self._memory_step)\n115:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n116:         self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n117:         self._resuming = False\n118: \n119:     def resolve_instrument_context(self, ticker: str, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n120:                                    trade_date: str | None = None) -> str:\n121:         \"\"\"Resolve ticker identity once and return the full instrument context.\n122: \n123:         Deterministic yfinance lookup (cached, fail-open) injected into a\n124:         context string so every agent anchors to the real company instead of\n125:         hallucinating one from the price chart (#814). Both the propagate()\n126:         path and the CLI call this so the resolved identity reaches the whole\n127:         graph regardless of entry point.\n128:         \"\"\"\n129:         identity = resolve_instrument_identity(ticker)\n130:         return build_instrument_context(ticker, asset_type, identity, trade_date)\n131: \n132:     def _memory_as_of(self, trade_date) -> str | None:\n133:         \"\"\"Point-in-time cutoff for past-context lessons (#1251).\n134: \n135:         A historical/backtest run (trade date before today) filters lessons to\n136:         those already resolved by the trade date. A current-date run returns\n137:         None, disabling the filter so live behavior and pre-migration entries\n138:         (which have no stored resolution date) are unaffected.\n139:         \"\"\"\n140:         return str(trade_date) if is_historical(trade_date) else None\n141: \n142:     def _run_signature(self, asset_type: str, portfolio=None) -> str:\n143:         \"\"\"Run inputs that must invalidate a checkpoint if changed.\n144: \n145:         Keyed into the checkpoint thread ID so a resume under a different analyst\n146:         selection, debate/risk depth, or asset mode starts fresh instead of\n147:         silently continuing the previous graph (#1089). The rest of the config\n148:         counts too (provider, models, endpoint, language, vendors, limits): a\n149:         resume must not carry reports that other settings produced. Only where\n150:         the run keeps its files and how it retries are left out.\n151:         \"\"\"\n152:         settings = {k: v for k, v in self.config.items() if k not in _NOT_IN_SIGNATURE}\n153:         digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(settings, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]\n154:         return \"|\".join([\n155:             \"analysts=\" + \",\".join(self.selected_analysts),\n156:             f\"debate={self.config['max_debate_rounds']}\",\n157:             f\"risk={self.config['max_risk_discuss_rounds']}\",\n158:             f\"asset={asset_type}\",\n159:             # None, an empty book and a changed book are three different runs.\n160:             f\"portfolio={portfolio.fingerprint() if portfolio is not None else 'none'}\",\n161:             # The layout itself: a checkpoint saved when analysts ran one after\n162:             # another has pending nodes this graph no longer has, and one saved\n163:             # before the Memory Log step would resume without the lessons.\n164:             \"analysts=parallel\",\n165:             \"memory=parallel\",\n166:             f\"settings={digest}\",\n167:         ])\n168: \n169:     def propagate(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n170:         \"\"\"Run the trading agents graph for a company on a specific date.\n171: \n172:         ``asset_type`` selects between the stock pipeline (default) and the\n173:         crypto pipeline (``\"crypto\"``) shipped in #567 — the CLI auto-detects\n174:         from the ticker; programmatic callers pass it explicitly. When\n175:         ``checkpoint_enabled`` is set in config, the graph is recompiled with\n176:         a per-ticker SqliteSaver so a crashed run can resume from the last\n177:         successful node on a subsequent invocation with the same ticker+date.\n178: \n179:         Returns ``(final_state, signal)`` where ``signal`` is one of the 5-tier\n180:         ratings (Buy / Overweight / Hold / Underweight / Sell) or ``\"REVIEW\"``\n181:         when the decision had no parseable rating (#1170); guard with\n182:         ``tradingagents.agents.rating.is_review`` before mapping it to the\n183:         PortfolioRating enum.\n184:         \"\"\"\n185:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n186: \n187:         with run_config(self.config), \\\n188:                 self.checkpoint_scope(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio) as thread_id_value:\n189:             return self._run_graph(\n190:                 company_name, trade_date, asset_type=asset_type,\n191:                 checkpoint_thread_id=thread_id_value, portfolio=portfolio,\n192:             )\n193: \n194:     def begin_checkpoint(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None) -> str | None:\n195:         \"\"\"Recompile the graph with a per-ticker checkpointer and return the\n196:         ``thread_id`` to inject into the stream/invoke ``config`` (or ``None``\n197:         when checkpointing is disabled).\n198: \n199:         Pair every call with :meth:`end_checkpoint` in a ``finally``. Both\n200:         ``propagate`` (via :meth:`checkpoint_scope`) and the CLI stream path use\n201:         this so ``--checkpoint`` actually resumes (#1249); previously the setup\n202:         lived only inside ``propagate`` and the CLI streamed the checkpointer-less\n203:         graph, making the flag a no-op.\n204:         \"\"\"\n205:         self._resuming = False\n206:         if not self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n207:             return None\n208:         signature = self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio)\n209:         self._checkpointer_ctx = get_checkpointer(self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name)\n210:         saver = self._checkpointer_ctx.__enter__()\n211:         self.graph = self.workflow.compile(checkpointer=saver)\n212: \n213:         step = checkpoint_step(\n214:             self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date), signature\n215:         )\n216:         self._resuming = step is not None\n217:         if step is not None:\n218:             logger.info(\"Resuming from step %d for %s on %s\", step, company_name, trade_date)\n219:         else:\n220:             logger.info(\"Starting fresh for %s on %s\", company_name, trade_date)\n221:         return thread_id(company_name, str(trade_date), signature)\n222: \n223:     def checkpoint_input(self, init_state):\n224:         \"\"\"The value to stream/invoke: ``None`` to resume an existing checkpoint,\n225:         else the initial state for a fresh run.\n226: \n227:         LangGraph resumes an interrupted thread when invoked with ``None``;\n228:         re-passing the initial state instead appends it through the message\n229:         reducer, duplicating messages in the resumed state (#1249).\n230:         \"\"\"\n231:         return None if self._resuming else init_state\n232: \n233:     def end_checkpoint(self):\n234:         \"\"\"Restore the plain uncheckpointed graph after a checkpointed run.\"\"\"\n235:         if self._checkpointer_ctx is not None:\n236:             self._checkpointer_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)\n237:             self._checkpointer_ctx = None\n238:             self.graph = self.workflow.compile()\n239:         self._resuming = False\n240: \n241:     @contextmanager\n242:     def checkpoint_scope(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n243:         \"\"\"Context-manager form of begin/end_checkpoint for the propagate path.\"\"\"\n244:         try:\n245:             yield self.begin_checkpoint(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n246:         finally:\n247:             self.end_checkpoint()\n248: \n249:     def clear_checkpoint_on_success(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n250:         \"\"\"Drop a completed run's checkpoint so a later run starts fresh (#1249).\"\"\"\n251:         if self.config.get(\"checkpoint_enabled\"):\n252:             clear_checkpoint(\n253:                 self.config[\"data_cache_dir\"], company_name, str(trade_date),\n254:                 self._run_signature(asset_type, portfolio),\n255:             )\n256: \n257:     def run_settings(self) -> dict:\n258:         \"\"\"What produces this graph's runs, for the saved report and state log.\n259: \n260:         An allowlist: endpoints (a backend_url can carry credentials), keys and\n261:         local paths are never recorded.\n262:         \"\"\"\n263:         cfg = self.config\n264:         return {\n265:             \"version\": tradingagents.__version__,\n266:             \"llm_provider\": cfg.get(\"llm_provider\"),\n267:             \"deep_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"deep\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n268:             \"deep_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"deep_think_llm\"),\n269:             \"quick_think_provider\": tier_provider(cfg, \"quick\") if cfg.get(\"llm_provider\") else None,\n270:             \"quick_think_llm\": cfg.get(\"quick_think_llm\"),\n271:             \"analysts\": list(self.selected_analysts),\n272:             \"max_debate_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_debate_rounds\"),\n273:             \"max_risk_discuss_rounds\": cfg.get(\"max_risk_discuss_rounds\"),\n274:             \"output_language\": cfg.get(\"output_language\"),\n275:             \"data_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"data_vendors\") or {}),\n276:             \"tool_vendors\": dict(cfg.get(\"tool_vendors\") or {}),\n277:         }\n278: \n279:     def save_reports(self, final_state, ticker, save_path=None, html=True) -> Path:\n280:         \"\"\"Write the report tree for a completed run, like the CLI does.\n281: \n282:         Programmatic callers get the same on-disk reports the CLI produces. Pass\n283:         an explicit ``save_path`` or let it default under ``results_dir``; the\n284:         report is also written as one HTML page unless ``html`` is False.\n285: \n286:         FR-01 / INV-01: an official report is written only from the publication\n287:         gate's own ``publication_result``. A state that never passed the gate — no\n288:         result, or only a flat ``publication_status`` someone set — raises\n289:         ``PublicationRequiredError`` and writes nothing, so a candidate can never\n290:         be saved as an official decision. A real BLOCKED result still writes a\n291:         diagnostic report: the same tree without an official rating, without the\n292:         candidate body and without ``5_portfolio/decision.md``.\n293:         \"\"\"\n294:         from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import (\n295:             PublicationRequiredError,\n296:             publication_result_from_state,\n297:         )\n298: \n299:         result = publication_result_from_state(final_state)\n300:         if result is None:\n301:             raise PublicationRequiredError(\n302:                 \"save_reports() needs the publication gate's publication_result; this \"\n303:                 \"state has none (a flat publication_status is not a gate result), so no \"\n304:                 \"official report was written\"\n305:             )\n306:         if save_path is None:\n307:             save_path = self.default_report_path(ticker)\n308:         return write_report_tree(\n309:             final_state, ticker, save_path, settings=self.run_settings(), html=html,\n310:         )\n311: \n312:     def default_report_path(self, ticker) -> Path:\n313:         \"\"\"Where a run's reports go unless told otherwise: under results_dir, stamped now.\"\"\"\n314:         stamp = datetime.now().strftime(\"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S\")\n315:         return Path(self.config[\"results_dir\"]) / \"reports\" / f\"{safe_ticker_component(ticker)}_{stamp}\"\n316: \n317:     def create_run_state(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\", portfolio=None):\n318:         \"\"\"Build a run's initial state; propagate() and the CLI both start here.\n319: \n320:         Injects the resolved instrument identity for every agent (#814). The\n321:         memory log's lessons are not here: the graph's Memory Log step settles\n322:         and loads them alongside the analysts (see ``_memory_step``).\n323:         \"\"\"\n324:         trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)\n325:         # The initial state mints this run's one ``course_run`` identity, so the\n326:         # propagator call must read this graph's config on every entry path\n327:         # (propagate(), the CLI stream, a bare create_run_state()): inside its own\n328:         # ``run_config`` block the identity no longer depends on whatever happened\n329:         # to be serving config at call time. Nested blocks restore the outer one on\n330:         # exit, so propagating callers see the config they set.\n331:         with run_config(self.config):\n332:             return self.propagator.create_initial_state(\n333:                 company_name,\n334:                 trade_date,\n335:                 asset_type=asset_type,\n336:                 instrument_context=self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date),\n337:                 portfolio_context=portfolio.render(company_name) if portfolio is not None else \"\",\n338:             )\n339: \n340:     def _run_budget(self, init_agent_state) -> RequestBudget | None:\n341:         \"\"\"The metered budget for this run, or ``None`` when metering is off.\n342: \n343:         One ``RequestBudget`` per main analysis flow (NFR-01 / INV-02, C4), keyed\n344:         by the run identity the initial state already minted, with the limit\n345:         recorded on its ``course_run``. ``None`` outside ``request_budget_enabled``\n346:         (no budget is fabricated). Under it, a run with no usable identity refuses\n347:         rather than running unlimited: a missing or malformed ``course_run`` raises\n348:         ``ValueError``, and :class:`RequestBudget` refuses a missing or non-positive\n349:         limit.\n350:         \"\"\"\n351:         if not self.config.get(\"request_budget_enabled\"):\n352:             return None\n353:         course_run = init_agent_state.get(\"course_run\") if isinstance(init_agent_state, dict) else None\n354:         if not isinstance(course_run, dict):\n355:             raise ValueError(\n356:                 \"request metering is enabled but the initial state carries no course_run; \"\n357:                 \"refusing to run unmetered\"\n358:             )\n359:         return RequestBudget(course_run.get(\"run_id\"), course_run.get(\"request_limit\"))\n360: \n361:     def _terminal_state(self, graph_input, init_agent_state, exc: BaseException, latest=None) -> dict | None:\n362:         \"\"\"The one final state of a run that ended on a recognized C4/C5 failure.\n363: \n364:         Built from ``init_agent_state`` — so a resumed run that streamed ``None``\n365:         still has the identity the gate needs — then overlaid with whatever the run\n366:         had produced (``latest``) and the terminal C0 code in the flat\n367:         ``execution_status`` and on its ``course_run``. ``None`` when the failure is\n368:         not a recognized budget/context/provider refusal: the caller re-raises.\n369:         \"\"\"\n370:         if latest is None:\n371:             latest = graph_input if graph_input is not None else init_agent_state\n372:         terminal = terminal_request_status(exc)\n373:         if terminal is None:\n374:             return None\n375:         # Actual latest values win over the initial state; a partial state never\n376:         # removes an identity field it did not see.\n377:         final_state = {}\n378:         for source in (init_agent_state, latest):\n379:             if isinstance(source, dict):\n380:                 final_state.update(source)\n381:         final_state[\"execution_status\"] = terminal\n382:         course_run = final_state.get(\"course_run\")\n383:         if isinstance(course_run, dict):\n384:             final_state[\"course_run\"] = {**course_run, \"execution_status\": terminal}\n385:         return final_state\n386: \n387:     def _memory_step(self, state):\n388:         \"\"\"The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every\n389:         ticker's due decisions (#1445), then return the lessons known by the\n390:         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).\n391: \n392:         Settling fetches prices and asks the model for a reflection per decision,\n393:         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here\n394:         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in\n395:         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.\n396:         \"\"\"\n397:         note = \"\"\n398:         try:\n399:             # Settlement and reflection are historical work, not part of the run's\n400:             # model flow (NFR-01 / INV-02, C4): their requests are made outside the\n401:             # run's budget scope, so they never consume a slot from it. An explicit\n402:             # ``None`` scope keeps that true even when a caller has one published.\n403:             with request_budget_scope(None):\n404:                 # Another run settling the same log does the work; this one goes on.\n405:                 done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)\n406:             if done.failed:\n407:                 note = (f\"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run \"\n408:                         \"and stay pending.\")\n409:         except Exception as exc:\n410:             logger.warning(\"Settling past decisions failed: %s\", exc)\n411:             note = f\"Past decisions could not be settled this run ({type(exc).__name__}); they stay pending.\"\n412:         try:\n413:             past_context = self.memory_log.get_past_context(\n414:                 state[\"company_of_interest\"], as_of=self._memory_as_of(state[\"trade_date\"]))\n415:         except Exception as exc:\n416:             logger.warning(\"Reading the memory log failed: %s\", exc)\n417:             past_context = \"\"\n418:             note = note or f\"The memory log could not be read this run ({type(exc).__name__}).\"\n419:         return {\"past_context\": past_context, \"memory_note\": note}\n420: \n421:     def settle_pending(self, company_name) -> settlement.Settlement:\n422:         \"\"\"Settle this ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded.\n423: \n424:         A run settles every due decision alongside its analysts, so its own\n425:         decision stays pending until a later run. A caller that is done\n426:         analyzing a ticker (a backtest sweep, a scheduled job) calls this to\n427:         settle it now. Returns what was settled and what failed.\n428:         \"\"\"\n429:         with run_config(self.config):\n430:             return settlement.settle_pending(company_name, self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config)\n431: \n432:     def settle_all_pending(self, wait: bool = True) -> settlement.Settlement:\n433:         \"\"\"Settle every ticker's decisions whose holding window has now traded (#1445).\n434: \n435:         For a scheduler whose tickers rotate: a ticker it stops analysing would\n436:         otherwise keep its decisions pending, and their lessons out of later runs.\n437:         With ``wait=False`` a pass already running on the same log is not waited for.\n438:         \"\"\"\n439:         with run_config(self.config):\n440:             return settlement.settle_all_pending(self.memory_log, self.reflector, self.config, wait=wait)\n441: \n442:     def record_decision(self, company_name, trade_date, final_state):\n443:         \"\"\"Record a finished run: its state log, and its decision in the memory log\n444:         for reflection on the next same-ticker run. propagate() and the CLI both end here.\n445: \n446:         FR-01 / INV-01: a run the publication gate blocked writes nothing to\n447:         decision memory — not a rating, not even a REVIEW entry — and its state log\n448:         omits the candidate body.\n449:         \"\"\"\n450:         self._log_state(trade_date, final_state)\n451:         from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import publication_result_from_state\n452: \n453:         result = publication_result_from_state(final_state)\n454:         if result is None or not result.approved:\n455:             logger.warning(\n456:                 \"Publication blocked for %s on %s (%s); nothing added to the memory log\",\n457:                 company_name, trade_date,\n458:                 result.reason if result is not None else \"no gate result\",\n459:             )\n460:             return\n461:         decision = final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\")\n462:         if not decision:\n463:             logger.warning(\"No final decision for %s on %s; nothing added to the memory log\",\n464:                            company_name, trade_date)\n465:             return\n466:         self.memory_log.store_decision(\n467:             ticker=company_name, trade_date=trade_date, final_trade_decision=decision,\n468:             rating=run_rating(final_state),\n469:         )\n470: \n471:     def _run_graph(self, company_name, trade_date, asset_type: str = \"stock\",\n472:                    checkpoint_thread_id: str | None = None, portfolio=None):\n473:         \"\"\"Execute the graph and write the resulting state to disk and memory log.\"\"\"\n474:         init_agent_state = self.create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)\n475:         args = self.propagator.get_graph_args()\n476: \n477:         # Inject the checkpoint thread_id (from checkpoint_scope) so the same\n478:         # ticker+date+graph-shape resumes; a different one starts fresh (#1089).\n479:         if checkpoint_thread_id is not None:\n480:             args.setdefault(\"config\", {}).setdefault(\"configurable\", {})[\"thread_id\"] = checkpoint_thread_id\n481: \n482:         # None resumes an existing checkpoint; init_agent_state starts fresh (#1249).\n483:         graph_input = self.checkpoint_input(init_agent_state)\n484:         if self.debug:\n485:             # A state repeats the messages before it, so each prints once (#1027).\n486:             final_state, printed = {}, set()\n487:             for messages, state in self.stream_run(graph_input, **args):\n488:                 for msg in messages:\n489:                     key = getattr(msg, \"id\", None) or (type(msg).__name__, getattr(msg, \"content\", None))\n490:                     if key not in printed:\n491:                         printed.add(key)\n492:                         msg.pretty_print()\n493:                 if state is not None:\n494:                     final_state.update(state)\n495:         else:\n496:             # NFR-01 / INV-02 (C4): one budget for this run, published for the\n497:             # whole invoke so every outbound request of the flow is metered. A\n498:             # recognized refusal ends the run with a terminal state instead of\n499:             # propagating a half-finished graph — recording the terminal code on a\n500:             # final state whose normal tail still runs (the gate then blocks it),\n501:             # so the API and CLI end the same way; any other error re-raises.\n502:             budget = self._run_budget(init_agent_state)\n503:             try:\n504:                 with request_budget_scope(budget):\n505:                     final_state = self.graph.invoke(graph_input, **args)\n506:             except Exception as exc:\n507:                 terminal_state = self._terminal_state(graph_input, init_agent_state, exc)\n508:                 if terminal_state is None:\n509:                     raise\n510:                 run_id = (init_agent_state.get(\"course_run\") or {}).get(\"run_id\")\n511:                 logger.warning(\n512:                     \"Run %s for %s on %s ended as %s\",\n513:                     run_id, company_name, trade_date, terminal_state[\"execution_status\"],\n514:                 )\n515:                 final_state = terminal_state\n516: \n517:         # The graph returned normally, so the run finished: only now does its\n518:         # execution state become COMPLETED. Configure output allowance and provider-envelope reserve independently. Validate the selected model capacity, counting method, schema overhead and provider conversion before enabling this policy. Until then, token enforcement remains unverified. NFR-01 boundary fixtures use limit 3. Configuration evidence accompanies baseline comparisons; changes to public semantics require a contract revision.\n46: \n47: ## Consequences and review triggers\n48: \n49: Benefits are localized changes and explicit failure states. Costs are shared dispatch/publication integration and nullable-state compatibility across existing consumers. Review this decision when provider retries become opaque, a sink bypasses publication checks, required context routinely cannot fit, or requirements need different orchestration.\n50: \n51: Changes to shared fields, date semantics, thresholds, safety behavior or dependencies require affected-owner review and synchronized requirements, interfaces and tests. Record the human decision and supporting evidence.\n52: \n53: ## FR-01 reference selection adapter — 19 November 2026\n54: \n55: The coordinator requested live verification and repair of long model reference copying on the integrated `77938d0` tree. The recorded AAPL rerun rejected a shortened Bull reference and accepted a complete Bear reference. Build and freeze the mapping from the menu actually supplied to that invocation. Resolve returned selections to canonical IDs before the existing C1 validators. Keep canonical IDs available for existing callers. Unknown selections remain invalid. Every stored record, candidate and publication chain uses canonical IDs. An alias has meaning only within the menu of its current invocation; ownership continues to be established from full C0/C1 records.\n58: \n59: This adapter adds no model request. Diagnostic rejection logs identify the actor and reference without including raw claims or changing public reason codes. A fixed model replay exercises the revised prompts before delivery. Live provider limitations remain separately recorded."
