Status: Proposed. Shared boundaries use JSON-compatible records. Internal dataclasses, TypedDict or Pydantic models may use adapters that preserve these fields and semantics. ADR-001 records the design decision.\n4: \n5: ## Ownership and integration\n6: \n7: | Contract | Authority | Producers and consumers |\n8: | --- | --- | --- |\n9: | C0 run identity and outcome | Run coordinator | All five owner modules, CLI, Python, report and memory |\n10: | C1 evidence and publication | FR-01 publication gate | Analyst evidence, accepted arguments, candidate, all official sinks |\n11: | C2 verified metrics | FR-02 metric registry | Fundamentals inputs, controlled downstream fields and metric table |\n12: | C3 sentiment coverage | FR-03 coverage component | Existing source adapters, analyst, state, report and downstream agents |\n13: | C4 dispatch budget | NFR-01 request-budget component | Both model tiers and every in-scope transport send |\n14: | C5 prepared context | NFR-02 context component | Analyst closure and neutral risk debater, then C4 |\n15: \n16: Shared-file integration owner: EverForests. Feature owners submit narrow patches for state, schema, graph/client and reporting adapters. Task plans identify exact paths. The integrator preserves approved contracts across patches; shared files must not be independently replaced by feature branches.\n17: \n18: ## C0 — identity, state and errors\n19: \n20: Every authoritative record carries `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and `as_of_date`. Evidence and metric IDs are only resolvable inside that run. Never retrieve a matching-looking ID from a previous run. A restarted run gets a new ID. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.\n21: \n22: Keep three concepts separate:\n23: \n24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.\n25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.\n26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.\n27: \n28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.\n29: \n30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication\n31: \n32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.\n33: \n34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.\n35: \n36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.\n37: \n38: The FR-01 model adapter may offer invocation-local `E1` evidence selections and `A1` accepted-argument selections. Freeze the mapping from that invocation's actual menu and resolve selections before C1 validation. Existing canonical IDs remain supported. Persist canonical IDs in evidence, accepted arguments, candidates and publication results. Unknown selections and truncated canonical IDs remain subject to rejection. Each short selection refers only to the current menu; the full records establish run ownership. See the [ADR reference-selection amendment](adr/001-choice-tbd.md#fr-01-reference-selection-adapter--19-november-2026).\n39: \n40: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.\n41: \n42: ## C2 — verified metrics\n43: \n44: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.\n45: \n46: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.\n47: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.\n48: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.\n49: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.\n50: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.\n51: \n52: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.\n53: \n54: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.\n55: \n56: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score\n57: \n58: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.\n59: \n60: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.\n61: \n62: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). AAPL as-of 2026-11-10 therefore covers 2026-11-03 through 2026-11-10. Freeze the clock for date-dependent fixtures. Historical undated content cannot prove window validity. Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.\n63: \n64: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. Never claim these statuses prove that no real-world messages/news exist.\n65: \n66: | Valid logical sources | coverage_status | Sentiment output |\n67: | --- | --- | --- |\n68: | 0/3 | NO_DATA | overall_band UNKNOWN; overall_score null |\n69: | 1/3 or 2/3 | PARTIAL_DATA | Coverage remains explicit; any measured score uses valid evidence only |\n70: | 3/3 | AVAILABLE | Coverage available; score still requires a valid assessment |\n71: \n72: Coverage is authoritative data state; the model cannot increase it. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. A genuine measured Neutral/5.0 remains legal.\n73: \n74: Missing scores never become 0 or 5 and never enter a numerical mean. Structured state, analyst message, downstream prompt and persisted/rendered report must agree. Handle nullable scores without numeric-format errors. Apply the contract to structured **and** free-text fallback; model narrative cannot override authoritative coverage. Keep the existing sentiment_report text as a compatibility view; the new sentiment_assessment record below is authoritative. Both must agree. Internal schema adaptation may change, but the v1 shared record does not drift silently.\n75: \n76: The original baseline stores `sentiment_report` as text and requires a nonnull numeric SentimentReport score. Updating only the prompt cannot establish this contract. No raw social bodies or credentials belong in public evidence. Missing optional sentiment does not stop otherwise valid market/fundamental analysis; C1 still decides publication.\n77: \n78: ## C4 — atomic per-run model dispatch\n79: \n80: Supported scope: one single-stock main analysis, both model tiers, structured/fallback requests and application retries. Count actual outgoing model attempts, not nodes, tool invocations, callbacks or tokens. Historical settlement is excluded. Disable SDK/transport implicit retries in supported course runs; unsupported hidden-retry modes are outside the verified configuration, not silently compliant.\n81: \n82: Budget state: positive integer `limit`, charged sends, active reservations and exhaustion. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation. Validate C5 first so context rejection obtains no reservation.\n83: \n84: No slot => BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no request, no official recommendation. Limit 3 allows exactly 3 attempts; the fourth is refused. Concurrent runs do not share counters. Include application fallback/retry attempts separately. C4 does not promise a monetary or token cap. Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.\n85: \n86: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context\n87: \n88: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. Other analyst turns and risk roles are not implicitly covered. Before reserving C4, fully expand/convert the scoped final message sequence into one agreed provider-facing representation.\n89: \n90: Canonical v1 measurement: the final provider-facing message array encoded as JSON with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon) without optional whitespace, allow_nan=False, then UTF-8. Use the ChatMessage representation below and freeze byte fixtures before implementation. Do not measure before template expansion or change representation after measuring. Tool schemas and other separately bound fields are excluded from this message metric and must be recorded/bounded separately; this is not a cap on the whole HTTP body.\n91: \n92: Required blocks: role/task identity; standing safety/publication rules; ticker/date/run identity; current required evidence/verified metrics/source coverage; and the active tool-call/result exchange. Optional blocks: explicitly marked older discussion/history. A tool-call/result pair is indivisible; if a member is required, preserve the whole pair. Text-wrapped tools retain name, arguments and corresponding result. Removing context cannot delete authoritative evidence/state from storage.\n93: \n94: At the configured 65536-byte acceptance cap: short input passes unchanged. If oversized, remove optional groups oldest first (stable original index for ties), reassemble, reinject critical constraints and remeasure. Do not summarize required evidence with another unmetered model call. If required blocks cannot fit or pairing cannot be preserved, return CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE; zero send, reservation and debit. Same normalized input/config produces identical prepared output. Run final retention/pairing checks before C4.\n95: \n96: This byte cap does not implement the separate D2 token-budget requirement. ADR-001 records that architecture design and the remaining tokenizer/model-capacity validation. Do not infer token counts from bytes/4 or claim provider safety from 64 KiB alone.\n97: \n98: ## Contract-change and approval record\n99: \n100: Before implementation, record requirement IDs, contract revision, baseline SHA, exact read/edit paths, fixture/case revision, reviewer and approval time. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Feature PRs link the approved plan and actual evidence; the coordinator runs integrated regressions before release.\n101: \n102: \n103: ## V1 shared record layout\n104: \n105: Version field: `contract_version = \"1.0\"`. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. Lists have deterministic order; ID-indexed registries are mappings, not unordered output prose.\n106: \n107: | Record | Required shared fields beyond identity | Owner |\n108: | --- | --- | --- |\n109: | RunContext | contract_version, execution_status, request_limit (positive integer) | Existing graph/run entry; integration by coordinator |\n110: | EvidenceRecord | evidence_id, source_kind, vendor, source_ref, content_ref, window_start, window_end | FR-01 collection/index adapter |\n111: | AcceptedArgument | argument_id, claim (nonempty text), evidence_ids (nonempty list) | FR-01 validates against run-local evidence; a model flag is not acceptance |\n112: | CandidateDecision | rating (untrusted string or null), argument_ids | Model/adapters produce; C1 decides |\n113: | PublicationResult | publication_status, reason_codes, rating (allowed string or null), argument_ids, evidence_ids | FR-01 |\n114: | Operand | role, value (finite decimal string), unit, period, source_ref, field_ref | FR-02 input adapter; roles current/prior/numerator/denominator/reference |\n115: | MetricRequest | kind (yoy/ratio/price_delta), operands | FR-02 input |\n116: | VerifiedMetric | metric_id, kind, operands, result_value (decimal string), result_unit, formula, source_refs | FR-02 immutable run-local registry |\n117: | MetricResult | status (VERIFIED/UNVERIFIABLE), metric (VerifiedMetric or null), reason_codes | FR-02 |\n118: | SourceOutcome | source_id, window_start, window_end, available (bool), valid_record_count, reason_codes, evidence_refs | FR-03 normalization adapter |\n119: | SentimentCoverage | coverage_status, valid_sources, total_sources (=3), sources (mapping keyed news/stocktwits/reddit) | FR-03 deterministic coverage |\n120: | SentimentAssessment | all SentimentCoverage fields, assessment_status (MEASURED/UNKNOWN), overall_band, overall_score, confidence, assessment_reason_codes, narrative | FR-03 deterministic finalization |\n121: | ContextBlock | group_id, required (bool), messages (list of ChatMessage); grouping metadata is never sent to the model | NFR-02 scoped adapter |\n122: | PreparedRequest | status (READY/CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE), messages (list or null), message_bytes, original_message_bytes, dropped_group_ids, required_groups_ok | NFR-02 or nonreducing adapter |\n123: | Reservation | reservation_id, run_id, state (reserved/charged/cancelled); opaque to other features | NFR-01 |\n124: \n125: `Operand.period` is `{kind, start, end, label}`: kind is quarter/year/instant, start/end are ISO dates, and label records the source's fiscal period or quote timestamp. Currency and scale are part of unit (for example USD vs USD_millions); conversion must be explicit and preserve original operands. Do not silently take abs(capex), invent comparable periods or round source values to make a fixture match. An EvidenceRecord source_ref identifies the source, while content_ref locates the retained shareable material/fixture; an ID with no resolvable retained material is insufficient.\n126: \n127: For SentimentAssessment, overall_band is one existing measured band or UNKNOWN. overall_score is a finite float in [0,10] for MEASURED, otherwise null. confidence keeps the existing low/medium/high vocabulary; UNKNOWN uses low and is not a measured weak-neutral signal. Missing sources are unavailable with reasons; valid sources have valid_record_count >=1. Missing uncollected source entries are normalized as unavailable with NOT_COLLECTED rather than increasing the denominator or silently disappearing. Extra providers do not count as fourth sources. Source order is news, stocktwits, reddit.\n128: \n129: `ChatMessage` contains provider-facing role, content and, when present, name/tool_call_id/tool_calls/reasoning_content. Preserve content strings or JSON-compatible content blocks without paraphrasing. Preserve each tool call's id, type, function name and arguments plus the paired tool result. Reasoning fields required by the selected provider's tool round-trip are mandatory if present. Do not add ContextBlock metadata to ChatMessage. The cap measures the agreed canonical message representation, not HTTP whitespace, the whole body, output tokens or hidden provider overhead.\n130: \n131: ## V1 callable boundaries (specification signatures, no implementation)\n132: \n133: Inputs are read-only to consumers. Return the declared records; do not attach extra authoritative fields through prose. Signatures below describe Python-callable boundaries; they do not create five network services.\n134: \n135: | Planned owner | Public v1 call | Behavior |\n136: | --- | --- | --- |\n137: | publication_gate.py | validate_argument(argument, evidence_index, run) -> AcceptedArgument or validation failure | Check current-run references before acceptance |\n138: | publication_gate.py | evaluate_publication(candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run) -> PublicationResult | Recheck accepted references and rating; one result for all official sinks |\n139: | verified_metrics.py | verify_metric(request, run) -> MetricResult | Compute from validated operands, register only verified records |\n140: | verified_metrics.py | resolve_metric(metric_id, registry, run) -> VerifiedMetric or null | Resolve trusted ID; never accept a caller-supplied replacement value |\n141: | sentiment_coverage.py | normalize_source(raw_result, source_id, run, window_start, window_end) -> SourceOutcome | Derive availability from collection receipts and approved metadata rules |\n142: | sentiment_coverage.py | build_sentiment_coverage(sources, run) -> SentimentCoverage | Count three logical sources once each |\n143: | sentiment_coverage.py | finalize_sentiment(coverage, model_assessment_or_null, run) -> SentimentAssessment | Coverage is authoritative; validate score/band; no imputation |\n144: | context_limit.py | prepare_context(blocks, max_message_bytes=65536) -> PreparedRequest | Only the two scoped sites reduce; reject irreducible context |\n145: | request_budget.py | RequestBudget(run_id, limit); try_reserve() -> Reservation or null; charge_attempt(ticket); cancel_before_send(ticket); snapshot() | Atomic lifecycle; cancellation only when transport is known not to have started |\n146: | request_budget.py | dispatch(prepared, budget, send) -> sender's normal response type | Require READY, reserve, charge at attempt boundary, invoke send exactly once; refusal is a typed failure, never a Hold/default rating |\n147: \n148: The sender callable accepts the prepared messages and performs exactly one underlying request with SDK retries disabled. Application fallback/retries call dispatch again. Dispatch failure types are BudgetExhausted, ContextTooLarge and ProviderFailure (defined in the responsible owner module); the graph entry maps them to C0 terminal state. Provider failures after an ambiguous attempt remain charged. Snapshot separates charged attempts, known actual sends and unknown-delivery attempts; a connection attempt is not claimed to be a billed model response.\n149: \n150: Publication evaluation first respects C0 terminal failure/incomplete execution (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or RUN_NOT_COMPLETE); then rejects an invalid rating; then rejects insufficient references. APPROVED has an allowed rating, nonempty accepted argument/evidence references and no rejection reasons. BLOCKED always has rating=null. An incomplete workflow cannot publish an earlier candidate.\n151: \n152: ## V1 graph handoff and compatibility\n153: \n154: Add the following keys to the existing AgentState through narrow integration edits: course_run (RunContext), evidence_index, argument_index, verified_metrics, sentiment_assessment and publication_result. These are separate state keys; do not have parallel nodes overwrite an entire common nested dictionary. Existing nodes own their existing report strings. New owner records are not reconstructed from those strings. Avoid new dependencies or replacement of the orchestrator.\n155: \n156: For sentiment, the analyst emits sentiment_assessment and renders its legacy sentiment_report from that same record, including the model-message/report views. At 0/3, the selected v1 path skips the sentiment model call and creates a deterministic missing-data narrative with UNKNOWN/null. With data, finalize the model assessment while preserving coverage; provider/free-text fallback cannot restore a made-up default score. The FR-03 task plan tests schema/renderer compatibility before selecting the internal Pydantic adaptation. FR-01 can publish from valid non-sentiment evidence when its own gate passes.\n157: \n158: The shared model client receives PreparedRequest. At the two NFR-02 sites use prepare_context; elsewhere use a nonreducing READY adapter so NFR-01 covers all sends without accidentally applying a 64 KiB cap to every call. All branches then use the same C4 dispatch boundary. Tests can use fixed fake producers/consumers until integration, but combined graph acceptance needs the real connected owner modules.\n159: \n160: ## Working defaults and limits with different purposes\n161: \n162: | Setting | V1 choice / purpose | Change rule |\n163: | --- | --- | --- |\n164: | Application baseline | 9fa1196; retain existing package layout | New baseline needs explicit rationale and regressions |\n165: | Local environment | Reuse verified Python 3.11 environment; record exact patch/dependencies | Align a team-approved baseline when needed, no automatic reinstall |\n166: | Course profile model | School CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash for both tiers; explicit thinking-disabled request after compatibility check | Record actual settings; do not infer backend revision from alias |\n167: | Course profile output allowance | 4096 tokens as initial run-profile choice, not an acceptance threshold | Raise only with a truncation reason and recorded configuration |\n168: | Product request_limit | 40 per single-stock run as initial configurable profile | Revisit against completed baseline; D1 hard rule is actual requests <= configured limit |\n169: | NFR-01 boundary fixture | limit 3, exactly-three succeeds, fourth refuses | Fixed test condition; not the normal application's default |\n170: | NFR-02 message cap | 65536 bytes at analyst closure and neutral risk role | Normal configurable setting; changes update the affected fixtures/contracts |\n171: | Token architecture proposal | 16384 input tokens, 80% trigger remains unactivated design pending counting/capacity evidence | Not an automatic global gate or an extra feature |\n172: \n173: Production metered resume remains disabled until counter restoration is implemented and verified.\n174: \n175: ## Change control\n176: \n177: Internal class and function organization may vary while preserving shared record names, types, authority and failure semantics. Changes to public fields, source-validity rules, thresholds or shared dispatch/publication paths require a versioned contract/test revision and affected-owner review. Existing modules remain integration adapters; do not duplicate business rules across CLI, API and reports.\n4: \n5: | Requirement | Owner and boundary |\n6: | --- | --- |\n7: | FR-01 / INV-01 | Publication gate owns the official outcome; pass its result to all sinks, including memory. |\n8: | FR-02 | Verified metrics owns arithmetic and reference resolution. Downstream renders resolved values. |\n9: | FR-03 | Sentiment coverage owns missingness and reasons. Consumers do not invent numeric defaults. |\n10: | NFR-01 / INV-02 | Request budget owns the atomic run counter. Only a reserved dispatch may send. |\n11: | NFR-02 | Context limit owns payload sizing and deterministic reduction; it cannot bypass the budget or remove mandatory content. |\n12: \n13: For each new or modified module and function, document the associated requirement, ADR and invariant where applicable in a short comment or docstring. Integration code may orchestrate but cannot override an authoritative rejection. The team must name a shared-file integration owner and exact paths for state/schema, reporting and dispatch changes. Each feature may use an approved fake producer/consumer for independent tests; integration tests must later replace those doubles with real connected components. Do not treat a mock-only pass as proof that the integrated graph satisfies the contract."

FR-01: give the model this run's evidence IDs and material together, so\n48:         # a cited ID resolves to real run material.\n49:         evidence_state = state.get(\"evidence_index\")\n50:         aliases = _select_aliases(as_index(evidence_state).evidence_ids, \"E\")\n51:         evidence_block = evidence_menu(evidence_state, aliases)\n52: \n53:         prompt = f\"\"\"You are a Bull Analyst advocating for investing in the {target_label}. Your task is to build a strong, evidence-based case emphasizing growth potential, competitive advantages, and positive market indicators. Leverage the provided research and data to address concerns and counter bearish arguments effectively.\n54: \n55: Key points to focus on:\n56: - Growth Potential: Highlight the company's market opportunities, revenue projections, and scalability.\n57: - Competitive Advantages: Emphasize factors like unique products, strong branding, or dominant market positioning.\n58: - Positive Indicators: Use financial health, industry trends, and recent positive news as evidence.\n59: - Bear Counterpoints: Critically analyze the bear argument with specific data and sound reasoning, addressing concerns thoroughly and showing why the bull perspective holds stronger merit.\n60: - Engagement: Present your argument in a conversational style, engaging directly with the bear analyst's points and debating effectively rather than just listing data.\n61: \n62: Resources available:\n63: {instrument_context}\n64: Market research report: {market_research_report}\n65: Social media sentiment report: {sentiment_report}\n66: Latest world affairs news: {news_report}\n67: {fundamentals_label}: {fundamentals_report}\n68: Conversation history of the debate: {history}\n69: Last bear argument: {current_response}\n70: \n71: Available evidence (cite these exact IDs in evidence_ids; do not invent IDs):\n72: {evidence_block}\n73: \n74: Each evidence line ends with a short selection such as '= E1'.                 "text": "Read file [REDACTED_HOME]/Desktop/learningfile/cityu/CS5351/Project/TradingAgents_Pro/tradingagents/agents/schemas.py, lines 1-506\n1: \"\"\"Pydantic schemas used by agents that produce structured output.\n2: \n3: The framework's primary artifact is still prose: each agent's natural-language\n4: reasoning is what users read in the saved markdown reports and what the\n5: downstream agents read as context.  Structured output is layered onto the\n6: three decision-making agents (Research Manager, Trader, Portfolio Manager)\n7: so that:\n8: \n9: - Their outputs follow consistent section headers across runs and providers\n10: - Each provider's native structured-output mode is used (json_schema for\n11:   OpenAI/xAI, response_schema for Gemini, tool-use for Anthropic)\n12: - Schema field descriptions become the model's output instructions, freeing\n13:   the prompt body to focus on context and the rating-scale guidance\n14: - A render helper turns the parsed Pydantic instance back into the same\n15:   markdown shape the rest of the system already consumes, so display,\n16:   memory log, and saved reports keep working unchanged\n17: \"\"\"\n18: \n19: from __future__ import annotations\n20: \n21: from enum import StrEnum\n22: from typing import Literal\n23: \n24: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator\n25: \n26: # LLMs sometimes write a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\", ...) into an optional\n27: # numeric field instead of omitting it. Coerce those to None so the structured\n28: # call validates instead of erroring (#1058). Pydantic still parses real numeric\n29: # strings (\"189.5\") to float.\n30: _NULLISH_FLOAT = {\"\", \"none\", \"n/a\", \"na\", \"null\", \"nil\", \"-\", \"tbd\", \"unknown\"}\n31: \n32: \n33: def _coerce_optional_float(value):\n34:     \"\"\"Normalise an LLM-written optional numeric field before validation.\n35: \n36:     Three shapes show up in practice: a placeholder string (\"None\", \"N/A\") in\n37:     place of an omitted value (#1058); a percentage where a price was asked for\n38:     (\"15%\", #1288); and a human-formatted price (\"$1,234.50\"). A percentage\n39:     cannot be salvaged into an absolute level -- reading \"15%\" as 15 would put a\n40:     stop at $15 on a $600 stock -- so it is dropped like a placeholder, leaving\n41:     one bad field to null out instead of failing the whole proposal. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the\n7: program itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating\n8: fallback is honoured around the gate.\n9: \n10: Design (plan revision 1, superseded by the R8-B C1 v1.0 section below):\n11: - The run's evidence index is built *before* the first debate turn from material\n12:   the run actually retained (the market analyst's verified snapshots), so every\n13:   accepted argument cites material that exists in this run.        if not isinstance(item, dict):\n299:             continue\n300:         evidence_id = item.get(\"evidence_id\") or item.get(\"id\")\n301:         if not evidence_id:\n302:             continue\n303:         evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n304:             evidence_id=evidence_id,\n305:             source=item.get(\"source\") or item.get(\"source_kind\", \"\"),\n306:             excerpt=item.get(\"excerpt\") or _excerpt(item.get(\"source_ref\", \"\")),\n307:             run_id=item.get(\"run_id\") or run_id,\n308:         )\n309: \n310:     index = EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n311:     if isinstance(value.get(\"arguments\"), list):\n312:         argument_rows = value[\"arguments\"]\n313:     else:\n314:         argument_rows = [\n315:             record for key, record in value.items()\n316:             if isinstance(record, dict) and (record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\"))\n317:         ]\n318:     for arg in argument_rows:\n319:         if not isinstance(arg, dict):\n320:             continue\n321:         argument_id = arg.get(\"argument_id\") or arg.get(\"id\")\n322:         if not argument_id:\n323: or arg.get(\"claim\", \"\"),\n327:             evidence_ids=tuple(arg.get(\"evidence_ids\", [])),\n328:         )\n329:     return index\n330: \n331: \n332: def build_evidence_index(run_id: str, state) -> EvidenceIndex:\n333:     \"\"\"Index this run's non-empty analyst reports, one ``evidence_id`` per report.\n334: \n335:     Only material actually present in the run is indexed. Deterministic: ids and\n336:     iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.\n337:     \"\"\"\n338:     evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}\n339:     for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:\n340:         text = state.get(key)\n341:         if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():\n342:             continue\n343:         evidence_id = f\"ev:{run_id}:{key}\"\n344:         evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(\n345:             evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=_excerpt(text), run_id=run_id,\n346:         )\n347:     return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)\n348: \n349: \n350: def evidence_menu(index, aliases: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:\n351:     \"\"\"The evidence IDs and their material, for the researcher prompt.\n352: \n353:     The model may cite only these IDs; they are the program-built index for this\n354:     run, so a cited ID resolves to actual run material.\n355:     \"\"\"\n356:     idx = as_index(index)\n357:     if not idx.evidence_ids:\n358:         return \"(No evidence is available in this run; you cannot cite any evidence ID.)\"\n359:     selections = {reference: alias for alias, reference in (aliases or {}).items()}\n360:     lines = []\n361:     for record in idx.evidence_records:\n362:         suffix = f\" = {selections[record.evidence_id]}\" if record.evidence_id in selections else \"\"\n363:         lines.append(f\"- {record.evidence_id}  [{record.source}] {record.excerpt}{suffix}\")\n364:     return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n365: \n366: \n367: def _excerpt(text: str, limit: int = 160) -> str:\n368:     \"\"\"A short, single-line pointer into the material (for traceability only).\"\"\"\n369:     flat = \" \".join(text.split())\n370:     return flat if len(flat) <= limit else flat[: limit - 1] + \"\\u2026\"\n371: \n372: \n373: # FR-01 / ADR-001: aliases are local model selections. C1 receives canonical IDs.\n374: def _select_aliases(references, prefix: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n375:     \"\"\"Build an invocation-local menu without shadowing opaque canonical IDs.\"\"\"\n376:     canonical = tuple(dict.fromkeys(\n377:         reference for reference in references if isinstance(reference, str) and reference\n378:     ))\n379:     reserved = set(canonical)\n380:     aliases = {}\n381:     number = 1\n382:     for reference in canonical:\n383:         while f\"{prefix}{number}\" in reserved:\n384:             number += 1\n385:         aliases[f\"{prefix}{number}\"] = reference\n386:         number += 1\n387:     return aliases\n388: \n389: \n390: def _resolve_selections(selections, aliases: dict[str, str], actor: str) -> list[str]:\n391:     \"\"\"Resolve exact selections, preserving invalid references for C1 rejection.\"\"\"\n392:     canonical = set(aliases.values())\n393:     resolved = []\n394:     for selection in selections or ():\n395:         if isinstance(selection, str) and selection in aliases:\n396:             resolved.append(aliases[selection])\n397:         else:\n398:             if selection not in canonical:\n399:                 logger.warning(\n400:                     \"Reference rejected: actor=%s reference=%r reason=UNKNOWN_REFERENCE\",\n401:                     actor, repr(selection)[:160],\n402:                 )\n403:             resolved.append(selection)\n404:     return resolved\n405: \n406: \n407: def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:\n408:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.\n409: \n410:     Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.\n411:     ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.\n412:     \"\"\"\n413:     if value is None:\n414:         return None\n415:     rating = getattr(value, \"value\", value)\n416:     if not isinstance(rating, str):\n417:         return None\n418:     return rating if rating in _RATING_SET else None\n419: \n420: \n421: def evaluate(index, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids) -> GateOutcome:\n422:     \"\"\"Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.\n423: \n424:     ``index`` may be the state dict or an EvidenceIndex. Order matters: an invalid\n425:     rating is reported before a missing chain, so a candidate that fails both\n426:     returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is consulted here.\n427:     \"\"\"\n428:     idx = as_index(index)\n429:     rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)\n430:     if rating is None:\n431:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)\n432: \n433:     cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)\n434:     resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n435:     for argument_id in cited:\n436:         if not idx.has_argument(argument_id):\n437:             continue\n438:         argument = idx.argument(argument_id)\n439:         for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:\n440:             if idx.has_evidence(evidence_id):\n441:                 resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, idx.evidence(evidence_id).source))\n442:     if not resolved:\n443:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)\n444: \n445:     return GateOutcome(\n446:         status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),\n447:     )\n448: \n449: \n450: def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:\n451:     \"\"\"Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.\n452: \n453:     On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the\n454:     candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the\n455:     returned state carries no candidate material at all — the candidate body,\n456:     candidate rating and candidate argument ids are removed from the mapping, so\n457:     the Python API's returned state cannot expose or re-derive the candidate. The\n458:     only place ``REVIEW`` appears is the API's second tuple member (computed by the\n459:     caller via ``run_rating``); ``final_rating`` is emptied here, not set to REVIEW.\n460:     \"\"\"\n461:     status = outcome.status\n462:     final_state[\"publication_status\"] = status\n463:     final_state[\"publication_reason\"] = outcome.reason\n464:     final_state[\"publication_chain\"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)\n465: \n466:     if outcome.approved:\n467:         body = final_state.get(\"candidate_decision\") or final_state.get(\"final_trade_decision\") or \"\"\n468:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = outcome.rating\n469:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = body\n470:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n471:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n472:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n473:     else:\n474:         # No candidate material leaks into the returned state: the body, its rating\n475:         # and the ids it cited are all removed. ``final_rating`` is emptied rather\n476:         # than set to REVIEW; REVIEW is the API's second tuple member only.\n477:         final_state[\"final_rating\"] = \"\"\n478:         final_state[\"final_trade_decision\"] = \"\"\n479:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_decision\", None)\n480:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_rating\", None)\n481:         final_state.pop(\"candidate_argument_ids\", None)\n482:     return final_state\n483: \n484: \n485: # --- C1 v1.0: mapping-authoritative evaluation -------------------------------\n486: #\n487: # The authoritative indexes are ID -> record mappings: ``argument_index`` keyed by\n488: # ``argument_id`` and ``evidence_index`` keyed by ``evidence_id``. The legacy\n489: # shapes ``index_to_state(...)`` (lists under \"evidence\"/\"arguments\") and\n490: # ``accepted_arguments`` are a compatibility layer only: an argument that exists\n491: # solely in that view never resolves a reference.\n492: \n493: \n494: _IDENTITY_KEYS = (\"run_id\", \"ticker\", \"as_of_date\")\n495: \n496: # C1 v1.0 required shared fields, beyond identity. \"A missing required field is an\n497: # invalid record\": a record without one is not admissible evidence/acceptance.\n498: _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED = (\n499:     \"evidence_id\", \"source_kind\", \"vendor\", \"source_ref\",\n500:     \"content_ref\", \"window_start\", \"window_end\",\n501: )\n502: _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED = (\"argument_id\", \"claim\")\n503: \n504: \n505: def _field_present(record: dict, key: str) -> bool:\n506:     \"\"\"Whether a required field is present and non-empty.\n507: \n508:     A missing value, ``None``, an empty string and a whitespace-only string are\n509:     all the same thing here: no value. A list is present when it is non-empty.\n510:     \"\"\"\n511:     value = record.get(key)\n512:     if isinstance(value, str):\n513:         return bool(value.strip())\n514:     if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):\n515:         return len(value) > 0\n516:     return value is not None\n517: \n518: \n519: def _required_fields_ok(record, required) -> bool:\n520:     \"\"\"Whether every C1 required field of ``record`` is present and non-empty.\"\"\"\n521:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n522:         return False\n523:     return all(_field_present(record, key) for key in required)\n524: \n525: \n526: def _identity(record, run: dict) -> tuple[str, str, str] | None:\n527:     \"\"\"The record's ``(run_id, ticker, as_of_date)`` when it *fully* matches the run.\n528: \n529:     Ownership is checked on the record's full identity, never on how its ID is\n530:     spelled: an ID needs no prefix and must not contain the run id. All three\n531:     fields are required and must equal the ``RunContext``'s, so a record with a\n532:     missing identity, a partial identity or a foreign run's identity is not this\n533:     run's material and never resolves.\n534:     \"\"\"\n535:     if not isinstance(record, dict):\n536:         return None\n537:     if not all(isinstance(run.get(key), str) and run.get(key) for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS):\n538:         return None\n539:     for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS:\n540:         if record.get(key) != run.get(key):\n541:             return None\n542:     return tuple(run[key] for key in _IDENTITY_KEYS)\n543: \n544: \n545: def _material_resolves(record: dict, run: dict, results_dir) -> bool:\n546:     \"\"\"Whether the record's referenced retained material exists **and has content**.\n547: \n548:     Only a record that names retained material (``content_ref``) and whose material\n549:     can be re-read from this run's retention root counts. A record with no\n550:     ``content_ref`` — an analyst report indexed only in memory — has no traceable\n551:     source material, so it is **not** admissible evidence: the prose itself is not\n552:     a retained source. A reference whose file is expired, deleted or foreign does\n553:     not resolve either.\n554: \n555:     C1 v1.0: \"assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content\n556:     valid\". A retained file that resolves but holds only whitespace has no\n557:     substance, so it is not evidence.\n558:     \"\"\"\n559:     content_ref = record.get(\"content_ref\")\n560:     if not isinstance(content_ref, str) or not content_ref:\n561:         return False\n562:     if not isinstance(results_dir, (str, Path)) or not str(results_dir):\n563:         return False\n564:     from tradingagents.agents.evidence_collection import resolve_content_ref\n565: \n566:     try:\n567:         material = resolve_content_ref(content_ref, results_dir, run)\n568:     except (OSError, ValueError):\n569:         return False\n570:     if not isinstance(material, str):\n571:         return False\n572:     # A retained file that exists but holds only whitespace has no substance.\n573:     return bool(material.strip())\n574: \n575: \n576: def _evidence_records(evidence_index, run: dict, results_dir=None) -> dict[str, dict]:\n577:     \"\"\"The run's own evidence, keyed by ``evidence_id``.\n578: \n579:     Only the authoritative v1 mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which\n580:     carries the same records) is read; an in-memory ``EvidenceIndex`` object is\n581:     the compatibility layer and is refused here, because an object carries no\n582:     per-record ``content_ref`` and would therefore skip the material read-back.\n583: \n584:     A record counts only when its **full identity** matches the ``RunContext``;\n585:     the ID's spelling is irrelevant. A record whose referenced retained material\n586:     cannot be resolved is not evidence, so a report record with no ``content_ref``\n587:     never backs a release.\n588:     \"\"\"\n589:     if not isinstance(evidence_index, dict):\n590:         return {}\n591:     rows = _mapping_rows(evidence_index, \"evidence\", \"id\")\n592:     records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n593:     for _key, record in rows:\n594:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n595:             continue\n596:         # C1: \"a missing required field is an invalid record\". The *record* is\n597:         # judged, never its mapping key or a legacy ``id`` alias: an index entry\n598:         # that supplies ``evidence_id`` only by being keyed under it still has no\n599:         # ``evidence_id`` of its own, so it is not evidence.\n600:         if not _required_fields_ok(record, _EVIDENCE_REQUIRED):\n601:             continue\n602:         evidence_id = record[\"evidence_id\"]\n603:         if not isinstance(evidence_id, str) or not evidence_id:\n604:             continue\n605:         # Ownership is the record's full identity, never the ID's spelling.\n606:         if _identity(record, run) is None:\n607:             continue\n608:         if not _material_resolves(record, run, results_dir):\n609:             continue\n610:         records[evidence_id] = record\n611:     return records\n612: \n613: \n614: def _argument_records(argument_index, run: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:\n615:     \"\"\"The run's accepted arguments, keyed by ``argument_id``.\n616: \n617:     Only the authoritative v1 mapping (or the legacy serialized list, which\n618:     carries the same records) is read; an ``EvidenceIndex`` object or a\n619:     ``{\"accepted_arguments\": [...]}`` view is the compatibility layer and is not\n620:     a release authority, so it yields nothing here.\n621: \n622:     A record counts only when its **full identity** matches the ``RunContext``\n623:     (``run_id``, ``ticker`` and ``as_of_date`` all equal). An ID needs no prefix\n624:     and must not contain the run id. A record that states no identity at all is\n625:     not owned by any run and is refused, whether or not a run id is available.\n626:     \"\"\"\n627:     if not isinstance(argument_index, dict):\n628:         return {}\n629:     if \"accepted_arguments\" in argument_index and \"arguments\" not in argument_index:\n630:         return {}\n631:     rows = _mapping_rows(argument_index, \"arguments\", \"id\")\n632:     records: dict[str, dict] = {}\n633:     for key, record in rows:\n634:         if not isinstance(record, dict):\n635:             continue\n636:         argument_id = record.get(\"argument_id\") or record.get(\"id\") or key\n637:         if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n638:             continue\n639:         if _identity(record, run) is None:\n640:             # No identity, a partial identity, or another run's identity.\n641:             continue\n642:         # C1: an AcceptedArgument needs a nonempty claim and a nonempty\n643:         # ``evidence_ids`` list. ``text`` is the legacy spelling of the claim.\n644:         normalised = {\n645:             **record,\n646:             \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n647:             \"claim\": record.get(\"claim\") or record.get(\"text\") or \"\",\n648:         }\n649:         if not _required_fields_ok(normalised, _ARGUMENT_REQUIRED):\n650:             continue\n651:         if not _field_present(normalised, \"evidence_ids\"):\n652:             continue\n653:         records[argument_id] = record\n654:     return records\n655: \n656: \n657: def validate_argument(argument, evidence_index, run, results_dir=None) -> dict | None:\n658:     \"\"\"C1 v1.0: check current-run references before accepting an argument.\n659: \n660:     The v1 callable boundary from ``interface-contracts.md``. Returns the\n661:     **accepted record** — the argument's full identity plus its claim and the\n662:     resolved evidence ids — or ``None`` when the submission is not acceptable.\n663: \n664:     An argument is accepted only when every part of C1 holds:\n665: \n666:     * it carries the run's **full identity** (``run_id``, ``ticker``,\n667:       ``as_of_date`` all equal the ``RunContext``'s), so a foreign or\n668:       identity-less submission is not this run's argument;\n669:     * it has an ``argument_id`` and a nonempty ``claim``;\n670:     * ``evidence_ids`` is a nonempty list, and **every** cited id resolves to\n671:       admissible evidence in this run: present in the index, complete, and\n672:       backed by retained material that exists and has content.\n673: \n674:     A model flag is not acceptance, and a partially resolvable citation is not a\n675:     partial acceptance: one unresolvable id refuses the argument. This is the\n676:     validation layer; ``evaluate_publication`` rechecks the whole chain again,\n677:     because a record can reach the index without passing through here.\n678:     \"\"\"\n679:     if not isinstance(argument, dict):\n680:         return None\n681:     if _identity(argument, run) is None:\n682:         return None\n683:     argument_id = argument.get(\"argument_id\") or argument.get(\"id\")\n684:     if not isinstance(argument_id, str) or not argument_id:\n685:         return None\n686:     claim = argument.get(\"claim\") or argument.get(\"text\") or \"\"\n687:     if not isinstance(claim, str) or not claim.strip():\n688:         return None\n689:     evidence_ids = argument.get(\"evidence_ids\")\n690:     if not isinstance(evidence_ids, (list, tuple)) or not evidence_ids:\n691:         return None\n692:     if any(not isinstance(eid, str) or not eid for eid in evidence_ids):\n693:         return None\n694: \n695:     available = _evidence_records(evidence_index, run, results_dir)\n696:     if any(eid not in available for eid in evidence_ids):\n697:         return None\n698: \n699:     return {\n700:         \"contract_version\": str(argument.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n701:         \"run_id\": run[\"run_id\"],\n702:         \"ticker\": run[\"ticker\"],\n703:         \"as_of_date\": run[\"as_of_date\"],\n704:         \"argument_id\": argument_id,\n705:         \"claim\": claim,\n706:         \"speaker\": argument.get(\"speaker\", \"\"),\n707:         \"evidence_ids\": list(evidence_ids),\n708:     }\n709: \n710: \n711: def _mapping_rows(index: dict, list_key: str, id_key: str):\n712:     \"\"\"``(key, record)`` pairs of a mapping index or of its legacy serialized form.\n713: \n714:     Three shapes are read:\n715: \n716:     * a bare ID -> record mapping yields its own items;\n717:     * the authoritative v1 wrapper ``{\"run_id\": ..., list_key: {id: record}}``\n718:       yields the wrapped mapping's items, so metadata is never mistaken for a\n719:       record;\n720:     * the legacy serialized form ``{list_key: [ {...id_key: ...} ]}`` is read\n721:       from that list.\n722: \n723:     The key a record is found under is a fallback only; the record's own ID field\n724:     wins.\n725:     \"\"\"\n726:     if list_key in index:\n727:         wrapped = index[list_key]\n728:         if isinstance(wrapped, dict):\n729:             return list(wrapped.items())\n730:         if isinstance(wrapped, list):\n731:             return [(None, item) for item in wrapped]\n732:     return list(index.items())\n733: \n734: \n735: def _rating(value) -> str | None:\n736:     \"\"\"The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` when not publishable.\n737: \n738:     Only the exact five tiers count. ``REVIEW``, casing variants, surrounding\n739:     text (\"Buy (small size)\") and null are all invalid: free text is not a call.\n740:     \"\"\"\n741:     if not isinstance(value, str):\n742:         return None\n743:     return value if value in _RATING_SET else None\n744: \n745: \n746: def evaluate_publication(\n747:     candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run, results_dir=None\n748: ) -> PublicationResult:\n749:     \"\"\"C1 v1.0: the one deterministic publication result for a run.\n750: \n751:     Rows are checked in the approved order, and the first matching row decides:\n752: \n753:     1. C0 terminal failure / incomplete execution (``BUDGET_EXHAUSTED``,\n754:        ``CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`` keep their own code; anything not ``COMPLETED``,\n755:        including a missing ``RunContext``, is ``RUN_NOT_COMPLETE``).\n756:     2. An invalid rating (``INVALID_RATING``).\n757:     3. Missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted references\n758:        (``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``).\n759:     4. Otherwise APPROVED, with the rating and the validated references.\n760: \n761:     References are rechecked here, not taken from the model: a cited argument\n762:     must exist in this run's ``argument_index``, ownership is decided by each\n763:     record's full identity (never by an ID prefix), and each of its evidence ids\n764:     must resolve in this run's ``evidence_index`` with its retained material still\n765:     readable under ``results_dir``. A record with no retained material never\n766:     resolves. BLOCKED always carries ``rating=None``.\n767:     \"\"\"\n768:     run = run if isinstance(run, dict) else {}\n769:     identity = {\n770:         \"contract_version\": str(run.get(\"contract_version\") or \"1.0\"),\n771:         \"run_id\": run.get(\"run_id\") or \"\",\n772:         \"ticker\": run.get(\"ticker\") or \"\",\n773:         \"as_of_date\": run.get(\"as_of_date\") or \"\",\n774:     }\n775: \n776:     def _blocked(*codes: str) -> PublicationResult:\n777:         return PublicationResult(\n778:             **identity, publication_status=BLOCKED, reason_codes=tuple(codes),\n779:             rating=None, argument_ids=(), evidence_ids=(),\n780:         )\n781: \n782:     # Row 1: C0 execution state.\n783:     status = run.get(\"execution_status\")\n784:     if status in _TERMINAL_EXECUTION_NAMED:\n785:         return _blocked(status)\n786:     if status != EXECUTION_COMPLETED:\n787:         # FAILED, RUNNING and a missing RunContext: the workflow did not finish\n788:         # normally, so nothing it produced may publish.\n789:         return _blocked(RUN_NOT_COMPLETE)\n790: \n791:     # Row 2: the rating must be one of the five tiers.\n792:     candidate = candidate if isinstance(candidate, dict) else {}\n793:     rating = _rating(candidate.get(\"rating\"))\n794:     if rating is None:\n795:         return _blocked(INVALID_RATING)\n796: \n797:     #
